I can't say I recommend this game, and honestly, it doesn't really have anything to do with the sheer litany of technical problems this title has running on PC. It ran fine for me, maxed out with some occasional sound loss (I think that's an Unreal Engine bug, it's not the first UE game I've seen it happen in) and some hangups. But those issues are fairly minor and forgivable. I'm going to take this opportunity now to preface that I think Arkham Origins is probably the best in the series for story and overall feel, so I will be relentlessly comparing Knight to its predecessor.
I would give my list of pros as "boy the environment sure looks pretty" but frankly, it's so busy, every single corner has been crammed with so much detail that there's nowhere for the eye to focus on or rest. And the lighting is just kind of out of control. "Hey guys, we got our fancy new rendering, so we can have a lot of lights and reflections!" "PUT GIANT TUBE LIGHTS EVERYWHERE"
And honestly, aside from bigger texture sizes, more lights and reflections, it really doesn't look much better than Arkham Origins, and it certainly doesn't aesthetically look better than Origins. The character models especially just feel kind of bleh. They're fantastic technical and artistic showcases, but they don't feel like they have any character in these characters.
The story so far honestly kind of just meanders, it just doesn't have the same sort of intensity, the same sort of gut-punching urgency that its forebears did. It just sorta starts, and then the game goes COMPLETELY out of its way to go tell you to do some side stuff.It actively wants you to not mainline the story to get it over with, they want you to go do some of this fun stuff over here! Except it's not really fun, and oh, I could find the next firefighter rescue, or Azrael fight, but I have to comb the entire effing city to do so. In Arkham City and Origins, it would force you to do kind of one of each, or lead you down a wrong door that led to side content, but it did it fairly early, and then they would♥♥♥♥♥♥right off, letting the story take center stage, not this "oh, well you've done 3 main story missions, its time for you to do some side content" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
Mechanically, kind of the same story as above. It lacks character, the same feeling that the earlier games in the series had. It kind of feels like Rocksteady really just wanted to make any game that wasn't this one, because boy let me tell you, they absolutely cannot get enough of that Batmobile. Does it handle well? No, but it can turn into a tank. Is the environment designed with the Batmobile in mind? Well, sort of, but due to the aforementioned handling comparable to a cow in a supermarket trolley, the AI will always be a better driver than you. Is it fun? Potentially, but all of the controls are slow to respond, and placed in awkward positions on the gamepad, so you know, good luck with that.
And speaking of the gamepad, whose dimwit idea was it to put AR and Missions on the D-Pad?!?!?! OF ALL PLACES. What, was the back menu getting too crowded with its 4 items?!?! I cannot tell you how many times I want to just switch to a gadget, because Gel is always left on the D-Pad. Remode Batarangs are Upper Right. Hacker is Lower Right. But no. I have to hold the Down input, which pauses the game, then you have to rotate the thumbstick to select, then its equipped, so then you can use it.
Did some numbskull go to the Metal Gear school of inventory management and think that was a good idea for the next iteration of an already streamlined and intuitive interface? It breaks the last shed of immersion of me being able to feel like I'm the gawd-damn BATMAN because it's such a huge pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to switch gadgets, that I just don't even bother with them. In Origins, it's super easy and fun for me to set up a Rube Goldberg machine of sheer pants-wetting, bat-related, "i-hope-he-doesn't-do-bad-things-to-my-butt" terror, and in Knight, it's really just "sod it, I guess I'll just sneak up behind this guy and give him a naptime hug. Oh, there's his buddy, I'll give him a hug, too."
I'll wind up finishing this game, because hey, I already spent the money, but for my money, I'd much rather recommend Arkham City and Arkham Origins over this one.

This game man...this game.
There is no argument with saying this is one of the best game series ever made.  It has everything you need to make a good game: compelling characters, a deep and rich story, great combat mechanics, killer music, good graphics (for it's time, and even by today's standards they aren't bad.), and action.  Lots and lots of action.
If you're clueless about what this game is about, you dive into the shoes of Gordon Freeman, a theoretical physicist that escaped twenty years in the past from the Black Mesa laboratories.  In Half-Life, Gordon accidently releases a portal to Xen, an alien world, which causes massive chaos.  This includes zombies, aliens, zombies, aliens, and more zombies.  After the events of Half-Life (go play the game), you are placed into stasis by the mysterious, "G-Man," who wakes you up from it right before the events of Half-Life 2.  You awaken as Freeman to a world controlled by a military group called the Combine, who have placed humanity into strict order, which is led by your old Black Mesa supervisor Dr. Breen.  You quickly learn that there is a resistance led some of your former fellow scientists, who plan to overthrow the Combine in order to make the world as it was once again.  So you get at it, becoming the face of the resistance, in order to take earth back once again.
I truly can not give enough praise to Valve for making this incredible game.  I tip my hats to you, developers.
So, if you haven't played this game, now is the time.  Put on your hazard suit.  Pick up your crowbar.
Become the Freeman.

I was a KF 1 veteran and put in over 300 hours into the game. I loved how you can post up in one position and steadily take on higher levels of specimens.
Since this game is still in early access mode, I recommend for the developers one thing for KF 2 - "make it more like KF 1". The specimens were much more fear invoking in KF 1 compared to KF 2.
One thing I liked about KF1 was that ammo was always an issue no matter what level you were playing. You feel like the specimens are coming toward to you like molasses while you empty your clips. This isnt the case in KF 2. It is easy to run away from the specimens compared to KF 1. You can more easily survive without your team in KF 2. Team work isn't as crucial in KF 2.
Also the scrakes used to invoke fear to every KF 1 player unless you were a sharper shooter, medic or beserker. This isn't the case for KF 2 - the scrakes are much easier for every class to take on which takes away the challenge and dependency on team work.
Last the map positioning makes it almost impossible to not restock on weapons. In KF 1 the maps could be very large sometimes and unless you planned accordingly, you can miss out on restocking weapons which adds more challenge to the game. KF 2 maps are smaller or the running option makes it easier regarding the logistics of restocking weapons.
All in all, I still play KF 2 for the updated version but I am very much upset KF 2 isn't as good as KF 1.

The DLC gets worse and worse, there's about £40 worth of DLC and none of it is worth playing although I haven't yet played Season of Infamy since I gave up with it. It's quite funny because the game has decent length to it given it took me about 40 hours to 100% it and yet all the DLC combined other than Season of Infamy is about 8 hours of gameplay. Great value for money.

The first game is great and I used to no life it on the weekends on my old PC that was absolute♥♥♥♥♥♥♥and could only run KF1 @ 25-30fps. With my new computer I don't even understand how I found 30fps playable.
I'm a couple hours into the August Beta and I can say that the Beta has sparked my interest in KF2 again. The game feels fresh with the new features and with that comes a new fresh Pro/Con list.
Pros:
- Enemy Variety: Previous builds lacked Enemy variety and felt more like a KF1 reskin + a run button after a while playing (minus the quick kill combo nuance). August introduced (what i'm going to call) enhanced Zeds. These guys seem to take from the playable Versus Zeds and has interesting effects such as the suicide crawlers, Alpha Clots that can roar and buff enemy speeds and Stalkers that flip a whole lot more. One of my complaints of the last build was the lack of enemy variety and TWI seems to be going in the right direction. It's reasonable to expect a couple new enemy variations and maybe one new enemy by the time the game is finished. A new boss would be cool but I doubt it will happen because it seems like a big distraction and could possibly lead to another delay.
- Animations: Game is a wee bit more nuanced now and for the better. Zeds will sidestep more often, gorefasts and bloats will cover their faced with their blades when dinked in the head. I love these changes.
- Graphics: [insert generic "it look purdy" comment here]
- Teleportation Decrease: One of the problems I had in the last build was doing multiple 360 spins in one place in a open area, spotting one enemy and getting butt slapped by a horde while I killed the 1 zed I spotted. This seems to be fixed/reduced now.
Cons:
- Internet Connectivity: This is probably a rare problem (guessing b/c I haven't checked the forums) but what made me quit the game was getting a random "you lost connection to the host" message during the buying period despite having good ping. It seems rare since the people I've talked to in game havent said much about it. Idk if this is a valid Con.
Physics: This will probably be fixed soon but the Beta's addition of animations have lead to at least 4 glitchy bodies per game. It is probably worse online (as I got those numbers from solo) but its nothing game breaking. More funny than anything.
- Stun: TWI biggest game mechanic mistake. It makes everything way too easy. i.e. using LAR + Stun skill to dizzy scrakes and spam R1 in their face, GS nades that turn big zeds into a punching bag, SWAT flashbangs basically being GS nades minus the damage to the zed and yourself at close range. Stun is stupid and shouldn't be in the game.
Nuetral:
- Perk Utility: Some perks don't seem that good and vice versa. I haven't touched berzerker since the nerf and SWAT seems like a psuedo replacement for commando when it comes to killing trash. I feel that SWAT usage is going to be at an all time high post-official-release as SWAT just melts everything and has no recoil. Everything seems viable (except firebug) for solo suicidal at the least atm and only time will tell what perks are suicide inducing in a 6man. Side note, Sharpshooter is stupid good, remove stun please.
I pretty much ditched KF2 for CSGO due to the combination of low player count but this Beta sure has my attention. Overall I recommend this game if you're looking for something to play for fun and arcadey, maybe a game to play casually with buds while you're drunk. If you're looking for nuance in your game go play KF1 or save your money for L4D3.

Having spent some time recently playing Killing Floor 2, after a LONG break it seems as if it took a step in the right direction. The game is again fun to play, with the difficulty curve increased. To my own amusement I must say that I can recomend this game now. It's fun, it's challenging and great to play with friends, a lot of the issues the game had when I was previously playing have been fixed. Well done TW
OLD REVIEW:
Having spent over 500 hours in KF1 i was really looking forward to Killing Floor 2. I'm sad to say that this is not what I was expecting.
The absolute lack of content and dumb mechanics (trying to run away from a raged fleshpound? Let me just teleport it right behind the next corner) are one thing. Lowering the skill ceilling by a great margin is what I was upset about the most. You need to dispatch of that scrake/fleshpound quickly? Better pray the the whole team just unloads their AA12 at it! The speedkills in KF1 made the game for me. They took skill and practise to master, and were really rewarding. Uppercutting scrakes or making fleshpounds turn to red mist with a couple of nades, stunlocking scrakes and managing the fleshpound's rage mechanic. It didn't make the game too easy in my opinion as like I said, to succesfully pull them off you would need some skill and practise. Messing up one speedkill could mean a wipe of the whole team when the raged scrake/fleshpound just tears through you and your teammates. But this is absent in Killing Floor 2, the enemies are just bigger and bigger teleporting bullet sponges, which makes the game A LOT LESS FUN.
The game is in fact in Early Access, yet people paid money for it, expecting "early access done right", if this is early access at its finest then I am really dissappointed with Tripwire. I though early access would mean that we get to play our long awaited game a little bit sooner, with a little less in it but with new contend pouring in. Hey, its not like TW had to re-invent Killing Floor, the formula was already there, in Killing Floor 1! But instead we got yet another cash grab. Killing Floor 2 ladies and gentlemen, new maps? New perks? New zeds? Maybe, somtime, just wait a couple of months, mkay? But look at this fancy hat! It's GOLD! And you only need to spend more £££ to get it in a UNFINISHED game! Quick! Buy buy buy our keys!
I understand that making games requires funds, but why start a project when you don't know if you can support it all the way through? Did Tripwire start working on KF2 and thought "Well, we don't have the money to complete the game, but lets hope people pay for early access, we can get more funds that way and maybe actually finish this game"? TW already got out money from the early access, and now they say that the microtransactions will help them with future "free DLC" as they call it. That would be alright, IF the game was out of early access. I find it insulting that the money the people paid for this game is used to implement MICROTRANSACTIONS instead of actually delivering a full release. Finish the darn game first, then implement ways to have the £££ flowing in.
Don't get me wrong, I enjoyed playing the game, granted, it's not as good as the first one, still it attracted me for a long time. But the direction it's heading in is just not right in my opinion and I will not be supporting this title anymore. I am afraid that KF2 will meet a smiliar fate as TF2, CS:GO or PD2, a microtransaction sh*tfest, where the game doesnt really matter anymore. Because, who cares about actuall gameplay as long as you can get a cool, ingame hat, right?
To add insult to injury, Tripwire is censoring the forums. Discussions where people do not agree with the dev's actions have been locked, and the people posting have been banned. PLEASE STAY AWAY FROM THIS SINKING SHIP!
To conclude, I would advise not to purchase this game, as it seems it is on a downward spiral, leading it into oblivion. Cheers

The world of Arkham Knight is dark, large and organic. Roaming mobs and riots make the game world come to life, something that the other games lacked. While the world is fairly large, it is also highly detailed, with lots of Easter eggs for those with a keen eye.
This is the first game in the Arkham series to put the player behind the wheel of the Batmobile, and it sure is a tank. The controls are clearly designed with a controller in mind, but it shouldn't take too long to get used to using a keyboard and mouse with the game.
The biggest selling point of this game should be the story. Many story elements are pulled directly from the comics or from Batman: The Animated Series. While this may make it predictable, there are a lot of twists and turns that should keep even the most knowledgeable BatFan entertained.
I was skeptical about them bringing the Joker back for this game, but after playing it I can now say that he was really tastefully done and he really adds to the development.
The game is not perfect though. There has been performance issues on some computers, even after several patches. There is the over use of the Batmobile which wears down the impact of the vehicle and makes it seem like a gadget late game. There is also the dumbing down of the Riddler challenges, in the earlier games it was fun to solve some riddles and piece together a puzzle, here you just have to blow up a wall and pick the trophies up for the most part.
The Good
The Bad
The Ugly
Even with all of the issues, I would still recommend this game.

So buy it I did! I was confident in my purchase. Tripwire was responsible for the massive success of KF1, and one of my favourite FPS games of all time, Red Orchestra 2. This also didn't seem like it would be in Early Access for long at all! At the time of release, the devs stated in a gameplay session with TotalBiscut that the game should definetely be out of Early Access by September 2015, and they were confident with that fact. I wasn't too alarmed, as I expected just one massive launch update. Well, I actually stopped playing the game, and forgot about it, waiting for it to be released. Then I heard of all the microtransaction controversy, and warning sirens went off in my head. I checked back on the store page for this game, and sure enough, game is still Early Access in December 2015! This type of developer behaviour should not be tolerated, and thus I urge you not to buy this game. Not to mention that there is hardly a difference in content since the release of the game into Early Access and now. Same boss. Same 5-7 enemies. Same guns. Same four maps (how many have they added? four? two?)

Having spent some time recently playing Killing Floor 2, after a LONG break it seems as if it took a step in the right direction. The game is again fun to play, with the difficulty curve increased. To my own amusement I must say that I can recomend this game now. It's fun, it's challenging and great to play with friends, a lot of the issues the game had when I was previously playing have been fixed. Well done TW
OLD REVIEW:
Having spent over 500 hours in KF1 i was really looking forward to Killing Floor 2. I'm sad to say that this is not what I was expecting.
The absolute lack of content and dumb mechanics (trying to run away from a raged fleshpound? Let me just teleport it right behind the next corner) are one thing. Lowering the skill ceilling by a great margin is what I was upset about the most. You need to dispatch of that scrake/fleshpound quickly? Better pray the the whole team just unloads their AA12 at it! The speedkills in KF1 made the game for me. They took skill and practise to master, and were really rewarding. Uppercutting scrakes or making fleshpounds turn to red mist with a couple of nades, stunlocking scrakes and managing the fleshpound's rage mechanic. It didn't make the game too easy in my opinion as like I said, to succesfully pull them off you would need some skill and practise. Messing up one speedkill could mean a wipe of the whole team when the raged scrake/fleshpound just tears through you and your teammates. But this is absent in Killing Floor 2, the enemies are just bigger and bigger teleporting bullet sponges, which makes the game A LOT LESS FUN.
The game is in fact in Early Access, yet people paid money for it, expecting "early access done right", if this is early access at its finest then I am really dissappointed with Tripwire. I though early access would mean that we get to play our long awaited game a little bit sooner, with a little less in it but with new contend pouring in. Hey, its not like TW had to re-invent Killing Floor, the formula was already there, in Killing Floor 1! But instead we got yet another cash grab. Killing Floor 2 ladies and gentlemen, new maps? New perks? New zeds? Maybe, somtime, just wait a couple of months, mkay? But look at this fancy hat! It's GOLD! And you only need to spend more £££ to get it in a UNFINISHED game! Quick! Buy buy buy our keys!
I understand that making games requires funds, but why start a project when you don't know if you can support it all the way through? Did Tripwire start working on KF2 and thought "Well, we don't have the money to complete the game, but lets hope people pay for early access, we can get more funds that way and maybe actually finish this game"? Okay, so after having spent 8 hours on this game and completed about 23% of this game, I've decided to write my first review.
Pros:
-The look of the environment: Absolutely gorgeous. The whole Gotham City looks amazing. Even after I raised 2-3 levels above the settings recommended by Nvidia GeForce, I could still play the game smoothly. I'm using a GTX970 4GB.
-New predator fear takedown option is a huge plus.
-The Batmobile is super powerful, and it looks just way too badaxx. The additional skin options are cool, too.
-The new map UI is looks really high-tech.
-The story is appealing. It really makes you want to progress through further and further.
-The puzzles are veritably challenging. You really have to some efforts into it. I like it.
Cons: -Sigh...
-The focus on Batmobile is a bit too much. The game is supposed to be about Batman himself, not his vehicle. Warning: If you are not very good at racing game, you might need some more practice. You're expected do a lot of chasing in this game.
-The skill tree. I hate the UI and the way it works. Gonna take some time for old players like me to get use to.
-The combat system. Sigh, the addition of the Batmobile control forced the developers to remap the takedown actions. I have to manually remap every single key in this game so that I get it "straight" again.
-Predator encounters are much more harder. You don't have a lot of options. Arkham origins gave the best predator experience in the series.
-Riddler's challenges are very very very hard. For player who is not good at racing game, I struggled a lot to finish them. Too many failures are a bit too discouraging.
-Although many patches have been applied since its second release, I experienced a severe crash within 5 hours of gameplay. I ended up rebooting my PC!
Conclusions:
-This is NOT the typical Batman Arkham experience that most players would find it to be enjoyable. To fully appreciate this game, you really have to be patient and get use to its new system. It is definitely rewarding if you can stick to the end.
-The overall gameplay is smooth. Not stuttering or significant frame rate drops have occurred during my first 8 hours of gameplay. Yet there are minor crashes that need to be resolved.
-This game is for serious Batman Arkham series fans who are okay with integrating racing game features into the general gameplay experience. For players who would like to stick to the City and Origins experience, then this is not going to be a good buy for you under a high price.
So .... I'm kinda ambivalent about whether I should recommend this game. Personally speaking, if you can be patient enough to adapt to its system, buy it. The rich content of this game definitely won't disappoint you. If you are impatient or just hating racing game features, then probably you should stay away from it.

Risk of Rekt's goal is very simple- Get to the final stage, defeat the final boss. Each character class has 4 skills that are specific to the type of character, and there are 8 classes in all so far, so it won't be too difficult to find one to be attuned to. Along with the class skills, there are also items that help some characters more than others. By going through the levels and collecting items, the player becomes stronger. With the game still updating every now and then, there are even more enemies, classes, and items to be introduced. There's never a dull moment while playing Risk of Rekt, even when you die, you jump right back in and start wreaking havoc. It's a game that's easily addicting and even more fun when you play with friends, and I'd reccomend this to anyone(whether you have friends or not) because it's definitely worth a go. I have played this game for an extensive amount of hours. To make things clear now, just because I played it for a long time, doesn't mean I enjoyed the experience of it very much.
First off as to why it's a poor quality game, is the obvious port problems. They have released many patches and updates trying to fix this but with each one they just bring in more problems that make the game even worse. I will say they have made the frame rate stable (for me at least) and they have fixed almost all the game crashing bugs (can't say the same about Arkham Origins).
The story in this game, honestly wasn't very enjoyable. There were some plot twists that did throw the story around in a few directions but none of them ever lasted. The reveals and deaths weren't too effective, and many parts of the story that should have been important (including the Arkham Knight reveal) was basically shoved in your face the whole story leading up to it.
Gameplay: Well it's terrible in most parts.
Pros-The gliding and the overall look of the city is really nice and well done.
The graple controls are nice including the upgrade.
The upgrade system was clear and easy to understand
Cons-The feel of everything else was just awful. (This is going to be long)
You could haer on the police radio that there is a riot taking place in an area nearby, so you can see with detecive vision that there is about 50 or so thugs just smashing stores and trashing the area, so you want to be a cool Batman and jump down and bash all those criminals up. BUT YOU CAN'T! They all run away except for about 5. It is so sad just watching as everyone runs away and you aggrivate them at all to get their attention so they can turn around and join the fight. Even Arkham Origins did this better with the Crime in Progress system where you can have everyone in the big fights try and kill which was about 20-30 or so thugs. So why not in this game? I want to test my skills against a big group of thugs.
Another thing is the Batmobile, I was so excited to hear that you can drive the Batmobile, however when they first showed the design, it was extremely dissapointing, especially the look. The back of it is horrible, it looks like a bug from some angles which is awful. The feel of it is terrible too. Don't think I'm a bad driver because I am quite high in almost every single race event in this game, however it is just awful to drive. The race mechanics are just outright messed up. "Drifting slows down the timer to make one second in the timer last 3 in the real world". That is just awful because it means that people don't get rewarded for being really fast and driving at high speeds. You will get a better reward (and faster time) for driving really slowly and drifting than you would by doing tight turns and driving at high speeds (and the difference can be up to 1 minute depending on your style). Another thing about driving is the physics. There are many physics problems in this. You can touch a wall which you will normally smash right through any normal time, but far to often, you will be sent flying doing flips in the sky. Ridiculous. And I haven't even gotten to the part where they over use the Batmobile so much. *spoilers* they destroy the Batmobile at one stage against a stupid drill machine which is almost faster than the Batmobile itself, and then less than 5 minutes later they give you another one. They can't keep it away from you. *end spoilers* They use it for everything. And every puzzle and trap possible just so happens to be only activated by the Batmobile! I will say that the combat challenges in the Batmobile are alright. Not good but alright. They are mostly easy and get very simple very quick. I don't put much more than 3 minutes of effort into it because that's as much variety as there is and it's not worth getting high on the leaderboard.
Now moving onto combat. Oh boy, oh boy. This is the biggest problem in this game by a long shot. I can spend hours and hours talking about everything wrong with it, but I wont because I've been making youtube videos to do that for me. The combat is awful and broken and just down right disapointing. I will start with the normal problems that need to be modified (this is excluding glitches).
1. Charging thugs: This was a stupid idea. A thug that runs at incredibly slow speed can only be stopped by a batarang to the face. (Or evade which doesn't stop them but avoids them). For some reason a flying kick from Batman to the face is beaten by a man doing a bit more than a jog. It's incredibly odd and stupid, and their hit box is far to big. They have a hit box of about 2 thugs wide.
2. Camera in combat: It is the worst of the series. It will pan around for stupid reasons even when you don't want it to, and the problem with that is that the combat priotisation is based on your camera direction. Also a move you can unlock and perform is the Special Batclaw slam which grapples the target and you fly at him and flip over you and slam him into the ground. (A bit different when doing this to a Brute but the same problem is there) The camera does this stupid movie action look where it zooms in on their torso's and you can't see a damn thing. Sometimes there is a glitch where that camera shot doesn't work and it stays at the distant 3rd person look (and you know you messed up when a glitch makes what you have look sh*t). They need to get rid of the zoom on that move. It cause everyone to step back but it spins the camera as well messing things up for about .75 of a second (and that's important). Also the camera doesn't do well when near a wall (it might be a glitch so I'll explain it in that part).
3. Target Priorisation: This is one of the worst. They have many challenge maps in this game such as the combo master which means you need to keep one combo for as long as possible. I am not bad at Arkham Combat, I've gotten hundreds of thousands of points (millions for some) in challenge maps and I've gotten a nice score in combo master of over 250. Which was good for the first 3 days when it came out and the frame rates absolutely murdered itself when the timer starts on the screen and the frames drop to 1 per second. But now it's terrible. Keeping combos for more than 200 is almost impossible. Special moves such as disarm and destroy don't know what they are doing. They need a proper order of importance beacuse for some reason, the game seems to think that poles and baseball bats are more of a threat than stun sticks or shields. (Even though baseball bats and poles are weapons Batman can use) Basic Free flow combat has got it wrong also. I can look straight at a thug without anything in his hand, I aim at him, I go for him, but the game decides that the man 3 thugs behind him with a stun stick is the right target to pick which kills the combo and fails the challenge. It's just terrible. In one of the videos I'm making, I will be including a full length statement including how priotisation and the combat should be working to make things good again.
There is more but I will move onto the glitches.
Camera against walls: Combo challenge is a perfect example. There isn't a proper boundary in that challenge, it just some purple walls that fizzle which used to murder frame rates right? Well for some reason the camera glitches like crazy when you try and look behind you when punching someone against those walls. Those walls need to let the camera go through them at least cause it messes so much up.
Counters: They are broken as hell. I get so many instances where a thug wants to attack so me so I counter, but they just freeze and don't attack and Batman doesn't move so it drops the combo. You can't do anything but watch for one second as nothing happens and watch your chance of getting a high score vanish. These need to fixed because they cause extreme game impacting problems.
I have run out of room for this review. Don't buy.

XCOM will probably be the only game I review without having actually beaten it. Why? It's just too damn hard. But, believe it or not, that's a good thing.
XCOM puts the player in the role of a commander controlling a squad of 1-6 (typically 4) troops. In turn based fashion, each soldier can be directed to move, take cover, shoot, or utilize any ability unique to his class (Assault, Sniper, Heavy, or Support). Objectives vary between eliminating hostiles, rescuing civilians, or escorting VIPs.
At its heart, XCOM is a game of balance. With little to no guidance, players alone must decide on how to distribute resources, which countries to save, and when to tackle story objectives.
For the most engaging experience, players are recommended to play in "Ironman Mode". Here, everything is permanent, from the choices made to the deaths of soldiers. Consequences have never felt more real.
XCOM offers an unparalleled experience rich with freedom and filled to the brim with tension.
Grade: B+

Okay, so after having spent 8 hours on this game and completed about 23% of this game, I've decided to write my first review.
Pros:
-The look of the environment: Absolutely gorgeous. The whole Gotham City looks amazing. Even after I raised 2-3 levels above the settings recommended by Nvidia GeForce, I could still play the game smoothly. I'm using a GTX970 4GB.
-New predator fear takedown option is a huge plus.
-The Batmobile is super powerful, and it looks just way too badaxx. The additional skin options are cool, too.
-The new map UI is looks really high-tech.
-The story is appealing. It really makes you want to progress through further and further.
-The puzzles are veritably challenging. You really have to some efforts into it. I like it.
Cons: -Sigh...
-The focus on Batmobile is a bit too much. The game is supposed to be about Batman himself, not his vehicle. Warning: If you are not very good at racing game, you might need some more practice. You're expected do a lot of chasing in this game.
-The skill tree. I hate the UI and the way it works. Gonna take some time for old players like me to get use to.
-The combat system. Sigh, the addition of the Batmobile control forced the developers to remap the takedown actions. I have to manually remap every single key in this game so that I get it "straight" again.
-Predator encounters are much more harder. You don't have a lot of options. Arkham origins gave the best predator experience in the series.
-Riddler's challenges are very very very hard. For player who is not good at racing game, I struggled a lot to finish them. Too many failures are a bit too discouraging.
-Although many patches have been applied since its second release, I experienced a severe crash within 5 hours of gameplay. I ended up rebooting my PC!
Conclusions:
-This is NOT the typical Batman Arkham experience that most players would find it to be enjoyable. To fully appreciate this game, you really have to be patient and get use to its new system. It is definitely rewarding if you can stick to the end.
-The overall gameplay is smooth. Not stuttering or significant frame rate drops have occurred during my first 8 hours of gameplay. Yet there are minor crashes that need to be resolved.
-This game is for serious Batman Arkham series fans who are okay with integrating racing game features into the general gameplay experience. For players who would like to stick to the City and Origins experience, then this is not going to be a good buy for you under a high price.
So .... I'm kinda ambivalent about whether I should recommend this game. Personally speaking, if you can be patient enough to adapt to its system, buy it. The rich content of this game definitely won't disappoint you. If you are impatient or just hating racing game features, then probably you should stay away from it.

I have played this game for an extensive amount of hours. To make things clear now, just because I played it for a long time, doesn't mean I enjoyed the experience of it very much.
First off as to why it's a poor quality game, is the obvious port problems. They have released many patches and updates trying to fix this but with each one they just bring in more problems that make the game even worse. I will say they have made the frame rate stable (for me at least) and they have fixed almost all the game crashing bugs (can't say the same about Arkham Origins).
The story in this game, honestly wasn't very enjoyable. There were some plot twists that did throw the story around in a few directions but none of them ever lasted. The reveals and deaths weren't too effective, and many parts of the story that should have been important (including the Arkham Knight reveal) was basically shoved in your face the whole story leading up to it.
Gameplay: Well it's terrible in most parts.
Pros-The gliding and the overall look of the city is really nice and well done.
The graple controls are nice including the upgrade.
The upgrade system was clear and easy to understand
Cons-The feel of everything else was just awful. (This is going to be long)
You could haer on the police radio that there is a riot taking place in an area nearby, so you can see with detecive vision that there is about 50 or so thugs just smashing stores and trashing the area, so you want to be a cool Batman and jump down and bash all those criminals up. BUT YOU CAN'T! They all run away except for about 5. It is so sad just watching as everyone runs away and you aggrivate them at all to get their attention so they can turn around and join the fight. Even Arkham Origins did this better with the Crime in Progress system where you can have everyone in the big fights try and kill which was about 20-30 or so thugs. So why not in this game? I want to test my skills against a big group of thugs.
Another thing is the Batmobile, I was so excited to hear that you can drive the Batmobile, however when they first showed the design, it was extremely dissapointing, especially the look. The back of it is horrible, it looks like a bug from some angles which is awful. The feel of it is terrible too. Don't think I'm a bad driver because I am quite high in almost every single race event in this game, however it is just awful to drive. The race mechanics are just outright messed up. "Drifting slows down the timer to make one second in the timer last 3 in the real world". That is just awful because it means that people don't get rewarded for being really fast and driving at high speeds. You will get a better reward (and faster time) for driving really slowly and drifting than you would by doing tight turns and driving at high speeds (and the difference can be up to 1 minute depending on your style). Another thing about driving is the physics. There are many physics problems in this. You can touch a wall which you will normally smash right through any normal time, but far to often, you will be sent flying doing flips in the sky. Ridiculous. And I haven't even gotten to the part where they over use the Batmobile so much. *spoilers* they destroy the Batmobile at one stage against a stupid drill machine which is almost faster than the Batmobile itself, and then less than 5 minutes later they give you another one. They can't keep it away from you. *end spoilers* They use it for everything. And every puzzle and trap possible just so happens to be only activated by the Batmobile! I will say that the combat challenges in the Batmobile are alright. Not good but alright. They are mostly easy and get very simple very quick. I don't put much more than 3 minutes of effort into it because that's as much variety as there is and it's not worth getting high on the leaderboard.
Now moving onto combat. Oh boy, oh boy. This is the biggest problem in this game by a long shot. I can spend hours and hours talking about everything wrong with it, but I wont because I've been making youtube videos to do that for me. The combat is awful and broken and just down right disapointing. I will start with the normal problems that need to be modified (this is excluding glitches).
1. Charging thugs: This was a stupid idea. A thug that runs at incredibly slow speed can only be stopped by a batarang to the face. (Or evade which doesn't stop them but avoids them). For some reason a flying kick from Batman to the face is beaten by a man doing a bit more than a jog. It's incredibly odd and stupid, and their hit box is far to big. They have a hit box of about 2 thugs wide.
2. Camera in combat: It is the worst of the series. It will pan around for stupid reasons even when you don't want it to, and the problem with that is that the combat priotisation is based on your camera direction. Also a move you can unlock and perform is the Special Batclaw slam which grapples the target and you fly at him and flip over you and slam him into the ground. (A bit different when doing this to a Brute but the same problem is there) The camera does this stupid movie action look where it zooms in on their torso's and you can't see a damn thing. Sometimes there is a glitch where that camera shot doesn't work and it stays at the distant 3rd person look (and you know you messed up when a glitch makes what you have look sh*t). They need to get rid of the zoom on that move. It cause everyone to step back but it spins the camera as well messing things up for about .75 of a second (and that's important). Also the camera doesn't do well when near a wall (it might be a glitch so I'll explain it in that part).
3. Target Priorisation: This is one of the worst. They have many challenge maps in this game such as the combo master which means you need to keep one combo for as long as possible. I am not bad at Arkham Combat, I've gotten hundreds of thousands of points (millions for some) in challenge maps and I've gotten a nice score in combo master of over 250. Which was good for the first 3 days when it came out and the frame rates absolutely murdered itself when the timer starts on the screen and the frames drop to 1 per second. But now it's terrible. Keeping combos for more than 200 is almost impossible. Special moves such as disarm and destroy don't know what they are doing. They need a proper order of importance beacuse for some reason, the game seems to think that poles and baseball bats are more of a threat than stun sticks or shields. (Even though baseball bats and poles are weapons Batman can use) Basic Free flow combat has got it wrong also. I can look straight at a thug without anything in his hand, I aim at him, I go for him, but the game decides that the man 3 thugs behind him with a stun stick is the right target to pick which kills the combo and fails the challenge. It's just terrible. In one of the videos I'm making, I will be including a full length statement including how priotisation and the combat should be working to make things good again.
There is more but I will move onto the glitches.
Camera against walls: Combo challenge is a perfect example. There isn't a proper boundary in that challenge, it just some purple walls that fizzle which used to murder frame rates right? Well for some reason the camera glitches like crazy when you try and look behind you when punching someone against those walls. Those walls need to let the camera go through them at least cause it messes so much up.
Counters: They are broken as hell. I get so many instances where a thug wants to attack so me so I counter, but they just freeze and don't attack and Batman doesn't move so it drops the combo. You can't do anything but watch for one second as nothing happens and watch your chance of getting a high score vanish. These need to fixed because they cause extreme game impacting problems.
I have run out of room for this review. Don't buy.

I'm not one for Turn Based Strategy. I usually hate games that go beyond the Total War-level of complexity. Somehow, though, XCOM grew on me ever since I first played it. It's the fact that you CAN play meticulously and plan each and every step, carefully pick the equipment for your squadmembers and go through the mission's briefing three times over - But you do not have to. XCOM comes with quite a few difficulties, with easy being a (very) casual ride and Classic a challenging experience for fans of the old XCOM. No matter the difficulty, luck is always a factor in this and you'll find yourself thinking about whether or not to save-scum your way out of your inevitable doom. The game has a variety of missions that will always play out differently in each playthrough, with an overarching campaign that has you managing your base and soldiers between encounters. Soldiers can be customised and level up as they are used, after a while you will start feeling attached to them. Thumbs up.

Pretty good game, considering I haven’t played the original or any other Xcom games, and usually never play turn-based games I enjoyed this quite a bit. In the end the game got quite stale and boring the way that I played it (saving and reloading) and I think that the best way to play the game might be with  Ironman (no saving/loading) and classic mode (smarter/harder AI).
I personally won’t do that anytime soon, the game is too long for my own taste, steam reports it took 26 hours for me to get through, but I think I left it running a couple of hours while I went and did other things, so probably around 18-20 hours.
It has a few bugs that are irritating as hell, the most obvious one is with the camera and several floor levels, but some where you are flanking and hugging an enemy and he still receive full cover bonus. Luckily they are not game-breaking and will hopefully get patched away, mostly irritating.
My biggest gripe is that the game feels like its wasting your time constantly. Setting up/removing equipment between the characters in the team loadout takes forever and have you jumping through menu after menu and no easy way of getting an overview of what you have and which character have which. Making the set up time take 5 minutes of you jumping through menus and trying to remember the names of the dudes in the current squad when removing equipment from units not in use. When it all could take 30 seconds if they just had the sense of putting everything in a common pool between missions and then remembering the loadout of characters between missions.
So while the interface works well for the individual character, it’s annoying and hard to get an overview when outfitting for 2 or more squad setups with different people in the sick-bay.
There’s also no way of making the fights go faster, disabling the action cam doesn’t shorten the animations, I just want the results of the shot, so stop wasting my time. The sniper is the worst offender, first you see the camera zoom out to have both the character and the target in the view, then you sit and wait, and wait, and wait, and wait, then the sniper takes the shot. It probably looks cool in the action cam, but I can only see two ants on the ground doing ♥♥♥♥ all.
Graphically its good, might not win any prizes but it’s certainly not ugly or hard on the eyes.
The game is kind of confusing in the beginning, I can recommend playing a month or two (game time) and then restarting once you’ve done all of the big mistakes and learned how to manage your economy.
I enjoyed the game a lot, time flew and suddenly a couple hours have passed by when I thought it was just a short while. There are some things that are really annoying and time-wasting but I had fun and it was challenging.
As for who this is for, I think most people can enjoy it, but you got to have a masochistic side to take the turns where everything really just goes to hell. If you enjoy a game that can be unforgiving for the careless and rewarding for the patient then it might be for you.

I have already played Half Life 2 numerous times on various platforms and am quite shocked that a sequel has not turned up after a decade. Is HL3 in production? I don't know. A definite 10 out of 10 experience, and an absolute bargain at its current price.

The only real reason this game has such a mixed set of user reviews on PC is due to the bugs and especially the awful performance this game still has on many systems.
I think the biggest mistake the developers made was that they released an untested, incomplete port. Granted, some of these bugs also exist on the consoles (some of the progress and combat/movement bugs) but the main issue is really the bad performance. Firstly, there is no true 'low setting' meaning you need quite the expensive rig just to run the game on lowest. Double that expensive rig for the kind of crazy rig you need to max out the settings of this game.
As a result, I think most people will actually buy and play this game in the future, similar to the case of Crysis when it came out, very few people could run it with the affordable tech out at the time of release. Batman Arkham Knight is no different.
Once you can run it though you are in for one hell of a treat. Firstly, visually the game is pure eye candy and you immediately see the reason for the high hardware demands that the game has. It just hits you with pure visual fidelity achieved by maximising the amount of polygons that modern programming techniques allow. Thus too why the game is so demanding, as they achieved high visual fidelity by approaching the design focused on polygon count.
What is odd though is that if you look at how it looks on consoles, there is a massive 3D render downgrade on the consoles, which you do not have as an option on PC, if the PC version had the same option then much lower performing PC's could run it fine too.
Besides the visuals, the content in the game is really great. There is a lot of content to do and you never feel forced to do it all. If you find certain side quests boring, you do not have any real reason to do them. The main quests are always fun anyway so each player can play the game as they desire and pick and choose the side missions that they find fun while ignoring the side missions they find boring.
I wish more games were like this, content wise. Also it is great to have such quality story writing and dialogue/voice acting make a comeback to gaming.

I'm not one for Turn Based Strategy. I usually hate games that go beyond the Total War-level of complexity. Somehow, though, XCOM grew on me ever since I first played it. It's the fact that you CAN play meticulously and plan each and every step, carefully pick the equipment for your squadmembers and go through the mission's briefing three times over - But you do not have to. XCOM comes with quite a few difficulties, with easy being a (very) casual ride and Classic a challenging experience for fans of the old XCOM. No matter the difficulty, luck is always a factor in this and you'll find yourself thinking about whether or not to save-scum your way out of your inevitable doom. The game has a variety of missions that will always play out differently in each playthrough, with an overarching campaign that has you managing your base and soldiers between encounters. Soldiers can be customised and level up as they are used, after a while you will start feeling attached to them. Thumbs up.

Pretty good game, considering I haven’t played the original or any other Xcom games, and usually never play turn-based games I enjoyed this quite a bit. In the end the game got quite stale and boring the way that I played it (saving and reloading) and I think that the best way to play the game might be with  Ironman (no saving/loading) and classic mode (smarter/harder AI).
I personally won’t do that anytime soon, the game is too long for my own taste, steam reports it took 26 hours for me to get through, but I think I left it running a couple of hours while I went and did other things, so probably around 18-20 hours.
It has a few bugs that are irritating as hell, the most obvious one is with the camera and several floor levels, but some where you are flanking and hugging an enemy and he still receive full cover bonus. Luckily they are not game-breaking and will hopefully get patched away, mostly irritating.
My biggest gripe is that the game feels like its wasting your time constantly. Setting up/removing equipment between the characters in the team loadout takes forever and have you jumping through menu after menu and no easy way of getting an overview of what you have and which character have which. Making the set up time take 5 minutes of you jumping through menus and trying to remember the names of the dudes in the current squad when removing equipment from units not in use. When it all could take 30 seconds if they just had the sense of putting everything in a common pool between missions and then remembering the loadout of characters between missions.
So while the interface works well for the individual character, it’s annoying and hard to get an overview when outfitting for 2 or more squad setups with different people in the sick-bay.
There’s also no way of making the fights go faster, disabling the action cam doesn’t shorten the animations, I just want the results of the shot, so stop wasting my time. The sniper is the worst offender, first you see the camera zoom out to have both the character and the target in the view, then you sit and wait, and wait, and wait, and wait, then the sniper takes the shot. It probably looks cool in the action cam, but I can only see two ants on the ground doing ♥♥♥♥ all.
Graphically its good, might not win any prizes but it’s certainly not ugly or hard on the eyes.
The game is kind of confusing in the beginning, I can recommend playing a month or two (game time) and then restarting once you’ve done all of the big mistakes and learned how to manage your economy.
I enjoyed the game a lot, time flew and suddenly a couple hours have passed by when I thought it was just a short while. There are some things that are really annoying and time-wasting but I had fun and it was challenging.
As for who this is for, I think most people can enjoy it, but you got to have a masochistic side to take the turns where everything really just goes to hell. If you enjoy a game that can be unforgiving for the careless and rewarding for the patient then it might be for you.

This is possibly the first game based off a TV show that I actually love. If you are an avid fan of South Park you would be committing an atrocity if you did not buy this game. Even better is if you are a lover of RPGs due to how this game pokes fun at the genre and is an RPG itself. If you are not a fan of South Park I would be cautious about buying this as the game makes lots of funny references to the actual show (even the show's main characters have closets which are dedicated to their previous adventures).
The big reason it's a must recommend for fans of the show though, is how it feels like a true South Park experience. The whole game plays out like an entire season of the show, with you as the main character. Exploring the town of South Park is a blast. You can go to explore familiar locations from the show and find collectables that are actually WORTH collecting, mainly friends. You can also do some side missions, one includes finding jesus. This brings me to the cast of the game. You see a lot of familiar faces from South Park and even some really minor characters only seen in one or two episodes such as Damien or the satan worshiping forest animals. Every main character's house is explorable and almost all major locations in the show are present and accounted for.
Now how does the gameplay fare? Really well actually. South Park does a lot of things right with the RPG and combat portion of things. First off is that every move you perform requires you to a button prompt of some sort (such as mashing a and d) that can boost your damage or in some more extreme moves, prevent you from self-injury while attacking with said move. Each class and the buddies have their own unique style of moves, each of which are fun to watch being performed. Some of my favorites are Cartman's V-chip, Professor Chaos, and Pestilence for the Jew class (yes there is a Jew class, suprised me as well and made me fall out of my chair). The game also allows you to bypass some fights by using the environment to KO your enemies before engaging. As per RPGs you gain exp which allows you to level abilities, and for every friend list milestone you make you get a perk. You also can perform magic by farting. You get four spells, each of which can be used in battle and out. As mentioned before you get a selection of 6 companions to fight with you in combat, and can select from 4 classes to play as. All of them have their own unique skillset and all of them have unique dialogue when exploring certain areas. In the case of classes you can still play any play style you want. Mages can focus on melee damage, thieves can focus on armor, ect. ect. The only difference between them are what abilities you get, and what default gear you have. Then there are the summons, four of them, all of them ending a battle instantly (save for bosses, because as Jesus puts it: they are scary), all of them entertaining. You can also "mod" your equipment by adding patches to them which can give things like bleeding or armor piercing.
Really my only complaint is that the game is WAY EASY even on the hardest difficulty. Play this game on hardcore otherwise you will zomgwtfbbqpwn everything in your path (which you actually will still do in hardcore). Adding into this is the seemingly endless amount of potions that you most likely will never use (even revive potions, which should always be hard to acquire). Also there is no reason to play the other classes as they all play out pretty much the same, severly detracting from replay value (I still did multiple playthroughs as there were two major choices in the game I wanted to try out for the opposite side, plus the character dialogue). These gripes however are easily overshadowed by the decent-to-great RPG gameplay.
Overall this is possibly the GREATEST South Park game ever, and easily one of the best licensed titles. The gameplay is done pretty well but could have used some tweaks like difficulty.  If you are a fan of the show and don't have this game, please, just come out of the closet and buy it. If not then I cannot recommend this at it's current price tag. I would still buy it when it goes on sale though. Now if you'll excuse me I'm gonna go fart on every thing in this game.
tl;dr:
Great game, buy if you are a fan of the show, buy if you like RPGs a lot. Do not buy if easily offended. Only major issue is game is too easy.

If you want to check out a game that's been doing early access right, look at Grim Dawn. This game is not one of them.
KF2 has been in early access for over a year and the updates are released at a snoozing pace. I have not even touched the game for a long time because of annoying things like teleporting enemies, which apparently are still in the game. Releasing PvP and microtransactions instead of working on things that are core to the game and actually trying to make a finished product is something I can't even understand. The maps are way too few and the perks are incomplete, yet they put efforts into a PvP mode in a game that has always been about co-op? Releasing an early access with only four perks out of ten in the game was a bad decision in the first place, because players are unable to test the core of the game which are the different perks and the ability to mix them in a team and try different strategies together. There's not much to be gained for Tripwire since the game will be changed so drastically in the future anyway.
Grim Dawn did early access so well because they prioritized finishing the actual integral parts of the game and now after release they're working on additional content like survival mode, new dungeons and items, and even an expansion pack - all which take nothing away from the player experience, they just add to it. Tripwire should have done the same and released PvP after being done with the game, not when there's still a ton of other stuff to work on that are core to the game.

reviewing an early access game is always a weird thing to do but after i have played way more than 600 hours in the last 8 months i think it's time to talk about it.
most importantly: do i recommend it?
hell yeah!
if you like FPS games and are into the zed killing business then this game is your ticket to ride.
obviously there is no kind of story involved. it's all about fast paced action and gory carnage. but that is how i like my zombie games.
currently there are 7 perks (or classes) in the game, a decent selection of weapons and as soon as the official maps bore you there is a huge supply of community created maps to continue the slaughter.
killing zeds just never gets boring and you always have lots of fun at it. perfect for relaxing in the evening, killing one or two hours of time before going to bed or blowing off some steam after an annoying day.
if you are looking for a bloody good time then KF2 just never fails to deliver.
but what is the downside?
good question, i'm glad you asked!
at lot of people are really annoyed by the slow pace of the game's development. the recent reviews got more and more negative because of that.
and i certainly have to agree. it takes the developers soooo loooong to get anything done.
fixing bugs takes very often months and since i started playing this game 8 months ago they added one new perk, a few weapons and i think three official maps.
that's just really poor by any standard.
at the same time they added a CSGO-like crate / key system, lots of hats, masks and other wearable stuff and tons of weapon skins, a crafting system and a pvp mode with player controlled survivors fighting player controlled zeds.
but since i am totally not interested in that kind of stuff this whole thing is just one giant box of 'nothing' for me and it seems a lot of people feel the same about it.
when compared to my other favorite early access game at the moment 'subnautica' you clearly see the difference. they pump out a major update at least once per month. obviously i am no game developer but i am pretty sure that a large scale survival game is a lot bigger and way more complex than some game about shooting zeds in the face on a relatively small map. but they got their priorities right. they try to get the base game finished as soon as possible and tend to the specialized details later. after all you can't add the cherry to a cake before you finished the cake!
but sadly that is exactly what they have been doing with KF2 for as long as i have been playing it and imho there is no way this game leaves early access before the very end of 2017 or even way later.
like i said: if you like the shooter genre then this game is just great.
but even i can't deny that there are quite a lot of problems all over the place.
edit: as you can see a lot of people still don't know that 'helpful' / 'not helpful' is not the same as 'i agree' / 'i disagree'. but well, i guess that's just what you have to expect on the interwebz.

Half Life 2 Review (Spoiler Free)
(Story)
"Wake up and smell the ashes".  Set sometime after the events of Half Life, Half Life 2 follows the franchises central protagonist, Gordon Freeman, as he explores the aftermath of the Black Mesa incident.  The resonance cascade caught the eyes of a sujugative alien race known as the Combine who invaded and conquered earth while Gordon was away.  Half Life 2 begins with Gordon arriving in City 17, a fictitious location that also happens to house the Combine's nerve center.  After meeting some old friends, Gordon joins the resistance element in the city.  Slowly but surely, Gordon and his friends wring the city from the Combine's hands in epic fashion.
(Gameplay)
Half Life 2 is a first person shooter with platforming, vehicular, and puzzle solving elements strewn about.  This type of game strucutre would be imitated for years to come but what makes Half Life 2 standout is its excellent pacing.  Just as you begin to get bored of a certain aspect, the game throws you a curve ball in the form of new mechanic, environment, weapon, etc. that keeps you interested.  Physics also play an important role in the game, with some puzzle solutions depending on your knowledge of weight or momentum.  Gordon's arsenal is fairly standard shooter fare with a few unorthodox weapons like the gravity gun (which can levitate and throw any non-fixed object).  One chapter of the game is somewhat slow but all provide a reasonable challenge within the limits of the game.  Vehicle segments are fun and puzzles not too challenging.
(Design)
The environments in Half Life 2 range from dreary towns and beaches to wetlands, caves, abandoned towns, interiors, and city streets.  The art style feels post-modern but with no discernable culture dominating.  The game has an industrial look.  Lighting and sound are both well done.  Characters feel believable too thanks great facial animation and excellent voice acting.
(Final Comments)
Though dated, Half Life 2 stands out as one of the most influential games of recent years.  With a good storyline, fast gameplay, and amazing effects, it is a game that you can recall every moment of.  While many have tried, the pacing of this game has yet to be matched in my mind.

However, I have to say I was pleasantly surprised.  XCom Enemy Unknown is one of the best turn-based strategy games I have played.  The graphics are excellent, the AI is competent and above all the gameplay is great.  All the elements of the original are incorporated well into this new incarnation; researching new technologies, building base facilities, and above all fighting the huge variety of aliens with an ever-increasing arsenal of weaponry.
The game isn't perfect, and it's a lot more simplistic than the original, but I would heartily recommend this to all turn-based strategy fans.  And it's a far better remake than Total Recall.

Grim Dawn did early access so well because they prioritized finishing the actual integral parts of the game and now after release they're working on additional content like survival mode, new dungeons and items, and even an expansion pack - all which take nothing away from the player experience, they just add to it. Tripwire should have done the same and released PvP after being done with the game, not when there's still a ton of other stuff to work on that are core to the game.
In a world where FPS and Minecraft get all the attention, this is a great exaple of how a modern RPG made by guys who make a TV Show can be a great thing.

reviewing an early access game is always a weird thing to do but after i have played way more than 600 hours in the last 8 months i think it's time to talk about it.
most importantly: do i recommend it?
hell yeah!
if you like FPS games and are into the zed killing business then this game is your ticket to ride.
obviously there is no kind of story involved. it's all about fast paced action and gory carnage. but that is how i like my zombie games.
currently there are 7 perks (or classes) in the game, a decent selection of weapons and as soon as the official maps bore you there is a huge supply of community created maps to continue the slaughter.
killing zeds just never gets boring and you always have lots of fun at it. perfect for relaxing in the evening, killing one or two hours of time before going to bed or blowing off some steam after an annoying day.
if you are looking for a bloody good time then KF2 just never fails to deliver.
but what is the downside?
good question, i'm glad you asked!
at lot of people are really annoyed by the slow pace of the game's development. the recent reviews got more and more negative because of that.
and i certainly have to agree. it takes the developers soooo loooong to get anything done.
fixing bugs takes very often months and since i started playing this game 8 months ago they added one new perk, a few weapons and i think three official maps.
that's just really poor by any standard.
at the same time they added a CSGO-like crate / key system, lots of hats, masks and other wearable stuff and tons of weapon skins, a crafting system and a pvp mode with player controlled survivors fighting player controlled zeds.
but since i am totally not interested in that kind of stuff this whole thing is just one giant box of 'nothing' for me and it seems a lot of people feel the same about it.
when compared to my other favorite early access game at the moment 'subnautica' you clearly see the difference. they pump out a major update at least once per month. obviously i am no game developer but i am pretty sure that a large scale survival game is a lot bigger and way more complex than some game about shooting zeds in the face on a relatively small map. but they got their priorities right. they try to get the base game finished as soon as possible and tend to the specialized details later. after all you can't add the cherry to a cake before you finished the cake!
but sadly that is exactly what they have been doing with KF2 for as long as i have been playing it and imho there is no way this game leaves early access before the very end of 2017 or even way later.
like i said: if you like the shooter genre then this game is just great.
but even i can't deny that there are quite a lot of problems all over the place.
edit: as you can see a lot of people still don't know that 'helpful' / 'not helpful' is not the same as 'i agree' / 'i disagree'. but well, i guess that's just what you have to expect on the interwebz.

Overall I do recommend this game. Now there's not as much content as KF1 and there's some controversy over adding microtransactions and PVP mode, but I still think that it's an overall good game. Starting with the fact that it's Early Access, there are still fairly regular content updates which is great considering it's only a 50 man team working on this and the detail they put into the animations, voicing, and of course, the gore.

However there are also drawbacks. The microtransactions have made a fair amount of people upset and the PVP gamemode  is still pretty buggy and it can be hard to find a match. Some people also have issues with the balancing, as some perks are totally necessary and others are totally useless on higher difficulties. Hell, you really only need zerks, medics, and firebugs for most HoE maps.
Time to break it down:
Pros:
1. Good graphics, the attention to detail with playermodels, guns, and gore is great (though may require a higher-tier PC)
2. Actually defined characters. Remember in KF1 how everyone had the same voice? Well now every character has a distinct identity.
3. An increasing amount of content. There are still 3 perks that have yet to be released, at least one new boss, and hopefully several new maps and characters so there's still more to look foreward to.
4. Satisfying gameplay. Personally I haven't run into any huge bugs but I really have to say it's very satisfying to use a shotgun-sledgehammer to blast through a wall of zeds.
Cons:
1. Still technically Early Access. This game isn't a finished product and therrefore doesn't have all content.
2. Microtransactions. Personally I don't mind these at all but some people do. They're just cosmetic items though so nobody gets an edge over anyone else.
3. PVP. I don't think the game really needed this, it can be fun to play but in my experience it's still unbalanced, buggy, and sparsely populated.
4. Varying levels of perk usefullness. Certain perks are just better on some difficulties. You absolutely need a medic and a zerk on HoE and commando and support are basically extras from a godzilla movie if you have the other necessary perks. You know, like, they're shooting at the monster, but its not really doing much.
In the end I'd say make up your own mind about it. The gameplay itself is fun but if you have issues with some of the other stuff I'd say just wait till release.

South Park: The Stick of Truth *NON Spoiler review*
The Stick of Truth is a very entertaining game, with around 12-16 hours of gameplay including the sidequests, the storyline is nothing far from what we would expect from South Park, from having a very comic, random but enjoyable storyline. With gems from most episodes of the TV Show itself ranging from the very first pilot episode towards the later Black Friday episodes.
Throughout the game you will be meeting our favorite characters from the four boys, Stan, Kyle, Cartman and Kenny to Butters, Jimmy, Craig, Clyde and many others! The dialogue within the game will split your sides with laughter most of the time, either it be from actual character to character interaction or be it on the quest journal, or as we would see it, “Facebook”.
As you journey in your epic quest for the Stick of Truth adding the many characters of South Park to your friends list to either unlock achievements or even for a quest, but it doesn't stop there, it just isn’t for the looks either, it also has its perks what can also upgrade your character, allowing certain damage/resources/resistance modifiers to your character.
The combat system within the game, is a very smooth style of combat, at first glance wouldnt seem to fit in a South Park game, but once you get started in the game, it feels very natural.
Pros of the game;
> Original content and dialogue
> Fresh intake into the world of RPGs
> A good amount of customization, what effects dialogue and interaction with characters.
> Many hidden gems/easter eggs to the TV show what you will find a nice little laugh if you remember the episode.
> Controls and interaction are very simple to use with an informative tutorial at the start of the game.
Cons of the game;
> Once you have completed the game once, the feeling of replayability goes out the window, due to the story being the same each time you would play. Despite what class you would play.
> The difficulty in the game even on the hardest setting isn’t deeply challenging, all but par some boss fights.
> No end game content, now for me in the end of an RPG once you are done with the main storyline I always feel there could be something else to do, whether it be exploring or finishing up side quests, but there is a lack of side quests and you will most likely finish them during the main storyline.

In summary, even though the game is fairly short for its price, I personally felt it was worth to pay that little extra for hilarious content what was provided.without a doubt and even with some of the minor cons of the game, I felt it was a good investment into buying the game.
I would recommend this game for any South Park fan, as I feel you would only have to be a SP fan to understand all the witty lines and items ingame to get the maximum enjoyment.
Thanks for reading.

I'm not really considered a die-hard fan of KF considering I've only casually played the first one for about 2 years on and off. I thoroughly enjoyed that game though so I had to try this one out. This game exceeded my expectations because I thought it was just going to be a visually superior copy of KF1 with same everything else. Not quite.
Although weapons and characters are not as plentiful as the first game (yet), the current selection still offers a lot of enjoyment considering how much special attention the audio and animation get. But not to say that the textures, lighting, physics, gore, etc are also really amazing. The best aspects of this game are probably the weapons, gore, and bullet time that makes it seem like your Neo minus the stunts.
Throughout an entire game, no matter how many zeds you kill, there blood splatter will remain on the map and eventually lead to large blood soaked areas. It's a really cool thing because I have yet to see another game that does this.
The weapons are loud, detailed, and just plain fun to use. It's hard to describe in detail but just keep in mind a lot of work went into them. The fact that there's to two end-match bosses now are really cool because you didn't get that option in the previous game. You won't know who you're going to fight until it's time to fight it.
Bullet time is cool as hell. Things slow down for a few seconds allowing you to react and make a few extra carefully placed shots. The zeds are a whole lot creepier too. Lively animation and sounds completes the immersion in this game, especially for Scrakes and Fleshpounds. First time I heard the stomping of the Scrake as he was pointing at me was insanely intimidating.
As for bad there really isn't anything major at all. I have a few gripes. The characters now have dialogue with unique voices but limited lines. Most of what they say is just stupid and cheesy too. Things like "If I weren't killing zeds, I'd make a snowman". The randomness in characters was fitting in the first game because it felt more like a casual arcade-style survival shooter. In this it makes me feel uncomfortable as if there should be some consistency. Here you got some samuri guy, a gangster, generic military guy from first game, Mr. Foster, a punk girl, etc. This line-up would have felt better in KF1 but this no longer feel like the type of game that would work in. Idk maybe it's just me.
Other things is the workshop. Tripwire decided to go the CS:GO approach and let people buy keys to unlock cases or USB drives that can be achieved from in-game. Only purpose of these is to unlock random accessories to be used by your character. All of which is optional of course but IMO it all looks ugly and not something I would ever use. So to me receiving these cases and USB drives are completely useless and only good for getting a nickel in the community market. This seems to be the topic of a lot of controversly lately and I don't think it constitutes a negative review at all. That and PVP which I have yet to try, because co-op is amazing enough I don't really want to try anything else.
So maybe the devs jumped the gun buy implementing microtransactions in Early Access before releasing more maps and weapons. Just ignore it and carry on. But people are going crazy and are just looking for another negative review to agree on so they can feel better about their opinion on the insigificant crap. Which is why you all gave me a thumbs down for a "helpful review". Personally I feel like the game is going uphill from when it was first released and everyone needs to chill. Come back and complain when you invest in a Early Access game where the developer disappears forever and there's no way to get your money back.
Another thing people seem to complain about is forum cencorship. I don't visit the forums so I can't speak on this. But your review is supposed to reflect the game itself for the most part. Not what goes in the the forums. If things are going downhill in there, make a note of it in your review but don't let it determine your overall recommendation for this game. I feel the vast amount of negative reviews is unjustifiable all because Tripwire decided to implement PVP and Versus early and started policing their forums. Relax.
Anyways, so for the most part yeah there's a lot of the same things carried over from the first game to this, but they built upon everything so much that it doesn't even feel remotely familiar. It's an amazing game worth every cent to me. Let the developers do their thing and just enjoy their game in the eman time.
