If only the state of the PC port was the only problem with this game.
I will admit it right away, I'm a big fanboy when it comes to Batman, having seen nearly all the movies. Both live action and animated, as well as the animated TV series from the 90's and I'm hardly no stranger when it comes to comics either. So it should come as no surprise when I tell you that the Arkham games are some of my absolute favorites and one would think that with this final installment of the series you would finally be able to explore the full and living Gotham City, essentially "Be the Batman" which was the tagline in all the trailers pre-release. But no, right away the city is completely evacuated leaving only an emtpy and very "gamey" and dead feeling theme park. Which wouldn't have been too big of a disappointment if all the activities were actually fun like they were in Arkham City, unfotuntely while there are many different kinds of "quests" to undertake pretty much all of them become repetitive and end up feeling like busy work long before you reach the end credits.
"But at least the game finally introduces the batmobile!" you say. Yeah, that would had been nice if it wasn't forced in to almost everything you do in this game, shoving nearly the rest of Batman's gadgets aside. The game almost feels entirely build around it. It is the solution to nearly every puzzle and the Riddler has even conveniently enough built you tons of racetracks to use it for. Why he would do this I will never know, it just ends up feeling very unimmersive and takes you completely out of the experience. Oh, and don't get me started on all those tank battles. Yes folks, tank battles, tons of them, and here I thought for a second I was playing a Batman game.
Even the story which always has been the main reason why I play the Arkham Games turns out to be completely uninteresting and all the villains are handled very poorly, including the Arkham Knight and the Scarcrow. In much of the marketing material we were shown the all the villains joining forces in order to take down the Batman for good. This never happens in the actual game, instead they are mostly up to their usual criminal activities, the only ones really working together are the previously mentioned Arkham Knight and Scarecrow. Speaking of the Arkham Knight, he who the game is named after is just nothing more than your average Saturday morning cartoon villain, constantly shouting "You have already lost Batman, I'll get you next time!" and despite claiming to know your every weakness all those tanks and drones he sends after you are completely unmanned when he should be aware that you, the Batman doesn't kill. Had they actually been manned it would have presented a real and difficult challenge for our Dark Knight, but we can't have that now can we? The identity of the Arkham Knight is also super easy to figure out, but apparently impossible for "The world's greatest detective", laughable.
Which brings me to the Scarecrow, one of my favorite Batman villains there is. I was very excited for this game when I heard that he was not only coming back for this installment, but he was also going to run the show. In reality though, while he is supposed to be the main villain he is barely in it and the few times he does show, those moments are unfortunately not nearly as memorable as those found in the excellent Arkham Ayslum. When the scarecrow threatens to release his fear toxin all over the city I feel nothing as there is just me and some thugs left in it. The same goes for all attempts the story does to make you care of what happens to your city and your loved ones. They mostly end up feeling like tricks with no real devistating and lasting consequenses, so the sense of fear is quickly washed away. Ironic since fear is supposed to be what this game is all about.
As for the graphics, they are very eye pleasing from a pure technical standpoint even though the city is nearly empty. With that said a game built with the Unreal engine should be running way better than this, at least it runs better now than it did at release and I barely had any problems myself I can only imagine the frustration trying to run this game on a lesser rig or with and AMD graphics card as this another one those Nvidia Gameworks titles and the recent news that the game is never getting official SLI/Crossfire support poured even more salt in the wound. There is also very little visual variation in the game, sure the events in this game are supposed take place all during the same night but I still cannot help to shake that feeling that too much of the game looks the same. I'm also not a fan of the art style change since Arkham City, all the characters appear uglier and more generic ("realistic") looking, where as earlier games looked more like they were pulled straight from the comic books
It's not all bad though,  the combat seen here is the best combat in an Arkham game to date. It feels deeper and more varied than ever before. But if Rocksteady thinks the combat is main reason why we all play the Arkham games they are sorely mistaken, still the game does make some pretty neat improvements here and I got to acknowledge it for that.
Batman: Arkham Knight is far from a bad game, and it is completely functional (performance issues aside), it is just an extremely disappointing one. There are some bursts of brilliance but all in all the Arkham series deserved a way better conclusion than this and I know Rocksteady are capable of so much more. I would even hold Arkham Origins (a game made by another developer which Rocksteady likes to pick on a lot for its lackluster quality to the point to where they don't even see it as a canon Arkam title) as a higher quality product. I would only recommend getting Batman: Arkham Knight during a deep Steam sale and if you have a monster rig to run it properly. Then again you could always try it and use the refund that is valid until the end of the year. Just keep your expectations lower than you normally would when buying a Rocksteady title.

If you're debating on whether or not to get this game, don't (there will be a TL;DR at the bottom giving a brief explanation as to why in case you don't want to read a novel). If you do, you're supporting all of Tripwire's terrible desicions. I was hoping KF2 would restore my faith in early access games, as Dungeon of the Endless, Endless Legend, and Darkest Dungeon were all amazing games in their early access form, and were updated frequently and finshed as soon as possible. With KF2 this is not the case.
As it stands now, KF2 is not near as good as its original. None of the perks seem fun to play anymore due to being heavily dumbed down, and I have no incentive to play any of them. Why switch perks if all I'm getting is a small damage buff and maybe a useful perk skill? It's still going to cost an arm and a leg for any of the weapons. But honestly gameplay is the least of all the complaints I have with this game.
At the time of this review, KF2 is 11 days away from going
in early access, despite saying that they wanted to finish by the end of 2015. Now, delays are expected and it's very difficult to hit deadlines like that, but after nearly a year in early access you would think that it's at least nearly done. Instead of focusing on gameplay balances and adding in new weapons, perks, and maps for everyone to enjoy, they decided the best course of action would be adding
before the game is actually finished. They then decided to add in a new gamemode that nobody had asked for. Tripwire's increasingly bad decisions have killed any desire for me and my friends to play this game.
TL;DR
Don't bother with KF2, you're supporting a business practice that needs to die out. Please, don't let this be okay just because the original KF was good, this game is setting an awful example for all developers out there.

Excellent game.  Played on my MSI Apache 264 GE72 with GTX960m low graphics deemed suitable for this card.  You need a 4-5 gig ddr higher end card to see this game in its glory.  The attention to detail is outstanding -visually.  The story is engrossing. The Jokers role in this plot is the best part.  And such Immersive gameplay, let me tell ya.  So many various activities; you wont be running out of side stuff to do in any short time.  My only gripe is that Vehicle chase missions are somewhat annoying.  A bulky cumbersome van should not be able to out maneuver the Batmobile.  I can't wrap my head around who thought it would be an excellent idea to make the Batmobile chase very nimble, nitrous induced high center of gravity heavy asrmored vans that take several immobilizer MISSLES to stop.  Seriously?  Quite frankly, it turned me off to the chase story plot in general.  The other side missions are intelligentlly put together and the plots are great, however this does not forgive that they are quite short, but only in depth of writing comapred to the subplots.  The main story is the most gripping beyond and beyond Orgins.  I do believe the voice actor for the orgins Batman seemed a bit more believeable.  I am not knocking the AK Batman actor by any means, but there are places where he sounds a bit too much like a "superhero" than a "Dark Knight".  Some of his lines are seemingly forced, and can be occasionally campy.  The game is definatly worth a buy, reguardless of any residual backlash from the nay-sayers who had game launch issues that dont give second chances to a company that has provided them with several great Batman games.  Much like they like to see failure instead of hope.  The company fixed these issues,  Stuff happens.  Even to the best of us.  And Id have to say that this game is a masterpiece so far.

Batman: Arkham Knight, this game was extremely poorly ported to PC, it made a lot of people get annoyed with it and they are right, that the WB did for PC gamers is inadmissible.
But leaving that aside, after a lot of patches, I finally got to play this game and only I can get very sad when I think: "Why I didn't play this before.".
This game is definitely a masterpiece, I played every other game of Arkham and can say that this is the best one (Arkham City was another great game).
Pros:
-Gotham City is a great city with a lot of things to do, it's very fun to explore the city.
-Batmobile adds new gameplay mechanics.
-The Plot is really good.
-A lot of fun side quests to play.
Cons:
-A lot of bugs, glitches and game crashes (At the launch of this game it was unplayable, now you at least can play. With some bugs and glitches, but you can)
Comments:
Story (Main quest / City of Fear):
*The story follows the pattern of other games of Arkham, a lot of bad guys show up, but there are one or two that are truly important.
*This game has the mysterious "Arkham Knight" that gives the game an atmosphere of mystery, since you (and Batman) want to know who he is.
*The game also had a lot of plot twists. I liked a lot.
Batmobile:
The Batmobile is certainly a great addition to the game, you can move large distances faster than gliding. It adds a lot of new types of puzzle to play and the battles with enemy tanks (A lot of them at the same time) are very difficult.
Conclusion: If WB had not screwed with the game release this game could potentially be GOTY. Because the game itself is well made.

Having over 200 hours played on Batman: Arkham Knight since launch, I can safely say after the last patch the game runs a lot better than before. Playing this game on a moderate rig which I'll post on the bottom of this review, the game runs at 60 FPS at nearly all times for me on max settings with the exception of Nvidia Gameworks, I have all those turned off except enhanced rain. The game is stable with a mild overclock and the only time my FPS drops from 60 is when gliding around the city, although it's usually just a 5-8 FPS lost at most from 60. For reference I could barely keep 30 FPS at launch, now the lowest it dips is to the mid 50's on high settings. I'm overall very satisfied with the game in its current form.
This is the first review I'm leaving on Steam and it really was a shame a pretty good game like Arkham Knight came out in such an atrocious state at launch, to the point that a lot of people will never give the game a chance again. I really do hope developers in the future learn from this fiasco and take just a little extra time to polish up their PC ports.

As a huge Batman fan, maybe most of my opinions regarding Batman are biased, but here, I can only state the truth, because it reflects my opinions.
Most people see the fact that the ratings for this game suck, and that is because at first it encountered some major technical difficulties. The ratings for this game sucked for two or three months, and later on, after the update that fixed everything, no one really cared and just left it. I understand that first impressions are very important, but now, it is just simply unfair.
I recently bought the game, and it ran smoothly without glitches, lags, or force quit whatsoever. The rain effects and textures are all perfect, having walked around, zooming in of almost anything, I would now. It is kept as a constant 60fps even at the highest resolution, with a moderate Graphics card. And as long as you don't overpile your computer, it's going to run fine.
The gameplay is even better. There are a lot of modes, with slow-motions woven seamlessly into gameplay. The fighting is fluent and the Batmobile is more than easy to control. Let's go over the main modes:
-1 vs many mode: Batman takes on a lot of thugs at once, beating them all to a pulp
-Infiltrate a Room mode: Batman takes down many armed thugs one by one, lurking in the dark
-Battle mode (Batmobile): Batman uses the Batmobile in the battle mode to take on numerous tanks, dodging shells and shooting tanks with armor penetrating shells

It's very rare I recommend triple A games, I simply don't think they need my voice to add to their profits. However firaxis have done the impossible and taken a much loved nostalgia riddled game and brought it into 2012. This game has almost completely evolved and built on what the original was while only trimming away unnessecary quirks and baggage. Something that every previous attempt at an X-COM sequel has failed to do. (And there have been quite a few). Your units will live and die by your tactics and stratagy, this game brutely punishes carelessness. The games Ai is smart enough to flank and fallback on harder difficulties.
Almost completely evolved yes, but sadly not quite. The alien movements within the geoscape is a static scripted system. Which is a far cry from the originals aggressive AI that would attempt to win the game from you by expanding and performing missions to gain presence and power within the world.
There are clearly defined points in the game where if you do not choose to progress. The aliens cannot win, they are frozen and must await your completion of key missions before the AI and script will advance to the next stage.
This has a profound effect on replayability. Because of the lack of unpredictability in alien movements on the world map. Every playthrough runs through exactly the same script. But worse than this, is the fact that with a little thought you can easily make the game unlosable, regardless of the difficulty setting.
A great tactics game sadly hampered by the scripted plot and alien geoscape scripting.

The idea of a South Park video game may not sound very appealing, but Trey Parker, Matt Stone, and Obsidian found a way to capture an episodic experience with The Stick of Truth.  Unlike many RPG’s, South Park: The Stick of Truth doesn’t ask you to be a hardcore gamer. The combat system is simple, yet entertaining. However, you should be a fan of the show’s sense of humor. There are plenty of Easter eggs for longtime fans of the TV series, but you don’t have to be one to enjoy it.
The game starts out like most games do with an introduction to the mechanics and combat. What sets this apart is that it’s fun from the start.  The combat is never too complicated. There are multiple characters to use, leaving many ways to attack each battle, and the commentary during battle keeps you laughing. South Park uses a classic turn-based system with some timing elements.  Once the timing is figured out, it’s smooth sailing. I only have a couple of small complaints about the mechanics. Using a controller I find the combat wheel isn’t as smooth as I would have liked. The fart tutorial instructions are also very unclear and can become increasingly frustrating, especially for a tutorial. These are small complaints though, and I find it doesn’t ruin the experience at all. They made a good choice keeping it simple so that the player can focus on the heart of the game, the South Park humor.
Video Games are not traditionally known for their sense of humor, but The Stick of Truth bucks the trend. There are many references to past South Park episodes to enjoy and plenty of typical jokes that always put South Park in its’ own category.  The jokes extend even further. If you have been playing video games for years then you are familiar with many systems, mechanics, and techniques that are common place. You probably don’t even notice them anymore, but they find a way to make humor out of those too. They touch on boss fights, combat systems, audio logs, and much more.
Pacing would normally be a concern with an open world RPG trying to tells jokes and keep a coherent story.  The Stick of Truth doesn’t have these issues. South Park is known for outlandish stories and this created many plots and side missions to experience in game. The sense of humor is maintained with one liners even when the story is not advancing.  If you only want to play the main story, it can be enjoyable, but I do recommend the fun side missions.  Exploring the town has many humorous collectables, fun places to see, and humorous people to talk to.
Overall the game is technically sound. There are a couple of glitches where the main character’s face disappears but this actually proves to be quite funny. Playing on PC, I was curious to see if they were going to have any graphical options since South Park has traditionally looked bad on purpose.  Not surprisingly, they kept it simple and there wasn’t much to alter other than resolution. They decided to lock the frame rate at 30 frames per second to help maintain the choppy animation they strive for and it works just fine. The only time I notice it is when the character runs. This proves to be a bit blurry, but doesn’t take away from the experience at all. It looks just like a South Park episode which is what we all want.
Without a doubt, The Stick of Truth is the funniest game I have ever played. I don’t remember laughing while playing a video game other than Grand Theft Auto and I laughed from beginning to end.  This isn’t an intimidatingly long game. You are looking at about 13 hours if you play straight through and it took me about 16 with some exploring. At the heart of this game is the South Park sense of humor so if you don’t find the show entertaining, you may want to pass on this game. However, if you are a fan of the series, then you should play this game.

The Stick of Truth is at its best when it straddles the incredible - but true - ability of a bunch of kids to bring a game of pretend to extreme heights of seriousness, with limited stakes appearing huge.
It's at its best when it is about play.
In these phases, the succinct turn-based combat, the battleground navigation, the limited character interaction and shape of the world exist as a masterful and coherent whole. They generate this fantastic flow that - in one trick - justify the game pretense while engaging the player in it, epic battle throughout fake taverns and parental curfew taken in strides.
When the world of 'normal' adult gets involved or when the game brings back some of the series lore along with stalwart tropes, it is far less successful: the veil of pretend falls and what's left is a giddy but dull self-awareness that highlights the least  flattering parts of the game structure.
Chief of these is the turn based combat and its place in the progression: it allows for tedious conservatism (same moves all the time) instead of encouraging experimentation with your equipment and with your buddies during encounters. In the same way, the block system has very unreliable sign and feedback; which makes it difficult to use.
Beside that, your mileage may vary: South Park has built several facets during its run and I don't care for the scat humor from the first seasons or the easy lampooning of popular culture icons that recent years have brought.
Some people do and I expect they'll enjoy the game to through and through. I couldn't because what really interests me is the writers harsh tackling of controversial topics or of the darker aspects of the  logic and ecosystem that you'll find in a pack of kids. There's a significant amount of that (along with a nearly invisible touch of social commentary), but the scat and the pop-ref ARE what the last two thirds of the game ride on.
And I can't support that choice: it makes the game less of a beast of its own - self contained, designed for the experience - and makes it rely on a bunch of crutches that are offputtingly obvious and ultimately unnecessary.
The music is awesome though.

As a huge Batman fan, maybe most of my opinions regarding Batman are biased, but here, I can only state the truth, because it reflects my opinions.
Most people see the fact that the ratings for this game suck, and that is because at first it encountered some major technical difficulties. The ratings for this game sucked for two or three months, and later on, after the update that fixed everything, no one really cared and just left it. I understand that first impressions are very important, but now, it is just simply unfair.
I recently bought the game, and it ran smoothly without glitches, lags, or force quit whatsoever. The rain effects and textures are all perfect, having walked around, zooming in of almost anything, I would now. It is kept as a constant 60fps even at the highest resolution, with a moderate Graphics card. And as long as you don't overpile your computer, it's going to run fine.
The gameplay is even better. There are a lot of modes, with slow-motions woven seamlessly into gameplay. The fighting is fluent and the Batmobile is more than easy to control. Let's go over the main modes:
-1 vs many mode: Batman takes on a lot of thugs at once, beating them all to a pulp
-Infiltrate a Room mode: Batman takes down many armed thugs one by one, lurking in the dark
-Battle mode (Batmobile): Batman uses the Batmobile in the battle mode to take on numerous tanks, dodging shells and shooting tanks with armor penetrating shells
-Pursuit mode: Batman uses the Batmobile to chase down and immobilize fleets of high-speed cars and tanks.
Aside from those, there are also some other modes that are also extremely awesome (prepare for some jumpscares!). There are some effects that are very eerie, for example (don't worry, no spoilers), some things change when you turn away from it, so when you turn back, everything's different. It contains everything gamers love about the previous Arkham games, added with new, more awesome features like the Fear Multi-Takedown and better interfaces and music.
I don't even have a Pros/Cons list because I sincerely can't think of any cons.
Last note: if you loved the previous Arkham games, buy this game. If you didn't like or never heard of the previous Arkham games, still buy this game. If you are not even a gamer, also buy this game, it is the best place where you can spend your money.

This one is every bit as exciting as the original with as much enhancement as I had hoped.  And I'm not easily impressed.  This one is a keeper. The gunplay in KF2 is by far the best thing going for this game. It's very hard for a game to make shooting a gun 'feel' good, but every weapon in KF2 'feels' good, and theres alot of them to shoot. There could be more weapons, maps, enemies and modes, and there will be more, which is the biggest (and in my opinion only) negative thing there is to say about KF2.
The game is in Early Access, and has been for over a year, since its release there has been a grand total of 5 maps, 3 perks (each with 4 weapons for a total of 12 weapons), and 1 new enemy that has been implemented post EA release.
Their (Tripwire Interactive) current development pace is roughly 3-4 months per content patch, which normally includes 1 perk and 1 map. This is frustratingly slow and the only negative thing i can say about KF2.
KF2 is still easily far and beyond a greater co op wave based shooter than anything that is currently out there, so if thats the kind of game you are looking for KF2 is definitly the game for you, just remember to be patient (very patient) when waiting for new updates.

Batman: Arkham Knight is a very enjoyable and addictive game to play but it did have a fair amount of flaws. Overall though I would have to say that the game is worth it as it has a lot of content and it is more Batman in the style of the other games in the series which Rocksteady does so well.
Let's start of with the negatives and get those out of the way.
First thing for me was the graphical settings, I enjoy gaming with high framerates as well as good graphics, the fact that most of the settings I would expect to be on High I had to run on medium or low and those I expected to be on low were on their highest was just strange. This game eats VRAM like a black hole consumes light, even though they have the bar showing how much was used it took a lot of tweaking to get the settings which felt the most playable for me but I got there.
The other negative is that there were just random pauses where the entire game would lock up for a second or two for no known reason and then suddenly carry on as smooth as ever. I got used to that fairly easily so I could deal with it, it just sucked when it happened during a fight and messed up my flow. I know it wasn't due to hectic stuff happening on scene because it even happened when crawling inside of ducts.
The only other negative I have which is actually related to gameplay is some of the side missions just felt like filler missions to just grind through and waste time. Mostly I mean the missions where you had to remove the checkpoints, kill all the tanks and destroy the towers. They just felt way to tedious and didn't offer anything to the story at all, it's like they were just added on to add time to the overall game.
That is about it for the negatives, as for the positive aspects, combat has been improved and felt way more fluid and when you are upgrading your skills it gives nice demonstrations on how to use those skills in combat with video which was great. It really added to the experience when it came to deciding on how to approach different scenarios and which methods of attack to use.
The tank combat was another thing which a lot of people did not like but I actually enjoyed it. It have something to do with the fact that I was playing the game with a gamepad throughout but when it came to the tank combat I switched to keyboard and mouse as this made it feel way better and easier. I've never been good at FPS type games with a gamepad so this may have been why it felt fun for me.
As for the story, I liked the it immensely, it might have helped that I have never been a huge batman fan but have always liked the character so I did not know much about the lore and back stories at all so learning all of that through playing all the games in the series probably helped as I was constantly want to know more.
If you have played the other two Batman games and would like to know how the story ends but are trying to decide whether or not to get this game due to all the negativity surrounding how it runs then I will say that you must get the game. Just spend some time tweaking the settings before you start and get the game running smoothly at the get go and then you can sit back and just play and enjoy without any real issues. I honestly did not see much difference with some of the graphical settings anyway, especially textures, so don't let that put you off from a great overall gaming experience.

Killing Floor 2 lives up to its predecessor in several aspects, as in others it ends up taking another perspective, which makes the game in fact a sequel, rather than just a more beautiful and polished version of the original KF.
The most noticeable different perspective is its more chaotic essence, less calculating/slow paced as in the first game. Here everything is very frantic and happens very fast, which requires the players good response and agile decision making in the game, plus knowledge in how to kill enemies efficiently.
Attention to detail is also something that stands out in KF2. Each weapon has its animation worked in detail at 120FPS so that when in Slow Motion (ZedTime) the details can be seen perfectly, each vibration of the weapon as it shoots, the bullets flying towards the target, mixed up with the colors black, white and red highlighting the beauty and how detailed are the animations and models of the game. In addition, as you increase the difficulty of the game, enemies gain more animations, attacks and details, which makes everything cooler and more frantic.
Yet, even more visually appealing (perhaps in an attempt to attract more audiences to the game?) And trying to simplify the game more, making it more frantic, the game still retains its niche position. Not everyone likes to repeatedly play the same scheme of hordes and bosses, hordes and bosses, against the same enemies on different maps.
So if you liked KF1, you're going to like this one, even being a little different.
If you like Horde Games, you will also love KF2.
Just remember that in case you do not like Horde Games, you can get bored easily by repetition.
Mesmo após 1100 horas de jogo, continuo me divertindo com ele, sempre! :)
Killing Floor 2 faz jus a seu predecessor em vários aspectos, assim como em outros acaba por tomar outra perspectiva, o que faz do game de fato uma sequência, invés de apenas uma versão mais bonita e polida do original KF.
A perspectiva mais notávelmente diferente é sua essência mais caótica, menos calculista como no primeiro game. Aqui, tudo é muito frenético e acontece bem rápido, o que exige dos jogadores boa resposta e tomada de decisão ágil no game, além de conhecimento em como matar inimigos eficientemente.
A atenção aos detalhes é algo que se sobresai em KF2. Cada arma tem sua animação detalhadamente trabalhada em 120FPS para que, quando em Slow Motion (ZedTime), os detalhes possam ser vistos perfeitamente, cada vibração da arma enquanto atira, as balas voando em direção ao alvo, junto das cores preto, branco e vermelho destacam a beleza e o quão detalhado são as animações e modelos do jogo. Além disso, conforme você aumenta a dificuldade do jogo, os inimigos ganham mais animações, ataques e detalhes, o que deixa tudo mais legal e frenético.
Ainda sim, mesmo mais atraente visualmente (talvez numa tentativa de atrair mais público ao jogo?) e tentanto simplificar mais o jogo, tornando-o mais frenético, o game ainda se mantém em sua posição de nicho. Não é todo mundo que gosta de jogar repetidamente o mesmo esquema de hordas e chefes, hordas e chefes, contra os mesmos inimigos em mapas distintos.
Por isso, se você gostava do KF1, vai gostar desse, lembrando ser um tanto diferente.
Se gosta de Horde Games, também amará KF2.
Apenas lembre-se de que, caso você não goste de Horde Games, pode enjoar facilmente pela repetição.

I REALLY want to recommend this game, I do. I loved KF1, but, with all the cons that KF2 brings it seems to outweigh how much the game is good about.

As for the Pros, there are a couple, but they don't overweigh the cons enough.
No more paying for the DLC weapons: Cool!
Its a sequel to a pretty good game: Ehh... A couple of sequel games are pretty terrible, this is almost in that category.
It seems to be on sale most of the time: Thats pretty cool, but some may think that it might be because of bad sales.
More perks than last game: Cool, but they really need to get that in order. Balancing, ADDING THEM, ect.
Overall, KF2 isn't a BAD game, but, it doesn't seem to live up to the name of KF1.

As of right now... no I wouldn't want to recommend Killing Floor 2 until it's out of Early Access. Unless you really really loved the KF1,  but wanted a bit more, and you can live without the campiness. (Although they have classic skins with the two original male voices).
I love both games and I'll still be playing after this review, however it's just sad how even on the Early Access part that Tripwire said they'll be doing it right. Yes you can ignore microtransactions, but what people seem to not understand is how bad of taste microtransactions left in gamers mouths. I'm all for supporting devs, but the best support they can get is new players purchasing their game. That's pretty much how KF1 got so popular (Also getting a PC powerful enough to run that wouldn't be that expensive, oh and can't forget steam sales).
Versus is all right, if you've played L4D well with great teamwork then you should have no trouble with this. However I'd like the rest of the perks in. There is the workshop so maps aren't going to be too much of an issue, unless modders add perks themselves.
So overall the game is great, however it definitely feels like Tripwire is giving it a second thought, although they are still holding mapping contests it seems. Enemies are fun to fight, guns are fun to use, current perks as well. But it just needs those final perks and maps. Honestly less skins and cosmetics would be nice until this gets out of EA.
TL;DR I love the game but can't recommend it like I could do for Killing Floor 1. I can only hope the final release is better than what we have now

No, I seriously do not believe what I'm seeing- a true, GOOD remake of my all-time favorite game. I had mediocre expectations for it, especially regarding the atrociously short and restrictive demo, but this game turned out to be pretty much equal in terms of fun, tension and free-time sapping as its famous predecessor.
It is now a fast paced, streamlined, but not in the least dumbed down game, with pretty much all tedious, boring elements that plagued the first game removed, improved or made more interesting- even the pistols remain useful throughout the campaign!
The good old U3 engine runs smooth as butter, the visual style is cartoonish and effective, and the alien design from the first game is expanded upon really well.
I've had my doubts about the troop specialization and reduced squad size, but those were dispelled while playing, and those mechanics really add interesting tactical options to the game.
Fully recommended, be you X-COM veterans or not!

I've been wanting to review this game since it was first released in June, but I held back because of the game being pulled from the Steam store and the fact that it was still messy after it was released again. But I decided to review the game anyway, but I'm going to start off with one important thing.
Yes, although I'm giving this game a positive review, this review is based on the game just
Since I only played it on PC, there will be some bias here. However, I'm going to try and keep this review as generalized towards all console versions as possible.
The heaviest blow compared to the other versions, Arkham Knight's graphics were indeed just "meh" compared to the other versions of the game. That being said, however, it's still a fairly pretty game. The rain looks pretty for me, and is used nicely. However, the overall feel I had with the game wasn't all that "dark" or "evil," but rather just bland. The atmosphere wasn't all that thrilling for the most part. But then again, PC bias could just be kicking in here.
The combat is the smoothest out of all of the Arkham games. It's fast-paced, intense, and very fluid. I had a blast beating up thugs and is one of the strongest points Arkham Knight has to offer. The Batmobile is the main part I would like to discuss about the gameplay. I wasn't AGAINST the Batmobile being in the game. Seeing how large Gotham City is, I wouldn't mind having some quick transportation to get from one place to another. It didn't disappoint for the most part in game. However, my main qualm with it all is the fact that the Batmobile was crammed into the game as much as possible. If you want to show off a new feature to a game, that's fine, but abusing it just ruins the experience. The tank form is especially annoying to me. You'll soon realize that 90% of the time, you're just destroying wave after wave of drone vehicles when you could just face the militia soldiers head-on. This leads to the "boss fights" to be incredibly disappointing. The side missions were also fairly interesting, but I wasn't entirely hooked to them. They were satisfactory, but nothing to write home about. In the end, the gameplay is definitely a mixed bag that's still above average.
The story is definitely the best part to Arkham Knight. It was actually very entertaining and kept me on the edge of my seat. The scenes with the
were especially interesting. Sometimes, they might be really annoying, but I could still manage them. When the game reached the climax, I was actually genuinely WORRIED whether or not Batman would be able to survive the wrath of Scarecrow or not. The final mission was amazing and also mind-bending. Plus, the twists were very well played and added onto the very enjoyable main story. The one glaring flaw with the storyline in my eyes was the fact that the Arkham Knight's identity is fairly predictable if you're a Batman fan like myself. But, there wasn't many other people cut for the Arkham Knight role, so it was a reasonable choice. The side mission stories were somewhat decent, but it depends on which one you're doing. But, in the end, the main storyline is awesome and was an excellent way to end the Arkham series.
Not much to say here when it comes to music. When it comes to voice acting, it's a mixed bag. On one hand, you have people like
and Scarecrow, who were interesting and enjoyable to listen to. Batman, however, wasn't the best when it came to voice acting. He seemed very cheesy, and although that's what he's often known for, it didn't feel right in a game like this.
Despite Arkham Knight's large world full of different things to do, you more than likely won't get too much replayability out of the game. Aside from 100%ing it, you won't stick around for long unless you worship the game. There isn't really much else to say, as it depends on how much you enjoy the game.
Arkham Knight is definitely not the best Arkham game in the series. However, it isn't a horrible game. There was so much potential with the game that it isn't deserving of a GotY award in my eyes, but it's still a fairly enjoyable experience that you should be able to have some fun with the game.

I've been wanting to review this game since it was first released in June, but I held back because of the game being pulled from the Steam store and the fact that it was still messy after it was released again. But I decided to review the game anyway, but I'm going to start off with one important thing.
Yes, although I'm giving this game a positive review, this review is based on the game just
Since I only played it on PC, there will be some bias here. However, I'm going to try and keep this review as generalized towards all console versions as possible.
The heaviest blow compared to the other versions, Arkham Knight's graphics were indeed just "meh" compared to the other versions of the game. That being said, however, it's still a fairly pretty game. The rain looks pretty for me, and is used nicely. However, the overall feel I had with the game wasn't all that "dark" or "evil," but rather just bland. The atmosphere wasn't all that thrilling for the most part. But then again, PC bias could just be kicking in here.
The combat is the smoothest out of all of the Arkham games. It's fast-paced, intense, and very fluid. I had a blast beating up thugs and is one of the strongest points Arkham Knight has to offer. The Batmobile is the main part I would like to discuss about the gameplay. I wasn't AGAINST the Batmobile being in the game. Seeing how large Gotham City is, I wouldn't mind having some quick transportation to get from one place to another. It didn't disappoint for the most part in game. However, my main qualm with it all is the fact that the Batmobile was crammed into the game as much as possible. If you want to show off a new feature to a game, that's fine, but abusing it just ruins the experience. The tank form is especially annoying to me. You'll soon realize that 90% of the time, you're just destroying wave after wave of drone vehicles when you could just face the militia soldiers head-on. This leads to the "boss fights" to be incredibly disappointing. The side missions were also fairly interesting, but I wasn't entirely hooked to them. They were satisfactory, but nothing to write home about. In the end, the gameplay is definitely a mixed bag that's still above average.
The story is definitely the best part to Arkham Knight. It was actually very entertaining and kept me on the edge of my seat. The scenes with the
were especially interesting. Sometimes, they might be really annoying, but I could still manage them. When the game reached the climax, I was actually genuinely WORRIED whether or not Batman would be able to survive the wrath of Scarecrow or not. The final mission was amazing and also mind-bending. Plus, the twists were very well played and added onto the very enjoyable main story. The one glaring flaw with the storyline in my eyes was the fact that the Arkham Knight's identity is fairly predictable if you're a Batman fan like myself. But, there wasn't many other people cut for the Arkham Knight role, so it was a reasonable choice. The side mission stories were somewhat decent, but it depends on which one you're doing. But, in the end, the main storyline is awesome and was an excellent way to end the Arkham series.
Not much to say here when it comes to music. When it comes to voice acting, it's a mixed bag. On one hand, you have people like
and Scarecrow, who were interesting and enjoyable to listen to. Batman, however, wasn't the best when it came to voice acting. He seemed very cheesy, and although that's what he's often known for, it didn't feel right in a game like this.
Despite Arkham Knight's large world full of different things to do, you more than likely won't get too much replayability out of the game. Aside from 100%ing it, you won't stick around for long unless you worship the game. There isn't really much else to say, as it depends on how much you enjoy the game.
Arkham Knight is definitely not the best Arkham game in the series. However, it isn't a horrible game. There was so much potential with the game that it isn't deserving of a GotY award in my eyes, but it's still a fairly enjoyable experience that you should be able to have some fun with the game.

I absolutely love this game. It kind of reminds me of Binding of Isaac in that it's a difficult rogue-like item based action rpg, with the two main differences being that it's a 2D platformer instead of a 2.5D isometric room to room dungeon crawl and that this one is actually fun... Anyhow, there's very little I can say of the negatives. The biggest problem the game faces is the difficulty. Easy mode is laughably easy aside from the final bosses which were very tense, climactic battles and normal mode is near impossible to beat. I dread to think about hard mode... You have two choices on how to play the game. Take your time and get all available items but let the difficulty meter rise up by a large amount which gets overwhelming very fast with the insane amount of monsters spawning or rush to the next level avoiding everything, which doesn't allow the difficulty to rise up too far but still screws you over because you have no items to get far. Pick your poison. The rest relies mainly on luck, depending on what items you get when. On a lighter note, everything else about the game is great. After an outcry of bad reviews, media and refunds. They realised they had to do something and couldn't get away with it, why? because they were losing money, not because they care.

Firstly, before the game was out they said that people that bought a select GPU, GTX 970/980 etc, would get this game for free thanks to a promotional deal with Nvidia, as they often do for big upcoming titles, and that you would also get the pre-order bonus. Which they decided to change their minds on last second before the game was released "Oh you don't get this pre-order bonus now, you have to pay for it" not to mention that DLC, pre-order bonuses or anything of the like being announced/there before the main game is even released is ridiculous and is just content that could have been in the main game itself, but they realise it is something they can cut out and make money on.
WB knew that the game was in a terrible state for PC months and months before the game was released, but once again, didn't care, it's the PC market.
The PC PORT of the game was outsourced to Iron Galaxy Studios, a smaller game developer rather than the one that everyone thought was doing it, and was promoted as being the developer, Rocksteady. So the PC market got the worse end of the stick with a lack of attention.
When the game first released, it was a huge mess, there were freezes, stuttering and all sorts of performance issues all over the place, I remember my game actually reaching up to 14GB of ram usage which is pretty ridiculous considering what the game is, and that was with an i7 4930k at 4.5Ghz and two Gtx 970's at 1.35Ghz, it was not about the computer not being able to handle the game, because it can handle a lot better than this, at some points it would be fine and I would be around or over 100 frames at 2560x1440p, even in fighting situations or running around, but then randomly it would decide it wants to run like crap, stutter, freeze and crash, or just play at below 30fps for no reason at all. Since the updates it has been a bit better, it doesn't use as much ram, around 6-8GB now most of the time, and the FPS drops seem to be mostly gone, and there is no more stuttering, freezing or crashing, but I am not getting as high as I use to.
They made promises over and over that they would fix the game and admitted to what a mess it was after they started getting such bad reviews and losing money, they said they would fix SLI and continue to optimize the game, but after a while they said they "can't" fix everything and decided that they are not going to fix SLI because, well they don't care and it's not in their biggest interest money wise.
Generally WB have behaved♥♥♥♥♥♥poor with this game, maybe if they didn't outsource to a smaller developer to handle the PC version of the game, most of these issues would not be a problem, but alas they are. On another note, I would say if you've played one WB game, then you can probably expect the others to be very similar. Batman, Mad Max, Middle-Earth: Shadow of Mordor all feel pretty much the same to me, just different skins. The controls are nearly identical, the enemies are pretty much the same with different skins, and it has the same mindless "side missions" 'collect this' 'collect that' 'do this' 'do that' over and over. Even the maps seems pretty darn similar.
I might finish this game eventually just because I own it and got it for free, but would I recommend it to anyone for them to buy it? no. Not unless it was on a 60-75%+ sale, even then I would feel somewhat bitter about supporting WB.

Risk of Rain is a roguelike platformer with lots of trial and error, similarly to a game like The Binding of Isaac. It may be extremely tough for you to get a handle on the game early on, but later on in the game it becomes easier once you know enemies patterns, types, abilities, and unlock characters that you can play to your own liking. You can unlock artifacts, which also make the game incredibly fun while also making it somewhat easier, depending on which ones you choose. There are some that harshly reduce your health while giving you a giant damage bonus, and there are some which make only the most powerful types of monsters appear. If I were you, I would definitely play this game with online friends. Playing this game with a friend on the same screen becomes a burden, and sometimes we would argue for items or one of us would fall out of the screen region and we would have to scramble to get the other player on screen. It's a fun but challenging game that you should play on your own monitor for the best experience.

I’ve played your typical snow, lava, or water level but a rectal, yes rectal as in your butt, level has now completed every possible variation of level design. This is just one small over the top humor and craziness found in South Park. If you watch or have ever seen the show you know this is typical SP humor.
In South Park you play as the silent new kid who just moved into town and are told to go outside and make friends. You meet Cartman, Butters, Princess Kenny, and a few others who are LARPing (Live Action Role-Playing) and playing as the humans. They ask you to join and help protect the Stick of Truth because whoever controls it can control the Universe.
You start out fighting against the elves who are played by Stan, Kyle, and some other kids. Things just get even crazier though as you go onto fight aliens, bums, and Nazi zombies. Majority of the story takes place in South Park but will also see Canada and a spaceship along the way. The story is funny and enjoyable to go through. Especially if you love the South Park show.
The game is a turn based RPG where you control a party of two but the option to switch one character with others who join you. When you pick your attack you try to hit the button at the right moment to get a perfect hit which can add a boost to the attack. Each character has one main weapon, melee or projectile, and magic attack except your character may do both melee and projectile. You can also do gaseous attacks which can explode or cause people to be grossed out.
Throughout the game when you meet new people they will send you friend requests just like Facebook. After you become friends you will start seeing posts on your “Facebook” profile from them. These can be very funny and sometimes creepy. You also have many collectibles to find in the game like all the weapons and outfits. You can also try to locate all the Chinpokomon, which are SP’s parody of Pokémon in case you didn’t know. Hence the name.
My only gripe with the game was it felt short and I would have loved many more hilarious side missions. Maybe we could get lucky and see some DLC or maybe even a sequel if it sells enough. The game was a blast to play and had a great story that had me laughing many times. If you enjoy South Park and are looking for some really good laughs or even disturbing images, some of these I can never forget, than this is the game for you to play.

I’ve played your typical snow, lava, or water level but a rectal, yes rectal as in your butt, level has now completed every possible variation of level design. This is just one small over the top humor and craziness found in South Park. If you watch or have ever seen the show you know this is typical SP humor.
In South Park you play as the silent new kid who just moved into town and are told to go outside and make friends. You meet Cartman, Butters, Princess Kenny, and a few others who are LARPing (Live Action Role-Playing) and playing as the humans. They ask you to join and help protect the Stick of Truth because whoever controls it can control the Universe.
You start out fighting against the elves who are played by Stan, Kyle, and some other kids. Things just get even crazier though as you go onto fight aliens, bums, and Nazi zombies. Majority of the story takes place in South Park but will also see Canada and a spaceship along the way. The story is funny and enjoyable to go through. Especially if you love the South Park show.
The game is a turn based RPG where you control a party of two but the option to switch one character with others who join you. When you pick your attack you try to hit the button at the right moment to get a perfect hit which can add a boost to the attack. Each character has one main weapon, melee or projectile, and magic attack except your character may do both melee and projectile. You can also do gaseous attacks which can explode or cause people to be grossed out.
Throughout the game when you meet new people they will send you friend requests just like Facebook. After you become friends you will start seeing posts on your “Facebook” profile from them. These can be very funny and sometimes creepy. You also have many collectibles to find in the game like all the weapons and outfits. You can also try to locate all the Chinpokomon, which are SP’s parody of Pokémon in case you didn’t know. Hence the name.
My only gripe with the game was it felt short and I would have loved many more hilarious side missions. Maybe we could get lucky and see some DLC or maybe even a sequel if it sells enough. The game was a blast to play and had a great story that had me laughing many times. If you enjoy South Park and are looking for some really good laughs or even disturbing images, some of these I can never forget, than this is the game for you to play.

It is not uncommon for human beings to find themselves bored with the monotony of regular life. Day after day we find ourselves experiencing new things, yet we still long for something. We feel as if we need an escape from the world in which we find ourselves. This need has given rise to a plethora of movies, books, and games, among many other things, to distract us from our life. It is with this same feeling that I decided to embark upon such a distraction.
Leaping forth to immerse myself in a new world, I was excited at the new possibilities it offered. Although my character's landing had been rough, I was optimistic for the future. What never before seen wonders would I uncover. What beauty that had yet to grace the sight of man would I be blessed to lay my eyes upon? The imagination of man falls short in the face reality and I knew not what I would come across. The wonderous awe I felt as my feet touched the ground of this new world would be torn brutally away. Naïvety soon wears out its welcome, as did I apparently.
What followed was a quick and horrifying descent into madness. As I gazed upon the flora of this new world, never having seen comparable beauty in Earth's, I was soon greeted with the fauna. A surprising variety of creatures met me with death in their minds. I fought as hard as I could, killing many, but the longer I lingered, the more arrived and the more dangerous they were. An endless flood of enemies assailed me, precious little time was I safe.
Worse still were the monsters who were so much greater than the others. Towering beasts of great strength and tenacity hunted me down. Desperation seeped deep into my bones and I began to savour those rare moments when the creatures of a new area had yet to discover my presence.I would watch as the many different beings who so oft fell dead before me lived. They went about their bussiness, so similar to the animals of Earth.
Realization struck me, I was the alien in this world, the terrifying invader. I represented an outside force that, if I was being totally honest, would in all likelyhood destroy this world's life for greed.
It allowed me to take a step back and gain a new perspective on my existence. 'My' fight for survival, humanity's fight for survival, comes at a great cost. What right did I have to murder so many, just so I could continue on? In what way can I justify so many lives lost for my own? The same can be said for us as a whole. We slaughter our way through countless animals without a second thought. We do not visit new land, we destory it. We do not give to this world, we take from it.
It's an eye-opening experience in which everyone should partake. This game is no mere escape, it is a wake up call.
Scared and confused by my new outlook on life, I was in a daze. My only consolation whilst traversing this desolate virtual land... it never rained.

As a fan of the original titles, but a critic of their dated approach to graphics etc, I was very pleased to see that this latest edition to the X-Com series has been highly polished, from almost all angles.
The story is entertaining (albeit simplistic) and gameplay is challenging, even on easy. It requires complete concentration when making decisions for the X-Com alliance. This can lead to some frustrating moments if the wrong decisions are made, but adds a feeling of 'anything can happen' to each play-through.
Visuals and audio are very nice, and controlling your squad characters around the battlefield  is precise and easy. The interface is the only gripe, which was clearly designed for console systems. The game engine utilizes the Unreal engine nicely for the isometric viewpoint and brings excellent framerates, even to older systems.
All-in-all, an excellent addition to any game library, that'll bring (potentially) hundreds of hours of replayability.
Highly recommended!

The primary issue is, obviously, the terrible optimization. Even after the patches, the game was unplayable on my system and required a 270 Euros upgrade.
The other issues come from a strictly game design standpoint. There is too much reliance on the Batmobile. Over half of the game is wasted on either shooting tank drones or solving puzzles with the Batmobile. Free-Flow and Predator not only have taken a backseat, they also suffer on their own. Free flow breaks combos far more often than in City (though considerably less than in Origins) and the sheer variety of enemy types can turn combat into a cluster♥♥♥♥. Predator mode fares somewhat better, but the uninspired level design undercuts the flow of constant movement that made Predator work in previous installments.
If the draw for you is the fully-featured Gotham City, you'll be disappointed at how little there is to do in it. Outside of "liberating" the various areas (via taking down enemy outposts), it's a huge sandbox filled with criminals and empty boxes.
As for the story, it's heavily derivative of Nolan's Dark Knight Trilogy, the twists are woefully predictable and the characters are unsympathetic and internally inconsistent with the rest of the series.
If you enjoyed the previous games, you may want to have a look at this one eventually (during a sale, the Season Pass is a must as it offers the only classic Batman bits in this product), but otherwise steer clear.

Oh my God, where do I begin. Half-Life 2 is the master of all video games. The game is absolutely fantastic in every way possible, from the surroundings to the combat, and from its intuitivity to the beautiful graphic effects on water.
The combat feels perfect, and aiming is very precise despite the lack of down-sight aim. There is also a very wide range of weapons, as well a gravity gun and a crowbar. In addition, there is a very good variety of enemies, from combine soldiers to zombies with headcrabs.
In addition to great combat, the plot is immersive and fantastic and really outlines the great things that Gordon Freeman can
The graphics and mechanics are amazing for a game released in 2004, and really helped to advance 3D engines. The Source engine, the engine used in the game, is still used today and has been used in recent games such as Counter Strike Global Offensive and Portal 2. This is incredible when you consider the fact that the engine is a decade old. (That's around 10-15% of your life!) In addition to fantastic graphics, Half-Life 2 features advanced physics features from an engine called Havok, which was rigorously used in games throughout the late 2000s and even today.
Overall, Half-Life 2 is an absolutely amazing game with excellent replay value, so I am giving it a grade of A* with distinction.
Congrats Valve and I hope to eventually see number 3!

Played over 600 hours of Civ V and finally I believe I can give it a fair review.
So lets get the obvious out of the way is Civi V good ? Yes otherwise I wouldn´t have spent 600 hours in it and still booting it up now and then.
Civi V lacks nothing on graphics or gameplay, it is top of the line and there it is 100´s of mods for those who wishes to change their gameplay in anyway possible.
Civi V is not as detailed or brutally hard as the former games in this installment, however that is a great thing in my eyes as it gets a lot of new players to test out the series that the rest of us have enjoyed for so many years.
The DLC`s Gods & Kings and Brave New World adds a lot of the things we are use to from ealier series and is diffenetly worth getting for anyone who likes the more complex version of the Civ series, that beeing said the other DLC`s is mainly just new maps or new nations to play with and really only something you should pickup if you are a huge fan or on sale.
So Civ is as it always have been, you start with a settler and one more unit and here you go form a nation that will stand the test of time. There is multiple ways to achive victory and it is important that you play to your nations strenghts and use your enemies weaknesses through the different time periods of our planet. This is classic Civ after all.
Tho do not let it fool you, Civ is a game that takes a long time often 6+ hours pr map and often one nation is just gonna hate you more than anyone else, in my case it was Poland wich wanted to nuke and kill me no matter what, they did a good job sometimes too.
All in all a great game and a great installment of the Civ series that brings a lot of new players and a lot of life into the series, so if you like complex games that takes time and patience then make sure you pick it up!

I'm about 35 hours into this game, and I'm taking it slowly because I'm enjoying it so much. Others have been complaining about the game being "broken" (even after the rerelease), but that hasn't been my experience at all. My gametime has been almost entirely bug free, and the game is, in a word, awesome. The gameplay is fun, the graphics are great, the storyline is interesting and very dark, the side missions are plentiful and varied, and the Batmobile is pretty great.
About the Batmobile. I'll admit, I didn't like it at first. After 3 long games of gliding and grapneling through the world, I felt like I was suddenly being forced to drive around in a crappy car that I found difficult to control. "Battle mode", where the car becomes an ultra-maneuverable weapons platform, was better but I wasn't loving that, either. Pretty quickly though, I figured out 1) how to drive, 2) how to aim more efficiently in battle mode, 3) that most of the time you don't have to use the Batmobile if you don't want to. There's plenty of gliding and grapneling to be done. However, now that I've gotten a bit of practice with it, I sometimes find myself choosing the Batmobile when I don't have to use it.
It's tough to say much about the story without spoilers (and because I'm not through with it yet, right now I'm at about 65%), but there have been some surprises, some very dark moments, and some great mysteries.
Gameplay is very similar to the previous games, except for the addition of the new Batmobile. The interface has been cleaned up and refined, with some great improvements to the way you select gadgets and missions. Finally, chosing a bat-gadget feels slick and easy.
One last thing, if you've played the previous games, you'll find little touches here and there that you'll recognize as allusions to your past experiences. Many are subtle and go by quickly, but they're pretty awesome.
If you liked the previous Arkham games, you'll love this one.

XCOM for a new generation.
The music, cinematic cameras, and wonderful killshots all make combat very fun to play. The combat challenging but fair and much like the  original, people are going to die, a lot.
The lack of inventory management or economy fudging with manufacturing/selling is disappointing. Everything has been streamlined so the game is focused on combat and making broad decisions. The base building, although visually appealing, is lacks choices that matter. A singular base means no more specialized bases or strategic placements.
Those new to the franchise or genre in general will find this a very nice starting point. The game is simplistic enough to get into and just deep enough to hold interest to the end of the game. The story is very limited but a nice touch to give the player incentive to carry on.
In short, those seeking a new version of the original will be disappointed. Those seeking a solid turn-based strategy will find this very enjoyable.

Ok, there's a lot to cover on this game, but I'll just lay out the most glaring feature - it looks and feels exactly like you're part-taking in not just an episode, but in a whole interactive season of the show! The presentation is pitch perfect and all the characters are voiced by their original voice actors (mostly Trey Parker and Matt Stone). Perfect characters aside, the combat is another robust feature. It's easy to learn, but difficult to master; even if you've put hours in it. The story makes you feel both like an observer and a vital part of it at the same time, since you get to witness epic cutscenes and make crucial joices which influence the unfolding of the story. The humor, however, is what takes the ovations from the crowd, but beware - only long time South Park fans will get all the nods and references to various episodes, as well as feel more closely bound to classic characters. It's crude, offensive, with poor taste sometimes, but that cynical attitude makes South Park stand out from the crowd of mainstream TV flicks.  All and all, the game would be perfect if it had been a little more appealing to the newcomer audience, but I urge you to at least watch some episodes before you buy it, prefferably from the newer seasons.

Pretty quickly though, I figured out 1) how to drive, 2) how to aim more efficiently in battle mode, 3) that most of the time you don't have to use the Batmobile if you don't want to. There's plenty of gliding and grapneling to be done. However, now that I've gotten a bit of practice with it, I sometimes find myself choosing the Batmobile when I don't have to use it.
It's tough to say much about the story without spoilers (and because I'm not through with it yet, right now I'm at about 65%), but there have been some surprises, some very dark moments, and some great mysteries.
Gameplay is very similar to the previous games, except for the addition of the new Batmobile. The interface has been cleaned up and refined, with some great improvements to the way you select gadgets and missions. Finally, chosing a bat-gadget feels slick and easy.
One last thing, if you've played the previous games, you'll find little touches here and there that you'll recognize as allusions to your past experiences. Many are subtle and go by quickly, but they're pretty awesome.
If you liked the previous Arkham games, you'll love this one.

Super Hexagon at first glance is a game that, well, is about Hexagons. It is much deeper than that. Much, much deeper.
First you must assess what a Hexagon is. A hexagon is a 216 sided shape made of whatever shapes are made of (probably energy and matter or something). A hexagon has no purpose in the world because it is not a animate object, it is rather inanimate actually.
You then must assess who YOU are. YOU are a triangle. A lonely triangle vs. the world. Vs. those pesky lines that want to crush you! Think of yourself as a microscopic organism running away from a massive microscopic organism and those lines are the suction of the massive microscopic organism trying to eat you. If you get pulled into the mouth, you lose. Funnily, the massive microscopic organism is a hexagon.. who is pretty super. As you get farther and farther away, he takes new shapes to try and trick you into falling into his suction thingies and he goes faster. Which in turn, makes you more likely to mess up.
The game is Hexagon (and multiple other shapes) vs. you. Running is your only option. Do you have what it takes to become the best at running away from things that want to eat you?
It also had good music and the game is actually pretty fun if you get past the fact that you're going to lose A LOT. If you have epilepsy,  stay far away from this game as it will light the neurons in your brain up faster than a virgin boy's phallus looking at a naked woman. It's got decent replayability and it is recommended you have a few friends to go along with you in your purchase because it makes challenging eachother quite fun.
I'd buy it if you like really challenging games and don't care to blow a few cents. Or a dollar.

This game has insane replay value and some of the best weapons in gaming. The concept is simple but executed near perfectly, making this one of the best games out there.
Killing Floor 2 (KF2) is a wave-based horde mode survival shooter where you and five others pick one of ten perks to stand against massive amounts of 'zeds'. Zeds come in a bunch of different flavors, there's small 'trash' zeds that are more distraction than anything, there's 'medium' zeds dotted inbetween who can back up trash and actually deal some damage, and there's 'big' zeds who you really don't want to touch unless there's at least three more men backing you up. The zeds all force teamwork and diverse perk teams.
The perks themselves all have their specialty. Usually they are proficient against one or two of three types of zed: trash, medium or big. The better a perk is against one type, the worse it typically is against the others. Perks do have unlockable skills that can change your perk's strengths and weaknesses slightly and the choice of weapons can also affect your proficiencies, but a perk focused on big zeds will always have trouble with trash hordes. These skills have to be unlocked though, by leveling up, and the game is designed to make that take a damned long time. You need some 50 hours just to max out one perk, I currently have over 200 hours clocked and I only have three perks maxed. Progress can feel slow, but this does make sure that you'll have fun leveling for at least 500 hours.
Difficulty is also a big part of the game. Killing floor has four different difficulty settings so you can have a challenge at every perk level. It's third difficulty is already challenging even when you have maxed out perks and the final difficulty offers a challenge that requires solid teamwork as well as individual skill. After 200 hours I'm still trying to beat the rest of the maps on suicidal, the second hardest mode. Personally I haven't touched the hardest yet. You won't have to repeat levels you already beat until you are already really deep in, so don't worry about repetitiveness.
The weapons in this game are the main mechanic, just shooting zeds. That's nothing new or interesting so the devs are forced to rely on exceptional quality if they want players coming back. Luckily they understood this, and weapons have exquisite animations, sound design and feedback. Shooting zeds with some of the heavier weapons will tear them apart and send what's left flying halfway across the room. There is not a game in existence that offers this kind of kick behind a weapon, and that is the main reason this game works. Popping those headshots or throwing a grenade in a crowd will *NEVER* stop being fun. This game would be decent without it, the gameplay is solid enough, but the magnificent weapon design is truly what sets this apart from other games in the genre. I promise you that you will keep coming back to shred more zeds.
The game seemed to be stuck in early access purgatory for a long time, but it has since been released and has already seen two content updates. I was fearing for the support for this game when early access wasn't going anywhere, but so far the developers have been pretty quick with more content. I can only hope that stays this way, but with Tripwire promising seasonal events I'm optimistic. This game currently relies on cosmetics to keep revenue and future content going, since I'm a big fan of this model where content is always free and supported by people who choose to spend, I always make sure to open a box or two with a content update. The drops are usually♥♥♥♥♥♥ but I do it more to support further content updates. Besides, the cosmetic system is actually pretty fun. I like customizing my character and looking awesome, it's honestly a large part of what kept me in TF2 for thousands of hours. I'm hoping KF2 can keep me as involved by taunting me with new fashion items.
This game is also *very* open to mods and custom maps, if you're ever bored you can always try some of the insane♥♥♥♥♥♥people mod into this game. They're pretty creative. Devs also implement community maps and cosmetics into the game, creating a large community of content creators. Also a smart move on Tripwire's side since this will keep content flowing even when the devs are slacking.
In summary I think this game is destined for greatness. It has all the properties a game needs to stand the test of time. I think I will be playing this for years to come, and that is truly exceptional. For 30 dollars I don't think anyone can regret buying this game, to me this is one of those essential videogames, a leader of the genre, and you should own it.

Played over 600 hours of Civ V and finally I believe I can give it a fair review.
So lets get the obvious out of the way is Civi V good ? Yes otherwise I wouldn´t have spent 600 hours in it and still booting it up now and then.
Civi V lacks nothing on graphics or gameplay, it is top of the line and there it is 100´s of mods for those who wishes to change their gameplay in anyway possible.
Civi V is not as detailed or brutally hard as the former games in this installment, however that is a great thing in my eyes as it gets a lot of new players to test out the series that the rest of us have enjoyed for so many years.
The DLC`s Gods & Kings and Brave New World adds a lot of the things we are use to from ealier series and is diffenetly worth getting for anyone who likes the more complex version of the Civ series, that beeing said the other DLC`s is mainly just new maps or new nations to play with and really only something you should pickup if you are a huge fan or on sale.
So Civ is as it always have been, you start with a settler and one more unit and here you go form a nation that will stand the test of time. There is multiple ways to achive victory and it is important that you play to your nations strenghts and use your enemies weaknesses through the different time periods of our planet. This is classic Civ after all.
Tho do not let it fool you, Civ is a game that takes a long time often 6+ hours pr map and often one nation is just gonna hate you more than anyone else, in my case it was Poland wich wanted to nuke and kill me no matter what, they did a good job sometimes too.
All in all a great game and a great installment of the Civ series that brings a lot of new players and a lot of life into the series, so if you like complex games that takes time and patience then make sure you pick it up!

Ok, there's a lot to cover on this game, but I'll just lay out the most glaring feature - it looks and feels exactly like you're part-taking in not just an episode, but in a whole interactive season of the show! The story makes you feel both like an observer and a vital part of it at the same time, since you get to witness epic cutscenes and make crucial joices which influence the unfolding of the story. The humor, however, is what takes the ovations from the crowd, but beware - only long time South Park fans will get all the nods and references to various episodes, as well as feel more closely bound to classic characters. It's crude, offensive, with poor taste sometimes, but that cynical attitude makes South Park stand out from the crowd of mainstream TV flicks.  All and all, the game would be perfect if it had been a little more appealing to the newcomer audience, but I urge you to at least watch some episodes before you buy it, prefferably from the newer seasons.
