This game has insane replay value and some of the best weapons in gaming. The concept is simple but executed near perfectly, making this one of the best games out there.
Killing Floor 2 (KF2) is a wave-based horde mode survival shooter where you and five others pick one of ten perks to stand against massive amounts of 'zeds'. Zeds come in a bunch of different flavors, there's small 'trash' zeds that are more distraction than anything, there's 'medium' zeds dotted inbetween who can back up trash and actually deal some damage, and there's 'big' zeds who you really don't want to touch unless there's at least three more men backing you up. The zeds all force teamwork and diverse perk teams.
The perks themselves all have their specialty. Usually they are proficient against one or two of three types of zed: trash, medium or big. The better a perk is against one type, the worse it typically is against the others. Perks do have unlockable skills that can change your perk's strengths and weaknesses slightly and the choice of weapons can also affect your proficiencies, but a perk focused on big zeds will always have trouble with trash hordes. These skills have to be unlocked though, by leveling up, and the game is designed to make that take a damned long time. You need some 50 hours just to max out one perk, I currently have over 200 hours clocked and I only have three perks maxed. Progress can feel slow, but this does make sure that you'll have fun leveling for at least 500 hours.
Difficulty is also a big part of the game. Killing floor has four different difficulty settings so you can have a challenge at every perk level. It's third difficulty is already challenging even when you have maxed out perks and the final difficulty offers a challenge that requires solid teamwork as well as individual skill. After 200 hours I'm still trying to beat the rest of the maps on suicidal, the second hardest mode. Personally I haven't touched the hardest yet. You won't have to repeat levels you already beat until you are already really deep in, so don't worry about repetitiveness.
The weapons in this game are the main mechanic, just shooting zeds. That's nothing new or interesting so the devs are forced to rely on exceptional quality if they want players coming back. Luckily they understood this, and weapons have exquisite animations, sound design and feedback. Shooting zeds with some of the heavier weapons will tear them apart and send what's left flying halfway across the room. There is not a game in existence that offers this kind of kick behind a weapon, and that is the main reason this game works. Popping those headshots or throwing a grenade in a crowd will *NEVER* stop being fun. This game would be decent without it, the gameplay is solid enough, but the magnificent weapon design is truly what sets this apart from other games in the genre. I promise you that you will keep coming back to shred more zeds.
The game seemed to be stuck in early access purgatory for a long time, but it has since been released and has already seen two content updates. I was fearing for the support for this game when early access wasn't going anywhere, but so far the developers have been pretty quick with more content. I can only hope that stays this way, but with Tripwire promising seasonal events I'm optimistic. This game currently relies on cosmetics to keep revenue and future content going, since I'm a big fan of this model where content is always free and supported by people who choose to spend, I always make sure to open a box or two with a content update. The drops are usually♥♥♥♥♥♥ but I do it more to support further content updates. Besides, the cosmetic system is actually pretty fun. I like customizing my character and looking awesome, it's honestly a large part of what kept me in TF2 for thousands of hours. I'm hoping KF2 can keep me as involved by taunting me with new fashion items.
This game is also *very* open to mods and custom maps, if you're ever bored you can always try some of the insane♥♥♥♥♥♥people mod into this game. They're pretty creative. Devs also implement community maps and cosmetics into the game, creating a large community of content creators. Also a smart move on Tripwire's side since this will keep content flowing even when the devs are slacking.
In summary I think this game is destined for greatness. It has all the properties a game needs to stand the test of time. I think I will be playing this for years to come, and that is truly exceptional. For 30 dollars I don't think anyone can regret buying this game, to me this is one of those essential videogames, a leader of the genre, and you should own it.

This game, man.  It's something else.  This is my first review, so if it's not that great, then blame my lackluster reviewing skills.  Just a quick note, I got the game from Amazon around early March, so I had the game before its Bahraini release date of April 8.
TL;DR: South Park: The Stick of Truth is a solid RPG that's like an interactive episode of South Park.  However, the game too easy, too short, and the menus are too bland.
For those of you who want to read my full thoughts:
In the turn of the 21st century (1999-2000s), three South Park games were released, and they all sucked.  But in 2009 and 2011 (if my memory serves me right), a tower defense and a platform game, respectively, were released, and they were alright.  But the thing that these five games have in common is that they didn't truly shine as a South Park game.  South Park: The Stick of Truth (which we will refer to as The Stick of Truth) changes all of this.
The Stick of Truth is full of South Park references, from Mr. Hankey, to Timmy and the Lords of the Underworld, to even the South Park film from 1999.  This game is so authentic, you won't even know it's the game if somebody didn't tell you.  It looks exactly like the show, and it's pretty much an interactive 14-hour South Park episode.  The will make you laugh and chuckle quite a lot if you watch the show.  If you hate full-force crude humor, then this game isn't for you.
If you didn't know already, The Stick of Truth is a turn-based RPG.  With the previous South Park games, you may expect combat to be light, but it's actually pretty deep (not super deep though, just done pretty well).  As with all turn-based RPGs, you and your enemy (obviously) take turns attacking each other.   The gameplay is in the style of "Paper Mario" and "Mario & Luigi," as you time your attacks to do more damage and initiate more attacks.  Combat also has armor (reduces damage taken by armor number; minimum damage being 1), shields (1 shield=1 hit doing no damage), status effects, different stances (blocks melee or ranged attacks), etc.  The game even pokes fun at this in the tutorial.  It's a pretty solid RPG.
However, the game isn't without it's flaws.  For one, the default difficulty is too easy.  I found this out on my first playthough, so I put it to the hardest difficulty.  Also, for $60, the game is a tad too short to be $60.  Maybe $30 would be rightful.  Finally, the menus feel a little bland.  I understand is supposed to be a parody of Facebook, but, it's just SO bland.

This is my favourite game of all time. There is actual pacing to the gameplay and story. It's not like a Michael Bay film - an abstract expressionist painting with explosions. It's been almost 14 years at this point and the facial animations and gesticulation still hold up amazingly. The characters don't awkwardly pivot on their feet to face you. The characters end up seeming so natural and real. Alyx is possibly the greatest sidekick I've ever encountered in a game. She's not annoying, doesn't get in the way and her being around never feels like an escort quest. The world is involving too. The setting feels like it's fallen out of a brilliant work of dystopian fiction. The story is there, but if you pay attention to the surroundings you can get a lot just from contextual clues. It's a 14 year-old game but it's well worth your money.

Do you like games that offer a hand to help you up when you fall down, then once you are up, proceed to beat the living crap out of you and make fun of you when you fall down, to only repeat the process?  Are you masochistic enough to take the hand again because you want to beat the game by being able to stand up at what it throws at you?
If you answered yes to these questions, A. You might need some therepy, B. Get this game.  This game does not hold any bars when it comes to proving that you are pathetic at their game, but the thrill comes when you progress enough to be able to deal with what the game has to throw at you.
It has an awesome soundtrack, minimalistic graphics that really work for what the game is, and is an action platformer.
There is a lot of progression in the game, as you try to unlock all of the characters, which are not neccisarily better than the last (Though there are some that are better than others) but have different playstyles.  There are logs that gives a background of the monsters you fight through the eyes of your character if you are into replayability. This game, man.  It's something else.  This is my first review, so if it's not that great, then blame my lackluster reviewing skills.  Just a quick note, I got the game from Amazon around early March, so I had the game before its Bahraini release date of April 8.
TL;DR: South Park: The Stick of Truth is a solid RPG that's like an interactive episode of South Park.  However, the game too easy, too short, and the menus are too bland.
For those of you who want to read my full thoughts:
In the turn of the 21st century (1999-2000s), three South Park games were released, and they all sucked.  But in 2009 and 2011 (if my memory serves me right), a tower defense and a platform game, respectively, were released, and they were alright.  But the thing that these five games have in common is that they didn't truly shine as a South Park game.  South Park: The Stick of Truth (which we will refer to as The Stick of Truth) changes all of this.
The Stick of Truth is full of South Park references, from Mr. Hankey, to Timmy and the Lords of the Underworld, to even the South Park film from 1999.  This game is so authentic, you won't even know it's the game if somebody didn't tell you.  It looks exactly like the show, and it's pretty much an interactive 14-hour South Park episode.  The will make you laugh and chuckle quite a lot if you watch the show.  If you hate full-force crude humor, then this game isn't for you.
If you didn't know already, The Stick of Truth is a turn-based RPG.  With the previous South Park games, you may expect combat to be light, but it's actually pretty deep (not super deep though, just done pretty well).  As with all turn-based RPGs, you and your enemy (obviously) take turns attacking each other.   The gameplay is in the style of "Paper Mario" and "Mario & Luigi," as you time your attacks to do more damage and initiate more attacks.  Combat also has armor (reduces damage taken by armor number; minimum damage being 1), shields (1 shield=1 hit doing no damage), status effects, different stances (blocks melee or ranged attacks), etc.  The game even pokes fun at this in the tutorial.  It's a pretty solid RPG.
However, the game isn't without it's flaws.  For one, the default difficulty is too easy.  I found this out on my first playthough, so I put it to the hardest difficulty.  Also, for $60, the game is a tad too short to be $60.  Maybe $30 would be rightful.  Finally, the menus feel a little bland.  I understand is supposed to be a parody of Facebook, but, it's just SO bland.
Green light community take note, this is how early access should be done. If you like co-op games and shooting things in the face then this is the game for you.

I have played KF games for a long time. I was excited about KF 2, I bought it around a year ago when it came out.
* This review includes new content patch that is PVP zombies. *
Intro aside, is the game good? Short story it's ok. It feels like KF 1,5 rather than something new. Before you get on rage wagon let me explain.
- Same enemies ( albeit this time around higher difficulties add extra attack/moves that enemies can use )
- Music ( in my opinion ) is horrible. I had to turn it right down because its distracting especially if you are using Voice Chat with friends and need to coordinate. This is especially true in PvP mode that requires sticking together and killing big threats.
- Maps, they feel a smaller compared to first KF but at the same time they are well designed and look good.
- Perks system... Come on guys! It's boring as hell. No active skills only passives. Number + Number = Damage. Seriously, I would prefer to have a choice with a berserker to go full attack dual wielding sacrificing defense but the game doesn't give me the option. There are perk skill that let you play using parries or blocks but it's not worth it. When you get surrouned and trust me you will, the only thing you can do is to keep on swinging. You can block enemies in the front but those on the sides and back will get you.
- Horrible weapon choice for perks. Seriously No Sword n Shield for Zerk? No chainsaw this time around. Just katana, sledgehammer, nailgun and pulverizer ( which is a hybrid long range weapon/melee ). Not many weapons after a 1 year in EA. Not much variety, it boils down to keep on swinging, Aim for the head for to stumble... really repetetive and boring. Therefore would like to see Halberds for longer range attacks or Active skills for berserker JUST anything to allow players to have their own playstyle.
- No listen servers yet.
- Weird decision with cash shop. Sometimes you get a box containing loot. You need to buy a key for 2.5 Dollars to unlock it. Then you get a random item from a list... Fricking HATE lotteries. Just have a damn shop so I can buy what I want for 2,5 Dollars rather than dunking 10 dollars and getting junk I DONT NEED OR WANT! You greedy basturds ! Fricking hate lotteries....
- PvP is way unbalanced. You can get players with low perks like 4-5 lvl and then people with level 25. Heck you can get 6 ppl with level 25 and you will still loose. You see I can take down a red zed with a claymore with one hit with my Zerg. BUT if player controls red zerg then suddenly that player has more hp than normal zed. NOT only that but they have unlimited sprinting! so they can RUN n ATTACK at the same time. Not only you have no chance to escape them because survivors will run out of stamina when sprinting, thusly Zeds will keep attacking you in the back but they have more health and RESPAWN almost immediately. YOUR ONLY CHANCE of survivor is to STICK together and attack. No tactics. Currently this mode is WAY unbalanced. I felt sorry for surviors when I played as a ZED.
- There are also some small things like re-used characters or guns ( they added crossbow and lever gun WHY?! It's useless ) voice commands are not as funny as in the original KF. Still not many mods yet released but that I hope will change.
So what you get is prettier version of original KF with some updated gameplay mechanics but less content. I cant recommend it just yet. Maybe in a years time, seeing how slowly the updates are coming.I didnt ask for PvP... I wanted new perks, active skills GUNS and melee weapons to create my own gameplay style.

I don't always play FPS games, but when I do, I play Half-Life.
This was the game that introduced me to Valve games back in 2004 and like its predecessor, it's one of the few FPS games that I have enjoyed to play even to this day. Though, to talk about Half-Life 2 is more than talking about just a game. Its influence upon the gaming industry has made Valve one of its leading developers and have for a long time been the measuring stick for what's considered a good FPS game. Valve earned my respect from this game alone and is the very reason I even started using Steam in the first place.
What else is there to say about this game? Its mechanics; very well designed and innovative for its time. Its story; a well paced, thrilling experience through landscapes and cities/towns with visuals that still hold up to this day. Its engine; a technological marvel that have brought us 10 years' worth of Valve games as well as an excellent modding community. Its legacy; one that will continue to echo for years to come.
If you haven't played Half-Life 2 or the first game when reading this, then I have to ask, why are you reading this? Go play them now and see for yourself why this series has got the praise it has.

Just to provide context, I have never played Killing Floor 1. I picked up Killing Floor 2 very early on when it was made early access, and liked it from the get go. It has a very casual, fun approach that doesn't require endless grinding. You get tangible benefits from leveling up, but I never felt like I was holding my team back during the early levels. The music is fun, the guns feel meaty and loud, there is neat variety to the weapons and the classes feel very different in their approach. The maps are also varied and require adjusting your play style to compensate for each ones quirks.
There isn't much to say negative about KF2, it isn't a game I'd sit down for eight hours and marathon, but there aren't any L4Deadalikes I would. KF2 currently seems on target to expand the options, but if no weapons or classes or new enemies were added after today I'd probably feel a little let down with the final product. I also hope to see some new options that expand what classes can DO beyond static bonuses, a few small buffs, and weapon selection.
There is a microtransaction/crate system that I have never touched (beyond selling 99% of the stuff I pick up on the marketplace) please note that if its inclusion would scare you away, don't let it! It is all purely cosmetic stuff with zero impact on gameplay.
I absolutely recommend the game for anyone looking for something you can play in quick, fun little spurts and never feel left out or threatened by the competitive metagame.

As for the South Park, and Paper Mario fan I am, I have had alot of fun playing this game. Surely it's not the lengthiest RPG (with a barely 15 hour long gameplay time), and while the combat is rather tame with the lack of depth, balance and variety, as some spells or attacks are more ineffective than others, while you'll find some devastating attacks which will prevent you from varying the way you play, but for it's short storymode it should keep you entertained until you've played through all the sidequests and the main story.
As for a South Park game, it truly feels like you're watching an actual South Park episode, or even a whole season, at the same time while playing.
Also, important mention is how the game plays alot like Paper Mario, with ''active turnbased combat'', by which I mean every move you perform requires you to either tap a button, or time a button pressing in order to successfully perform an action.
The game also has partners, which all have their own unique abillities and spells, like such as Butters's Professor Chaos transformation (which by the way, is my favourite pick).
However, if you have no interest for South Park, or even have a certain disgust for it, you won't be missing out at all if you're not going to buy it. A must have for a South Park fan however.

Risk of Rain is a 2D, sidescrolling, rogue-like, shoot 'em up utilizing over a hundred items, 8 characters and a wide and varied array of skills and abilities. Combat is fast paced but strategic and every second counts as the difficulty is constantly increasing from the second you start a game. Multiplayer is either online or hotseat. The only downside to hotseat gameplay is that you all share the same game window meaning that your mobility is limited and because of the large amount of info that must be displayed on one screen items and other stats that are normally displayed in one player aren't during hotseat multiplayer. It's manageable but annoying. Other than this one downside, however, the game shines and is a fantastic, relatively cheap experience that has hours of potential gameplay and huge replayability. Highly recommended for single and multiplayer experiences. But beware, as the game's difficulty is extremely high even on the easiest of settings. It will take new players a little while to get used to it. Enjoy.

This game is great. I highly recommend it.
The game is highly replayable. 10 very unique classes each have their own playstyles, and getting good at everyone will take a while. however, some classes are more/less useful than the others.  For instance. The huntress is currently "the best" class because she is the only one who can attack and move simultaneously. and the sniper, who's good on paper, but struggles compared to everyone else.
the graphics are decent, but nothing to shout about.
The random aspect of the game keeps everything interesting and stops it getting repetitive. The game isn't truly random, but it's random enough to stop it becoming a guessing game, while still keeping everything fresh. The large amount of items, each of which unique, are also randomly obtained, so it makes each item memorable. Like one making all your attacks explode, and one making time stop for a couple of seconds when you're close to dying. The artifact system they also added adds more to the game, making it easier, harder, or less random. It's mostly for hardcore players who've played a ton of the game.
Plot:VERY little plot. Of what there is, it's "you are stuck on this planet, Survive and get out". And then there's the idea of you actually being the bad guy. No more because spoilers. Lore can be obtained through monster logs which randomly drop from enemies rarely. and through the "item logs". that you get when picking up new items.
Soundtrack: Very good, the soundtrack is actually within the steam folder so if you buy it you can listen to it!
Multiplayer: I've hardly played multiplayer, but from what i've heard, it works, but doesn't work well. With some supposedly bad netcode and lots of bugs. But don't let that deter you. The game is a ton of fun with friends
Complaints: The final teleporter has two options. Go to first level, or go to final level. hard to explain, but the way you choose this really bugs me. Just a minor thing. Some people report very bad performance in this game, despite having great rigs. some characters less useful. Some achievements are ridiculous, like reaching the 3rd teleporter without taking damage.
Conclusion: This game is great. there's a demo out there you can try if you want. If you have lots of friends to play with, it is more fun. It's worth the price, even more so on a sale.

UPDATE: As of official game launch and Survivalist release: New enemy tactics such as blocking and evading, some have new abilities, and changes to behavior as well as player icons so you can see where teammates are as well as the last ~3 zeds of the wave so you can find out if it's despawning constantly or a teammate is kiting it around to troll the team. Team trolling is still out of control for some with the vote kick being abused on public servers.
It's faster paced than the previous title with a few tweaks to how zeds attack you.
Pros:
-More head bob as well as full body movement on a few zeds
-No more secondary perk locked exp requirements. Perks now only gain a small bonus exp for doing those things.
-You don't have to fight over exp as much compared to KF1. You only need to tag a zed to get exp so even if they are decapitated by a teammate. But exp is tied to perk weapons just like KF1 except for Survivalist where they can use any weapon to gain exp. EG: Berserkers using a magnum or deagle for crawlers will only get exp for gunslinger perk for those kills unless you had melee'd them somewhere before they die, then the exp will be split among them.
-On top of perk bonuses, you get to choose an ability every 5 levels from 5-20. On a few classes, they're kind of useless though.
-All classes spawn with a base weapon for their perk so you don't have to run around with just a pistol and knife.
-Combined chainsaw with buzzsaw crossbow for berserkers.
-Two different bosses to fight. They also take different amounts of damage depending on where you hit them: body/core, head, arms, and legs and what type of damage
-Zeds can still fight each other although it doesn't happen as much it did in KF.
-Gun butting/stab/thrust depending on what weapon you're holding at the moment so you can escape a clot's grasp when your gun runs out of rounds between mags, bash the head, to stumble a zed and get 1-2 seconds of breathing room or to save a teammate.
-Sprinting.
-Parry and block, all classes can only do this with a melee weapon (Eviscerator will allow you to block too).
-Different grenades for classes.
Cons
-Long start up time and depending on your computer, load in time too.
-The knock down and stumbling have a cooldown still but they need to be built up to trigger now.
-FPs rage function changed, they will rage after a certain time has gone by even if you're out of vision.
-Leveling up does not grant discounts of on-perk weapons.
-Kiting around the map does not work anymore up to a point, mobs will "teleport/respawn" behind the closest corner if they can not see you, the team, or the team does not have vision of them minus stalker and Patriarch cloak.
-Firebug burn no longer applies a -movement% to crisped zeds
-Invisible walls still exist; only certain cars, boxes, rocks, and rails can be jumped on/over.
-Background noise/music that isn't part of the music you can shut off. Atleast two maps has zeds in the background that will make noise so it might make things a little difficult for people that like to depend on hearing to play if they choose to hold out in those areas.
-You can no longer outrun the bosses forever, they will catch up eventually even on perks with increased movement speed.

Arkham Knight... a game that I had the most supported review of mine ever (96% useful, out of ~100 votes) for, and it was a wall of pure hate text about going into detail on how messed up, absolutely unplayable piece of sh*t it was, how Warner and their incompetent PC porting team Iron Galaxy tried to fix it, then when realized how bad the situation is just shove it under the rug like they did with Mortal Kombat X scandal, but given the size of the Batman franchise they had to deal with the problem despite their desperete try to buy people off by giving away free other games for those we bought this game. Things have gotten so bad they had to pull back every copy from every store wordwide not to get sued over selling faulty product, and that's where they know they are in deep♥♥♥♥♥♥ So yet again, they gave the project to another small team (back to Rocksteady's PC department), who through several patches, actually fixed up the game to the point where it was still unplayable to most, but at least ran nice to many.
2 years have passed since, and people can afford bruteforcing through the badly optimized game's hardware requirement more easily (I did with a GTX1060), so I picked it up again. Needless to say I ran it on absolute maxed out settings with all NVidia GameWorks features on, and I managed to get a stable 60 fps out if it - no thanks to the optimization, that's for sure, so unless you got the hardware to bruteforce through the game that shouldn't need as strong resources as it demands, nothing changed for you, avoid this game like plague.
So, how is the game itself? Besides being stunningly beautiful, and offering another Gotham to fly around in. It's actually fantastic. I wish everyone could have had this experience 2 years ago, I had with it in the recent days.
The story is great. For the first time (besides Arkham City's ending) there is real, heavy weight to the story. People die, permanent and long known characters die, and the enemy actually feels real, threatending and terrorizing both the body (Gotham itself) and the mind (the player / Bruce's character), causing everlasting damage in an epic conclusion of the Batman's history that no longer has a reset button at the end, with everyone being in jail and breaking out for the next game. There is no next game, no next time, and things really matter and get really ugly.
What I liked the most is the brutality of Batman: there is no playing around anymore. Gotham is in flames, there is a literal war going on with tanks, helicopters, drones, a massive army, biological terrorist attacks. Sure, in small text somewhere in the diaries it's explained how Batman's car (a tank more like) uses nonlethal bullets, but c'mon - using water to electrify thugs from a 20kV transformator isn't only guranteed death, it's burning to your bones in a glimpse of an eye so don't tell me Batman doesn't kill anyone. I can ram with my tank to a huge crowd of thugs with at least 100km/h speed and send them flying, of course game tells you "the tank's surface electroshocks them and it's non-lethal", but c'mon, you just rammed a human body with a tank, or shot one with a literal tank cannon. Or literally exploded the car with a rocket launcher that crashed and flew through half the street into a wall (man those carchases are the best). Don't tell me hundreds of tank, helicopters and quad-rotor air combat vehicles are unmanned, remote piloted, each and every one of them. The game tries to make excuses (thankfully not pushed to the player's face so you can work with the brutality version), but it's impossible that Batman isn't committing Ben Affleck style mass murder here. And I love it, it really is the endgame for the Arkham Universe, and feels that way.
The gameplay? Well, 1:1 the same as Arkham City and Origins, you know those, you know this. The batmobile is a fantastic addition (though overused), the Riddler is now more tiresome and boring / annoying than ever, the sidemissions and the general sandbox going around are great, easily the best in all the Arkham series. The ending was kind of lame though, not too satisfying (and the secret ending, locked behind grinding over 230 riddler challanges and completiving everything in the game to the last collectible) is while better, it's still not too satisfying and raises more questions than delivers satisfactory endings - Rocksteady went with the unexplained mindf*ck way here - I have a theory, people have theories, but that's it really, there is no genius puzzle that would blow your mind about it.
+ Easily the best Arkham game in the series.
+ Brutal mass murder Ben Affleck Batman with the Batmobile
+ Story that really matters and ends the Batman franchise. Civilians die on a large scale, important characters die, important character profiles change and turn on their used to be allies, finally a story that doesn't feels like "everyone safely goes home at the end of the day and we start over tomorrow".
- The whole relase scandal and how Warner handled the situation.
- It is still extremely hardware demanding, and even if I overkilled it with a GPU upgrade 2 years after it's relase, still makes my HDD work brutally hard at times for no reason (for a long time I assumed it's background loading but happens even after 5-6 hours of playing).
- The ending is not satisfying at all, I want to see things happen that I know happens, just not shown.
- There is no way to cheaply upgrade to the premium edition if you are an early owner of the game, and the season pass is far more expensive than the base game + season pass (which is the premium edition), yet I still have to pay for the base game if I want to upgrade by buying the premium edition to get the DLC content.

Arkham Knight... a game that I had the most supported review of mine ever (96% useful, out of ~100 votes) for, and it was a wall of pure hate text about going into detail on how messed up, absolutely unplayable piece of sh*t it was, how Warner and their incompetent PC porting team Iron Galaxy tried to fix it, then when realized how bad the situation is just shove it under the rug like they did with Mortal Kombat X scandal, but given the size of the Batman franchise they had to deal with the problem despite their desperete try to buy people off by giving away free other games for those we bought this game. Things have gotten so bad they had to pull back every copy from every store wordwide not to get sued over selling faulty product, and that's where they know they are in deep♥♥♥♥♥♥ So yet again, they gave the project to another small team (back to Rocksteady's PC department), who through several patches, actually fixed up the game to the point where it was still unplayable to most, but at least ran nice to many.
2 years have passed since, and people can afford bruteforcing through the badly optimized game's hardware requirement more easily (I did with a GTX1060), so I picked it up again. Needless to say I ran it on absolute maxed out settings with all NVidia GameWorks features on, and I managed to get a stable 60 fps out if it - no thanks to the optimization, that's for sure, so unless you got the hardware to bruteforce through the game that shouldn't need as strong resources as it demands, nothing changed for you, avoid this game like plague.
So, how is the game itself? Besides being stunningly beautiful, and offering another Gotham to fly around in. It's actually fantastic. I wish everyone could have had this experience 2 years ago, I had with it in the recent days.
The story is great. For the first time (besides Arkham City's ending) there is real, heavy weight to the story. People die, permanent and long known characters die, and the enemy actually feels real, threatending and terrorizing both the body (Gotham itself) and the mind (the player / Bruce's character), causing everlasting damage in an epic conclusion of the Batman's history that no longer has a reset button at the end, with everyone being in jail and breaking out for the next game. There is no next game, no next time, and things really matter and get really ugly.
What I liked the most is the brutality of Batman: there is no playing around anymore. Gotham is in flames, there is a literal war going on with tanks, helicopters, drones, a massive army, biological terrorist attacks. Sure, in small text somewhere in the diaries it's explained how Batman's car (a tank more like) uses nonlethal bullets, but c'mon - using water to electrify thugs from a 20kV transformator isn't only guranteed death, it's burning to your bones in a glimpse of an eye so don't tell me Batman doesn't kill anyone. I can ram with my tank to a huge crowd of thugs with at least 100km/h speed and send them flying, of course game tells you "the tank's surface electroshocks them and it's non-lethal", but c'mon, you just rammed a human body with a tank, or shot one with a literal tank cannon. Or literally exploded the car with a rocket launcher that crashed and flew through half the street into a wall (man those carchases are the best). Don't tell me hundreds of tank, helicopters and quad-rotor air combat vehicles are unmanned, remote piloted, each and every one of them. The game tries to make excuses (thankfully not pushed to the player's face so you can work with the brutality version), but it's impossible that Batman isn't committing Ben Affleck style mass murder here. And I love it, it really is the endgame for the Arkham Universe, and feels that way.
The gameplay? Well, 1:1 the same as Arkham City and Origins, you know those, you know this. The batmobile is a fantastic addition (though overused), the Riddler is now more tiresome and boring / annoying than ever, the sidemissions and the general sandbox going around are great, easily the best in all the Arkham series. The ending was kind of lame though, not too satisfying (and the secret ending, locked behind grinding over 230 riddler challanges and completiving everything in the game to the last collectible) is while better, it's still not too satisfying and raises more questions than delivers satisfactory endings - Rocksteady went with the unexplained mindf*ck way here - I have a theory, people have theories, but that's it really, there is no genius puzzle that would blow your mind about it.
+ Easily the best Arkham game in the series.
+ Brutal mass murder Ben Affleck Batman with the Batmobile
+ Story that really matters and ends the Batman franchise. Civilians die on a large scale, important characters die, important character profiles change and turn on their used to be allies, finally a story that doesn't feels like "everyone safely goes home at the end of the day and we start over tomorrow".
- The whole relase scandal and how Warner handled the situation.
- It is still extremely hardware demanding, and even if I overkilled it with a GPU upgrade 2 years after it's relase, still makes my HDD work brutally hard at times for no reason (for a long time I assumed it's background loading but happens even after 5-6 hours of playing).
- The ending is not satisfying at all, I want to see things happen that I know happens, just not shown.
- There is no way to cheaply upgrade to the premium edition if you are an early owner of the game, and the season pass is far more expensive than the base game + season pass (which is the premium edition), yet I still have to pay for the base game if I want to upgrade by buying the premium edition to get the DLC content.

Risk of Rain, for its price, is a great game to play for a short time and forget about later. Its visuals are appealing, the mechanics feel right, and the variety of characters, abilities, and power-ups help its replay value.
I'm not a fan of the difficulty-altering mechanic, however. You've given the impression that you can choose your playstyle: speed through each level as fast as possible to beat the difficulty creep, or seek out each treasure chest and budget your earnings effectively to utilize what power-ups are given to you. However, there's no chance of surviving if you choose to take your sweet time anywhere in this game.
Also, you'll find that local, same-screen multiplayer to be a much bigger pain than online co-op. Local involves sharing the same screen, which really inhibits your ability to spread out and find chests and level exits, which is the entire goal of the game.
Despite its faults, it's good fun for about a week with a friend.

-You don't have to fight over exp as much compared to KF1. You only need to tag a zed to get exp so even if they are decapitated by a teammate. But exp is tied to perk weapons just like KF1 except for Survivalist where they can use any weapon to gain exp. EG: Berserkers using a magnum or deagle for crawlers will only get exp for gunslinger perk for those kills unless you had melee'd them somewhere before they die, then the exp will be split among them.
-On top of perk bonuses, you get to choose an ability every 5 levels from 5-20. On a few classes, they're kind of useless though.
-All classes spawn with a base weapon for their perk so you don't have to run around with just a pistol and knife.
-Combined chainsaw with buzzsaw crossbow for berserkers.
-Two different bosses to fight. They also take different amounts of damage depending on where you hit them: body/core, head, arms, and legs and what type of damage
-Zeds can still fight each other although it doesn't happen as much it did in KF.
-Gun butting/stab/thrust depending on what weapon you're holding at the moment so you can escape a clot's grasp when your gun runs out of rounds between mags, bash the head, to stumble a zed and get 1-2 seconds of breathing room or to save a teammate.
-Sprinting.
-Parry and block, all classes can only do this with a melee weapon (Eviscerator will allow you to block too).
-Different grenades for classes.
Cons
-Long start up time and depending on your computer, load in time too.
-The knock down and stumbling have a cooldown still but they need to be built up to trigger now.
-FPs rage function changed, they will rage after a certain time has gone by even if you're out of vision.
-Leveling up does not grant discounts of on-perk weapons.
-Kiting around the map does not work anymore up to a point, mobs will "teleport/respawn" behind the closest corner if they can not see you, the team, or the team does not have vision of them minus stalker and Patriarch cloak.
-Firebug burn no longer applies a -movement% to crisped zeds
-Invisible walls still exist; only certain cars, boxes, rocks, and rails can be jumped on/over.
-Background noise/music that isn't part of the music you can shut off. Atleast two maps has zeds in the background that will make noise so it might make things a little difficult for people that like to depend on hearing to play if they choose to hold out in those areas.
-You can no longer outrun the bosses forever, they will catch up eventually even on perks with increased movement speed.

Genre: Action, Indie, Platformer, RPG
Publisher: Chucklefish
Release Date: November 8, 2013
With an array of mutant and alien characters to choose from, this roguelike RPG from Chucklefish is creative from every aspect. Risk of Rain blends pixellated animation with a soundtrack that is like none other. The all original music reminds me of a metal opera, and drips with emotion like the blood of your enemies laying in your wake. This game is much more than it appears, far more complex than it seems, Risk of Rain is a fast paced adventure that everyone can enjoy.
When I first started to look into this game all I could think was Under The Garden. I remembered it from playing it in a free indie bundle a while back. Graphics engine wise, its almost exact, but to me that isn’t a bad thing. Because with Risk of Rain, they took something cool, and made it even better. Once it was available on Steam I bought it and began to play. At first, I really liked the feel and aesthetics, the music seemed to blend perfectly with the gameplay. 10 different characters to choose from, you begin as the Commando and from there trust me, it’s on like Donkey Kong. Risk of Rain is one of those games that caught my eye because of its unique pixel art and intriguing gameplay. Something that I’ve always said in the past is that the game in review is hard, but trust me, even if you were to choose easy these monsters get tougher with every second that passes.
Risk of Rain is an action platformer with roguelike elements. With permanent death as a primary feature, players will have to play their best to get as far as possible. Fight on a mysterious planet with randomly spawning enemies and bosses, either alone or with 3 friends in online co-op. With over 100 items at your disposal, you will find the tools you need to find the teleporter back home. Discover a myriad of randomly chosen stages, from the desolate forest to the frozen tundra. The game begins with a transport and delivery ship flying through space. Then suddenly, its attacked by some superhuman being and taken over, exploding into pieces leading you to the main menu.
Ten different characters with 4 different special abilities a piece, gives this game the potential for endless fun. Throw in a multi-player option and enter the word infinite, because there is no end to the game as it only repeats over and over again until YOU die, and trust me, you will. The main goal in Risk of Rain is to find the teleporter and get the hell out of dodge, but not without taking down every creature that inhabits each planet you are beamed too. The RPG aspect kicks in when it comes to gaining levels. You do this by killing every living thing you come across. The higher your level the more health and power you are given. Different power ups are scattered throughout the levels and some need to be purchased. This is done with the gold you collect from each monsters death. You can active robotic sprites that follow you around and help you fight the monsters around you, but once the robot takes too much damage you must pay to repair it, or leave it behind.
As time progresses and you level up so do all the enemies in each level, giving each stage a sense of urgency. This is where your power up items come into play. In Risk of Rain there are two different kinds of items you can pick up. One of them being the items that are constantly on and working like Firesheild which causes the player to detonate when under heavy attack. The other kind of items are ones that only can be used every 30-90 seconds. An example of one of these items would be Missile Box which sends out 16 missiles to hunt down enemies. These “action” items are an important part of gameplay and essential to making it through later levels.
Incredible gameplay, intriguing graphics, Risk of Rain is a ton of fun to play.So many different options and weapons with each character sets the game aside from most rougelikes. Musically, this is one of those games that I didn’t turn all the sound levels down the second I turned the game on. Reason being, is that this is one of those rare occasions where the music is as good as the gameplay. When it comes down to it in the end, Risk of Rain is an amazing game that will provide hours and hours of fun. If you haven’t gotten the chance to pick this gem up make sure you do during the next sale on Steam, because Risk of Rain is one of my favorite games of 2013.

After the disastrous launch in June I held off on playing the game until the "re-launch" at the end of October, so this review is based on the current state of the game.
First of all, I played this game on an i5 with a single Geforce 970 and 16GB of RAM. The system is about 3 years old, but the graphics card is new.
I was able to play the game on high settings, and I locked it at 60FPS in the settings before starting. I had no frame-hitching at all throughout the entire game (20+ hours of playtime), including the parts with the batmobile. So as far as technical issues, whichever ones still exist (bugs, etc.) none of them hindered me and I didn't notice anything during my playthrough.
The story (despite having been spoiled on it in advance) was actually very good, including side-quests. I have absolutely zero complaints with the story portion of the game, and as far as a 'fitting" ending of the trilogy of Arkham games by Rocksteady, I think this was a great swan song.
The gameplay was very good for the most part, except toward the final 20% of the game things just get very frustrating. Every room you enter means it is Batman versus 50 random thugs. The tank battle against the Arkham Knight was frustrating, although I beat it on the first try by simply circling around a single building and shooting him every time he circled while following despite having only a few hitpoints. It feels as though it is a huge grind toward the end of the story for no good reason. It just makes you tired and frustrated and I had to put the controller down and stretch my hands after every section.
Side missions are much less frustrating, except for the Riddler missions which could very well take me an additional 5-10 hours to complete.
Other notes:
Random bad-guy dialogue is hilarious
The sense of humor in the game is very nice
It really felt like Batman TAS one last hurrah.
I'm happy to recommend it if you're a fan of the previous games. To their credit, they managed to solve the technical issues I was led to expect going in. Not GOTY or anything, but if you're a fan of Batman or DC Comics in general, this is really a no-brainer purchase.

Let me just start this review of by saying: This game is fantastic... It is, however, not 1993 XCOM with updated graphics. If that's what you wanted, don't buy this game and please don't bother us by giving 0 point reviews here.
As I said, this game is different from UFO: EU(X-com: UFO Defence in america) it is however not worse or dumbed down. They may have simplified the tactical combat, but simplifying is not the same as dumbing down. Dumbing down is making the game easier and losing strategic depth in the process, simpifying is making a game easier to understand while trying to maintain or improve strategical depth.
And XCOM: EU does the latter. The strategic base management is probably even more complicated than it was in the original and the tactical combat is, while streamlined and symplified, just as deep or even deeper than the original game.
It now involves units working together instead of having 14 nearly identical soldiers just scouting if every direction. Ammo is now more important unlike what many 1993 fanboys are saying. Guns still need reloading you just don't need to equip your soldiers with ammo anymore. And most of all there's the completely new cover system. Now, when you move your soldiers, you actually need to think about flanking aliens, because shooting aliens in full cover isn't going to kill them. I've come across a situation where my assault soldier tried to flank an alien but revealed another alien in the process which left him exposed. I then moved my support soldier in to throw a smoke grenade to protect my assault and used my heavy to suppress the flanking alien to avoid him shooting at my assault... Tactical situations like that would almost never occur in the original X-com so i completely disagree wit people who say this game is dumbed down.
The things that were simplified are mainly things like Time Units and i think the new system is actually better. It might kill the nostalgia a bit but this system is faster, easier and makes every decision more important and rewarding.

I could never really get into the first Killing Floor. The gameplay felt right, the ideas were very basic but top quality made and couldn't have asked for better. Yet, somehow the original game just "felt" bad. Like I was playing a different, older Unreal / Quake / Counter Strike / Call of Duty title with 1000+1 mods installed, and the whole game in general just gave away this feeling of cheapness and being limited by the original game that got modded to KF, expect there was no "original game".
Killing Floor 2 however, kept everything that was good in the first and made a top quality graphics and overall experience around it to host Killing Floor 1. And it achieved this marvelously, with more small but together meaningful twists that changed the KF experience for the better. Slow motion now includes stylized black and white + red vision, reaching higher levels for a class now include some gameplay customization via perks and overall got more specialized in what they do (though at the time of writing this, despite having a high number of classes some specific playstyles are not covered that were there back in KF1).
With the engine changes, everything got a quality tier higher - or more. The more treatening and massive enemies such as a scrake with a chainsaw are not only scary for being known for high damage in close range, now it's scary because it's massive, it's body communication is extremely agressive, usually covered in blood and relentlessly pursues you with such a burning hate and agression that it's really making it fearsome.
Adrenaline is usually on top because of the heartbeat demanding bloodpumping mix of rock, metal, industrial and electronic music that these types of games with these type of visuals usually scream for but rarely get. And you can even swich between turning vocals ON/OFF to customize the experience for your liking.
However there is always some downside, but these are really subjective topics. As a cooperative oriented game it's obviously intended to play with other people, however this either kills most of the gore-horror atmosphere if you guys use voicechat in ways... it shouldn't be used, or may include people who are "so hardcore" that they look at the game as statistics and numbers and well aware of the small exploits like standing on a specific spot to avoid getting hurt etc. and it's also killing the fun - for some. Again, it's just an opinion, some, including me are looking for the experience KF2's developers intended to share with us and I don't like when people mess that up. Like when some hardcore friend of yours keeps going on for 5 minutes on teamspeak about how this and that and this and that was better in KF1 and how this sucks. They can go to hell I say, Killing Floor 2 is a damn good game. Consider me a noob, but it's a perspective worth sharing in a review for others with similar thinking.
Another thing is microtrasactions: this just kicked in recently so I'm treading carefully, but it seems similar to CS:GO/TF2/DotA2 skindrops, crates and keys. I've always been against such things, but as long as it remains strictly visual, is balanced enough to have some skins even if you are not willing to open your wallet for half hour work of textures, I can accept it in exchange for not having actual content locked behind paid DLC business model. Keeping microtransactions a very well guarded secret in a partially crowdfund early access game (it's nothing like other EA garbages, feels done for a long time and gets lots of content upgrades!), is a very shady move some might feel as backstabbing.

This game is what a sequel should be: it improves on almost everthing that the original did with better graphics and more features. However, I can't recommend this game in good faith, not after everything Tripwire has done.
When Early Access was announced, they said that it would basically just be a glorified beta and that the game was already done. It was supposed to come out 6 months later, and Tripwire was going to "do Early Access right." A year after that announcement, I can safely say this is the furthest thing from the truth. Instead of finishing the game (which as it turns out was barely even running when it came out), they are working on gamemodes that nobody asked for and pumping out microtransactions to make a quick buck. There are still many classes and bosses missing from the game as well as weapons, maps, balance, and enemies. In fact, the only we're getting a steady stream of is cosmetic DLC characters and crates to open them (tf2/CSGO style).
Early Access done right. What a joke. Don't be fooled like the rest of us. Stay far away from this game, at least until it is released.

Risk of Rain is a rogue-like game where you choose 1 of 10 classes (10 classes as of the time of this review) and travel to different levels through a teleporter. These teleporters are guarded by a boss, and a large mob of enemies. If you can defeat the boss and this mob of enemies, you can traverse to the next stage, eventually arriving to the final level.
Pros
-Addictive
-LOTS of variety
-Tons of fun unlockables, none feeling useless or bad.
-Difficult but fair, with every class fitting a different playstyle
-Tons of collectables that feel valuable. Every item has a bit of lore or description to it, and every mob has a chance to drop a monster log, giving you more information about said enemy.
Cons
-The difficulty of some unlocks feels a bit silly. One unlock requires you to beat the first 3 levels without getting hit once.
-Framerate issues due to the engine (these are supposed to be patched out soon)
-It's boring to kite and slowly take out a mob of 60+ enemies, which you are often forced to do later in the game.
-As most classes, you quickly forsake the use of your first ability for more effective other abilities.
-Slight UI issues (half the items are blocked on my screen for some reason).
Other/Misc
-You never feel safe. It seems like you kill 1 enemy, and another 2 spawn.
-The game gradually becomes harder the longer the run lasts.
-Some unlocks depend on random chance. You have to hope you get the right level, and then you have to hope the unlock event actually spawns.
This game may have a few flaws, some that are due to a fixing soon, but it is truly an amazing and addictive experience. It especially blows my mind that this game was created by a small group of college kids. Every class feels balanced, every death feels like a learning experience, and as a rogue-like with so many items, not a single item feels truly useless.
90/100

Let me start by saying that I was lucky enough to not run into the frame rate, and other problems, many people had when playing this game. For me, it ran smoothly. With that in mind, my review is on the game itself, and how I found it compared to the other Arkham games before it.
I am actually mixed in my feelings for this game. But I am giving it a thumbs up for the things it does right. Simply put, as part of the Arkham trilogy it is enjoyable, however it is the worst of the three. All the parts of this game seem right, but the pacing is waaaaaaay off. Playability-wise, it feels like every other Arkham game - in a good way. However, the Batmobile plays too much of a role, and it is apparent that a good portion of the developers' time was spent putting in activities to justify having the batmobile. If I had a choice to have the game I wanted without the batmobile, or have the version we got, I would have chosen the former. That being said, I did enjoy playing this game, I only wish it had been better, especially since it was the end of the trilogy.
Pros
- Great assortment of Batman villains and allies. (though see cons)
- Fun combat and Predator missions, sticks to its roots
- Visually spectacular
- Nice sense of inevitability to the end of Batman's story arc.
Cons
- Too little time spent actually interacting with your enemies and allies, mainly you just interact over batman's video-phone.
- Terrible story pacing. Everything felt so disjointed. This game is supposed to make you feel like Batman is stretched thin by all his enemies attacking him at once. Instead, you can wait around and handle each crisis when you find it convenient.
- Gotham City did not have the great feeling that Arkham City did with a nod to the old New York style. I understand it represents a modern city, but it was so visually chaotic that I never felt like I got a sense of the place.
- The Batmobile. The number of missions requiring it could have been cut in half, especially since you can fly across the city in half the time it takes to drive.

Definitely the funnest Batman game, especially for those who enjoy driving and want to use the Batmobile. Despite some of the negative points listed through this review, it is a must play for anyone who enjoys the Batman universe. This game only has mixed review which must be outdated or some previous issues. The game is extremely enjoyable with at least a 2GB card and 3.4GHz processor. Even after 45 hours and getting all the riddles, I would love it to be 2x longer. This game could have used more Scarecrow involvement though, for those who love him.
There is a new game + mode after beating it once, which increased combat difficulty by making enemies tougher and no counter indicators etc. Not motivating enough to replay since combat isn't the main feature of this game and most of the time you play like an assassin anyways rather than go head to head.
The game heavily involves the Batmobile throughout which will be used about 50% of the game. When you first use it, the handling will be rather odd for anyone who plays racing games. It has very mobile movement is the reason why. When combined with toggling battle mode it makes it very easy to control and shouldn't take long to get used to, just stand still and try turning/moving a bit to see how the vehicle was designed. This is no ordinary car and much better than one.
Combat in this game can get frustrating as you accidently hit a stunner or shield (due to the way it is designed for free flow combat), or just caught from a blindside. What makes combat even more difficult at times is trying to remember all the different button combos and the use of the middle mouse button feels odd.
The PC requirements are important, this game will not run well on a video card less than 2GB. Technology evolves and we are in the age where 2GB cards are needed for most new games that have very nice graphics. Occasionally when destroying lots of stuff with the Batmobile or in very active areas the graphics have some issues and you may see some short term frame drops.
This game is not bug free either sadly, as a few are pointed out throughout here. The most annoying one was where Batman would just be stuck in an open spot not clipping on anything, forcing a restart or hoping there is a grapple point nearby. In the end they don't get in the way or happen often enough to where it kills enjoyment.
Personal experience score: 9.5/10 (would be 10 but has quite a few bugs which require restarts usually)
Story: 9/10 - Very interesting for fans of Batman, would have liked to see more to do with the Scarecrow
Sound: 9.5/10 - Sound effects are good, there seems to be some issues with sound going silent occasionally or a shutter type sound if you exit the mission wheel too fast after selecting a marker
Graphics: 10/10 - Very nice and thats playing with a 2GB card at what they call "low textures" Not a large difference going to the 4GB high setting
Controls: 7/10 - Can be very frustrating when you accidently hit an enemy you didn't want to and take damage because of it. An improved targeting system that would show who you will hit would be ideal.
Game Length: 10/10 - About 46 hours on hard if you plan to 100% it (excluding AR missions as it is not necessary, excluding steam achievements, no DLC) and with using a guide for a few riddler items. If you focus on the story only, it will be closer to 15 only.

Batman Arkham Knight is the worst port I have ever seen in all my years of gaming. I either haven't been unlucky enough to find the most broken port or this is the biggest screwup in gaming history. Either way, everyone and myself included was nothing short of♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
If you're new to Batman's world, the story will be decent and you may enjoy it. If you're a longtime fan or know a lot already, prepare for a disappointment. While the story is a decent one, Rocksteady flat out lied. I won't say what they lied about because it is a major spoiler, but on top of the terrible PC port release....this is infuriating. As Batman, you are tasked with finding and taking down Scarecrow before he unleashes his infamous fear gas to take over and destroy Gotham City and take down his accomplice the Arkham Knight.
The graphics are absolutely beautiful. Detail went into absolutely everything. The rain is realistic and it runs down Batman's cowl, armor and cape. It also flies off when Batman glides at times. And it doesn't stop with Batman. Everyone and everything is very detailed and looks amazing from beginning to end.
Easily the best of the Arkham series. Counters now have a 'critical' where, if timed right, will have Batman throw them on top of his counter. You can now use blunt objects in combat. Throw crates, fire extinguishers, use bats (no not literal bats unfortunately) to pound your enemies into the ground. You'll also be able to use hanging lamps and electric boxes to automatically take an opponent down and when near, use the Batmobile to fire a non-lethal bullet to automatically take one opponent down. The new fear takedown makes you feel like an absolute badass, taking out eventually up to 5 thugs in succession. There are a few new gadgets (excluding the Batmobile) but not like the previous titles. There are new and tough (and sometimes annoying) enemies to face.
The Batmobile really feels like an extension of Batman and is clearly shown throughout the story and puzzles. You can drive and pilot the best car in the world yourself or use your remote control gadget to fight or help solve puzzles. People say that this is "Batman: World of Tanks", but I honestly think Rocksteady did a good job balancing the Batmobile and on foot combat.....although to be honest, it's still hard to say this as there is no boss battle on foot. One of the biggest disappointments and one I feel needs to be known.
Yep. I'm covering the season pass for two reasons.
1. It's the very first season pass I've ever purchased.
2. It was an incredibly huge and disappointing mistake.
I knew that there would be skins and Batmobile race tracks. This was announced well before release. However, I expected actual quality content as well. So far, the only DLC worth your money (besides skins if you're into those) is the 'Matter of Family' Batgirl DLC. It's well done and about as lengthy if not lengthier than the 'Harley's Revenge' DLC in Arkham City and it has the boss battle we all were hoping for and were really looking forward to. Besides that, us season pass buyers have been completely ripped off. We are not getting our worth for our money. And at this point, I very heavily doubt the rest of the content will change my mind.
While there are clearly a lot of cons here.....I can't help but love this game. The story is still decent and the gameplay is solid. It could very clearly be a much better finale as it stands, but this is what we received and for what we got I think it's worth the purchase. Is it worth the full price? No. Do not purchase this until there's a decent sale. But it is still worth the discounted price you'll pay if you get it.

Risk of Rain is a rogue-like game where you choose 1 of 10 classes (10 classes as of the time of this review) and travel to different levels through a teleporter. These teleporters are guarded by a boss, and a large mob of enemies. If you can defeat the boss and this mob of enemies, you can traverse to the next stage, eventually arriving to the final level.
Pros
-Addictive
-LOTS of variety
-Tons of fun unlockables, none feeling useless or bad.
-Difficult but fair, with every class fitting a different playstyle
-Tons of collectables that feel valuable. Every item has a bit of lore or description to it, and every mob has a chance to drop a monster log, giving you more information about said enemy.
Cons
-The difficulty of some unlocks feels a bit silly. One unlock requires you to beat the first 3 levels without getting hit once.
-Framerate issues due to the engine (these are supposed to be patched out soon)
-It's boring to kite and slowly take out a mob of 60+ enemies, which you are often forced to do later in the game.
-As most classes, you quickly forsake the use of your first ability for more effective other abilities.
-Slight UI issues (half the items are blocked on my screen for some reason).
Other/Misc
-You never feel safe. It seems like you kill 1 enemy, and another 2 spawn.
-The game gradually becomes harder the longer the run lasts.
-Some unlocks depend on random chance. You have to hope you get the right level, and then you have to hope the unlock event actually spawns.
This game may have a few flaws, some that are due to a fixing soon, but it is truly an amazing and addictive experience. It especially blows my mind that this game was created by a small group of college kids. Every class feels balanced, every death feels like a learning experience, and as a rogue-like with so many items, not a single item feels truly useless.
90/100
95/100 (when engine enhancement is released)

Finally Civ V has become a worthy Civilization game. After two major expansions and several patches it is finally where it should have been when it was first released. Without these expansions the game is bare bones, so buy the complete collection or don't play at all, because the content added through the DLCs is a must. Personally I got it for 10€ when it was on 75% sale.
If you are not familiar with the series, CIvilization V is a 4X turn based strategy game where you choose one of 43 real life civilizations, and you:
a) Explore a random generated map (or one of the many real life maps).
b) Expand your empire through building new colonies or conquering existing cities.
c) Exploit the world's resources and locations to give your people more advantages, happiness and power.
d) Exterminate everyone that opposes you, which in Civ V you can do in various ways. From straight military conquer to cultural victory (make everyone bow to the awesomeness of your civilization), to a diplomatic one (be nice with everyone so they elect you world leader).
There are many aspects in the game that you have to balance if you want your nation to achieve greatness. Food, production, gold, research, culture, faith, strategic and luxury resources, trade routes. I won't go into details since this isn't a guide. All you need to know is that there are many different ways to give your empire the advantage and each civilization has it's own unique trait, making each of them play a bit different than the other.
Overall the mechanics are satisfying and offer a good amount of replayability.
The graphics are extremely pleasant to look at. They are not the usual stock 3D gfx most games use, the map features use textures that look like they are drawn, making the map almost look like a painting. Very satisfying is the feeling you get as the landscape slowly changes through the ages as you build mines, roads, farms, cities, bringing civilization to wild lands.
But the real reason to buy this game is for the mod community. If it wasn't for the great variety in mods, I wouldn't recommend this game, even with the two expansions. There are many awesome mods created by very talented people, that if you didn't know they were mods, you wouldn't be able to tell the difference from the official content.
The collection of mods in this game is really mind-blowing. You can add new civilizations, new game mechanics, new units, change the appearance of units, change how many units can stand in a tile, limit the technology so you can play only until Medieval times for example, or complete expansions that add more free content.
The replayability of this game is over 9000, you can play a game that is WWII themed, or another that is focused in ancient times. Ofcourse you will spend some time discovering these mods, but in the end that's half the fun and Steam workshop really makes it easy to find them.
So if you liked Civ IV BTS or any previous Civ game, buy the complete CIv V collection and you will get hundres of hours of fun. If you like playing with mods you will get thousands of hours of fun, the replayability is endless and the mods are THAT good.
The only major flow in my opinion is that if you play with mods the Steam achievements are disabled. Which is stupid if you think that if someone really wants to cheat there are ways to just unlock the achievements without playing the game. So in the end the people who get punished are those who actually play the game. But still this is just a personal opinion, most people don't even care about achievements.

This is a review coming from an avid KF1 fan.  I loved KF1 so much that my friends and I bought KF2 the first chance we got.  The hype was real and we were so excited.  Unfortunately KF2 did NOT deliver.  Everything I loved from KF1 was missing in KF2.  Here I list my comparisons between two games:
First, with KF1 you can reach max levels on all perks at around 400-600 hours mark.  With over 1800 hours gameplay on KF1, I continued to play KF1 simple for its replayability.  Having max levels doesn't necessarily ensure a win and strategy most often comes into play especially on higher difficulties.  Certain perks play certain roles and certain zeds need to be killed by certain perks for efficiency and minimal losses.  With KF2, I find that perk roles are more blurred and that almost any perk can kill any zed.  Any perk can also heal from a distance.  KF2 feels less strategical and more about luck - relying that you don't meet some unfortunate spawns in front of you as your run around the map.  The fact that doors don't respawn each wave almost entirely eliminates the ability to camp at the same spot (but the green welding effects look nice though).  Some people may disagree but that's fine.  This is my opinion.  I love that in KF1, you are able to hold camp spots till wave 10 and strategically eliminate threats like scrakes from wave 5+ and fleshpounds from wave 7+.  Whereas in KF2, I see most people running around - it feels like every map is KF-Farm.
Second, KF1 trader really gives the players the apocalyptic feel.  You see the trader is just like any other human trying to survive and make enough money to survive the apocalypse.  While on KF2, you are met by a computer trader in place of KF1's human trader.  If it was a digital trader, why would you still need to "find" the trader after each wave?  With technology, you should be able to access any digital interface anywhere - ANYTIME.  Why would you need to wait every end of the wave to access the digital trader?  I understand that the human trader needs to "close the shop and find a safe shelter" while the wave is ongoing but "shutting down" a digital trader will not save it from getting sawed off by a scrake.  Besides, many games have already implemented digital "shops" into their game.  Having a digital trader is another reason why KF2 is less special compared to KF1.
Third, KF2 leveling feels so much faster than KF1.  Now this is purely subjective as some people hate the grind.  But watching someone go from level 0 to 25 in a few days wasn't something possible in KF1 unless you play on custom maps.  But personally I liked KF1 leveling much better as it really forces the players to learn to play the perk before being awarded max level.  By the time you are legitimately level 6, you would've experimented with all the guns and know which ones you prefer to use.  You can definitely tell which player speed leveled their perks by the way they play, use their guns/dosh and how they keep themselves alive.
Fourth, spawning with guns on low level perks is outrageous.  What made KF1 so satisfying is the reward that you get to spawn with a weapon or armor at level 5-6.  Spawning with weapons other than the default pistol and knife at low level perks is like starting a sandbox game or mmorpg and being given free midgame to endgame tier items.  The essence of being a newbie is gone.  The challenge and thrill of climbing your way up is gone.  You no longer start from scratch.  On top of this, when you die you don't restart with 100-200 dosh.  You respawn with 1000+ dosh, which typically is enough for you to buy 80% of your items back - or more if you happen to drop all your guns.  So in reality, you don't get punished as much for dying and players don't feel the importance of not dying as strongly as in KF1.  In KF1, once you die, you must face the consequence of losing a portion of your current dosh (and not spawn with more dosh) and lose your guns.  This is why teams in KF1 do their best to keep everyone alive.  This is one of the reasons why KF2 has turned into a boring FPS game IMO.  Oh yeah, did I forget to mention that weapons are scrambled into different perks?  Machete is a support weapon and vlad is a zerk's and katana isn't belonging to any perk. Hmm.
Finally, the addition of a slasher is more frustrating THAN challenging.  If you are running away from a horde of zeds, you wouldn't want a zed to forcefully turn you around.  One slasher is not much of a nuisance but when there is a slasher in front of you and behind you, they just keep turning you around back and forth that you can't even shoot them without losing a good number of ammo.  This aspect of the game makes me so dizzy and makes me hate the way KF2 turned out to be.  Also the siren on KF1 is much better than the one on KF2.
TLDR: Overall, KF2 had too much hype but it was a disappointing sequel to KF1 in my opinion.  The graphics upgrade is not exceptional - I personally don't mind if they kept KF1 graphics.  SC and FP on KF1 looked way better than the ones on KF2.  The characters also don't look impressive at all - so do other cosmetic items.  The impersonal trader is also not impressive.  There is no post-apocalyptic feel to any of these maps.  This game is just like L4D2, running around killing zombies yet never reaching safezone unless you kill them all.  You don't feel like a team on an extermination mission.  It is less strategic than KF1 and lots of running.  Very boring to play - I can't even get past 50 hours.  Quick to level, you get spoiled with guns right from when you start your KF2 career.  KF1 didn't need a sequel anyway.  It was still an amazing game even when KF2 came out.  After trying KF2, I found myself returning back to KF1.  If this was a YouTube channel, this is the point where I hit unsubscribe.
FYI, some positive observations I've seen on KF2:
-nice welding effects
-more perks to choose from
-addition of perk benefits tree is a brilliant idea
-ability to choose levels of gore

Let me start by saying that I was lucky enough to not run into the frame rate, and other problems, many people had when playing this game. For me, it ran smoothly. With that in mind, my review is on the game itself, and how I found it compared to the other Arkham games before it.
I am actually mixed in my feelings for this game. But I am giving it a thumbs up for the things it does right. Simply put, as part of the Arkham trilogy it is enjoyable, however it is the worst of the three. All the parts of this game seem right, but the pacing is waaaaaaay off. Playability-wise, it feels like every other Arkham game - in a good way. However, the Batmobile plays too much of a role, and it is apparent that a good portion of the developers' time was spent putting in activities to justify having the batmobile. If I had a choice to have the game I wanted without the batmobile, or have the version we got, I would have chosen the former. That being said, I did enjoy playing this game, I only wish it had been better, especially since it was the end of the trilogy.
Pros
- Great assortment of Batman villains and allies. (though see cons)
- Fun combat and Predator missions, sticks to its roots
- Visually spectacular
- Nice sense of inevitability to the end of Batman's story arc.
Cons
- Too little time spent actually interacting with your enemies and allies, mainly you just interact over batman's video-phone.
- Terrible story pacing. Everything felt so disjointed. This game is supposed to make you feel like Batman is stretched thin by all his enemies attacking him at once. Instead, you can wait around and handle each crisis when you find it convenient.
- Gotham City did not have the great feeling that Arkham City did with a nod to the old New York style. I understand it represents a modern city, but it was so visually chaotic that I never felt like I got a sense of the place.
- The Batmobile. The number of missions requiring it could have been cut in half, especially since you can fly across the city in half the time it takes to drive.
