Definitely the funnest Batman game, especially for those who enjoy driving and want to use the Batmobile. Despite some of the negative points listed through this review, it is a must play for anyone who enjoys the Batman universe. This game only has mixed review which must be outdated or some previous issues. The game is extremely enjoyable with at least a 2GB card and 3.4GHz processor. Even after 45 hours and getting all the riddles, I would love it to be 2x longer. This game could have used more Scarecrow involvement though, for those who love him.
There is a new game + mode after beating it once, which increased combat difficulty by making enemies tougher and no counter indicators etc. Not motivating enough to replay since combat isn't the main feature of this game and most of the time you play like an assassin anyways rather than go head to head.
The game heavily involves the Batmobile throughout which will be used about 50% of the game. When you first use it, the handling will be rather odd for anyone who plays racing games. It has very mobile movement is the reason why. When combined with toggling battle mode it makes it very easy to control and shouldn't take long to get used to, just stand still and try turning/moving a bit to see how the vehicle was designed. This is no ordinary car and much better than one.
Combat in this game can get frustrating as you accidently hit a stunner or shield (due to the way it is designed for free flow combat), or just caught from a blindside. What makes combat even more difficult at times is trying to remember all the different button combos and the use of the middle mouse button feels odd.
The PC requirements are important, this game will not run well on a video card less than 2GB. Technology evolves and we are in the age where 2GB cards are needed for most new games that have very nice graphics. Occasionally when destroying lots of stuff with the Batmobile or in very active areas the graphics have some issues and you may see some short term frame drops.
This game is not bug free either sadly, as a few are pointed out throughout here. The most annoying one was where Batman would just be stuck in an open spot not clipping on anything, forcing a restart or hoping there is a grapple point nearby. In the end they don't get in the way or happen often enough to where it kills enjoyment.
Personal experience score: 9.5/10 (would be 10 but has quite a few bugs which require restarts usually)
Story: 9/10 - Very interesting for fans of Batman, would have liked to see more to do with the Scarecrow
Sound: 9.5/10 - Sound effects are good, there seems to be some issues with sound going silent occasionally or a shutter type sound if you exit the mission wheel too fast after selecting a marker
Graphics: 10/10 - Very nice and thats playing with a 2GB card at what they call "low textures" Not a large difference going to the 4GB high setting
Controls: 7/10 - Can be very frustrating when you accidently hit an enemy you didn't want to and take damage because of it. An improved targeting system that would show who you will hit would be ideal.
Game Length: 10/10 - About 46 hours on hard if you plan to 100% it (excluding AR missions as it is not necessary, excluding steam achievements, no DLC) and with using a guide for a few riddler items. If you focus on the story only, it will be closer to 15 only.

This is a review coming from an avid KF1 fan.  I loved KF1 so much that my friends and I bought KF2 the first chance we got.  The hype was real and we were so excited.  Unfortunately KF2 did NOT deliver.  Everything I loved from KF1 was missing in KF2.  Here I list my comparisons between two games:
First, with KF1 you can reach max levels on all perks at around 400-600 hours mark.  With over 1800 hours gameplay on KF1, I continued to play KF1 simple for its replayability.  Having max levels doesn't necessarily ensure a win and strategy most often comes into play especially on higher difficulties.  Certain perks play certain roles and certain zeds need to be killed by certain perks for efficiency and minimal losses.  With KF2, I find that perk roles are more blurred and that almost any perk can kill any zed.  Any perk can also heal from a distance.  KF2 feels less strategical and more about luck - relying that you don't meet some unfortunate spawns in front of you as your run around the map.  The fact that doors don't respawn each wave almost entirely eliminates the ability to camp at the same spot (but the green welding effects look nice though).  Some people may disagree but that's fine.  This is my opinion.  I love that in KF1, you are able to hold camp spots till wave 10 and strategically eliminate threats like scrakes from wave 5+ and fleshpounds from wave 7+.  Whereas in KF2, I see most people running around - it feels like every map is KF-Farm.
Second, KF1 trader really gives the players the apocalyptic feel.  You see the trader is just like any other human trying to survive and make enough money to survive the apocalypse.  While on KF2, you are met by a computer trader in place of KF1's human trader.  If it was a digital trader, why would you still need to "find" the trader after each wave?  With technology, you should be able to access any digital interface anywhere - ANYTIME.  Why would you need to wait every end of the wave to access the digital trader?  I understand that the human trader needs to "close the shop and find a safe shelter" while the wave is ongoing but "shutting down" a digital trader will not save it from getting sawed off by a scrake.  Besides, many games have already implemented digital "shops" into their game.  Having a digital trader is another reason why KF2 is less special compared to KF1.
Third, KF2 leveling feels so much faster than KF1.  Now this is purely subjective as some people hate the grind.  But watching someone go from level 0 to 25 in a few days wasn't something possible in KF1 unless you play on custom maps.  But personally I liked KF1 leveling much better as it really forces the players to learn to play the perk before being awarded max level.  By the time you are legitimately level 6, you would've experimented with all the guns and know which ones you prefer to use.  You can definitely tell which player speed leveled their perks by the way they play, use their guns/dosh and how they keep themselves alive.
Fourth, spawning with guns on low level perks is outrageous.  What made KF1 so satisfying is the reward that you get to spawn with a weapon or armor at level 5-6.  Spawning with weapons other than the default pistol and knife at low level perks is like starting a sandbox game or mmorpg and being given free midgame to endgame tier items.  The essence of being a newbie is gone.  The challenge and thrill of climbing your way up is gone.  You no longer start from scratch.  On top of this, when you die you don't restart with 100-200 dosh.  You respawn with 1000+ dosh, which typically is enough for you to buy 80% of your items back - or more if you happen to drop all your guns.  So in reality, you don't get punished as much for dying and players don't feel the importance of not dying as strongly as in KF1.  In KF1, once you die, you must face the consequence of losing a portion of your current dosh (and not spawn with more dosh) and lose your guns.  This is why teams in KF1 do their best to keep everyone alive.  This is one of the reasons why KF2 has turned into a boring FPS game IMO.  Oh yeah, did I forget to mention that weapons are scrambled into different perks?  Machete is a support weapon and vlad is a zerk's and katana isn't belonging to any perk. Hmm.
Finally, the addition of a slasher is more frustrating THAN challenging.  If you are running away from a horde of zeds, you wouldn't want a zed to forcefully turn you around.  One slasher is not much of a nuisance but when there is a slasher in front of you and behind you, they just keep turning you around back and forth that you can't even shoot them without losing a good number of ammo.  This aspect of the game makes me so dizzy and makes me hate the way KF2 turned out to be.  Also the siren on KF1 is much better than the one on KF2.
TLDR: Overall, KF2 had too much hype but it was a disappointing sequel to KF1 in my opinion.  The graphics upgrade is not exceptional - I personally don't mind if they kept KF1 graphics.  SC and FP on KF1 looked way better than the ones on KF2.  The characters also don't look impressive at all - so do other cosmetic items.  The impersonal trader is also not impressive.  There is no post-apocalyptic feel to any of these maps.  This game is just like L4D2, running around killing zombies yet never reaching safezone unless you kill them all.  You don't feel like a team on an extermination mission.  It is less strategic than KF1 and lots of running.  Very boring to play - I can't even get past 50 hours.  Quick to level, you get spoiled with guns right from when you start your KF2 career.  KF1 didn't need a sequel anyway.  It was still an amazing game even when KF2 came out.  After trying KF2, I found myself returning back to KF1.  If this was a YouTube channel, this is the point where I hit unsubscribe.
FYI, some positive observations I've seen on KF2:
-nice welding effects
-more perks to choose from
-addition of perk benefits tree is a brilliant idea
-ability to choose levels of gore

Beated the normal game 100%, all Riddler trophies, 3 stars in multiple AR challenges, and only THEN is a review in place.
So, if you are reading this, please skip the thousands and thousands of both bad/good reviews done by people that has invested only a few hours or less, or who just had a crashing game.
Second, I´ve had zero problems with this game, but I also didn´t start playing it before the October update, and it runs flawless 60fps with even Nvidias enhanced PhysX particles.
Where to begin? If you´ve played Asylum and City, then yes, those games are probably better. Asylum is still my favorite, City was a great followup but the awe you had playing the first game was not on par. Playing AK, 2 things top the series: the combat and the city. The story is just okay, and the gameplay is classic for the series, but AK has one problem: repetition. All sidemissions are build in a way so you´ll be doing the same things 5-10 times in a row to complete the entire mission and apprehend the corresponding villian. I guess this is the nature for some sandbox-type games, and it´s not that well executed in AK, although a few surprises makes it just fun enough to proceed. The good part is, that it always involves kicking♥♥♥♥♥ and the combat is as good as ever. If you spend some time with the challenges and hone your buttonmashing skills up to 3 stars, doing 1-string freeflow combat through the storymode makes you feel more batman-ish, rather than seeing the gameover animations all the time. When I had completed 50% mainstory, I did not die once even though I beat up hundreds of  bad guys completing the rest of the game. It made the flow of the game much more bearable.
(mild spoiler):
No, the batmobile is not hard to drive. Yes, it´s cool, and yes, there is slightly too much focus on the batmobile in this game. Finding and disarming the bombs planted around the city, I found to be the most boring of all the sidemissions. The best batmobile sequence is the very first at the ACE plant, with a few cool moments later on as well.(end spoiler)
After completing the game, I wish Batman would have all his tools available at the first playthrough, like in Story+. It´s a design choice that is made to lock certain parts of the game for later on, while adding a few "prizes" going through the game and finally get that upgrade. Though, when you see a place you can´t go but could with the right tool, you feel as if "this Bat is stupid". Batman would know what to do and do it. I didn´t enjoy these limitations where the solution was obvious if you had the gadgets you already knew exists from previous games. Once again, I found myself collecting all the 243 trophies at the very end of the game, bringing down the Riddler as the last thing I did before triggering the final/second ending. Same as I did in the Asylum and City, and I could have been half way already collecting through the main story. Just personal opinion.
All in all, a good farewell chapter in the series, but although graphically supreme, it´s not the best of the 3. Would recommend for any Batman-enthusiast.

What can I say, other than Risk of Rain is a must buy.
Don't be put of by the fairly simplistic art style (as many people do), the game mechanics is incredible. It's addictive. As you venture each map to find loot and items, you'll see yourself carrying an arsenal of weapons and powerups. The feeling is great. But it won't last too long, the longer you spend, the harder it gets. Super hard. And when you die, you'll be coming back for more, believe me.
The game also has a very layed out item and enemy log, which includes a personal and technical description of the specified item/enemy which draws you to understand the lore and context of an enemy in its location. I should also point out that it can be played with 10 different classes each with set abilities and attributes. Not to mention there are 3 difficulties to choose from (although they fair to become substantially difficult as time progresses in-game anyway) which affect the rounds. Local co-op and Online co-op is another bonus. Although local co-op does requires some technical configurations (port-forwading that is) if you want to HOST a server.
However, it is somewhat difficult to actually find a flaw for this game in my point of view. A rather common issue the game suffers at the moment is the notorious 'no-sound problem'. Beated the normal game 100%, all Riddler trophies, 3 stars in multiple AR challenges, and only THEN is a review in place.
So, if you are reading this, please skip the thousands and thousands of both bad/good reviews done by people that has invested only a few hours or less, or who just had a crashing game.
Second, I´ve had zero problems with this game, but I also didn´t start playing it before the October update, and it runs flawless 60fps with even Nvidias enhanced PhysX particles.
Where to begin? If you´ve played Asylum and City, then yes, those games are probably better. Asylum is still my favorite, City was a great followup but the awe you had playing the first game was not on par. Playing AK, 2 things top the series: the combat and the city. The story is just okay, and the gameplay is classic for the series, but AK has one problem: repetition. All sidemissions are build in a way so you´ll be doing the same things 5-10 times in a row to complete the entire mission and apprehend the corresponding villian. I guess this is the nature for some sandbox-type games, and it´s not that well executed in AK, although a few surprises makes it just fun enough to proceed. The good part is, that it always involves kicking♥♥♥♥♥ and the combat is as good as ever. If you spend some time with the challenges and hone your buttonmashing skills up to 3 stars, doing 1-string freeflow combat through the storymode makes you feel more batman-ish, rather than seeing the gameover animations all the time. When I had completed 50% mainstory, I did not die once even though I beat up hundreds of  bad guys completing the rest of the game. It made the flow of the game much more bearable.
(mild spoiler):
No, the batmobile is not hard to drive. Yes, it´s cool, and yes, there is slightly too much focus on the batmobile in this game. Finding and disarming the bombs planted around the city, I found to be the most boring of all the sidemissions. The best batmobile sequence is the very first at the ACE plant, with a few cool moments later on as well.(end spoiler)
After completing the game, I wish Batman would have all his tools available at the first playthrough, like in Story+. It´s a design choice that is made to lock certain parts of the game for later on, while adding a few "prizes" going through the game and finally get that upgrade. Though, when you see a place you can´t go but could with the right tool, you feel as if "this Bat is stupid". Batman would know what to do and do it. I didn´t enjoy these limitations where the solution was obvious if you had the gadgets you already knew exists from previous games. Once again, I found myself collecting all the 243 trophies at the very end of the game, bringing down the Riddler as the last thing I did before triggering the final/second ending. Same as I did in the Asylum and City, and I could have been half way already collecting through the main story. Just personal opinion.
All in all, a good farewell chapter in the series, but although graphically supreme, it´s not the best of the 3. Would recommend for any Batman-enthusiast.

No doubt this was a poorly ported game which unfortunately affected very many people, however it plays ok with my specs and this is what I base my review on.
Specs:
Processor - Intel Core i7 4720 2.6GHz
RAM - 16GB
SSD - 128 micro SSD/512 SSD combo
Graphics - Nvidia 970m 3GB
O/S - Windows 10
Pros:
Gorgeous game, one of the best I've seen for the Arkham series. The story itself makes the game worth playing with the addition of tearing up the streets in the Batmobile. Without revealing too much, it makes you want to take the fight to the Arkham Knight.
Cons:
Camera - This can be wonky at times especially when driving. The camera is supposed to swing as the car swings around a corner right? Instead the camera stays dead in the direction the car was facing before making the turn. What, did Batman see Cat Woman taking a stroll and couldn't pull his eyes away from her booty? Fortunately it doesn't happen often but it can elicit some choice, crude words during an intense car chase when it does.
Memory - I've heard about the memory leak issue and while I haven't experienced it, I just think the 8GB of memory requirement is a bit steep.
Glitches - Minor glitches like a downed enemy wiggling on the floor like he has a chest buster waiting to get out.
Conclusion
With all the controversy and issues surrounding Batman Arkham Knight, I can't recommend it to everyone. However, if you have a powerful system (aka 8GB or more of memory, solid state hard drive, a video card with at least 3GB of Ram and lady luck on your side <-- i'm not kidding) as well as the money to pick up a copy (definitely not at full price), it's worth a try. That is unless you can get the game on console and avoid the PC version altogether. :)
Final Score: 5/10 Recommended, with reservations.

I'm aware that this game suffers from significant performance issues. For me, the game was definitely playable, though I did have substantial framerate stuttering here and there whenever the batmobile was involved with something. My GTX 960 does pretty for the most part.
Aside from all the controversy regarding its release and the performance for many people, I think this very well may just be the most polished game in the Arkham series. The story is back up there in quality with Arkham Asylum, which is commonly lauded for its tightly-woven story. The combat and stealth are, I believe, the superior iterations compared to other games in the series. Fear multitakedowns are really satisfying. Gotham feels like a believable world, for the most part. The atmosphere of the overall game is really well-done.
Then there's the whole batmobile thing.
I liked the batmobile. Once you get used to how it handles, it's real fun to use. I think they did a good job bringing the batmobile into the game technically speaking (and ignoring things like framerate drops). My main issue with the batmobile was how prevalent it was in the core gameplay of the game. It felt like every 5 seconds the developers were trying to shove the damn thing down your throat because they were so proud of what they made, which got kind of obnoxious. Things that didn't need a batmobile section got a batmobile section. The vehicle combat was fun, but got really exhausting towards the end of the campaign. The whole thing was definitely a little overplayed.
Also, everything being destructible, while INCREDIBLY entertaining and super cool, seemed a little out of character for Batman. I thought it was a little odd.
That said, I'd recommend the game to those who are willing to risk seeing whether or not it works on your system. If you're a fan of the Arkham series then this game is definitely a must-play. It's a shame the release of this game went the way it did because it really is a great game.

This is a tentative yes, because it hinges on whether or not you can play the game. I experienced some frame rate issues during the beginning of the opening cinematic sequence that smoothed out towards the end. Since that point I've had only two minor glitches - 1) I somehow navigated Bruce onto his office desk but then could not get off, 2) One tank disappeared  during a battle scene and I was unable to complete the mission. Despite these, what I would consider relatively minor issues, it is still an excellent gaming experience. In fact, it's my favorite in the Arkham series, and one of the best games I've played in recent memory.
I think the manner in which the game was released speaks to a larger problem within the entire gaming comunity at this point, one that gamers have a right to be concerned and angered over, as the trend towards releasing "broken" games seems to be growing as developers are pushed to make deadlines. I see no easy fix here. Another reviewer posted the dilemma quite well - releasing quicker installments/sequels at the expense of quality/performance (or content) issues vs. longer time periods between installments in a game series to "complete" the game. I think I would honestly prefer the latter, but a corporate business model likely supports/encourages the former.
In any event, this is a great game, probably the best in the Arkham series. It is one of the few games recently I am attempting 100% completion on (the only other this year being The Witcher - The Wild Hunt). The missions for the most part are interesting and fun, although others have rightfully pointed out some of the tank missions/car chases are thin on story and heavy on the tedious. Overall I would recommend this game and believe it has some solid replayability all other issues nonwithstanding.

My original review of this title (above) was accurate and succinct, but it also failed to impart the true impact of Civilization 5.
The Civilization series has been around for 25 years and I’ve been playing for all 25 of them. Each iteration has adjusted and adapted aspects of the game some for the betterment of the series, some not so much.  But the evolution always appears to be a response to common playing styles the fans develop to min/max certain aspects of each individual game.
With Civ 5 the big change was unstacking the units. Civ 1 through 4 allowed players to load their units into large “stacks of doom” and then stomp them around the map. No more with 5, now the player had to think carefully about strategy and tactics. Along with the combat change came many other new challenges, a very in depth tech tree, beautiful new art work, a wonderful selection of world leaders/civilizations, excellent music, and excellent voice acting particularly from William Morgan Sheppard doing the primary narration.
Vanilla Civ 5 has a great beginning, a slow middle, and a good ending. The  Gods & Kings expansion pack added new techs, new units, religion, espionage, and several new Civilizations.  These additions made the middle game excellent and improved the endings as well. Then the Brave New World expansion came out adding even more tech, civilizations, trade routes, World Congress, wonders and much more. Then Civilization 5 ascended to, not only the best Civilization game, but the best 4x game on the market.  And several years later and multiple other 4x games played and I still find this to be true. Civilization 5 is the epitome of 4x games.
One can only wonder if the next entry in the series will be able to claim this mantle.

So in short Civ 5(with the dlc) is a game that everyone on steam should have as it is one of the best

Killing Floor 2 Review
Killing Floor 2 is a pretty basic game. That being said, it does what is does so well. It is a co-op based horde-mode shooter, a refreshing game in the mix of mediocre ones in the genre. You get money (DOSH) for surviving rounds, and with that money, you are allowed to purchase weapons at a trading post between rounds. You can purchase basic things like AR's and shotguns, and also crazy over-the-top weapons like flamethrowers, and this weird "microwave gun" thing. The gunplay overall is satisfying, as all weapons have a decent amount of kick and recoil. If you didn't know already, you fight the disgusting "Zeds", a sort of zombie like monster. There are different kinds of them, like the heavy fleshpounds and lound sirens that give variety to the gameplay. The gore in the game, while quite instense, makes getting kills quite satisfying. The character physics make for some awesome kills. You can pop a Zed's head with a pistol and they'll flop back and fall over. That alone feels quite rewarding, but you can also go a little further and send them flying with a shotgun. All of these crazy kills can be made even more awesome by the bullet-time system in the game, which pretty much triggers slow motion whenever a lot of damage is being dealt. It's surprisingly fun, as similar as each game may be. There are no objectives to the levels, only to survive until the end. Speaking of the end, the game gets progressively harder as you go, and at the end, a boss spawns. There are currently two bosses in the game, and I'm not going to give away what the are. You'd probably want to find that out for yourself. The graphics are actually quite good. The shine of the wet bricks on the Paris level look especially nice if your system's specs can handle the game at high enough settings. I can run the game at about 50-70 FPS on a GTX960 with 4gb of V-Ram, so the performance isn't perfect. But I wouldn't expect more from a game in such and early state. My game's not quite on max settings, so if you have a somewhat lower level system, while the game will still look good, don't expect to run it on ultra. While most progression is in-game, there is a class system that can provide for an out-of-game levelling system. There aren't really any unlocks as of now, only a small amount of perk progression, such as boosted handgun damage for the gunslinger class. Overall, the gameplay is so refined and well... flat out FUN, that I just don't really think it needs any more depth. It's  just a simple horde-mode game, and it's incredibly fun.

I like that the game is challenging, but not when luck plays a huge part in it; If you want to have a chance at the end boss, you need luck with finding the portal, finding items and getting the right items in time.
Few drones and a tanky character get you very far already, making the boss fights much easier (even if they die on the last boss). Sometimes you just don't find anything that increases your health/health regen much though... and most of the time you lack damage as well. This forces you to kite huge waves of mobs and search the scattered enemies on the map after using portal, wasting your time and making your difficulty go higher, which means lower damage... you might need over 20 hits to kill a tougher normal enemy at some point.
If you stop kiting/running you will get caught by high damage rockets/projectiles. Sometimes you just get a boss fight that is very hard to beat.. think Enforcer at 200/400 hp without regen/tanky items in impossible difficulty against Cremator for example.'
The game is still great fun in both single- and multiplayer even if it's rather unforgiving due to RNG, so I recommend buying the game.
Edit: After finding certain artifact items, the game becomes much easier so there is no more frustration with RNG.

The main thing to know about this game is it is very faithful to the TV show as a whole, though that should be a given since the game's story was written by South Park's creators. It is pretty much inserting yourself into the world of South Park, interacting with the world and its characters in fun and humorous ways.
The gameplay itself isn't that bad either, anyone familar with the battle systems of games like Paper Mario will adapt quick to this and its easy enough to pick up even if you haven't. However one thing I will criticise the game for is the lack of depth for character progression, your max level caps out at 15 and given how much you can progress your abilities, a max level of 25 I feel would have been better suited.
Aside from that, there are a lot of weird and wonderful weapons that you can acquire during the game from Darts to dodgeballs to vibrating ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Also many costume pieces can be found, each with their own passives attached such as extra armor or a boost in fire damage.
These pieces can be customised further through the use of 'Strap-ons' to give extra benefits like causing bleeding, giving more armor and even recovering hp and pp on perfect attacks.
The game provides choices in the game but really they do little to effect the game's story, just more something you will do for achievements and choosing who you will fight later on until a point where the two sides merge.
Also hope you like references, cause the game is full of them from the show such as the 30 Chimpokomon you can collect during the course of the game to well known references from the show.
As for those who will be affected by the censorship the game's makers put in, I found they don't really do much to spoil anything, just two minigames though I think some audio dialogue in the second half of the game (least in the Australian version) is cut out as well, or just my sound card ♥♥♥♥ing sucks, either or which.
All in all it's a solid rpg for those interested and also a game for diehard fans of South Park to enjoy, however I would suggest avoiding it if you are the sort of person easily offended by the style of crude humor shows like South Park provide.

Shelved this game after 10 hours of play around launch to wait for the fixes, so five months later I've come back and finished it.  I didn't really have many performance issues at launch, but knowing the game was going to be improved, and noticing low-res in some spots, I saw the potential for a better game and decided to wait.  I'm glad I did; I came back to better performance, improved textures, had a really good time and a smooth experience.
As for the game, it's really fun, it's well-made, plays really well, has some of the most gorgeous character modeling and general aesthetics, an interesting story with a diverse cast, absolute top-notch voice acting, and is a good ending to a great series.  The car is useful and offers a fun alternative option to travel, but I did find the tank combat stuff to get pretty tedious eventually; luckily the sequences were fairly short.  Even playing on normal difficulty, I felt really challenged in quite a few spots; it can be pretty dang hard sometimes, and that made the difficulty feel a little too uneven in places.
My biggest complaint was the time-wasting search to find all of the remaining side-mission stuff after finishing the main story.  Rocksteady buried two extended endings behind the side missions, which is a nice reward for people that want more out of the game, but probably a little frustrating for people who just wanted the story.  I completed the first extended ending, which involved doing just about everything except all of the Riddler puzzles, and felt somewhat unsatisfied.  The final extended ending is buried behind 235-some Riddler puzzles, and I just didn't feel like doing that this time around; maybe I'll go back later, but there are too many other good games to play right now.  I instead watched the final extended ending online, and think I would've been disappointed for putting in the many of extra hours to finish all the Riddler puzzles, though it was a bit more satsifying, I'm not sure it would've felt worth it.
Anyway, as for the controversy, I know WB is offering full refunds, regardles of playtime, for anyone, for any reason, through the end of the year, and some people are heartlessly taking advantage of that despite finishing the game, but that just isn't the right or fair thing to do if the game was playable enough to get through it.  I didn't mind waiting for the fixes (it was a banner year for great games, plenty of others to play in the meantime), and consider it money well spent. However, I do hope WB/Rocksteady learn from the opportunity and continue to support the PC market going forward.  Regardless, I still fully recommend this game; despite a little bit of tedium with the car and certain other sequences, it's really great and a worthy end to a fantastic series..

Ah, South Park The Stick Of Truth. It took a year longer to release than it should've, but it's finally here. Is it the South Park game we've been waiting for ? 'Yes, absolutely !' is what I would say.
Let's start with the graphics. The graphics are similar to the TV show, meaning they are 2D and have a bit of a grainy look. It's like watching the 2D show, there are basically no differences here.
Gameplay wise it's similar to games like Paper Mario. You walk around the town completing quests, searching for loot and taking part in battles. Quests are handed out by the people of South Park and normally consist of defeating certain enemies or finding specific items. Most of these quests are simple and relatively easy to complete, which fits the game in a way, but thankfully the main quest has a bit more variation and depth.
Note that the whole game can be completed in 10-15 hours so it's not the biggest game we've ever seen or played. And that's a good thing, because near the end of the game it starts to overstay its welcome with its repetitive nature. 'Why', you ask ? Well, the battles are turn-based and except for some stronger enemies halfway through and near the end they never become exciting or very difficult. The special powers and summons are fun to use but you've probably seen most of it, or maybe all of it, within a couple of hours. And the fact that summons can't be used for boss fights is slightly disappointing.
The humor is just fantastic, as is the voice acting. You can tell a lot of work and love was put into it. This is one of the reasons you should play The Stick Of Truth. There's some hilarious stuff in it.
One small thing that doesn't really affect my opinion of the game but should be said anyway is the fact that some of the collectibles can't be collected anymore once you've finished the story. So, to all completionists out there; make sure you grab everything before wrapping up the story.
Anyway, to wrap up my review:
South Park The Stick Of Truth is the South Park game we've been waiting for and if you even remotely enjoy the show you owe it to yourself to play it at least once. You'll have a good time with it, believe me.

Okay, now that I have some more time on my hands, I will elaborate a little more as to WHY I think you should NOT BUY this game.
To get things out of the way, in my oppinion, the game is quite solid when it comes to mechanics. Essentially, this game just adds to the formula of the first game, which is simple, but fun: Pick a class (Perk), pick a weapon, find a spot on the map where you can defend, kill hords of different monsters, buy new guns, rinse and repeat. Blasting things is fun, you need to use your head, everyone has to work to together, good times.
BUT, and this is a huge one, this game is in EARLY ACCESS - and there is certain things in EA that will irate your player base. The developers stated they wanted to do "Early access right". So far, I have to say we have different opinions on what constitutes that.
First of all, the game is behind schedule, as they wanted to release the game end of 2015, and it truly lacks hard content. It only has a handfull of maps (REALLY nice looking, atmospheric maps, admittedly), not all classes they have announced are in the game yet, each class only has very few weapons, and the balance is still basically nonexistent. Every 5 levels of a perk, you get to choose one of two abilities that, in theory, would allow you to choose between two different "playstyles" within that class. So far, however, the choises are almost ALWAYS absolute no-brainers.
All these things wouldn't be so bad, neither by themselves, nor in total - if they didn't add MICROTRANSACTIONS to the game with the latest update. Essentially, it is CS:GO's drop system for cosmetic items. There is nothing wrong with trying to increase the longevity of your product by adding microtransactions or DLC, but here, it is essentially glorified gambling - you have no guarantee to get what you want. Also, as the past with other medium sized developers has sadly shown, it is a rightful fear they might, sooner or later, hide hard content behind this gambling wall. Adding this kind of mechanics, however, when your game has not even LEFT early access, I do think is very shabby business-practice, because it only caters to people's fear that a Dev might just turn their EA-game into a quick cash grab, never add what they promised, and declare it "finished" when they can't "milk" it anymore and abandon it after full release.
Vote with your wallet to end such practices :)

I generally like rogue-like game and find some of them to be very enjoyable and addictive (Binding of Isaac, Rogue Legacy, Dungeons of Dredmor, Pixel Dungeon for example). Unfortunately, Risk of Rain is not one of them, it is way too brutal and doesn't do much to keep you interested in playing more.
To give an example, an average ennemy will take about 10 regular shots to kill. When you start, with a couple of ennemies you can handle them quite easily, but few minutes later, you will find yourself fighting against a horde of 10-15 ennemies, all running toward you. You might succeed in killing one or two, but after that you'll become overwhelmed quite fast as new ennemies are spawning as you kill them, forcing you to run away and try to avoid ennemies. When you're done with a boss, you still have to kill all remaining ennemies, which can be very hard when 20-30 are all at the same place. 1 to 3 seconds are enough for them to kill you if you don't avoid them.
The items that you can buy sometimes gives you a small advantage, but as the difficulty of the game increase the longer you play, the small advantages aren't enough to keep you continuing without getting kill.
That being said, I did enjoyed the music and the art direction of the game.
For me to recommend this game, two things would need to change: reducing the number of shots needed to kill ennemies (or make different levels of difficulty to please casual and very hardcore gamers) and remove (or make optionnal) the "gets harder the longer you play" caracteristic.

Shelved this game after 10 hours of play around launch to wait for the fixes, so five months later I've come back and finished it.  I didn't really have many performance issues at launch, but knowing the game was going to be improved, and noticing low-res in some spots, I saw the potential for a better game and decided to wait.  I'm glad I did; I came back to better performance, improved textures, had a really good time and a smooth experience.
As for the game, it's really fun, it's well-made, plays really well, has some of the most gorgeous character modeling and general aesthetics, an interesting story with a diverse cast, absolute top-notch voice acting, and is a good ending to a great series.  The car is useful and offers a fun alternative option to travel, but I did find the tank combat stuff to get pretty tedious eventually; luckily the sequences were fairly short.  Even playing on normal difficulty, I felt really challenged in quite a few spots; it can be pretty dang hard sometimes, and that made the difficulty feel a little too uneven in places.
My biggest complaint was the time-wasting search to find all of the remaining side-mission stuff after finishing the main story.  Rocksteady buried two extended endings behind the side missions, which is a nice reward for people that want more out of the game, but probably a little frustrating for people who just wanted the story.  I completed the first extended ending, which involved doing just about everything except all of the Riddler puzzles, and felt somewhat unsatisfied.  The final extended ending is buried behind 235-some Riddler puzzles, and I just didn't feel like doing that this time around; maybe I'll go back later, but there are too many other good games to play right now.  I instead watched the final extended ending online, and think I would've been disappointed for putting in the many of extra hours to finish all the Riddler puzzles, though it was a bit more satsifying, I'm not sure it would've felt worth it.
Anyway, as for the controversy, I know WB is offering full refunds, regardles of playtime, for anyone, for any reason, through the end of the year, and some people are heartlessly taking advantage of that despite finishing the game, but that just isn't the right or fair thing to do if the game was playable enough to get through it.  I didn't mind waiting for the fixes (it was a banner year for great games, plenty of others to play in the meantime), and consider it money well spent. However, I do hope WB/Rocksteady learn from the opportunity and continue to support the PC market going forward.  Regardless, I still fully recommend this game; despite a little bit of tedium with the car and certain other sequences, it's really great and a worthy end to a fantastic series..

I very much recommend Risk of Rain.
Simply put, there are no, truly new ideas here. Pixel art, an immersive soundtrack, roguelike elements, (such as randomized items enemies and locations) are all elements we have seen before.
Risk of Rain ; however, managages to bring all this together in a fun way. The first few games you will get beaten very hard. Theres a lot of fun in refining and slowly improving your approach and strategy to what the game throws at you. I remember feeling the same way about games like The Binding of Issac. Improvement is through iteration, yet somehow it all still feels fresh and exciting. Once you think you've got it - a new character, weapon or item unlocks and give everythign a suddenly fresh new take.
Perhaps one of my favorite things is the way items stack. Seeing the same item twice doesn't feel like you'v elost ground. Getting, say many missiles that increace the chance to fire a moarter blast can work toegher to turn your player into a mean machine, blasting rockets, bullets and mayhem everywhere. Theres is a great deal of satisfaction to unleashing a lot of carnage after an especially enemy filled screen or boss fight.
The slow and incremental increase of difficulty over time, prevents meaningless grinding. You find the game is now a matter of maximizing upgrading, destruction and treasure hunting vs level progression. Its a good formula- and it scales effectively.
I'm especially excited about the possibility of multiplayer, which I've yet to experience.
The only downside, if there is one- is that the characters you can play, while interestingly differnt, are also radically unbalanced in effectiveness. Some characters, like the huntress really compliment the nature of fighting enemy swarms, and tower over the other characters in overall effectiveness. the sniper, by contrast, I can only see being used as a fully support character, and is simply too unuseable, and therfore not fun or exciting to play. I consider these criticisms minor. I'd be much more nonplussed by playing carbon-copy characters with different shirt colors. The great variety of playable characters only lends to the games strength.
If you see this game on sale- just buy it. Its worth the money.

Before I get into the review proper, I want to quickly explain the context.  You may know that I recently posted an open letter over the poor state of
.  One user questioned this since I had no first-hand experience.  So with the option of an essentially no-questions-asked refund through the end of 2015, I decided to buy it to see how it performs.  You can see the letter here:
After it installed, I spent a couple of hours adjusting settings and testing through the in-game benchmark.  My system's GPU is officially BELOW the minimum requirements; I already need to upgrade for games like
.  What I discovered during testing, though, surprised me: The game was playable.  The full analysis is here:
To date, I have played about 41 hours through the campaign and sidequests, achieving 88% completion.  I did not buy or install any separate DLC; only costume packs now bundled in were also installed.  I have finished the campaign and enough sidequests to view a secondary ending; I am NOT trying to 100% it yet.  I can say that for the most part, the benchmark represented my in-game experience.  There are exceptions; I will talk more about this near the end.
If you have never played a game in the series,
is the end of a storyline which started with
.  Chronologically in terms of storyline, the games would be played in this order:
,
,
, and
.  All of the games follow roughly the same motif: You work as Batman in trying to stop some cataclysmic threat to Gotham City, all the while learning about side stories and additional tasks you can work through in order to earn combat and gadget upgrades and see additional, connected story.  You start with a decent amount of combat and gadget tricks anyway, but as you earn Wayne Tech Points, you'll earn upgrades to each.
Graphically,
looks GREAT.  I haven't posted them to Steam yet but did take screenshots of some of the early scenes.  Everything is well detailed, and standing on a rooftop and gazing at the Gotham City skyline is one of the better scenes you will find in a video game.  Even at lower settings during my testing, I admittedly couldn't tell THAT much of an improvement with the additional filtering.  Also, as my card doesn't have enough VRAM for higher texture resolution, I couldn't test this for myself, but even at lower resolution, everything appeared highly detailed.
The storyline is also incredibly detailed.  I won't spoil anything major, but we're dealing with Scarecrow, who wants to spread his fear toxin throughout Gotham and take control of the city through sheer madness, and the mysterious Arkham Knight, who has a grudge against Batman and has set out to kill him.  Your job, of course, is to prevent all of that from happening.  I like the overall setup, but I did find that deep into the campaign, it became somewhat non-sensical.  You'll have to discover this for yourself, but a few ending sections really didn't make sense to me, and I felt they somewhat detracted from the narrative instead of enhancing it.
From a gameplay standpoint, the biggest addition is the honest-to-goodness Batmobile.  This is where some of the problems come in.  Controlling the Batmobile is one of the hardest things I have ever done in gaming, and I very much developed a love-hate relationship.  I love the design and the concept, and it is fun driving around Gotham at high-speed, especially considering that so much of the environment is destructible; you can take down pillars, street signs, and at one point, I actually DROVE THROUGH a building with glass doors and windows in pursuit of a suspect.  But actually getting the Batmobile to steer can sometimes be a nightmare, and I frequently missed turns because, even though I was definitely pushing the controller in the direction I wanted it to steer, it kept driving straight ahead.  I lost many pursuits this way.  Even reversing is finicky; on a controller, pressing X both stops and shifts into reverse, but once you're IN reverse, you actually have to accelerate to stop.  This again caused me lots of trouble.  Additionally, the slow-motion effect of taking out an enemy vehicle automatically shifts your camera perspective, which can make it extremely difficult to get back to what you were doing--especially if that's chasing the next vehicle in the convoy.  Also, it feels like some Batmobile sequences are just filler to extend the story somewhat, and others are just INCREDIBLY difficult and frustrating!
Combat is a much harder affair than in the previous games, as well, and being able to execute certain quick-launch gadgets proficiently is an almost unavoidable skill in later fights.  This is something I have always struggled with, and it made these battles extremely difficult for me to win.  I have never felt that the controls for the quick-launch gadgets were very intuitive and thus couldn't memorize them.  The overall battle mechanics are still solid, and beating down a group of thugs is still loads of fun once you get the hang of everything.  But the types of enemies thrown at you in this game are sometimes much more difficult to defeat and can truly take a lot of effort.  "Predator" encounters--stealth encounters against firearm-toting enemies--also return but with a twist.  In later encounters, you'll have to learn how to deal with robotic gun turrets and flying drones.  This all makes for a much more complicated affair; while experience with previous entries in the series is certainly not mandatory, having some experience and knowledge of how all of this works can certainly be a benefit to progression in
just because of the more complicated scenarios thrown at you.
While most of my experience was smooth, I began encountering major technical issues starting at about 2/3 of the way into the story.  I began experiencing a large number of crashes, mainly dring fast-paced Batmobile chases but occasionally when gliding through Gotham.  As no error message was generated, it's impossible to say what may have caused them.  In all cases, I was able to restart the game and go on, and checkpoints are frequent enough that it caused little progress to be lost, but it was highly annoying.  These sequences also caused the most issues with stuttering and overall frame rate, though the Batmobile sequences were FAR worse.  This could simply be the result of my older hardware, but everyone should approach with caution, even at this late date since its initial removal from Steam.  Turning down the graphics settings a bit more might have helped a little bit, but I don't think it would have completely resolved this.
I also had two instances of falling through the world--one during a boss fight!  Oddly, I didn't have to restart the game; they resolved themselves into a recovery of sorts that let me continue, but they were jarring, to say the least.  I was in the Batmobile for each.  But maybe such clipping has been dealt with in a way that doesn't completely halt the game, at least in these experiences.
So is it worth purchasing?  I can't answer that; the scope and severity of technical issues plaguing the actual software is so broad that you really have no choice but to try it for yourself and hope for the best.  If it works, you likely will love it if you're a Batman fan; as a game, I LOVE
.  But I can't give a full recommendation, either.  Take advantage of the unlimited refunds and try it if you're interested; you probably won't ever get another chance like this with ANY game on Steam.
6.5 out of 10 (7.5 if technical issues are fixed later)

Ah, South Park The Stick Of Truth. It took a year longer to release than it should've, but it's finally here. Is it the South Park game we've been waiting for ? 'Yes, absolutely !' is what I would say.
Let's start with the graphics. The graphics are similar to the TV show, meaning they are 2D and have a bit of a grainy look. It's like watching the 2D show, there are basically no differences here.
Gameplay wise it's similar to games like Paper Mario. You walk around the town completing quests, searching for loot and taking part in battles. Quests are handed out by the people of South Park and normally consist of defeating certain enemies or finding specific items. Most of these quests are simple and relatively easy to complete, which fits the game in a way, but thankfully the main quest has a bit more variation and depth.
Note that the whole game can be completed in 10-15 hours so it's not the biggest game we've ever seen or played. And that's a good thing, because near the end of the game it starts to overstay its welcome with its repetitive nature. 'Why', you ask ? Well, the battles are turn-based and except for some stronger enemies halfway through and near the end they never become exciting or very difficult. The special powers and summons are fun to use but you've probably seen most of it, or maybe all of it, within a couple of hours. And the fact that summons can't be used for boss fights is slightly disappointing.
The humor is just fantastic, as is the voice acting. You can tell a lot of work and love was put into it. This is one of the reasons you should play The Stick Of Truth. There's some hilarious stuff in it.
One small thing that doesn't really affect my opinion of the game but should be said anyway is the fact that some of the collectibles can't be collected anymore once you've finished the story. So, to all completionists out there; make sure you grab everything before wrapping up the story.
Anyway, to wrap up my review:
South Park The Stick Of Truth is the South Park game we've been waiting for and if you even remotely enjoy the show you owe it to yourself to play it at least once. You'll have a good time with it, believe me.

Re-Release Review. Run on a PC able to handle the game.  This is a review of the game as I experienced it. This has nothing to do with the Pre-Order/broken drama.
My PC rough spec: 32gb ram, 2 x 980ti, ssd, i7-5930k, Win 10 Pro(fresh install)
I bought the game when it was re-releaed, I'm lucky enough to have a new Pc so performance wasn't an issue. I had all the graphics and Nvidia goodies maxed out.  At first I ran the game in 4k but ended up running it in 1440 as there was little to no difference visually and I lost about 5-10 fps overall.  These were the settings I ended up on, with the results of the Benchmark.
The 15 fps dip was at the very start of the benchmark test  for the first couple of seconds only. Nvidias effects are really nice, it is a shame they are so demanding. The smoke is particualrly impressive..
99% of the time the game ran smooth, the only jitters were on a couple of the cutscenes towards the end. I got lucky I guess but I had no crashes or Glitches throughout the game.
Pros:
Story. The side quests blend in with the main story nicely and don't extract from the feel of the game
Voice Acting. From the main characters to the generic thugs, all of the voice acting is brillant.
Ambience. The constant conversations taking place all around the city as you pass adds life to the gameplay.
Melee Combat. Simply the best system in any game.
Puzzles. Alot of these were great fun, none really felt like a chore or grind.
The Car. The handling is the best I've experienced on a keyboard.
Mobility. Both in the car and while gliding are extremely fast, this title seems to have polished the flying system a little, much sleeker than Origins.
Audio. Great combat thuds and bangs, the car is good enough, and the music is superb.
Cons:
Some minor cutscene stuttering,
All of the still images used during loading/save screens, I'm not sure if this was intended or it is a glitch but they all have a primitive look to them, lots of dots. Just didnt look nice to me.
Overall I thoroughly enjoyed the game from start to finish, the trophy puzzles, the car, melee combat, stealth, pretty much everything about it. I know this will probably be an unpopular opinion but I thought it was a great game. I have played the other Arkham titles and this one easily ranks near the top if not at the top for me.
If you have a powerful enough pc, at least until it's better optimized, then I would recommend this game in a heartbeat.

I very much recommend Risk of Rain.
Simply put, there are no, truly new ideas here. Pixel art, an immersive soundtrack, roguelike elements, (such as randomized items enemies and locations) are all elements we have seen before.
Risk of Rain ; however, managages to bring all this together in a fun way. The first few games you will get beaten very hard. Theres a lot of fun in refining and slowly improving your approach and strategy to what the game throws at you. I remember feeling the same way about games like The Binding of Issac. Improvement is through iteration, yet somehow it all still feels fresh and exciting. Once you think you've got it - a new character, weapon or item unlocks and give everythign a suddenly fresh new take.
Perhaps one of my favorite things is the way items stack. Seeing the same item twice doesn't feel like you'v elost ground. Getting, say many missiles that increace the chance to fire a moarter blast can work toegher to turn your player into a mean machine, blasting rockets, bullets and mayhem everywhere. Theres is a great deal of satisfaction to unleashing a lot of carnage after an especially enemy filled screen or boss fight.
The slow and incremental increase of difficulty over time, prevents meaningless grinding. You find the game is now a matter of maximizing upgrading, destruction and treasure hunting vs level progression. Its a good formula- and it scales effectively.
I'm especially excited about the possibility of multiplayer, which I've yet to experience.
The only downside, if there is one- is that the characters you can play, while interestingly differnt, are also radically unbalanced in effectiveness. Some characters, like the huntress really compliment the nature of fighting enemy swarms, and tower over the other characters in overall effectiveness. the sniper, by contrast, I can only see being used as a fully support character, and is simply too unuseable, and therfore not fun or exciting to play. I consider these criticisms minor. I'd be much more nonplussed by playing carbon-copy characters with different shirt colors. The great variety of playable characters only lends to the games strength.
If you see this game on sale- just buy it. Its worth the money.

Charming little indie title creatively named 'Risk of Rain' even though dire weather conditions will be the least likely of your concerns in-game. Much like its rouge-like indie brethren, 'The Binding of Isaac' & 'Rogue Legacy', Risk of Rain has the player trekking through randomly generated stages, looking for a way forward whilst searching for powerful items that, in hope, will make you broken enough to tackle the overwhelming odds the game throws at you.
Make no mistake when I say that this game is HARD, as hard as any of the titles previously mentioned, but perhaps a bit more forgiving than both. There is always a clear sense of progression even though it is a rouge-like and the real draw of the game lies in its -class- system. The player is given the option of choosing between 10 different characters at the start of every playthrough, most of which are unlocked by meeting special conditions. There are tons of unlockables and each character has a highly unique, defined skillset and play style, which add endless flavor to the game because not only are you getting a different experience each time with the randomly generated stages; each run can also be worlds apart due to how each class plays out.
Overall, a really great gem of a game and there's not much I have to say about it from a negative standpoint. It can be a little frustrating at the very start with nothing unlocked and only one character available, but it is only a matter of time before the game opens up and becomes far more enjoyable. The item buffs you can collect are all fairly ingenious and well thought-out but the game suffers a little from framerate issues in the final stages. Although that could be expected what with the -hundreds of missiles- probably flying around on your screen by then.  ;)
A risk of rain?  Maybe not.
A risk of losing track of time?  Most definitely.

Oh how I love Civilization, especially Civ V. The in-depth feel to it, overall, as well as the complexity of not only your world, and your oppoents, but your own empire, leads me to game after game played consecutively for hours upon hours. It's amazing.
That said, Civ V is definitely not for everyone. Anyone who enjoys an excellent turn-based strategy will eat it up, and love it forever. But it's a complex game, so anyone who prefers a game in which they can simply get in and get going is way out of their comfort zone. Fans of simple games where there isn't much to consider are also going to want to stay away.

Batman Arkham Knight should have been the epic sequel everybody wanted to Arkham City. There are a number of changes that improve upon the old, but overall, what they have added to the game lowers its value to point where it is definitely
Yes, even worse than Origins. Origins was a blatant copy of a game that worked great (Arkham City), so it is more of the same. Arkham Knight tries to improve upon the old, but it fails fantastically.
Contrast Issues - Possibly the worst part of combat in AK is the total lack of contrast. Enemies, props, the environment, 2D effects, all blend in to the background because everything is the same color. The predominate colors are black, gray, red, and green. Only riddler objects are green. Everything else is some shade of gray-red. This causes a significant eye strain on the player due to the fact everything is hard to see in your periphery. Very often I am hit simply because I did not see the enemy in time. Red Counter enemies can be hard to identify, because their prompt is red like everything else. This lack of contrast makes for a very frustrating experience.
Red Unavoidable - There are certain enemies that have undefendable “red prompts” during combat. In Arkham City this was limited to a selection of enemies. I did not like the red prompts in Arkham City that much since it was a little difficult to remember how to counter them, at first. Eventually, I could remember. In AK there are too many red prompts, so I can not keep track of how to counter what. There are also ways to defeat red counters, such as doing anything to a thug with a gun, or bataranging a charging thug. Being able to easily defeat red prompted thugs takes all of the challenge out of it and makes the red prompt more confusing. The lack of contrast in the game means I usually get shot by a thug with a gun since I always assume there is nothing I can do about the red prompt. Then I remember, after being shot in the back. Not fun.
Big Guys - I absolutely adore the new Big Guy mechanics in AK. Countering the minigun guy is fun. Figuring out how to beat up the Big Guys in combat, especially the electrical, is a lot of fun for me. However, there are certain predator missions where the objective is simply beat up the Big Guy without being caught by other Big Guys. Since the only counter to them is the beatdown it makes Big Guy gameplay in certain predator missions a bore. 1 or 2 big guys, sure, but too many and it feels like a chore. I always thought the point was to creatively take out one’s opponents, but with Big Guys there is only one way.
The Good - Dual Team Combat, new Big Guys (electrical is my favorite), playing as Nightwing and Catwoman. Oh wait, I played as those guys in Arkham City. Not much has improved on Batman’s combat.
Difficulty - The difficulty in predator missions has been massively nerfed. Instead of a scenario in which Batman must think how to achieve the goal, you simply attack the guards one by one in any order. You can use the numerous floor grates the Gotham City Council put in everywhere for no apparent reason. Or you can use the many perches, vents, tight rope wires, etc. Most predator maps have roughly the same number of safety zones like perches and vents, so there is not much variety.
Alarm Collars - Every predator mission feels the same to me, the challenge barely changes. The neck collars worn by inmates in Arkham City no longer exist, there is nothing replacing or improving that mechanic. Players can kill enemies in any order without fear of getting caught often, since guards have idea who is dead until they walk near them. If guards walk near them it is very easy to attack them as well. Most of my predator missions ended with a solitary pile of guard bodies.
Silent Takedowns - The radius for takedowning enemies has been increased, thereby decreasing the difficulty too much. There is little risk in performing a silent takedown.
Fear Takedowns - Fear takedowns were enjoyable at first, because it looked cool and played in to the dominating aspect of Batman. However, as the game went on I realized they became a crutch for players. It feels like somebody put Fear Takedowns in the game because a playtester said something like “Predator missions are long and boring, I only like combat!”. Fear Takedowns subvert having to eliminate guards, thereby lowering the challenge and importance of Predator missions. Eventually, I stopped the Fear Takedowning because it got in the way of fun.
Environmental Takedowns - In Arkham City environmental takedowns stunned enemies, forcing the player to swoop in and kill or merely use it as a distraction. In AK they kill on contact. First thing you do in a Predator mission is look for environmental objects like machines and use the, to eliminate your guards easily, and without effort. Screw that. I play games to have fun and challenge myself, not bypass content because I am lazy.
Two Face - There is only one predator mission with some kind of challenge, and that is Two Face’s mission. There the player can kill loudly without fear of being caught due to a loud alarm. Once Two Face’s thugs realize Batman is Batmaning them they go on full alert. This creates a more interesting scenario for players since it changes conditions forcing them to think about their tactics. Every other predator mission is the same compared to this one.
Driving - Driving the Batmobile in AK seems like the coolest feature ever. Hooray, the BATMOBILE!! Instead, it becomes an unnecessary device in Batman’s arsenal. The Batmobile can drive through anything, and I mean anything. Mailboxes, traffic lights, freeway supports, sides of buildings, churches, etc. Few objects in AK stop the player from driving the Batmobile. Batman AK is no GTA, Gran Turismo, or Mario Kart, I get that, it is not a driving game. But that’s exactly the problem. Driving is too easy in AK, there is no challenge to it. The car makes things too easy in some cases, such as killing riddler spies, and allowing the player to run down APCs. There are even a number potential predator missions that are finished completely by a few hits of the Batmobile’s Bathowitzer. Driving the Batmobile DOES NOT fit within the fantasy of Batman.
Riddler Challenges - A number of Riddler challenges involve the Batcar. I think it is good Rocksteady is playing with the Riddler levels (since they suck), but they failed in trying to improve them. The Riddler Racing levels were a chore, nothing more. This is not a racing game, it is a Batman game. When I think of Riddler I do not think of a underground race track organizer. I always thought Riddler tried to challenge Batman with riddles, not set up a race track for him to drive on. Riddler racing does not fit within the fantasy of Batman.
BatFlying - Flying as Batman is a superior form of travel than using the Batmobile. When I fly in AK have an advantage over the world, I can drop in on enemies. Flying tends to be faster as there is few objects to stop me. Most importantly, flight fits within the fantasy of BATman. Swooping in a killing a thug while flying is far more satisfying that running them down with a car.

I've tried to like this game, I really have.  It has nice graphics, some good music, overall the game is well presented, but as a strategy game it lacks a certain something.  There are good points to the gameplay, such as the hexes and the one unit per tile system, but too much has been "streamlined" (ie dumbed down) for this game to be rewarding.  And the fact of the matter is, it's too much like a boardgame, and not enough like a grand strategy game that makes you feel like you're running a country, let alone building an empire.  From the outset  it's obvious the game wants to make you go "tall", ie build four or at most five cities, go for tradition, and win a science or culture victory.  Boring, boring, boring.  Large, sprawling empires are almost discouraged due to ludicrous penalties to your nation's happiness, making it difficult for large empires to be viable, especially on higher difficulties, and disincentivising the player from coming up with their own strategies for winning (or even building and maintaining an empire) which is - to me at any rate - completely contradictory to what Civ has always been about.
Like I said, this game has its good points, but it is definitely more of a "gamey" game (if that makes sense) than the previous Civs, and for that it loses a lot.

This is the first time I've ever felt compelled to write a game review.  To start, I am a huge Batman and Arkham series fan.  I have all the games on both Xbox 360 and PC (who can resist Steam sales).  When Arkahm knight first came out it had some major issues; however, mine weren't that bad actually.  I removed the FPS cap and actually had decent frame rates with the game maxed out (with all the Nvidia stuff turned off since I'm using 2 7970s in crossfire).  I could put up with the FPS drops while gliding and fighting big groups of thugs becuase they weren't actually game breaking, annoying yes, game breaking no.  My biggest issue was when calling the Batmobile.  My game would somtimes drop to single digit FPS during the first few seconds but then normalize after that.  I put up with all of that and beat the game and actually enjoyed it for the most part, well except for the too often and too drawn out tank stealth battles.  I would say the game is slightly better than Origins but not as good as City.  I was content with my purchase.
Now comes the issues.  After the game was re-released on Steam and after having a large patch, I was hoping for a smoother experience.  I was also excited to finally play the DLC I payed for when I got the Season Pass at launch.  Well...my game won't even launch now.  I found a "fix" where I had to delete a certain .ini file to get it to work.  That did work and the game launched, but now I had graphical glitches everhwere.  Whole areas of textures and even small patches of polygons would continuously flicker making it nearly impossible to play.  I also could no longer max the settings like I could before.  The 4 months or so that WB and Rocksteady took to fix the game didn't really fix much on my end and actually made the game worse.  I'm glad they are honoring refunds until the end of 2015 no matter how long you played, that's good of them.  It's also a sign that they know how broken the game is.  I have 40ish hours into the game and I got a refund because the improvments made that game worse for me.  Some, hopefully, see a drastic improvment.  However, I did not and got my money back.
I will probably buy this game again to complete my Arkham collection, but only after it is heavily discounted and bundles all of the DLC.  I can't really be mad about all of the problems since WB is refunding everyone's money no matter how long they've played it.  But I am very disappointed with the entire experience.  Not a good way for the Arkham franchise to end.

So my number one problem with this game was that, while feeling incredibly polished, it lacked any real depth or feeling of personality whatsoever. What I mean by that is killing floor 1 had 6 different classes in the game, and each felt INCREDIBLY unique and different from eachother and filled completely different roles. Killing floor 2 took a massive leap backwords in this aspect at launch and throughout essentially the games entire lifespan up until this point. Even though there were many different classes in the game (more than kf1), none of them felt special in anyway. The perks have a leveling system (up to 25) and I reached level 17 on "commando", who is supposed to be the small zed killer. After that I got kind of bored of him so decided to try the other classes some more. I was incredibly disappointed to discover that, while on the outside they appeared very different, in reality every single class felt exactly the same just with slightly different guns. Classes didn't fill a "role" anymore, they all filled the same role of simply killing♥♥♥♥♥♥(excluding the medic, who could heal I guess).
So this recent patch (which can be seen here
) tripwire interactive FINALLY looks like they are starting to try to remedy this. I haven't gotten my hands on the patch yet (slow internet) but as you can see they have DRASTICALLY reworked several of the classes skill trees, giving each class a far greater purpose and driving them towards filling an actual role instead of being reskinned versions of eachother.

OK, this is the third review I am writing... as I progressed through the game, I deleted the previous one, and I believe this will be the final version.
Before I go on: I am very well aware that a lot of people are still having trouble with the game. Yes, it was one of the worst game launches in a long time, shouldn't have happened that way.However, I will not let that influence my rating, as the review and rating are based on the way the game works TODAY (for me), and the game itself. I didn't get the game until September or so, and it worked perfectly well almost immediately
I do have an i7-4790, 16 gigs of Ram, a GTX 960 with 4 gigs of Ram, using the settings suggested by GForce experience.
After the patches/fixes that have been released (today's the 7th of Nov), the game works absolutely fine for me, no reasons to complain. The performance is great, no frame rate issues at all.
Gotham looks beautiful, and I love the atmosphere of the game. Basically, it's another No Man's Land type situation, which kinda makes sense because otherwise, you'd run over citizens by the hundreds in your batmobile.
Which leads me to the biggest innovation of AK, the batmobile/battank.
I admit it is fun to race around Gotham in that thing. Driving is nice, the thing is pretty tough, like a tank, so you can run into walls etc, destroy fences etc. In battle-mode, there are some nice tricks you can do, and the controls are totally different. It somehow reminds me of that DaVinci-tank in AC: Brotherhood... and I wonder whether the handling and "style" of the battle mode was inspired by this.
Melee is fun as well, blocking works great, so do special combos. Eventually, you will need to use them to handle enemies with stun batons, shields, swords etc. It can be rough, but I never thought it was unfair. In some cases, like bank robberies, you should approach it tactically.
The boss fights are fun as well. They can be rough, but again, not unfair. Yes, it took me quite some time to take out the Arkham Knight's imba vehicles, but boy, was it satisfying.
Where the game absolutely SHINES is atmosphere and writing. I love the story. I am sure most of you know the big reveals in the game, but still, I'll try not to mention them. The state Batman is in, which kinda makes it harder for him, is extremely well done (with a certain villain talking to you a lot), and the end of that state is TOTALLY great.
There are some very very cool throwbacks to "A Death In The Family", which, to me as a fan of the comics, was a very special treat.
There are some very surprising twists in the story, not only the two big reveals I mentioned. Up until the very end, I felt entertained, and I thoroughly enjoyed the story and working my way through it...the boss fights were harrowing, but ultimately satisfying.
Now, for the negative parts (IMO):
- There is too much focus on using the mobile. Yes, I can understand they put a lot of work into the mobile, but it felt TOO much... fighting gazillions of drones, driving around, having to find ways of getting your batmobile into a certain area or building to use it to progress... it is ok, but I wish they had cut the amount of driving, drone fighting and "need to find a way to get the mobile in here" by about 30-40%.  YMMV
- The "after death teases". They are part of the series, sure, but they eventually got more than frustrating. They were tiring, especially with stuff like the Riddler challenges (races, riddles, etc.) which I didn't enjoy at all.
- The ending of the game, IMO, ROCKED; but... I didn't like the fact you have to complete ALL of the side-stuff in order to see the ultimate ending (Knightfall protocol). I loved playing the main-storyline, but when I realized I still had to finish ALL the side stuff to see that final part, I didn't like it. It DOES make sense that you need to do all that, considering what Knightfall is, but... I LIKED the fact that I didn't HAVE to do all the side stuff. Some of them were fun, but I liked that I had the freedom to leave out some of them. However, if you want to see the final ending, you will have to.
I wouldn't mind this, if not for the final, very frustrating Riddler challenge. I thought that some of his challenges (hint: glide and final race) were WAY harder than anything I had to do in the main-storyline. Add his very repetitve teasing and ridicule, it kinda sucks the fun out of stuff
So, PROs:
- GREAT storyline
- Some killer twists and surprises in the story (even without the Arkham Knight stuff, which at some point became predictable)
- Great atmosphere
- Graphics
- Sound/Music
- Some of the Batmobile related stuff
- New gadgets and moves
- Appearance of some lesser known villains, sometimes in a surprising way
- Duo fights...a ton of fun.  they could have put in more of that, but thats a minor complaint
Cons:
- Too much batmobile (way too much)
- Need to do every single side-quest to get the final ending
- Riddler challenges...from fun to challenging to frustrating with too much repetitive voice-acting
