If you like South Park then buy this game!
Right, now that we have that out of the way I will keep this brief. This is as close to playing South Park the TV show as we will ever get. The writing, art style and voice acting (original cast) is superb and perfectly matches the show in every way. For long time fans the game is pack full of easter eggs, side quests, in jokes and general hilarity.
The gameplay features light RPG elements with turn based JRPG style combat that is funny, fluid and deep enough to keep you interested and wanting to try new things without being overly complex. I did find that towards the end of the game I was avoiding combat as the encounters can get grating if they happen over and over, however this is also a testament to how good the writing and story is, as I simply wanted to push on and see what was next.
The combat is broken up by interesting mini games and simple puzzle elements. All in all South Park: The Stick of Truth is a fun light RPG but it is a stellar South Park game. If you don't like South Park you won't like what you find here but if you are even vaguely interested in the show or enjoying RPGs then this is worth a try.
My only real criticism is the limited replay value but other than that I enjoyed every second of this game and it's been years since I laughed so hard in an RPG.

But it's a complex game, so anyone who prefers a game in which they can simply get in and get going is way out of their comfort zone. Fans of simple games where there isn't much to consider are also going to want to stay away.
So, if you don't like keeping tabs on many things at once, weighing many different options, or any other complicated mechanics, this isn't your cup of metaphorical tea. But, if you enjoy a good strategy game that's a bit different from the others (at least the other's I've played), definitely pick this game up.

Incredible good game. If you like roguelikes and sidescrolling-shooters, you should grab it because it combines all the good things from both genres.
Graphics early on in the game aren't that impressive, but as you get more upgrades it's fun to watch everything die and i like the artstyle overall. The Soundtrack is really good as well.
The game is unforgivingly hard, but always fair and offers an insane amount of replayability. It doesn't screw you, if you die it's your fault most of the time. Sure you can get bad rolls on the items but that's the nature of roguelikes. Controls are tight and responsive, keys are fully rebindable on both keyboard and gamepad.
From a gameplaystandpoint there is to say, that difficulty increases over time, not due to progression on each level. You need to find a balance between grinding for upgrades and progressing to later levels. There is also a semi-progression-system in the game, where you unlock additional items, but you don't get them at the start of a new game, you still have to find or buy them.
Overall it's an incredible game and i absolutely recommend it to everyone with the slightest interest in roguelikes.

I have never left a review for a game before, but being a huge Batman fan and a big fan of the Arkham series in general I feel like I have to write something about this game and the experience I have had with it.
First off, I would like to say I have completed this game once, on hard mode ( played the previous games a lot so I know a combo or two haha ). However I didn't complete it on pc ( will get to this later ) I got a PS4 copy and played it on that. I enjoyed the game enough to finiish the story, but I didn't fall in love wiith it the way I did Asylum or city. Heres why.
Batmobile : I know theres many posts everywhere about how this ruined the game and to an extent I agree. The batmobile could have been great, I think it feels good when you drive it ( using a controller ) and I actually really enjoyed the tank battles, on hard mode there are some pretty tough ones that took me quite a few tries to get past. The big problem with the batmobile ( to me this is a huge issue ) is how forced you are to use it and how much of the feel of the previous games it takes away. In the campaigns off the older games I always loved the feeling of anticipation you got when you knew you where coming to a big fight or a big boss battle because the atmosphere of the city or asylum changed ( music, what villains on the ground spoke about etc ). You could feel the tension building thought the game to the big scenes and I just didn't get that feeling this time. Although a lot of that is really not the batmobiles fault I think it plays a big part in loss of atmosphere, the entire game has been changed to accomodate it and it was unnecessary.
Fighting : A lot smoother than the older games but no where near as many large scale fights in the campaign ( more tank battles than anything ) there is a lot of challenge maps though.
Story : I got bored with it and didn't care by the time the big reveal came of who the Arkham Knight is, it did have it's good points throught the campign, but as I said above, it would have been helped by less batmobile. Remember the part in Arkham City where you need to steathily glide around the map and take snipers out while the joker has Talia at the cinema, that atmosphere was what these games where about to me, and unfortunatley there are no moments like this in Arkham Knight because instead of glidiing around quietly, you would smash into the cinema in your big tank.
The game is not as bad as some of the reviews I have read, but my experi ence with it has been horrible. After waiting patiently for it to come out, upgrading my pc with a new nvidia 970 card becuase I got this game free with it and wanted to enjoy the final part of the trilogy in the best possible quality that I could afford, it still doesn't work properlly. I wanted to play the game so bad that I ended up buying it on PS4 ( it stutters pretty bad on this at points too ) and played it so that spoilers wouldn't ruin it for me. The story was NOT worth this much effort.
2 huge patches later and this game still looks and runs much better on my PS4 than my PC, since I got it for free and can't get a refund, it will sit in my Steam Library unplayed forever.
I really think Warner Brothers and Rocksteady should be ashamed of themselves with what has happened to the PC port of this game, basically, they didn't try.
If your a huge fan of Batman or this series I would suggest picking up a second hand copy of the game for one of the consoles if you have one, storywise it is not worth full price, and on the pc it is a total joke.

I've tried to like this game, I really have.  It has nice graphics, some good music, overall the game is well presented, but as a strategy game it lacks a certain something.  There are good points to the gameplay, such as the hexes and the one unit per tile system, but too much has been "streamlined" (ie dumbed down) for this game to be rewarding.  And the fact of the matter is, it's too much like a boardgame, and not enough like a grand strategy game that makes you feel like you're running a country, let alone building an empire.  From the outset  it's obvious the game wants to make you go "tall", ie build four or at most five cities, go for tradition, and win a science or culture victory.  Boring, boring, boring.  Large, sprawling empires are almost discouraged due to ludicrous penalties to your nation's happiness, making it difficult for large empires to be viable, especially on higher difficulties, and disincentivising the player from coming up with their own strategies for winning (or even building and maintaining an empire) which is - to me at any rate - completely contradictory to what Civ has always been about.
Like I said, this game has its good points, but it is definitely more of a "gamey" game (if that makes sense) than the previous Civs, and for that it loses a lot.

The summer sale may have already destroyed my wallet, but it's the game I spent the least on that I've gotten the most enjoyment. The game is simply brilliant, from the addicting rogue like gameplay to the excellent electronic soundtrack. If you enjoy challenging gameblay, roguelike RPG's, or sidescrolling games this is simply a must bnuy, and I highly reccomend it to anybody else.
Like any roguelike game this game does not hold back on the difficulty, but what's great about this one is that while the game is always challenging it has a perfect learning curve. You brobably wonn't make it 5 minutes your first playthrough, but each subbsequent playthrough you'll be able to see yourself getting better and better, you never feel like you're stuck at a certain point. This is a huge part of what makes the game so addicting, the ability to see yourself improve is satisfying beyond belief.
The game becomes increasingly difficult as time goes on as well as advancing through stages, so the player must balance taking time to unlocking new items and rushing through the next level. There are a few options for which  version of a stage you will play, for example the first level may take place in a desert stage, a lake stage, and a few other options, and each time the stage will be slightly different than the last time it was played. This makes it possible for experienced players to become familiar with different stage without making the levels predictable or easy.
The game boasts local and online multiplayer, and the co op play is a blast too. The fact that pleyers do not share items is a bit annoying, and since it is not possible to trade items it is hard to make sure your team mates are properly equipped. Also, online multiplayer is a bit unfinished so joining a game can be problematic, but the developers insist this is only a temporary issue and will be fixed, but is still worth mentioning (if this has been adressed at the time of reading, ignore this part).
So far, my only other real complaint is the difficulty of unlocking new characters. In fact, that''s why I did not mention them earlier, I have only played with two so far. The challenges required to unlock characters are tedious and/or excessively difficult, to the point that the casual player may only unlock two or three ne characters, and only after a very long time playing.
I highly reccomend anybody buy this game, and during a sale there is simply no reason to pick this one up

Gotta say, after playing The Stick of Truth, I hope that they NEVER make another South Park game without Trey Parker and Matt Stone's heavy influence on its development. Stick of Truth is literally everything that you could want from a South Park game, and actually is great in it's own right as well. The game is literally filled with references from the show (and I don't just mean that figuratively: the main characters' closets are LITERALLY filled with references). I also love the game's story, being about kids role playing as fantasy warriors and having imaginary wars with each other over "whoever controls the universe". It captures this set up perfectly, and kinda makes me miss the days when I did this as a kid. The whole plot also makes it so that you don't necesarily have to be a huge fan of the show to get the plot, since your character is a new kid in South Park and all the other characters treat you as such. However, non-fans will unfortunately not get all of the references and obscure characters from the show. Also, as expected from South Park, the writing is freaking hilarious, having laugh out loud joke after laugh out loud joke with no decrease in quality. The crudeness that was so upfront and hilarious from the show is back and better than ever, to the point where I'd even say it's more crude than Conker's Bad Fur Day.
And I have to say, making your own character and exploring the world of South Park is awesome. There is quite a bit of visual customization so if you really want to, you can recreate yourself as a South Park kid. The visuals really bring the South Park experience to full effect, with everything looking and moving exactly like the show. Also, exploring the town of South Park is a lot of fun, with tons of different areas all from the show like the School and the houses of the main cast. You also get to meet so many characters from the show, like Mr. Garrison, Randy Marsh, Al Gore, and Jesus. The developers wanted to create the ultimate immersive South Park experience, and they nailed it perfectly.
The combat is also a lot of fun, taking inspiration from action RPGs like the Mario RPGs (Paper Mario and Mario and Luigi specifically). The game uses action commands in order to effectively attack to increase your attacks' damage or block to decrease incoming damage. You also get to pick from one of six characters from the show to serve as your battle partners, who can be swapped out at will mid battle. Out of all of the partners, I personally found Butters and Kyle to be the most useful. You also get to pick from one of four classes, Fighter, Mage, Rogue, and Jew (let's face it, you all laughed when you first heard that, as did I XD). Each has their own unique abilities in battle, such as the mage "casting spells" by using regular objects, like waving a sparkler in someone's face until they catch fire (so wonderfully BRUTAL). You can equip your character with a wide arrangement of weapons and equipment you find or buy ingame, each with their own stats and effects. You can also earn perks that give your character permanent status effects by gaining friends in South Park and adding them on your ingame Facebook page. I gotta say, though, the game is pretty easy, even on hardcore mode, so don't expect this to be that challenging of a game. Also, in terms of RPG standards, the game is pretty short. Side quests included, the game should take you about 11-12 hours. Even though the combat is easy and the game is a bit short, it's still is a ton of fun to play.
All in all, South Park Stick of Truth is a great game. It may have a few flaws, but it's easily forgiveable for it's strategic yet engaging gameplay, it's laugh out loud storyline, it's and expertly and loyally crafted atmosphere. If your a fan of the show, this is a must have. If you don't know the show much but your a fan of RPGs, I think you'll still get a lot of enjoyment out of it.

Batman Arkham Knight Review:
CEO: We are going to release a 2.5gb patch to our game
Employee: And what will we improve
CEO: Well we'll make it run worse than before and add literally nothing else
Employee: I said improve
CEO: Oh, sorry. I misheard. I thought you said "how are we gonna get MORE NEGATIVE REVIEWS ON STEAM".
Performance:
This game runs horribly. I used to run at low settings, 1080p, with AA and 8x Anisotropic filtering, and run at a solid 60fps. Now I run 900p with AA off and 2x Anisotropic, and the game runs at 40fps. Rocksteady need to sort out their PC port. They had to relaunch there game because of the port, and it went from bad at launch, better after an update, to worse than ever after a 2.5gb patch.
Gameplay:
The batmobile in the game seems a bit overused. It is used for a lot of puzzles, and gets a bit boring. The combat is as fun as ever, utilizing counters a lot. Rocksteady have added some new moves as well. The new gadgets such as the remote hacking device are fun and well utilized, and are actually very useful in many situations. For example, you can knockout a goon by turning on the escalator, or setting off an explosion. I do find it quite funny that once a goon is knocked out, you can shoot them as much as you like with your lethal cannons and guns on the batmobile. Of course they are not dead though, because that would make it too dark.
Missions:
There is a good variety of story missions in the game, and a lot of side missions as well. An example of variety in the story is
At this point, I have finished the story, and it is a good length. It did not drag on like Saints row (my opinion as Saints row IV got very boring as I played the story), and is not too short like Mirrors Edge (an enjoyable game, but I was finished with the story within 3 hours). The side missions contain a lot of the regular batman villians, like Two Face and Penguin, and involve stopping their crime gangs for good. These are fun, and give you a lot of upgrade points, which like the other batman games, let you upgrade gadgets, and unlock new moves.
Conclusion:
Batman: Arkham Knight is a very fun game. The story is enjoyable, and even 29 hours in I am enjoying slowy completing all the quest lines. I just wish that Rocksteady would fix their PC port. It makes the game in some cases unplayable, and I will most likely be refunding the game when I get the oppurtunity.

Missions score: Side missions: 9 (a lot of batmobile use, but feels satisfying to take down crime gangs and villians)

Every aspect of the Killing Floor experience has been improved dramatically from the original, with a sad exception: content. Sure, the original killing floor has had years to build up stacks of custom maps, DLC and other neat additions to keep the game alive; but with that said, Killing Floor 2 put itself at a severe disadvantage by gimping the core of varied gameplay- A wide selection of classes. It could've panned out, with regular updates adding real, worthwhile content to the game. It has not panned out. What we get instead is a glacially slow, irregular move towards the finished product. The confusing choice to add skins (more than any other content, really) has not actually hurt the game, but it'll leave you feeling bitter and a bit messed around.
Even with typically Early Access behaviour such as this I might still have given this game a tentative recommendation because for some people there will be enough here to enjoy right now. It's not hard to see why: with satisfying gunplay, gorgeous and visceral visuals and all around refinement of the central mechanics I'll guarantee you'll have fun with the game. The problem is whether the fun will last, or whether you'll burn out before development is completed, robbing yourself of truly enjoying the superior end product. After all, completion of development is a big question mark ever since the 2015 promise was thrown out.
Finally, the truly depressing factor which tips me over the edge into not recommending the game is the surreptitious addition of microtransactions, during development and without warning.
So right now, I cannot pretend the game is not, at its heart, very good. What matters more is that by buying it now you're either robbing yourself of what is probably going to be a superior initial experience with the finished product or leaving yourself open to the developer adding other nasty surprises such as microtransactions (à la Payday 2, which this game styles itself a little too closely to already.)
With all this in mind, don't buy this, not for a while at least.

This Review is more a little techhelp to decide whether your RIG is good enough or not.
With full details, everything on max at 1080p the game uses 4116MB of VRAM. Nvidia gameworks doesn't add to the load.
This is about 20MB more then 4GB cards have and the average 3GB card is hopeless lost.

Only when the game saves i get short delays, which result out of my PCIe SSD. (These babies are fast as light, but need a second or two to get ready for writing)
I run the game smoothly at 60FPS without any drops till now (I know 2hrs atm aren't that much, but enough to test a lot of funny things out with the batmobil)

Reflex: Performance Enhancement via Super Hexagon
The gameplay videos of Super Hexagon do very little to show the depth of the gameplay. Yes, it is a very flat-looking game. And all you can control is a small pointer circling either clockwise or counter-clockwise, which has to duck into the dark, safe, areas and avoid the white area as everything in your visual field spins and closes in. My first reaction was, "This can't be good for my eyes. But maybe its good for my brain." As I adjusted to the initial frustration of dying after a few seconds repeatedly and cursing and wanting to quit, I tried to memorize patterns. And there are patterns, but they are far from static. I was just trying to survive 11 seconds of gameplay, then 18, then I hoped to reach the 20 seconds that would begin the next, "level." But after surviving until about 25 seconds, I died and started over, now with the benchmark for the next "level" at 45.
It wasn't a total shock to find this kind of retro difficulty from Terry Cavanaugh, who created the delightful 8-bit style platformer, VVVVVV. In that game my cute on-screen character always respawns a short distance from where he was, ready to repeat the previous challenge. Not so here.
Super Hexagon appeals to a darker part of me which strives for an unattainable perfection. When I am in it, it feels like a fight for my life. I am no longer a sadist manipulating a character who dies repeatedly, like in VVVVVV. I am a masochist. And like like any first-person gaming experience, it feels more personal when I die. And I die. And I die. I start to giggle each time. Some kind of nervous reflex action to my failures.
Yet, I can't resist the challenge of the robotic female voice when she says, "Again." I survive a fraction of a second longer than before and she says "Excellent," which is just enough to distract me for a millisecond and die. Next round, I overcompensate a bit and I die. One day, I sat with my Grandpa while he played slots on Facebook, and while I tried not to judge, I couldn't help, but think, "This game is a time-waster. And with limited time on earth, it seems strange to willfully waste any time." This seriously makes me consider the time I devote to a game. Yet, Super Hexagon actually seems to dilate time. Twenty seconds seems like an eternity in the Hyper modes. I am made more keenly aware of time, though I understand there is a social aspect to Facebook gaming that is lost on me and gaining the Steam Achievements that come from progressing from Line to Triangle to Square, etc. is not my goal.

Every aspect of the Killing Floor experience has been improved dramatically from the original, with a sad exception: content. Sure, the original killing floor has had years to build up stacks of custom maps, DLC and other neat additions to keep the game alive; but with that said, Killing Floor 2 put itself at a severe disadvantage by gimping the core of varied gameplay- A wide selection of classes. It could've panned out, with regular updates adding real, worthwhile content to the game. It has not panned out. What we get instead is a glacially slow, irregular move towards the finished product. The confusing choice to add skins (more than any other content, really) has not actually hurt the game, but it'll leave you feeling bitter and a bit messed around.
Even with typically Early Access behaviour such as this I might still have given this game a tentative recommendation because for some people there will be enough here to enjoy right now. It's not hard to see why: with satisfying gunplay, gorgeous and visceral visuals and all around refinement of the central mechanics I'll guarantee you'll have fun with the game. The problem is whether the fun will last, or whether you'll burn out before development is completed, robbing yourself of truly enjoying the superior end product. After all, completion of development is a big question mark ever since the 2015 promise was thrown out.
Finally, the truly depressing factor which tips me over the edge into not recommending the game is the surreptitious addition of microtransactions, during development and without warning.
So right now, I cannot pretend the game is not, at its heart, very good. What matters more is that by buying it now you're either robbing yourself of what is probably going to be a superior initial experience with the finished product or leaving yourself open to the developer adding other nasty surprises such as microtransactions (à la Payday 2, which this game styles itself a little too closely to already.)
With all this in mind, don't buy this, not for a while at least.

The character animation
The story conveyance
The pacing of new items
The character development
The secrets
The Scripted events
The object interation
The beautiful, memorable skyboxes
The level landmarks
Did I mention the character animation?
Seriously, the characters move, look and act like actual people and their eyes even follow you around the room.

What could I say about this...slaughter?
Random mooks can kill you with numbers or sheer power.
Bosses comes with a big health bar at the top of your screen, able to shrug everything you have, and punches you into oblivion.

Luckily, there are items to help you, which comes on form of treasure chest or a statue.
It comes with a price of course, which could be paid from coins dropped by monsters or boxes.
Unluckily, the items are quite...random.
You need to pray to get something you like, or even better, to get anything from the statue.
This randomness, combined with skills to control both your character and temper, are essential to clear this game.
Oh yeah, this game also has 10 different characters, with distinct specialty and playstyle!
If you want to taste countless death with satisfying reward of clearing multiple crazy carnage, this game is for you.

The game is a good batman arkham game, so far the story has been good and I love the incorporation of all the extra characters.
The batmobile does indeed feels forced, It has some cool sections but Rocksteady tried too hard for us to use the batmobile.
Voice acting is top notch and the graphics are great, this is indeed a new gen game.
Now the technical issues. It seems that it's a coin toss between a smooth experience and a bug ridden one.
I'm currently using:
AMD FX-8350
16 GB of Ram
Nvidia GTX 970
And the game works great, I'm getting between 55 to 75 fps during on-foot/gliding sections and drops to mid 40s when using the batmobile. I've seen people with far better rigs having lots of bugs, THIS IS NOT THE CASE FOR ME.
I'm playing on 1920x1080, everything on high and every nvidia gameworks option turned on.
Take this with a grain of salt since like I said earlier, it's a coin toss, if the game works it's a great one, if it fails it fails miserably.

Great game with plenty of variety in this roguelite which features such lovely things such as:
Good single player and better multiplayer, in the same mode!
Playable characters that all feel very unique and special in their own ways.
Levels with set layouts but 2 or 3 different variations for most.
Plenty of items to unlock and play with!
A risk/reward system in the longer you take, the harder it gets.
Interesting lore and story (for those interested in that type of thing).
In game achievements with a purpose: unlocking the characters and items!
The fairly recently added artifacts which change the very mechanics of the game in different ways varying from small to huge and beneficial to harmful and those that don't go either way.
A little warning though: the multiplayer can be a tad rough to get to work. You can use Tunngle to set up a VPN with your friends though, that works really well!

In principle this game is good. It continuates the system of Killing Floor 1 with far better graphics, smoother gameplay, more gore, more different zeds, etc. The gunplay feels as good as ever. Dismembering zeds is very satisfying and in slomo it's even better. There are more perks, there is a better progression system, and that's all very good.
But here is the big 'but', 'however' and 'yet'. There are fewer guns for each perk (only 4 each instead of 5-10 for each perk) which doesn't allow for much diverse gameplay. And, despite all their promises, the game is still in early access and they appear to spend time on other projects (like a mobile version or a playstation version) instead of finishing the game first.
Yes, there are more perks available now than at the start of the Early Access but even after almost a year, the game is still not finished (even though they said they needed only 6 months). We are still waiting for at least 4 perks and updates are very sparse.
In its current state and because of broken promises, I can't rate this game very high. There is promise, but they screwed over their fanbase and the players who had faith in them, myself included. They should stop mucking about and finish this game already. It's a shame they proved to be such a big disappointment, because there was such potential.

I almost don't want to recommend this game. It's so very frustrating, and not in a good way. I'm a fan of Roguelikes, but never have been a fan of the 'dwindling torch' trope. I guess, in this sense, it's a twist on the classic countdown to doomsday. Instead of running out of time and losing by default, Risk of Rain has a timer that counts UPWARDS TOWARDS YOUR TOTAL BAD TIME. Festooned with extremely high-health monsters, and elite versions of them with even MORE health, you are constantly and hopelessly beset upon by nigh-neverending waves of monsters that just have no mercy. The first level is meaty on first playthrough, but it's the second level where the mechanics of the monsters become staggering. Teleporting, full-screen attacks, you name it, there's a monster that can do it, and 99 more alongside him.
The monsters have so much health and without a perfect set of items from level 1, you're pretty much playing single-player Russian Roulette. You necessarily have to lose... just not immediately. You just can't deal enough damage to stop the onslaught. There's so much chaos on the screen that I just have to hope I jumped in time to dodge an attack whose function I only recognize by the sound byte attached to it.
The player is very much so at the mercy of RNG, hoping the items that drop (if the chests appear) are situationally valid enough to aid in your progress.
And I see from the selection screen that there are multiple characters to unlock, I've dumped a couple hours into this game and I've only unlocked one. So, it's possible, that my niche character is just indefinitely unavailable to me.
This isn't just a hard ♥♥♥♥ing game, it's downright cruel and unusual, and at times... just completely unfair. I'd rather go play XCOM:EU i/i, it seems like a fairytale compared to this abusive spouse. The game is fun, and the music is awesome... but prepare your body. It's not gentle.

Rocksteady Studios and Warner Bros. really let everyone down releasing this game in the state it was knowing full well it wasn't ready to be released. I waited up for the release and was extremely disappointed to find my game wouldn't even run for more than a few seconds without it crashing unless I went down to 720p and had everything on low. Even then it would still crash every 10 minutes or so.
Fast forward several months and several patches later and the game seems to run just fine for the most part, on my current GPU anyway. On my old R9 285 the game would crash even more frequently with the new patches, but after upgrading to a GTX 980ti I can say this game runs solidly at 1080p maxed out with the Nvidia settings on, and this is paired with my fx 8350 that still needs upgrading. I have finally managed to play the game all the way through without a single issue!
Performance aside the game itself is amazing, in fact, it may even be my favourite Arkham game in the series. Batman is much more aggressive in this game and the story itself is much darker than ever before. Combat has been improved with added moves, environmental takedowns and dual play, which allows you to fight alongside an accompanying ally (These sections are awesome!) The city itself is much bigger than ever before and is graphically stunning. Gliding through the city has never felt better with several major improvements. Batman can launch himself into the air using the grapnel gun which allows you to shoot across the sky at high speed. You can now grapple onto a higher ledge as you’re grappling up another. Both of these combined really gives a sense of fluidity and momentum making gliding through the city that extra bit more awesome! The batmobile is also an amazing addition to the series. It's a blast driving around the streets of Gotham ramming thugs off the road. You can even transform into battle mode which allows you to fire non lethal rounds, to incapacitate thugs, and lethal rounds, to take out the unmanned drones patrolling the city. With enough speed you can even launch yourself out of the Batmobile which gives you a huge boost of speed allowing another way for you to glide through Gotham.
Absolutely! If you’ve played any of the other Arkham games there's no doubt you'll enjoy this one. WIth all the added improvements to the gameplay and darker story telling I’d say Rocksteady Studios have created an absolute masterpiece.
There's always Steam refunds though!

The pros are that it is a very simple game and is challenging yet still manages to be enjoyable. However it is a game you will likely only play for minutes at a time. The cons are it is simply too difficult and the controls of rotation are often not precise meaning you depressing the key for what you precieve as the appropriate amount of time to do a 180 degree rotation may over or undershoot you, and the game mechanics make this unforgiving (should be a little more generous to human error). I had held off from getting the game at first, due to all the negative feedback.  I decided to wait until it was fixed and put back on sale, only to hear of people still complaining of problems.  But with WB offering a full refund, I decided to go ahead and bite the bullet, figuring the worst case scenario would be if it sucked and I got the refund, I could put it towards the purchase of Fallout 4.
Well guess what?  It plays awesome!  Yes, even the Batmobile!  Combat and movement were silky-smooth, with nary a graphic hitch in sight.  And I played it on my monitor's native resolution (1680x1050), which I think helped in the FPS department.
In case you're wondering about my specs, here they are:
Intel core i7 CPU (factory setting)
nVidia GTX 970
8 Gb of Crucial Ballistix system RAM
Windows 8.1
ASUS Sabretooth Z97 Mk 1 Motherboard
If your system is anything like mine, you should be golden.  Although I suppose I should mention that you may want to run nVidia's GeForce Experience program to properly optimize your game.  Interestingly enough, it does not enable the graphical bells and whistles like enhanced rain or interactive smoke.  And I think that's where people may be encountering problems.  But the game itself just looks so gorgeous as-is that I don't think you'll miss them.
As with Mortal Kombat X, it paid to hold off until things were fixed.  But hopefully WB will learn their lesson from this after such a public debacle.
That having been said, at this point I think many of the complaints are coming from a small, vocal minority.  Namely, either hardcore PC enthusiasts and tech-heads who have everything on their machines turned up to eleven, Windows 10 users complaining about the memory requirements, or - even worse - trolls just looking to kick WB when they're down "for the lulz."  Given the current "mixed" status the game has been receiving, that's a big step up from the "mostly negative" status it had at first.  And I feel that there's probably a silent majority for whom the game runs fine.
So, in closing, to those of you who have a rig like mine and running under the same OS, you ought to be fine.  For those still complaining?  To paraphrase Jay-Z, "If you're having game troubles, I feel bad for you son.  I've got 99 problems, but Batman ain't one!"

This is a game I recommend everyone play at least once.
Despite being released over a decade ago, Half Life 2 has aged incredibly well. Even today, the game oozes a rich atmosphere that immediately draws you in during the opening sequence and compels you to play to completion.
The gameplay is engaging throughout, with a variety of weapons that gradually become available to the player, ranging from the series' iconic crowbar to powerful energy-based weaponry. Combat is not all there is to do, however, as the game is littered with puzzles to solve and a treasure trove of secrets to discover.
The level-design is also unwaveringly immersive. It is difficult to put into words, but each and every "level" feels detailed and well thought-out. The relatively horror-oriented Ravenholm stage roughly halfway through the game is a particularly good example of this.
Furthermore, the story is told effectively and compellingly though both details in the environment and with a small but interesting cast of characters (Dr. Kleiner is my personal favorite). A few other reviews on Steam do not recommend Half Life 2 based on the fact that the long-awaited third installment has yet to be released, and thus the series lacks a conclusion, but I say it is absolutely worth experiencing Half Life 2's story despite that.
Revolutionary for its time and a classic today. Overall, I can not recommend Half Life 2 highly enough.

Utterly addictive, be it you are into slow-paced strategy or just love history (like I do). Although the learning curve is quite steep at first it is much easier to get into than its predecessor Civilization IV. Although the AI is quite poor at the whole warfare bit (ranged and naval units are very powerful) in a multiplayer game it can get quite a bit more interesting. Due to the slow pace of the game it is perfect for killing an afternoon with a friend or just casually click through all the way to the Information Era. The modding community's passion for making proper mods (like the Enlightenment Era mod or the Pre-History mod) sure keeps the replayability value high even after some 1000+ hours invested if you care to test away what mods work with one another and which do not. As with most Civilization games it took a few expansions to balance out the gameplay, since the Vanilla experience was kinda lacking, polish-wise, hence why I do recommend to buy both expansions if you are new to the game.
For $0.29, it's a good buy.

Summing up my experience with this game so far is fairly easy:
"Game Over!" - "Again?" - ... - "Game Over!" - "Again?" - ... - "Game Over!" - "Again?" - ...
You might better get used to the voice telling you those two lines, because you are going to hear them often if you dare to play this game. Not "often" as in "every now and then", but often as in "every few seconds"!
This game is not hard, it is "nintendo-hard" to the bone. But exactly that is also the core of its addictive nature. Simple graphics and a minmal, yet paced techno-soundtrack leave you with nothing more than the bare challenge of staying alive just a split second longer.
It is hypnotic.
It is frustrating.
It is addictive!
And it changes your perception of time. This game makes 30 seconds feel like 30 minutes. Until you hear that familiar voice asking you "Game Over! - Again?".
-And you will click "again".
Again and again.

Well I finally get to play this game, and I got to say this is the best Batman game I have ever played. Best superhero genre game I have ever played. Haven't completed the game yet but I'm just blown away by the direction, the story elements, atmoshpere, gameplay, and the stunning visuals.
Graphics - Stunning. Some of the most visually impressive details in the chracter models and animations. Zero framrate issues. No screen tearing, and really haven't seen any clipping so far.
Audio - Top notch. Everything from the punches and kicks, explosions, and voice acting bring this games atmosphere to life. The batmobile sounds like a monster! Exactly they way I would expect it to. Music is very fitting so far. Some familiar themes from old arkham games and very good new ones. There's a particular emotionally charged audio track that really hits the core. Awesome.
Gameplay - Smooth and perfected. The skill tree's, multifear take downs, and plenty of different and new ways to use your gadgets this time around give this series a breath of fresh air. Racetracks are insanely fun.
Story - Entirely subjective. I found it great! (atleast as far as I have gotten)
Unfortunatley the negatives draw the biggest crowds right now.
Cons - Bad launch.
- Very pricey Season Pass.
- Lack of Boss Battles

It was a long, tireless wait but my good god was it worth it. This game oozes genius and brilliance from the first seconds to the very last minute of the story. The delivery, perfect; the content, hilarious; gameplay? Repayable, exciting, fresh and surprisingly disgusting! Even by south park standards, creators Trey Parker & Matt Stone have raised the bar (much like James Cameron – “The bravest pioneer”) with revolting humour, storytelling and integration of their hugely rich universe they’ve created over the last 17 years. The Stick of Truth is not only the best south park game created, but the best game adaptation of cartoon or TV series as matter of fact, and that really says great things about the future of south park digital studios and Obsidian entertainment.
This game is a steal at the price and I whole fully endorse it through and through, not only as massive fan of the show but as a gamer with more than 2 decades of consistent gaming under my belt and a love for RPG’s in particular.
Ignore the criticism of the games ease and repetitiveness, both are integral to how the game is not only played but lived. There’s a good 15hours of main story without side quests and exploring, not to mention there will be some much welcome DLC on the way by the tell of the current map that will be every bit as grand as the release itself. I could bore you forever with reasons for why you should own this game and whip you endlessly for reasons as to why you have not already, the point is, if you are browising this game, you should own it and the creators and publishers are deserving of every damn, penny, cent, rupee, euro yaddadadad you get the point.... BUY IT!
Bravo, Obsidian and Bravo, South Park Studios, the wait was worth it and the game, perfect.

A cracking end to the Arkham Series by Rocksteady the ambiguous mindblowing 100% ending(a.k.a the true ending) leaves many questions cryptically answered inside the game itself. Lots of nods to the older games including Arkham: Origins made by Warner Bro's nice to see references to the events in that game with Firefly and Deathstroke among others. Attention to detail is amazing aswell probably the most detailed to date. Having Nightwing,Robin and Catwoman playable for a while was fantastic if short. There really needs to be a spin off game featuring one of them either in Gotham or Bludhaven. Also that surprise segment of FPS gameplay complete with Dr Who like "weeping angels" was unexpected and very cool as the battle of wills inside Batman's mind came to an epic conclusion.
I had no issues whatsoever running at 70-90fps with everything maxed out at 1080p the only setting turned off was the enhanced paper in Nvidia settings as that dropped the fps down to 45-50. I had 2 CTD's in 62hrs played with a few microstutters when entering vehicles from time to time. Nothing gamebreaking whatsoever.

Half-life 2 is a true sequel to the famous Half-life. Many players remember the first time that they walked the streets of City 17 and experienced the oppressive Combine rule, and the unsettling feeling that I got whenever the zombies eerily screeched over Ravenholm. In Half-life 2 you continue exploring the nightmare after the resonance cascade. You play as Gordon Freeman, a theoretical physicist forced to survive the alien invasion that took place during the incident. After the events of Half-life, you are put into stasis by the Government Man and awoken on a train similar to the tram in Black Mesa. As the train stops you exit to the train station and are greeted by Dr. Wallace Breen, your previous boss at Black Mesa and now the figurehead of the Combine on Earth. The Combine is a massive inter-dimensional organization composed of allied and enslaved alien species. They took control of Earth in an event called the 7-Hour War that took place in between Half-Life and Half-Life 2. Eventually you join the resistance and begin an uprising against the Combine. As you progress, you become even more powerful and your arsenal enlarges. You also gain more reputation and become the face of the Resistance.
Unlike the first game released in 1998, Half-life 2 introduced physics that make combat way more enjoyable and strategic. For example, when you see a group of combine police on a wooden bridge you could just shoot them; or you could shoot the platform above them to drop bricks onto their heads. What about that explosive barrel? Maybe you want to just shoot the wooden bridge that they are standing on. As you can see you have many options with the combat but it doesn't stop there. Instead of the first game's jumping puzzles they added in physics puzzles and better thought out puzzles in general. Graphically this game still looks great for being released in 2004 and looks even better as they upgraded the Source engine in the later versions and updates. The enemy and ally A.I. has improved a lot when compared to the original. Your allies will give you ammo and health when they see you are low and will take cover and duck around in a fire fight. If they see a better weapon then they will pick it up and begin to use it. Unlike the first game your allies don't get stuck around corners or objects for the most part. Unfortunately they can still get in your way in narrow corridors. The Source engine also excels in the new realistic facial expressions, and I think that the characters in Half-Life 2 still feel more realistic than most games nowadays.
Lastly, it's price is a steal! It's only $9.99 for one of the most entertaining and ground breaking FPS' you will ever play. This game has an amazing story combined with the great physics and nice graphics. It also has some replay value, due to how detailed the environments are, and if you want more, the modding community is enormous. Half-Life 2 is by far one of my favorite games personally. If you enjoy the game then consider trying the episodic chapters that you can buy seperately for a really cheap price. These take place right after and go in chronological order. Recommended 9.5/10

What would you get if you removed everything that made the original KF stand out except the basic concept? Well, probably something really close to KF2. If I didn't know better I would think that a different team altogether came to develop the sequel since so much of the formula that made the first game such an enjoyable experience is missing from here. It's like someone came out of nowhere, saw a couple of videos of gameplay on Youtube and decide to "improve"it for the sequel.
And on paper the changes to seem to be for the better, but for a seasoned KF almost all of them made the experience worse. "Let's make the maps smaller, removing any chance of teammates losing each other and Zeds picking them one by one. Let's add a sprint buttont, removing any sense of danger since now you can basically outrun even the worst of enemies. Let's add more levels on the skill tree, even though you get a perk only every five levels. This way we give the impression of deeper rpg elements, even though nothing changed at all. Let's add perks like everyone else, and while we are at it, let's make most of them useless.
The worst part is that they changed the mechanics so much but they barely added anything new for old KF players. With a few exceptions, all classes have basically the same range of weapons as the first game. I played mainly as support for more than a hundred hours on the original so making the transition and seeing again the same weapons was really dissappointing for me. The monsters are basically the same. With more details on their design yes, but there aren't any new monsters.
At this point, the only reason of getting KF2 is for the visual upgrade. The game is pretty good looking and with all the options enabled, the on screen carnage is impressive, but still this is not enough.
I know it seems that I'm bashing the game really hard, but it's not because it's a bad title. For the new players, it's still a fun little title that can provide countless hours of entertainment. But I doubt it will please most of the veterans of the original Killing Floor. Same/similar weapons, small maps that look more fitting on a CoD game, sprint button that removes almost all sense of danger, uninteresting level up system and perks...
The only hope I have is that the game is still in early access. Maybe the final product will have bigger maps, more weapons, and improved mechanics. But as it is now, I can't recommend it to old players. And seeing the servers quite empty I'm not the only one having the same opinions.

I love South Park and I've been looking forward to this game since I read about it in Game Informer. I didn't mind the delays and the wait. To me, it just meant that the game would be better and more true to what Matt and Trey wanted. To me, that was important. The game completely justifies the wait, in my opinion because it was the closest thing to perfect I've come across.
If you are a fan of South Park, be it die hard or passing, you will enjoy this game. It's in the style of the show, which is a big plus, and it allows you, the player, to experience South Park the way Matt and Trey experience it. There are references to almost every episode in the show and if a character has showed up at some point, there is a good chance they are in the game, even if they're a simple background character.
The game play is solid. It's a turn based RPG, where the turn based combat isn't hamhanded and awkward. It fits into the story thats set up by the game nicely. My favourite aspect of the combat is that you can use an item and do an attack in the game turn instead of having to choose one. This is genius and I hope more RPGs start to incorporate that into their combat systems. It doesn't break the combat and give either side an unfair advantage. Personally, I really dislike turn based combat systems, but it wasn't the thorn in my side that it usually is.
The biggest downsides of the game are the length of the game itself and the classes. This game is very, very short. You could easily beat it in one long gaming session, even if you chose to do all of the side quests. There is barely any differences in the classes. Jew and Mage are similar, as are Thief and Warrior. This really limits the replayability of the game and considering it's sporting the now standard $60USD price tag the limited replayability and the length of the game are big hits against this title. However, if you are a die-hard fan of the series, such as myself, you'll find yourself replaying it anyway just to relive the experience.

Now, I admit I just bought a 980 ti, so the performance for me won't reflect the average PC user. I'm running it at maximum settings at 2160p and I haven't noticed a single problem in the couple hours I've played it - solid 60fps with zero dropped frames and no frame rate drop. No stuttering, no texture glitches. Perfect so far.
The Batmobile is a lot of fun, and they have so far made good use of it as a game puzzle/combat asset. Combat seems about the same as the last two games. EDIT: The combat has been elevated in a few ways. Familiar enough to jump in and play, but with enought new things to do that it is a marked improvement over the last two games (I haven't played Arkham Asylum). The graphics are... there are no words. You have to see for yourself. All said, it seems to be a worthy continuation of the series.
Wholeheartedly recommended, assuming you have at least a 4GB video card.
EDIT: 2160p isn't sustainable. I don't know why I thought it was before. Yes. Yes, I do. I wasn't using a performance utility. I installed PrecisionX and found my framerate was dipping into the forties with (consistent frame times around twenty ms during the slowdowns). I didn't notice until I had the numbers in front of me, though.
So. Walking back what I said earlier, at 1440p I never get frametimes above 17ms and a steady, effortless 60fps. Buy without fear. This is the best video game I've ever played. This is after, what? 49 hours of gameplay.
Never mind where it came from or what mistakes were made -- it's a solid, fun game.
One last thing: with the heavy use of PhysX in this game, I find an average 10% increase in performance when using my old 680 as a dedicated PhysX processor. Sometimes it runs at 50%+ capacity. Take from that what you will.

Half-life 2 is a true sequel to the famous Half-life. Many players remember the first time that they walked the streets of City 17 and experienced the oppressive Combine rule, and the unsettling feeling that I got whenever the zombies eerily screeched over Ravenholm. In Half-life 2 you continue exploring the nightmare after the resonance cascade. You play as Gordon Freeman, a theoretical physicist forced to survive the alien invasion that took place during the incident. After the events of Half-life, you are put into stasis by the Government Man and awoken on a train similar to the tram in Black Mesa. As the train stops you exit to the train station and are greeted by Dr. Wallace Breen, your previous boss at Black Mesa and now the figurehead of the Combine on Earth. The Combine is a massive inter-dimensional organization composed of allied and enslaved alien species. They took control of Earth in an event called the 7-Hour War that took place in between Half-Life and Half-Life 2. Eventually you join the resistance and begin an uprising against the Combine. As you progress, you become even more powerful and your arsenal enlarges. You also gain more reputation and become the face of the Resistance.
Unlike the first game released in 1998, Half-life 2 introduced physics that make combat way more enjoyable and strategic. For example, when you see a group of combine police on a wooden bridge you could just shoot them; or you could shoot the platform above them to drop bricks onto their heads. What about that explosive barrel? Maybe you want to just shoot the wooden bridge that they are standing on. As you can see you have many options with the combat but it doesn't stop there. Instead of the first game's jumping puzzles they added in physics puzzles and better thought out puzzles in general. Graphically this game still looks great for being released in 2004 and looks even better as they upgraded the Source engine in the later versions and updates. The enemy and ally A.I. has improved a lot when compared to the original. Your allies will give you ammo and health when they see you are low and will take cover and duck around in a fire fight. If they see a better weapon then they will pick it up and begin to use it. Unlike the first game your allies don't get stuck around corners or objects for the most part. Unfortunately they can still get in your way in narrow corridors. The Source engine also excels in the new realistic facial expressions, and I think that the characters in Half-Life 2 still feel more realistic than most games nowadays.
Lastly, it's price is a steal! It's only $9.99 for one of the most entertaining and ground breaking FPS' you will ever play. This game has an amazing story combined with the great physics and nice graphics. It also has some replay value, due to how detailed the environments are, and if you want more, the modding community is enormous. Half-Life 2 is by far one of my favorite games personally. If you enjoy the game then consider trying the episodic chapters that you can buy seperately for a really cheap price. These take place right after and go in chronological order. Recommended 9.5/10

This is a review to mark the October 28th re-release of Batman: Arkham SH**E!
For the longest time I wanted to like it and I wanted to think it was the best game in the series, maybe even a game of the year contender but sadly with poor (and unavoidable) Batmobile combat and very disappointing villains with lame or no boss encounters that send the series huge steps backwards, I can honestly say that this is the worst in the series and my faith in rocksteady and Batman games in general has been completely dashed, perhaps permanently!
What's worse is the game performs slightly worse now from its September patch, with frequent driver crashes on Windows 10 and a frame rate that only stays a 60 during most cutscenes while the game is a mixed bag of between 60 and below 40, the Batmobile in particular rarely goes above 50 fps.
Even the performance test itself has issues with characters getting stuck against walls!
I wish I could write a more positive review, especially after they were nice enough to release all dlc to date (except for the Scarecrow challenges on PS4) but when you’re reduced to forcing yourself to carry on playing a broken down, underwhelming mess of a game only to find nothing spectacular at the end, certainly nothing that would justify finishing this game instead of watching it on YouTube, you know someone messed up spectacularly.
That person has to be held to account!
For those of you mad enough to buy this game, especially in its current state, I urge you to get it refunded back to the drawing board ASAP!!

I have played Killing Floor from the early days.  It started relatively small with few weapons and maps.  Tripwire stayed with it for a long while, gradually updated and expanded upon it.  Going into Killing Floor 2, content is limited, not all the perks are available yet, weapons and maps are slowly being released but are still in small numbers.  In my opinion this is similar to the original, Tripwire isn't going to abandon this project, given patience and time they will deliver a solid game.  The content so far has been excellent, as limited as it is there is unquestionable quality.
Weapons in general are well crafted and fun to use.  The maps seem pretty well planned and excecuted, some are better than others.  Difficulty levels seem appropriate, and with a great team this game is fun over and over again.
Micro transactions do exist, but its not shoved in your face and if you don't like the transactions, ignore them and do not partake.  Tripwire has stood by their promise that paid DLC will not split the community, its all skins and characters, no weapons and maps are withheld from the community.
If you can stand the wait, this game is great in its current condition.

For the longest time I wanted to like it and I wanted to think it was the best game in the series, maybe even a game of the year contender but sadly with poor (and unavoidable) Batmobile combat and very disappointing villains with lame or no boss encounters that send the series huge steps backwards, I can honestly say that this is the worst in the series and my faith in rocksteady and Batman games in general has been completely dashed, perhaps permanently!
What's worse is the game performs slightly worse now from its September patch, with frequent driver crashes on Windows 10 and a frame rate that only stays a 60 during most cutscenes while the game is a mixed bag of between 60 and below 40, the Batmobile in particular rarely goes above 50 fps.
Even the performance test itself has issues with characters getting stuck against walls!
I wish I could write a more positive review, especially after they were nice enough to release all dlc to date (except for the Scarecrow challenges on PS4) but when you’re reduced to forcing yourself to carry on playing a broken down, underwhelming mess of a game only to find nothing spectacular at the end, certainly nothing that would justify finishing this game instead of watching it on YouTube, you know someone messed up spectacularly.
That person has to be held to account!
For those of you mad enough to buy this game, especially in its current state, I urge you to get it refunded back to the drawing board ASAP!!

Killing Floor 2. The, sequel to Killing Floor 1. Fun game, good atmosphere, and great gameplay.
Pro's:
+ Great melee combat.
+ Great gun control.
+ Not too hard on easy, but also not that easy...
+ Boss battles actually require teamwork, and strategy.
+ Hack 'n' slash.
+ A lot of different types of Zeds.
+ Each Zed has it's own ability (i.e. Scrakes attacks can be blocked, while only certain Fleshpound attacks can be blocked.)
+ Great atomsphere.
Cons:
- Hans is OP on harder difficulty.
- Unbalanced classes, and gameplay. Medics heal low amounts of health over time, while Zeds deal tons of damage instantly.
- Zeds appear behind you randomly.
- You can barely hold anything, with only 15 pounds of weight able to be carried.
- I'll use an example for this one. Let's say, a weapon you want costs 1200, each round, on average, you're making 300 dosh. Now, half of that goes to your ammo, and your armor. Meaning, you're making 150, possibly less each round. So, not enough Dosh is made.
- Gameplay get's repetitive.
All in all though, great game. I enjoy it very much, and still waiting for new content to come out, rather than bug fixes. I'm not complaing, just, I haven't played in over 3 months (I think) because of lack of content. Gameplay gets reptitive, and boring.

Having never been a fan of turn-based RPGs, I was rather skeptical about buying this game (the last one I had played was one of the Final Fantasy games back in the last 90s). My love for South Park ultimately convinced me to get this, and I'm very glad that I did.
Within minutes I'd got to grip with the gameplay, which whilst very simplistic throughout, does remain mostly fun (although a few of the special move animations do become tiresome). The classic South Park humour is there, offensive and satirical in equal doses. The graphic style makes it feel exactly like an episode of the show, and due to this the cutscenes flow seamlessly with the gameplay. There's plenty of nods to all seasons of the show, you can see Scuzzlebutt hanging around in Jimbo's gun shop, the Jakovasaurs popping up in the loading menu and can even initiate a ManBearPig-related quest with Al Gore. The quantity of weapons is immense, so are the costumes that you can equip and customise. The recreation of South Park itself is nice, there's familiar locations and recogniseable characters aplenty, although traversing across the same areas constantly can get tiresome, and the forest on the outskirts of the town can be a real pain to naviagte if you find yourself lost. Roaming the streets for new characters to meet is enjoyable, and highly recommended too, given the large number of side quests and friends to be made.
Having only so far played as the Fighter class, I can't really comment on the others (although other reviews have seemed to note a lack of real distinction between them)
Overall, I would recommend this to fans of the show, if you're not a fan, the vast majority of the humour will be lost on you, and this will probably just feel like a run of the mill RPG.

One of the most unique rogue-likes of this generation, Risk of Rain is a full package consisting of stellar gameplay mechanics, slick pixel graphics, and an electrifying soundtrack, altogether forming a very fun and memorable experience.
The game is an action platforming rogue-like (what a mouthful) with a new twist on the genre; the longer you spend time in game, the harder it gets. Believe me when I say this game is challenging. Even on the easiest difficulty, you could easily get decimated by a group of mobs if you aren't careful. The entire time-element adds another layer of depth into the way you play the game. Should you try to rush through each level, picking up whatever items you can scrounge from the path you take, or try taking your time and grinding precious experience and gold? It's builds a very tense yet exciting atmosphere as you try to make the most out of each stage before the timer jumps to the next difficulty level. The difficulty in this game can be unforgiving at times, especially when you start out and can't seem to find the right items for your character, but is always fair. Very similar to Dark Souls, if you push and persevere hard enough to learn all the little nuances in the game, you will feel the most gratifying sense of achievement and victory from each successful playthrough.
Risk of Rain is also a very unique rogue-like mainly because of its varied playable characters. Typically in other rogue-likes in recent times, you pick from different classes that serve as a mere template for your stats. However, in Risk of Rain, the 10 different characters you can play as have some semblance to heroes in MOBA games, each having a set of 4 abilities that are unique to them. This means that each character represents a multitude of playstyles that are all very fun to play as. Add in the fact that each character gets their own small epilogue is a very nice touch to each victory.
As for presentation, Risk of Rain manages to do a lot more with a lot less. While most sprites are very small in comparison to the large, expansive environments you explore, incredible amounts of detail are put into each pixel on your screen. The animation on each character and monster is excellently done, sometimes almost feeling on par with the spritework of the Metal Slug series. Each level you go to is also incredibly detailed, and you visit a LOT of different locales on this alien world. From alien-infested caves covered in muck and slime, to a gigantic temple atop an evergreen mountain, you can tell a lot of thought was put into the world of the game, as each level has its own set of inhabitants that all fit well into the mythos of the mysterious alien planet. In the end, Risk of Rain manages to put a lot of care and attention into a very minimalistic style, and for that it gets it does a very great job.
Music in this game is simply great. Sometimes it can jolt your body with electricity during intense moments in gameplay. Other times, it acts very passive yet powerful during the times you are exploring the very alien world. It's hard to describe such an audial idea, but the least I can say is that the music complements the game in a major way, and will not disappoint in the least.
I'd also like to give a special mention to the Artifact System that was added recently. These new artifacts that you can find and turn on in the game can add some interesting mutators to your playthrough. For example, one artifact reduces your health to only 10% of your starting health, but increases your damage output by 500% (It's not as OP as it sounds). I'd just like to praise the developers for not making these artifacts simply add a layer of artificial difficulty on top of an already brutal game, as some of these artifacts can actually help newcomers learn more about the game's little nuances (like being able to get certain items quicker to see what works better each character).
All in all, Risk of Rain is an incredibly well-made game, and for such a low price, is practically a steal. You'd be doing yourself a disservice for not buying this game, because this is an experience you do not want to miss out on. See you on the planet!

This game is great. There's no other way to put it. Everything about this game has charm to it.
The characters, the art, the music, and everything else. In fact, the art is quite possibly my favorite part. All of the pixel art is fantastic, and it all has a very distinctive style. Combine all of this great content with fluid and dynamic combat, new things to unlock, bosses to fight, characters and artifacts to find, achievments to obtain, locations to discover, and a sense that there's always something new around the corner, and you have one hell of an indie game.
Now, as if ALL OF THAT wasn't enough to make you interested in purchasing this game, then here's a major point: This game has *FULL ONLINE PLAY*. You can play through this game as many times as you'd like with as many friends as you'd like. (I'm not entirely sure how many people can play at once, but I have seen groups of up to 7 people playing together at once. Beatiful chaos).
If there's anything to compare this game to, it's Binding of Isaac. With all the items that you unlock through completing specific criteria, along with the rouge-like elements, it does remind me somewhat of Binding of Isaac. That may be another reason I love this game so much.
The best way to explain this game in one long run on sentence would have to be...
Binding of Isaac along with full online multiplayer, coupled with interesting combat, more characters, new items, lots of achievments, a ton of bosses to fight, artifacts which change gameplay drastically, fantastic music, and fantastic art.
This game is a wicked ride, and I would HIGHLY recommend it to everyone! In fact, it's June 23rd right now, and this game is 50% off, selling at a dirt cheap $5 until the 30th! I'd pay $15 for this game if I had to, so $5 is practically stealing.
If you've been debating whether or not to purchase Risk of Rain, STOP. The only reason I could think of to not purchase this game is the lack of money. I've enjoyed all the time I've put into it thus far, and I'm looking forward to the time I put into it in the future.

So what do I have to say in rewritting this review?
Well to start off, let me spill the beans, I honestly secretly hated this game but others liked it and the music was f**king stellar so I "recommended" it.
Why did I hate this game? Because holy sh*t, its controlls seemed utterly busted.
Spoilers, they aren't really.
This game has a slight amount of lag due to vsync which will affect your play, it will make the controlls seem pretty sloppy and sluggish, that was the reason for the "this game feels like your spinning around with a sack of potatoes" comment in my old review (bad grammar intact), I just didn't know it.
So does turning vsync off help?
Maybe it's confirmation bias but I was immediately able to destroy my old score on the Hexagon stage when it was turned off, so I'd say there's no harm in it.
Well I WOULD say there's no harm in it but...
ᵗʰᵃᵗ'ᵈ ᵇᵉ ᶫʸᶦᶰᵍ⋅
You see, if you're not familiar with what Vsync is, it's a term that stands for Vertical Synchronization, it prevents what is known as tearing
In my experience, having vsync off in most games is fine but in Super Hexagon this is not the case, in fact Super Hexagon has some of the worst screen tearing I've seen in a video game and this tearing can be quite distracting, I'm not sure if this varies from monitor to monitor but at least in my case I'm pitted with two options: Keep Vsync on and prevent screen tearing and never complete a single stage or turn it off, bite the bullet, and play the game. Thankfully I'm able to eventually ignore what I consider god awful tearing but your experience may vary.
What else do I have to say about the game?
Well now that I can actually play it and failure feels like my own fault, it's pretty good.
The game has a pseudo rhythm game vibe that I can appreciate and the challenge it presents is fun to overcome.
I would have more to say but I've only completed the Hexagon stage, I will update this review when I have more knowledge on the game.

This brings the killing floor universe into the current generation of PC gaming. This has every right to be considered an AAA title I feel. The original Killing floor always felt a bit comedy and this game is no different.
Graphically, Killing Floor 2 is delicious. I don't know why something so simple as blood and gibs flying across the screen is so satisfying but I think PLEX really sets it off. Each zombie now sports a far more complex damage model, so you can entertain yourself for days blasting them into small pieces or counting out the number of particularly delicious headshots you can manage.
In terms of gameplay it is familiar FPS fare with new maps, a tonne of weapons, but with the same mutants to kill. It's a pick up and play type of game that will suit most people. In Co-op even the inexperienced will find themselves useful and entertained. But saying that, it is less comedy and cartoony than Left 4 dead, and I think provides more variety. This game more closely approximates the British film series '28 days later' than the big budget American equivalent. It feels more tense and more serious.
There are enough maps at the moment (Steam workshop will undoubtedly provide some more) and plenty of weapons, but knowing Tripwire there will be a load more added at some stage.
I would offer the game 10 out of 10 but the eery spectre of microtransactions have arrived in KF2 and I can't help but think I don't like it. It's not a game breaker in any way as you don't actually 'need' any of the stuff (we are talking different character and weapon skins, this is not pay to win or anything) but it just feels a bit sinister.
One thing I wish they devs had implemented was limb damage properly, I was hoping that the starter 9mm Berreta lookalike would blow legs off and leave crippled zombies crawling toward you but no such luck, I'll just have to stick to burning them instead. I think the melee weapons and effects are a bit too simple as well, they just don't seem to have the creative flourish I was expecting but hey ho.
Note also that there is NO PvP or adversarial mode to this game, this is strictly a co-op horde mode shooter which might not suit all tastes.

I think I've played enough of this game to know what it has and what it lacks at this point in the beta. I would definitely say that this game is worth it, but not perfect yet. Not by far. I love the original KF and this game is an awesome sequel. It has great graphics, a satisfying feel to the weapons (Tripwire knows how to do weapons right by animating all the small little detailed frames), the glorious MEAT system which is like the improved version of the GHOST system from Soldier of Fortune, balanced zombies for the most* part *(I say MOST because the scrake became almost non-existant and a Fleshpound can easily take out a whole team, other than that the clot, gorefast, witch and bloat are balanced fairly well), a good challenge while still being possible (unless you decide to go HoE then kiss yourself goodbye) and some great boss fights. Oh and also throwing the Patriarch in was a nice touch! But some of its flaws are very obvious, like the lack of variety in the classes and poor class balancing. Take for example the Commando class, it has about four assault rifles. That's a bit small, I mean they are all detailed great but after a while it feels like the same old thing using the same weapons every time. I know the weapons are balanced but you could make a few more weapons that are similar but with other special or different traits at different prices. Another thing about weapons, the microtransaction system doesn't quite cover for a lack of new in game weapons. A skin isn't the same, although it is cool. There's not a ton of maps yet which isn't as big of a problem since they are releasing new maps still like with the Patriarch update. Speaking of the Patriarch update, it seems like the bosses aren't nearly balanced. I remember being hyped up, anxious to beat the Patriarch, coming so far. Then all of the sudden it's like he's there and then he's gone. By far Hans is harder to beat, making the Patriarch look like a fly on the wall. One of the worst flaws in this game is the teleporting zeds. I mean they're not even subtle about it. It's just wonderful having a Fleshpound pop right in front of your face when you were just ahead of him. Plus another two flaws, the infinitely raging Scrakes and Fleshpounds at the end of a match and the classes being unbalanced/just running from everything. In KF1 you had to have skill to actually play through a match, but in this game it's like if you're a Commando you can just outrun your problems. You're a Support? Oh haha, sorry about you not having any ammo in your shotgun. Oh well. All of these things of course can be fixed in the beta, so other than that this game is great. Keep up the good work Tripwire, I know you can make the game great!

There is a saying in Videogames, something along the lines of, The sequel, is almost never better than the original.
Well, Tripwire Interactive, has succesfully accomplished the exact opposite.
Killing Floor 2 not only improves on every single element the original Killing Floor offered, but created new content that suddenly feels necessary. For instance, the class system has totally been reworked, has been simplified, and is now incredibly easy to work with, effectively smoothing all the bumps and rough edges the original had in it's class system.
The boss's suddenly feel more like... an actual boss, at this point in time, we have 2 boss's, the Patriarch, from the first game, who has also been reworked, with new dialogue, a new character model, animations, etc. Everything necessary for a familiar monster, and added a melee intensive boss, which makes choosing your weapon loadout even more important than in the first, you could rely on any weapon in the first game as a long range, medium, short, but now it is absolutely important that you have a very wide base of weapons in your loadout.
Killing Floor 2 is doing everything correctly, everything is moving in the right direction, and the developers couldn't be more supportive of their community, and leaving the game as available as ever to add new content to the game.
10/10, will buy all DLC in the near future.

Killing Floor was and is one of the best Shoot 'Em Dead games out there. When I heard that a second Killing Floor was going to get made after what, 5-7 years after the first one, I was ecstatic. After playing this for quite some time, I can honestly say that this game is a great sequel.
The graphics alone in this game are gorgeous! I loved the original Killing Floor's graphics and film grain they had implemented, but it being a whole new map zone, and getting some more "futuristic" updates, I love this one even more. I've grown bored of all the 'Futuristic' type guns and shooters that have come out recently, but this game has re-lit that light for me, and I'm able to enjoy it even more.
The weapons look and sound fantastic! Tripwire has put quite a bit of work into this game, and you can definitely see it. The sound quality of the guns being fired are beautiful. The game can have some glitches when it comes to sound, but they are hardly noticeable.  Some of the weapon models could use a bit more detail, like the HM-Tech guns. The glowing effect is nice, but the rest of the rifles just seem boring.
The gameplay feels nice. It doesn't just feel like you're holding down the mouse button and pointing at the zombies. You actually feel like you're getting recoil on the rifles, like where you hit decides whether or not the enemies will fall or not.
The perk systems have been reworked, and I absoultely love what they've done. It's not quite a "skill tree," but it does give you the decision on how you want your perk to play out. They are planning to bring even more types of perks. Personally, i always played Medic or Commando.
Pros & Cons
+Graphics look amazing
+Gameplay feels nice
+New Perk system
+Constant Development
-Commando class doesn't feel too rewarding
-Even though they said leveling is easier, it still feels very "grindey"
-Some guns could use more detail
