I've always liked South Park, and this review is probably gonna be a little biased by that. I can say straight away, if you don't like the series, then don't get this game, and stop reading.
I was a little worried about what to expect with this game when I saw the first gameplay videos. A mix of adventure and turnbased combat is a very rare thing to see these days, atleast among the "larger" titles. As soon as the game or rather episode started, my worries disappeared. This is not so much a game,as it is another episode in South Park.
You take on the role as the new kid in town, and as you get forced to make friends in the neighbourhood, all sorts of crazy adventures and humorous catastrophes happen. The story is very good and the progression in this, has never been to slow or to fast. I find that in some games the story gets lost in to much gameplay or the gameplay gets ruined by the story. This game seems to keep the balance between gameplay and story very nicely, which I find is very important to a game with so much comedy. This leads me to the main reason to get the game. The amount of profanity, insanity and sexuality mixed in with a nice amount of violence left me laughing out loud more times I can remember. If you like South Park humour the game is certainly required in your game collection.
The gameplay is nothing elaborate or even diffecult. You wander around on maps, interacting with items, people or enemies, and move between these maps without any load time. When you encounter an enemy, the game switches to a turnbased combat phase. The combat is fairly straightforward and for each attack there is a combination of mouseclicking and button-mashing to get it to work. Even if you fail in this sorta easy mash-click-buttoning (Which I did plenty of times), you will still damage your enemy, albeit for a smaller amount of damage. The combat sorta has a tactical element with selecting the right attack for the correct enemy and at the same time requiring a bit of skill with that click-button-mashing. The same applies to the enemy attacks, which you can defend yourself from.
The graphics and sound are the same as in the series, though there was a part in the game that changed considerably. I wont spoil anything in this review, but I can tell that I liked the retro-feel of it, and in combination with the story it was a little detail that left me smiling and laughing.
The game in itself would be 5 out of 5 stars from me. This however leaving out the price of the game and also the replay value. There are some small elements of choice in the game, but none that will make the story change to much. There are some choices with your class, and some choices during the game, none of which really makes that much of an impact on the story, which is my main reason to get the game. I spent 22 hours playing the game and with a price of 40 euros, that is a big price to pay for a game with nearly no replay value. Still, I look at this game as a gem, and 22 hours laughing and smiling, well... I pay around 10 euros to go to the movies, and those only last what? Like 2 hours?

How to NOT suck at this game (Single Player):
1. You can choose your civilization (Rome, Russia, or China I suggest)
2. Start your civilization and try to have as much peace as possible with the other civilizations
3. Make as many troops as possible over time
4. If a civilization wants you to team up and go at war with another civilizations, don't accept it since you'll lose many of your troops if you do
5. Don't just try to get as many troops, but try to have more than the other civilizations and spread them around to know what other civilizations lie out there.
6. If for whatever reason a civilization gets mad at you and steals one of your cities, then make more troops, surround your city, then make it into battle (be sure to have enough troops to drive your enemy out)
7. At the end, if you successfully get nukes before other civilizations and you are at peace with them, send in nukes and wipe them out.
8. Once you do this to one civilization, you know how to deal with the rest.
9. Good Luck!

Risk of Rain, is in my opinion, one of the beast indie rogue likes of the year, if not of all time. It pulls the nearly perfect synergy of random generation and unforgiving no save, one life, one go playstyle of the rogue like genre. The game's system of level progression and mob spawning is unforgiving and difficult, but is insanely addicting. Also the character selection gives a wide variety on different playstyles to fit you in particular, while still keeping the game interesting if you would like the challenge of switching up your particular playstyle. The random generation of chest items and boss items makes each run nearly unidentifiable from the previous. The only quip I have with this astounding game is the lack of random generation in the levels. There are normally 2 different "terrains" on each level and each "terrain" has about 2-3 different generations. Unfortunatley after your 10th or so time through the game, the level design becomes easily identifiable and stale. Nonetheless, this is still an incredibly addicting, satisfying, and frustatingly difficult game to spend hours on end mastering. 8.5/10

I've withheld my review on Arkham Knight til it came back up on the store so it will not be considered a pre-release review. First, let me say that I pre-purchased the Arkham Knight Premium Edition back at the start of June due to the being a longtime Arkham-series fan, and had actually had my hopes up that this would be as phenominal a game as it had been advertised in previews/trailers.
When the game originally launched, I could barely play it, as it was so horribly unoptimized that I was one of the 90+% of people that had to use a community-discussion workaround to make it playable. After I did get it up and running, the framerates I got weren't the best, but the game was quite playable with some moderate frame drops in overly busy areas. I completed the main storyline and a good amount (but not all) of the side content, and was satisfied with the story. However, I knew this was not the game I paid for, and sat down to wait for Rocksteady and Warner Brothers to clean up the mess they let Iron Galaxy Games make of the pc version.
Over 3 months later, the September patch came out, and at that point I couldn't even launch the game due to changes they'd made in the patch. This infuriated me, even moreso due to the fact that the pc DLCs had still been held back and the console players were still enjoying their games while the pc community was still in patch limbo.
Another month later, just a few days ago, another patch is promised to be released... and what did we get? No major changes except that they allowed the cumulative DLC-backlog that the original game-owners were due to finally be recieved and played. All the bugs/glitches from September were still there, and I still couldn't even start the game. I was able to figure out my particular issue and get into the game again, but the damage was done. I'll play the DLC from what I'm still owed in the season pass, but I frankly don't have the heart to even bother replaying the game again.
This whole 4-month (and soon to be half a year at this rate) fiasco just reeks of incompitence and flat out apathy on the part of the developers. The pc version of the game should NEVER have been outsourced to a 3rd party to complete. The fact that Warner Brothers re-released the game in this state and offered people who purchase it all the prior Arkham games is just a flat-out slap to the face, as it literally amounts to nothing, since people will have probably already had purchased most if not all of those games.
In conclusion, I cannont recommend this game as it is at this current time. It's a shame that the conclusion to the Arkham series had to turn out like this; I enjoyed many of Rocksteady's games in the past, but now I'm leery of anything they produce in the furture for pc, as I don't know if it'll get outsourced again.

I've withheld my review on Arkham Knight til it came back up on the store so it will not be considered a pre-release review. First, let me say that I pre-purchased the Arkham Knight Premium Edition back at the start of June due to the being a longtime Arkham-series fan, and had actually had my hopes up that this would be as phenominal a game as it had been advertised in previews/trailers.
When the game originally launched, I could barely play it, as it was so horribly unoptimized that I was one of the 90+% of people that had to use a community-discussion workaround to make it playable. After I did get it up and running, the framerates I got weren't the best, but the game was quite playable with some moderate frame drops in overly busy areas. I completed the main storyline and a good amount (but not all) of the side content, and was satisfied with the story. However, I knew this was not the game I paid for, and sat down to wait for Rocksteady and Warner Brothers to clean up the mess they let Iron Galaxy Games make of the pc version.
Over 3 months later, the September patch came out, and at that point I couldn't even launch the game due to changes they'd made in the patch. This infuriated me, even moreso due to the fact that the pc DLCs had still been held back and the console players were still enjoying their games while the pc community was still in patch limbo.
Another month later, just a few days ago, another patch is promised to be released... and what did we get? No major changes except that they allowed the cumulative DLC-backlog that the original game-owners were due to finally be recieved and played. All the bugs/glitches from September were still there, and I still couldn't even start the game. I was able to figure out my particular issue and get into the game again, but the damage was done. I'll play the DLC from what I'm still owed in the season pass, but I frankly don't have the heart to even bother replaying the game again.
This whole 4-month (and soon to be half a year at this rate) fiasco just reeks of incompitence and flat out apathy on the part of the developers. The pc version of the game should NEVER have been outsourced to a 3rd party to complete. The fact that Warner Brothers re-released the game in this state and offered people who purchase it all the prior Arkham games is just a flat-out slap to the face, as it literally amounts to nothing, since people will have probably already had purchased most if not all of those games.
In conclusion, I cannont recommend this game as it is at this current time. It's a shame that the conclusion to the Arkham series had to turn out like this; I enjoyed many of Rocksteady's games in the past, but now I'm leery of anything they produce in the furture for pc, as I don't know if it'll get outsourced again.

Risk of Rain is a refreshing twist on the action roguelikes that have become popular of late. With several character types to choose from, you have many ways to play the game. Items are exciting, enemies are tough but fair, and the level design is simple enough to allow the core features of the game to shine. On the standard difficulty, the game is quite a test, and a unique mechanic makes the game get harder the longer you take. This creates an interesting dynamic between "speedrunning" and "farming" and ensures that there is no one best way to move through the game.The soundtrack is also great. Highly recommended.

OK, So I've just completed the Scarecrow mission (is that the main mission by the way?)
What I've noticed since day 1 - obviously the initial release was pretty poor (but playable for me all be it at 30/60 fps) - I started the game and probably played a good few hours, but decided to wait for the first patch for the improved and much needed performance. (so my experience wouldnt be ruined)
I then played on the September patch, and things were massivly improved, the extra in game effects and 90fps are far superior - I played a bit more, but still I thought I'd wait for the October patch (I was busy with other things anyway).
October patch and at first it seemed like a downgrade - I play on some serious hardware i7 4770K @4.4Ghz, MSI 980Ti Gaming @ ~1400Mhz with 32Gb of system RAM! Also I have a G-Sync monitor @1440p (ASUS ROG P278Q).
I had the latest Hotfix drivers initially 358.59 and the game was running awful.
So I downgraded to 358.50 and things were still bad - however, turning off G-Sync made things much better (358.59 were supposed to fix some G-Sync framrate issues)
Finally I went back to 358.59 after removing the drivers properly with DDU and things seemed much improved with G-Sync ON.
What I do notice is, that for no apparent reason the framerate occasionally drops from ~80fps (with everything on max including gameworks) to 40fps, but also the GPU usage falls to 50%, this seems to happen when nothing much is going on and can be in a scene with low complexity - odd.)
Other than that, the framerate has been very good and the game has played mainly smoothly - I should hope so too with this hardware. (I can't remeber the September patch having this problem)
On that note I have very much enjoyed the Scarecrow campain, of note has been a very interesting story line and some absolutly awesome vocal acting, especially from the Joker - well written lines from all characters. The character detail is also superb, with all the main villains being superbly rendered and animated. Some great cutscenes too and very decent gameplay.
So all in all things are on the up, I would love to see the GPU usage bug squashed ASAP, I think I will pause my gameplay again until this patch is released.
Although still not perfect I would say great work so far considering the mess it was in on initial release, and please continue PC support even if the PC crowd is a bit fickle and hard to please (quite rightly so!)
A great game that I would highly recommend - especially when all the bugs are fixed - please hurry!
P.S. How do you get the consolation software that we are supposed to get for free? It's not in my library and is full price in the store.
Cheers,

I could forgive the rest of this game's misses and issues were it not for the fact that this dev team has invested time in creating a system of microtransactions rather than creating content for their unfinished, poorly functioning game. Sid Meier's Civilization V pits the player controlled protagonist, B.J. Blazkowicz, against the Nazi regime in a grim alternate history-in which the Allies lose World War II, and the Nazis hold power up until year 1960 (which is when the majority of the game takes place.) With emphasis on frantic, explosive combat, Sid Meier's Civilization V is not lacking in the violence department-the player can perform several gruesome takedowns, and dual wield most weapons, from pistols to assault rifles to fully-automatic shotguns to sniper rifles. Throughout the game, Civilization V consistently uses Nazi imagery to disturb the player and immerse them in the awful dystopia that is Nazi-controlled Earth. It also has a great story, but that's not something to spoil in the review box. All in all, I rate the game a 9/10-a must play!

Super hexagon is one of those small little games you expect to play for a few hours, and you end up wasting so much time on it you'll end up trying to force yourself to stop.
I ended up buying it simply because it looked pretty cool, not expecting much out of it. You start off with three levels being unlocked, with the other three being unlocked as you completed the levels you originally started off with.
The goal of Super Hexagon is simply to survive 60 seconds as you try to avoid 'walls' by controlling the little triangle. It's a simple concept but made tediously hard with the speed and constantly changing game. Each run through will be different, a mix of different patterns of walls which the longer you play, the better you'll learn.
Super hexagon is a game designed to get you hooked, however it's horribly difficult, with the last level taking hours and hours to complete even a 60 second play through. If you're not into difficult games and are prone to the lovely rage quit this game might not be for you, however others looking for a challenge may enjoy this greatly. It's one of those games that to get the full enjoyment you have to play for a short while - playing it for just 10 minutes will get you a lot of game overs and probably not a lof progress, but that's the point. Super Hexagon is a game where the longer you play, the better you play the game and the more you feel motivated to get to the end of the level.
So why buy Super Hexagon? If you love a catchy soundtrack, with hard but not impossible gameplay and something you'll end being too addicted to, this game is perfect. The price you'll pay for this fun little game isn't much too, so if you have the spare cash it'll be worth your time.

Super Hexagon is a game that is brimming with challenge in the form of reflexes, memory, and the ability to not blink.
When I bought it, I expected Super Hexagon to be a rhythm-based game. Gameplay instead involves dodging walls that converge towards the center shape alongside very nice chiptune tracks composed by Chipzel. When you restart a level after dying, the music will likely start at a different point, if not from what you may perceive as the "beginning" of the track. Despite this, as you continue to improve at the game, you will eventually experience previously unheard portions of the music. If you enjoy the chiptune genre, being able to hear more of a song you barely heard five seconds of is an additional reward.
The walls, unfortunately, do not follow the rhythm of the music, so there may be some confusion as to when you should actually press the left or right arrow key to dodge upcoming walls. The spin sometimes tricks you into thinking you can spin in one direction faster than another in order to dodge the wall, but the movement speed is the same regardless. Being able to overcome these challenges in order to get better record times and unlock harder levels is the gist of Super Hexagon.
If you want a game with relentless difficulty, or you enjoy the chiptune music genre, Super Hexagon is must-buy. Just don't get too frustrated.

This review encompasses Half-Life 2 and the two subsequent episodes.
The original Half-Life has been met with critical acclaim worldwide and is largely recognized as a milestone for FPS games, a title that revolutionized the genre among other things. Several years later, Valve released Half-Life 2 to another positive critical reception. This is where I disagree wholeheartedly with critics and the PC gaming populace. Whilst this game was among the first to use a physics engine, it remains stale in every other area.
Half-Life 2 is stuck in the past as there are zero innovative features in the game that elevate it over its predecessor, graphics and physics aside. The game still consists of travelling from shooting gallery A to shooting gallery B, while filling up your very spacious inventory with dozens of weapons. There is little variation in the formula and the beginning of the game plays indentically to the end, making the whole thing seem like a complete and utter waste of time. A notable addition to the game would be vehicles (the speedboat and the car); these sections of the game rank as the most dragged-on and uninspired levels in the game. You are thrown into either vehicle and have to drive down a linear path for what seems like an eternity, eventually gaining the ability to shoot MORE baddies. With every loading screen during this sequence, I was hoping that the game would finally move on and throw a bone at me, but this was not the case.
A bigger offender than the repetitive gameplay for me would be the bland and tasteless world in which the game takes place in. City 17 and every neighbouring area in the game (minus Ravenholm) is very generic and, quite frankly, dull. I don't get the impression that people live (or have ever lived) here. I feel no desire to explore this world because it is, for lack of a better word, just plain boring. Being a big fan of background music and game soundtracks, I am very disappointed with the tracks offered in this game: they're forgettable and actually detract from the game if anything. The fact that the majority of the game takes place in a silent world (music-less) is no better as I get the impression that nothing is happening and I just want to call it quits, partially because of my disinterest in the land. In comparison, the majority of Dark Souls' world has no background music, but because Lordran is such a mysterious, enthralling, and dangerous place, the silence actually compliments it and hearing music later on is rewarding in of itself.
I also don't understand why Gordon Freeman is such a loved character in the gaming community; he has ZERO personality and never speaks... not to mention, he doesn't even have a character model so I'm left wondering who the crowbar-wielding figure on the game's cover is. Link from The Legend of Zelda also never utters a single word, but we can catch glimpses of his thoughts and personality through his facial expressions, his history, and his actions. Gordon's history is entirely player-centric; he's a blank slate in Half-Life 1 and characters only know you for the events of that game in Half-Life 2, reminding me that this man is nothing without my control... that, in my books, is a huge immersion breaker.
To be honest, I couldn't care less about Half-Life 3 if it's just going to be more of this. I'm not "hating" on the franchise for enjoyment, I just don't see or understand why so many people adore this game to bits. In the end, your own opinion is more powerful than anything, but I still fail to see why this game was and still is such a huge success.

If you like South Park, you'll like this game. I've always found South Park to be funny and I enjoy the general sense of humor the show's creators have, but I actually don't actively watch the show and have probably only seen bits and pieces of the first 5 or 6 seasons (and the movie). You do NOT need to be an active viewer to enjoy this game.
The gameplay mechanics are fairly simple and straightforward. It uses turn-based combat with lots of variety in weapons, and a bit of variety in spells. Throughout the game you have "Magic," which is basically different types of farts which all seem to primarily gross out your opponent and drop their defense/attack. You also have "Abilities," which I think are more interesting than Magic. Each one is very unique to the character you're controlling, whether it be a party member or your main character. Some of them will be things from the show, like Stan's dog or Butter's secret villain identity, while others are jokes about gaming tropes and other surprises. You earn abilities for your character based on the class you chose, and all of them are pretty funny. You can also use your magic outside of combat to change the environment or even add negative status effects to your enemies before you actually engage them in battle.
During combat you're actually being more active than simply choosing an attack. Many attacks have unique instructions that you need to follow or else you will fail. For example, a specific attack of Kenny's requires you to hit the right button at the right time or the attack will fail and have a hugely negative effect on Kenny himself. You are required to block enemy attacks by pressing 'A,' and some attacks are very difficult (if not impossible) to block succesfully. The game gets less difficult, I found, as you progress through the story. By the end of the game most of my characters had very powerful battle-ending abilities that made fights pretty easy.
So the combat is actually pretty good for a satirical RPG, or at least it serves its purpose. The map of South Park is actually quite large and has a lot of secrets and fun activities for you to explore. Lots and lots of jokes are spread all around South Park and it's probably impossible to go a minute without a good laugh. There's a lot of references to other games, especially Skyrim (I swear Obsidian is obsessed with Bethesda), and even a few good movie references which made me laugh quite hard.
Finally, people who know South Park probably aren't surprised about this but this game makes you do some pretty ♥♥♥♥ed up♥♥♥♥♥♥ I was just fine with it, because I thought it was funny, but other people might be a little less willing to go along with some of the very *very* dirty jokes in this game. Let's put it this way: Do not play this game in front of any family members that you don't want looking at you weird. It's South Park, and it does not shy away from being South Park.
Love this game, it reminds me of a time when games were harder and frustration was inevitable, but welcome.

Update:
So after months of constant patches and updates and the season pass having been completed here is my full breakdown of the game
Pros:
- Story is great with interesting twists and turns
- The same stealth and combat elements that made the previouse games great have not only be preserved but addded some interesting improvements like the fear take down and the use of objects as weapons and the dual combos with partner characters
- Can now use the iconic Batmobile to get to places, partake in epic chases as well as solving possibles using the car's speed as well as weapons in its assault mode
- New puzzles that not only utilize Batman's arsenal but also the Batmobile
- Graphics look very stunning and gameworks effects like interactive smoke gives the PC version the greater edge in visuals
- Challenge modes are back and game has plenty of characters to play with
- Lost of interesting side missions
- Season pass is rich with additional content such as additional campaigns via other characters, more AR challenges, added story campaign and more cars and skins.
Cons
- Batmobile controls can be difficult to get used to, its not as tight as arcade racers like Need for speed
- Riddler puzzles are just WAAAY to much
- Game is well optimized with nvidia GPUs, not sure about AMD. and playable but not as well as it should be, I have solid 60fps when on foot but when on batmobile I get dips to the lower 50fps when dring in the city
- Gameworks functions are still terrible and best left for people with the heighest end rigs.
- Game is essentially a larger Arkham City, empty and full of thugs, which sucks because I was hoping we could have actual citizens to interact with this time and do side missions like rescuing babies or preventing murders and such, would have been a lot more immersive as a batman game.
- Season Pass is over priced despite what it has to offer, not worth more than €20 in my opinion.
- No SLI support
I overall enjoyed the game and at its current state its really difficult to argue against it, I picked this game up including season pass for €20 and since I got the other Arkham Games for free as a bonus I feel like I got an incredible deal, if you find this game and season pass for €30 or so euros then pick it up, anything above that however I would not recommend out of principle, WB's disregard for the PC community as of late is unacceptable, I will change my vote to a thumbs up once the game is reduced to an acceptable price range, as of now, the game is not worth its price tag.

This review encompasses Half-Life 2 and the two subsequent episodes.
The original Half-Life has been met with critical acclaim worldwide and is largely recognized as a milestone for FPS games, a title that revolutionized the genre among other things. Several years later, Valve released Half-Life 2 to another positive critical reception. This is where I disagree wholeheartedly with critics and the PC gaming populace. Whilst this game was among the first to use a physics engine, it remains stale in every other area.
Half-Life 2 is stuck in the past as there are zero innovative features in the game that elevate it over its predecessor, graphics and physics aside. The game still consists of travelling from shooting gallery A to shooting gallery B, while filling up your very spacious inventory with dozens of weapons. There is little variation in the formula and the beginning of the game plays indentically to the end, making the whole thing seem like a complete and utter waste of time. A notable addition to the game would be vehicles (the speedboat and the car); these sections of the game rank as the most dragged-on and uninspired levels in the game. You are thrown into either vehicle and have to drive down a linear path for what seems like an eternity, eventually gaining the ability to shoot MORE baddies. With every loading screen during this sequence, I was hoping that the game would finally move on and throw a bone at me, but this was not the case.
A bigger offender than the repetitive gameplay for me would be the bland and tasteless world in which the game takes place in. City 17 and every neighbouring area in the game (minus Ravenholm) is very generic and, quite frankly, dull. I don't get the impression that people live (or have ever lived) here. I feel no desire to explore this world because it is, for lack of a better word, just plain boring. Being a big fan of background music and game soundtracks, I am very disappointed with the tracks offered in this game: they're forgettable and actually detract from the game if anything. The fact that the majority of the game takes place in a silent world (music-less) is no better as I get the impression that nothing is happening and I just want to call it quits, partially because of my disinterest in the land. In comparison, the majority of Dark Souls' world has no background music, but because Lordran is such a mysterious, enthralling, and dangerous place, the silence actually compliments it and hearing music later on is rewarding in of itself.
I also don't understand why Gordon Freeman is such a loved character in the gaming community; he has ZERO personality and never speaks... not to mention, he doesn't even have a character model so I'm left wondering who the crowbar-wielding figure on the game's cover is. Link from The Legend of Zelda also never utters a single word, but we can catch glimpses of his thoughts and personality through his facial expressions, his history, and his actions. Gordon's history is entirely player-centric; he's a blank slate in Half-Life 1 and characters only know you for the events of that game in Half-Life 2, reminding me that this man is nothing without my control... that, in my books, is a huge immersion breaker.
To be honest, I couldn't care less about Half-Life 3 if it's just going to be more of this. I'm not "hating" on the franchise for enjoyment, I just don't see or understand why so many people adore this game to bits. In the end, your own opinion is more powerful than anything, but I still fail to see why this game was and still is such a huge success.

Update:
So after months of constant patches and updates and the season pass having been completed here is my full breakdown of the game
Pros:
- Story is great with interesting twists and turns
- The same stealth and combat elements that made the previouse games great have not only be preserved but addded some interesting improvements like the fear take down and the use of objects as weapons and the dual combos with partner characters
- Can now use the iconic Batmobile to get to places, partake in epic chases as well as solving possibles using the car's speed as well as weapons in its assault mode
- New puzzles that not only utilize Batman's arsenal but also the Batmobile
- Graphics look very stunning and gameworks effects like interactive smoke gives the PC version the greater edge in visuals
- Challenge modes are back and game has plenty of characters to play with
- Lost of interesting side missions
- Season pass is rich with additional content such as additional campaigns via other characters, more AR challenges, added story campaign and more cars and skins.
Cons
- Batmobile controls can be difficult to get used to, its not as tight as arcade racers like Need for speed
- Riddler puzzles are just WAAAY to much
- Game is well optimized with nvidia GPUs, not sure about AMD. and playable but not as well as it should be, I have solid 60fps when on foot but when on batmobile I get dips to the lower 50fps when dring in the city
- Gameworks functions are still terrible and best left for people with the heighest end rigs.
- Game is essentially a larger Arkham City, empty and full of thugs, which sucks because I was hoping we could have actual citizens to interact with this time and do side missions like rescuing babies or preventing murders and such, would have been a lot more immersive as a batman game.
- Season Pass is over priced despite what it has to offer, not worth more than €20 in my opinion.
- No SLI support
I overall enjoyed the game and at its current state its really difficult to argue against it, I picked this game up including season pass for €20 and since I got the other Arkham Games for free as a bonus I feel like I got an incredible deal, if you find this game and season pass for €30 or so euros then pick it up, anything above that however I would not recommend out of principle, WB's disregard for the PC community as of late is unacceptable, I will change my vote to a thumbs up once the game is reduced to an acceptable price range, as of now, the game is not worth its price tag.

Awesome game, great end to the Rocksteady arkham series.
I had few problems with the game at launch, and none at all now. I have a mid-range system and it plays great at 1080p with all settings max except for nvidia smoke (because it looks hilarious, like milk pouring out of the back of the car when spinning the tires), and I never drop below 45FPS.
I understand a lot of people had issues, and the game should never have been released in the state that it was.
But from my perspective, it's excellent. One of the best games in the last couple of years, and as good as arkham city, although still not quite as good as arkham asylum which will always have the top spot for me.
Batmobile isn't a great fit a lot of the time, turning the game into a kind of fun tank battle game, which would be fine if it wasn't in this game, because it just doesn't quite fit the franchise.
Voice acting is again top class, animations are flawless, graphics are just incredible, especially with advanced lighting and rain effects, and the new moves and gadgets keep the combat and predator encounters feeling fresh in a way origins never even came close to.
All in all, a fantastic game. I wouldn't ordinarily write a review to be honest, but with everyone hating on WB (rightly so in many cases), I figured that people who had no problems with the game should even it out. Because a lot of the hate is from people who had already made up their minds before the game was re-released, and no matter how well it ran they would say it was worse than before.
I heard there were over 100 bans handed out to people just being rude and aggressive on the forums the night it was re-released, and I can believe that. People were just determined to hate this game, and WB/rocksteady, no matter what they did. I can understand their frustration, but I honestly couldn't see WB doing anything better after the debacle that was the original launch.
Sure they were 100% wrong for allowing the game to be released in such a state, but they did do everything possible to sort it out, and to sort it out in the right way. Such as removing from the stores, and taking a few months to try and get it fixed up a bit.
Anyway, great game, runs a lot better for most people now since the re-release (although some still have issues, most are running it much better), and a fantastic finale to the series.

This is quite possibly the unniest game I have ever played.  As a southpark fan, there havent been many games that I felt capitalized on the potential of the franchise.  Matt Stone and Trey Parker were heavily involved in the creation of the game and along with developer Obsidian have created a fantastic RPG.
Story: 10/10  you are the new kid who moves to South Park. You soon meet the other children and begin playing their human's versus elves game.  Like each episode, the game soon spirals out of control, and everyone in the town wants you for your incredible "Dragonborn" abilities. Any fan of the show will love this story.
Gameplay 8/10 The game is a very simplified RPG.  The kids force each other to fight according to their game's rules.  Battles are fought turn based, with your kid (1 of 4 classes), and one friend.  abilities can be cast using power points, and each character has a designated health bar.  Like other RPG's you level up through fighting battles, and gain additional perks through helping others around town.  There are many side quests which unlock perks and summons.  The game takes about 15 hours to complete, but these 15 hours are very packed with fanservice and a very focussed experience.
Graphics 10/10  The game was designed to look just like the TV show.  It isnt made to push your PC to the max, but it perfectly accomplishes its goal of looking exactly like an episode of the show
Sound: 9/10  This game uses the exact sounds from the show, such as the turnaround when the show comes back from commercial.  If you like the show's sound you will liek this game.
Overall 9/10 =  This game is made for fans of the TV show.  It takes all the BS out of the RPG genre such as grinding levels and instead provides a very funny and enjoyable experience.  The writing alone is worth the price of the game, but the enjoyable combat and fun sidequests make this game worth paying full price.

This is quite possibly the unniest game I have ever played.  As a southpark fan, there havent been many games that I felt capitalized on the potential of the franchise.  Matt Stone and Trey Parker were heavily involved in the creation of the game and along with developer Obsidian have created a fantastic RPG.
Story: 10/10  you are the new kid who moves to South Park. You soon meet the other children and begin playing their human's versus elves game.  Like each episode, the game soon spirals out of control, and everyone in the town wants you for your incredible "Dragonborn" abilities. Any fan of the show will love this story.
Gameplay 8/10 The game is a very simplified RPG.  The kids force each other to fight according to their game's rules.  Battles are fought turn based, with your kid (1 of 4 classes), and one friend.  abilities can be cast using power points, and each character has a designated health bar.  Like other RPG's you level up through fighting battles, and gain additional perks through helping others around town.  There are many side quests which unlock perks and summons.  The game takes about 15 hours to complete, but these 15 hours are very packed with fanservice and a very focussed experience.
Graphics 10/10  The game was designed to look just like the TV show.  It isnt made to push your PC to the max, but it perfectly accomplishes its goal of looking exactly like an episode of the show
Sound: 9/10  This game uses the exact sounds from the show, such as the turnaround when the show comes back from commercial.  If you like the show's sound you will liek this game.
Overall 9/10 =  This game is made for fans of the TV show.  It takes all the BS out of the RPG genre such as grinding levels and instead provides a very funny and enjoyable experience.  The writing alone is worth the price of the game, but the enjoyable combat and fun sidequests make this game worth paying full price.

NEUTRAL THOUGHTS:
The micro transactions put some cool cosmetic items in the game, but the prices for most of the items worth having can get pretty high on the community marketplace.  $5 for a cool gun skin is nice, but the cost could rack up quick for multiple weapons.  A few items are are over $50.
THE BAD:
Not all of the classes are in the game yet, in a game where having the right team composition is part of what makes you win.  Some classes, like firebug, are significantly more powerful than others.  The firebug exploding zeds perk gives the firebug more explosives ability than the entire demolition perk.
Game needs a few more guns, community maps, and class balance.  It has been slow in coming, but I trust that Tripwire will finish it - someday.

Tripwire Interactive has been very, VERY smart about making this sequel.  Some will definitely look at this game and see more of the same or not enough iteration, but I argue that in this case that was kind of the point.  Rather than change things for the sake of experimentation (or worse, "just because") they merely took their current game, made note of what was GOOD, and then changed what could be done BETTER, all rebuilt from the ground up.  It's Killing Floor, but IMPROVED.
If you liked Killing Floor then there's high confidence you will like the sequel, since in major form and function it's all the same.  Beautiful environments for the kind of game it is.  You, five friends, your gun, and popping the heads of the same group of zed monstrosities through increasingly difficult waves of them.  Perks that serve as rough character classes, essentially the same as the last time around (the sniper has been changed to Gunslinger to focus more on pistols.)  Purchase better equipment from a trader between waves.  Weld doors.  Heal with miracle wonder drugs.  Hilarious British characters.  Fight a big final boss, etc. etc.
The things that have changed are pretty much improvements throughout, even if minor.
* Some are straight additions: there are two new types of common zeds, but they're both variations on the clot, making early rounds and crowd situations a bit more chaotic.  A melee bash was added too, similar to L4D (though it only hits a single target.)  Melee weapons can block, which has its uses tanking.  So on.
* Other changes modify how things used to work in order to streamline it.  Like the perks, for example.  Where before perks had 6 or 7 levels and took a huge grind to upgrade, here they have 25 levels and the upgrades proceed more incrementally.  It does mean the changes you see in yourself aren't that dramatic (+1% or +2% perk weapon damage per level, etc,) but they come much MUCH more frequently.  Likewise some of the more unusual or significant perk upgrades have been pulled out in favor of making them the big bonuses that occur every 5 levels, though you always have to choose between two upgrades (that you can change anytime between waves.)  Each perk also gets it's own variation of grenade so there's more thoughtful use of them and less "RARAGH I'M SURROUNDED ACTIVATE THE SELF-DESTRUCT!"
* Many changes are just little nice things: zeds are more dismemberable and the destruction overall is more deliciously gory.  Blood lingers on the battlefield for the rest of the level so that you can see where your major conflicts have been.  If you hit the reload key while your weapon is fully loaded the character actually checks the weapon to ensure that it is loaded.
There's more, but that's a pretty high level overview.  Since I adored the original Killing Floor, I've found the approach to the design of this sequel to be a blessing.  It's nothing but the proper followup for the kind of slaughterhouse game KF was.  Any complaints I have are marginal at best: for some reason the katana is not a berserker weapons, the auto-find server feature is lacking a few filters, perks between each other have variety but intra-perk only really has one path through the weapons... I'm already having a hard time thinking of other things.

Additionally, the game is very fluid feeling and has realistic physics that allow players to feel instantly immersed in the game. KF2 is similar to games like Team Fortress 2, Left for Dead 2, and Counter Strike: GO. KF2 includes a long list of acheivements, a rich item system, and significant replay value. A couple of highlights for this game are it's metal soundtrack and mid-combat bullet time feature. I highly recommend this game to FPS fans.

This is definitely the most ambitious Arkham Batman game to date, and it shows. Visually it's one of the best looking games of all time. It controls great, give you the tools to be the Batman, and for the first time ever you feel as if you can really roam about as the caped crusader all thanks of the inclusion of the batmobile. Sadly the game was not ported well to PC, and you need some of the beefiest tech to be able to run this game maxed out and with stable framerates. Even then you will experience stutter from time to time as assets load while you travel about. The game needs a lot of RAM, and even an SSD seems to be mandatory for it to be semi enjoyable.
It's all a big shame, since this is as close as you can get to the ultimate Batman expereince, the game has tons of content (especially if have the season pass), but it never truly was finished to the standard we expected, meaning there are still bugs/glitches and performance issues to be had no matter what platform you play it on.
On this basis alone I cannot it give it a thumbs up, but I wish I could! It is an extremely fun game, and if you can get it on a sale, and you have the system specs to power it properly, then you will still enjoy it, you will just have to swallow your pride and live with the performance issues.

Half-Life 2 is one of the most critically aclaimed games of it's time, and even now is still shocking the target audience.  This almost stereotypical game features intense Single-Player FPS gunfights, plus the ever-iconic Crowbar, which you get near the beginning of the game, a Gravity-Manipulating lasergun, and a few more creative items to kill the Combine, a quarantine military group with cycloptic helmets, and the various different alien-like creatures such as the Headcrabs and Antlions.
Now, a First Person Shooter with a few creative aspects with a 3-way war is not very common, but The Last of Us pulled it off, and it gave us 3rd Person action, insane brutality, and, believe it or not, scientific accuracy!  So, what sets Half Life 2 apart from the other games similar to it?  First of all, Half Life 2 is a classic!  It was one of the first games to feature the kind of 3-way plot that it does.  And the characters, oh the characters!  I remember when I first played HL2, I thought that the game felt so... so real!  All of the main characters have their own voice-actors, backstories, and roles in the game.  Alyx, being your assistant in bringing down the main antagonist, is one of the most important.  But still, TLoU did the same thing, and that's the point:  Half-Life has become a template for success. 96/100 from MetaCritic is jsut unheard of, and the game came out 10 years ago!  10 bloody years!
I'm not even going to talk about the weapons in this review, because many of them are spoilers inside of themselves.  All you need to know is that the are da bomb.  Anyway, go get this game right now if you don't already possess its holyness.  Good Ole' Half Life 2 gets a big at 11/10 from me, which is pretty cray.  WaterSlap Seal Of Approval Plus a couple Rolos :D:

As a loyal fan of the Killing Floor series, I can say only this: this game succeeds where its predecessor has failed, in many areas. For example, fellow fans would remember that the voice acting in the first game was kind of dull (Though the lines were kind of amusing.) Like there's only 2 different voice sets for over 20 plus playable characters, and it's rather tough to differentiate one voice set from the other. Still, it would be nice if the zeds could talk in this game, just pointing it out. (Best line from the first game is a line by the scrake which is, "I like trousers" or something like that. His voice was muffled!)
Then there's the new and improved animations, the Gore system, the improved zed time visuals hell, the whole visuals really. The Gore system in particular in conjuction with zed time is simply a good sight to behold.And the soundtrack is a killer.
The perks in this game has been reworked it would seem. Some get beefed up, others get a little downgraded but I'm sure Tripwire will get to that eventually. Personally I find the new melee combat system to be the icing on the cake for this game, in terms of gameplay.
However, as usual with all games, this one isn't perfect. Sometimes the zeds feel a little bit overpowered for some players. The zeds in HoE difficulty in particular were unyielding and unforgiving. In hard difficulty I have noticed that they could easily eradicate the newer players but I'm ready to blame their lack of skill for that. Seriously, try to level up a bit before tackling the higher difficulties. I've seen one too many tryhards trying to survive through a challenging match with a low level perk.
And I taffing hate that flame-spewing husk, he'd just roast me in seconds even if I was on full health. A beefed-up berserker. Roasted. In seconds. (Not really a complaint, just a reminder for my teammates and/or potential teammates to shoot down the husks while I take down the big guys.)
I'd say I would recommend this game for anyone seeking a challenge and those who wouldn't rage too much or blame medics for everything. Definitely avoid this game if you can't stand the sight of blood or are afraid of people who would blame you for their failures.

let's  get this out of the way shall we?
this game isn't as bad as people make it seem,
before buying this game, like any other person out there who plays on a budget
I decided to take a look at the reviews and comments before deciding on buying
or not.
When I first saw the comments, I was sorta discouraged, people kept saying it didn't
live up to their expectations, some nitpicking here and there and whatnot, but most
seemed to agree on the game (at least it's core gameplay) was indeed fun,
so after thinking it out for sometime I decided to buy it and see for myself,
I wasn't dissapointed,
from the viewpoint of someone who's started killing floor 2 (sadly I didn't get to live the
KF1 hype properly) the game feels and plays GREAT, some people out there complained
about holding shift to sprint, instead of pulling the knife out to boost speed,
I guess some people dislike this, some (myself included) do not, others complained
about the crosshair inclusion etc... but putting all that aside, I had a fun time.
As someone who likes to play support roles in many games (the medic in TF2, healers in MMO's
overall support in some fps) the first time I booted up the game, I came thinking that
probably my medic's starting loadout would look and feel crappy and probably would leave
me with guilt of knowing I picked a crappy class just so I could stick to my healer role I usually
do....
Man was I WRONG ;D
Playing as a medic in KF2 feels so good, not only do my starting weapons feel like they deal some
acceptable damage but are also capable of doing headshots and other cool stuff that I feared
would have been locked out because I was a healing class,
but instead, not only are my weapons pretty good for picking off zeds, I can easily heal from a
distance (I guess all that medic grinding in TF2 helps) but to my surprise, healing grants me
dosh, I can't believe how many times I've managed to complete just enough dosh for my
next tier weapon, solely because I took the time to heal someone out there in the middle
of a round,
I gotta say, being a medic or a support doesn't feel like as much as "being the load" over here
than in other FPS's I've played, so I got that going for me, which is nice.
Moving on, the perk system, loving it so far, being able to customize my perks is a great way
to replay a class which I believe might feel too stale or repetitive, sure some people
will most likely give you flak for not going for the "meta" perks for each class, but all in all
I do believe some core perks CAN change how you play certain classes, so I guess
mix and matches are recommended.
Now, as I kept on reading the reviews, most people seemed to complain about 1 particular
issue, and I do believe it's no coincidence, the microtransactions.
yup it's the one demise that I do believe makes or breaks most modern games nowadays
some people feel indiferent about it, while most people blatantly dislike it because they
feel like they're being cheated out of content which should have been included
in the game, in a way, I guess I could agree, this isn't F2P so a degree of what goes on
in the game's market shouldn't be sold as addons, a few buyable cosmetics should suffice,
add too many and you got yourself another TF2 or CS:GO, both good respectable games that
in a way, got ruined by their own economies, featuring scammers, beggars and overall
hardcore merchs who solely touch the game for a quick sale.
But all in all, moving all of it's flaws and failures to meet veteran's standards, I'd say this game
has a pretty strong core gameplay, it certainly left me wanting more,
TL:DR: The game's pretty good, not excellent, BUT also not as horrible as people make it seem.
give it a chance if you like co-op, or had a blast playing mann vs machine in TF2,

This, to me, is what a batman game should be. Huge open world, a lengthy main story campaign, intense and intriguing  side missions, and a very solid batmobile (not a bat-gimmick...). It honestly just reminds me of an intense open world grand theft auto super hero hybrid.
The game mechanics mirror those in the past arkham games. However, I will say it is fun to finally steal a thugs bat and start wailing on a group of militia/thugs. Some new additions to gadgets also add a new level of depth to some situations (lots of different ways to hack). The batmobile is really fun, especially after its totally upgraded, and don't be surprised if you end up fighting a group of 20-30 tanks at some points. It does take some getting used to, and can be semi frustrating until you get a full grasp of it (do the beginning of the riddler quest, it helps gets you oriented).
The story is very engaging. It flows at a good rate and keeps you wanting to know more up until the end. You can tell a lot of comic and movie arcs influenced a lot of the main and side quest stories, which is admirable. It's cool to see certain characters pop up out of nowhere and follow their own story in the midst of the Arkham Knights takeover. To let you know, the arkham episodes are each about 15 minutes so far (minus batgirl) and they are $2. If you want to do some cool missions involving other characters in the arkham universe, I'd say it's worth the $2. The new game plus and AR challenges add plenty of replayability as well. The amount of content you get with the base game is definitely worth the $60. Also, the voice acting in this chapter of the series is on par, and it's nice to see Troy Baker as a bad guy.
I'm a big fan of action adventure games, I don't care as much about gameplay and looks as I do story. This is on par with the Mass Effect series, Zelda, Deus Ex, Tomb Raider, and other story driven games. It does look beautiful as well. The lighting and shaders really do a lot for the overall creation of a dark, murky Gotham. And the rain is a really nice touch (there are 2 other phases Gotham goes through in the game, and they look beautiful). It's a huge enviornment as well, it's basically three Arkham Cities... And don't forget, you can drive through them now (with a tank).
I could always run it. I'm sorry for the people who cannot. I will say I hope if you have the specs to run it you really should buy it, it's a beautful finale to the series. The game is wonderful, the release wasn't. If you can run it, get it.

Half-Life 2 is one of the most critically aclaimed games of it's time, and even now is still shocking the target audience.  This almost stereotypical game features intense Single-Player FPS gunfights, plus the ever-iconic Crowbar, which you get near the beginning of the game, a Gravity-Manipulating lasergun, and a few more creative items to kill the Combine, a quarantine military group with cycloptic helmets, and the various different alien-like creatures such as the Headcrabs and Antlions.
Now, a First Person Shooter with a few creative aspects with a 3-way war is not very common, but The Last of Us pulled it off, and it gave us 3rd Person action, insane brutality, and, believe it or not, scientific accuracy!  So, what sets Half Life 2 apart from the other games similar to it?  First of all, Half Life 2 is a classic!  It was one of the first games to feature the kind of 3-way plot that it does.  And the characters, oh the characters!  I remember when I first played HL2, I thought that the game felt so... so real!  All of the main characters have their own voice-actors, backstories, and roles in the game.  Alyx, being your assistant in bringing down the main antagonist, is one of the most important.  But still, TLoU did the same thing, and that's the point:  Half-Life has become a template for success. 96/100 from MetaCritic is jsut unheard of, and the game came out 10 years ago!  10 bloody years!
I'm not even going to talk about the weapons in this review, because many of them are spoilers inside of themselves.  All you need to know is that the are da bomb.  Anyway, go get this game right now if you don't already possess its holyness.  Good Ole' Half Life 2 gets a big at 11/10 from me, which is pretty cray. A fantastic game for fans of the show. At first with all the delays, I thought the game would come out and be terrible, if the game ever came out. I am glad to see that the pushed back date was worth it, the combat is very much like paper mario, and paper mario the thousand year door, you have different attacks that with the correct button presses,you can score extra hits/extra damage. It had your multiple weapons like paper mario, like a sword and a bow, which enemies will take stances to which one of the weapons would be rendered usless, like how a enemy with a spike on his head would damage you if you jumped on it in paper mario. The special moves are also things that can be interacted with for more damage, which keeps battles from getting dull.
The game has a fairly decent challenge, though it can jump and catch you off guard, but never gets impossibly hard. The story plays out like a south park episode, taking jokes from the show, and serving wonderful fresh new gags and jokes as well. Everyone has something to say to you, and it's one of the few games that make me actually laugh out loud. The concept of making yourself in the south park world is super neat as well, or just putting anyone you want in south park, the customization of your character is vast.
The presentation is nice, the music is great to listen to, taking songs from the show, and putting that RPG-esque music in here and there. It's a very fun game, with amusing jokes, and feels like your watching a interactive south park episode. I reccomend it to anyone, even people who don't really watch the show, but are looking for a solid RPG. If you hate the show, then why are you even reading this? You silly little person you.

Half-Life 2 is one of the most critically aclaimed games of it's time, and even now is still shocking the target audience.  This almost stereotypical game features intense Single-Player FPS gunfights, plus the ever-iconic Crowbar, which you get near the beginning of the game, a Gravity-Manipulating lasergun, and a few more creative items to kill the Combine, a quarantine military group with cycloptic helmets, and the various different alien-like creatures such as the Headcrabs and Antlions.
Now, a First Person Shooter with a few creative aspects with a 3-way war is not very common, but The Last of Us pulled it off, and it gave us 3rd Person action, insane brutality, and, believe it or not, scientific accuracy!  So, what sets Half Life 2 apart from the other games similar to it?  First of all, Half Life 2 is a classic!  It was one of the first games to feature the kind of 3-way plot that it does.  And the characters, oh the characters!  I remember when I first played HL2, I thought that the game felt so... so real!  All of the main characters have their own voice-actors, backstories, and roles in the game.  Alyx, being your assistant in bringing down the main antagonist, is one of the most important.  But still, TLoU did the same thing, and that's the point:  Half-Life has become a template for success. 96/100 from MetaCritic is jsut unheard of, and the game came out 10 years ago!  10 bloody years!
I'm not even going to talk about the weapons in this review, because many of them are spoilers inside of themselves.  All you need to know is that the are da bomb.  Anyway, go get this game right now if you don't already possess its holyness.  Good Ole' Half Life 2 gets a big at 11/10 from me, which is pretty cray. Incredible game, had no problems from the start (including seamless batmobile animations), adds the mystery from Arkham City to a war-like situation, giving a completely fresh feel to the Arkham franchise. The graphics can be run on maximum settings with all settings maxed out with a gtx 780, at above 60fps ( dependng on other components ). As for all the complaints about the overusage of the batmobile in the campaign, well you asked for it... It feels like a more realistic approach as I doubt batman would not use the batmobile in fear of unavailable parking. much of the story can be completed without it, and travelling is amazing both in the car, on foot and in the air- I doubt humans will be punching tanks into submission anytime soon. I feel for those whom the game didn't run well for since the start, but that really shouldn't put people off now, especially with the patches and DLC available. The only things which are disappointing thus far are the lack of a Nolan skin, the lack of free roam for all characters (although mods take care of this), and the length of the Harley Quinn DLC-takes about 13 minutes, no exaggeration. Obviously, it being an Arkham game, we can't expect the mods to be Skyrim/Fallout/GTA standard, but MrJAG on youtube is doing a great job with this and the other arkham games, so check him out.
The best of the Arkham franchise, why?
1) Batmobile- enough said
2) Interesting and good looking skins
3) Overwhelming visuals, easily better than those of The Witcher 3 etc
4) Open world enough not to get bored, but not cumbersome and bland
5) Engaging and flowing narrative
6) Loads of interesting easter eggs
7) Somehow they improved the combat again...
8) Dual play is amazing
9) Narrative has a decent length- not witcher 3 by any stetch of the imagination, but longer than that of Asylum -or at least it felt this way
10) The ending- although lacking closure, is very symbolic, and very emotional
Compared to the other Arkham games:
1) Lacked the same level of mystery that was in city
2) No free roam catwoman etc :( as standard
3) Contrary to popular belief, it lacks the feel from origins which really made it a great game for me
4) Boss battles were nowhere near the other games
Conclusively, it is not a combination of the other Arkham games, however, it has its own new feel for the game, and gotham itself, with a story which-for comic readers is a refreshing and intelligent character development, with the addition of upcoming DLCs, and for non readers, is mindblowing- or so I've heard. The compensation for the game's late release isn't great for Arkham fans, but hopefully the fans's cries will be heard. However this shouldn't be a reason not to buy this game. A lot of developers worked really hard and have accomplished something breathtaking.
Yes, Rocksteady messed up big time, but if their previous games are anything to show their value as producers, then we should stop giving them the stick for the initial mess up that was the PC port, and enjoy the game with its patches.
And if you read this far, geez, you should be playing the game already.

Overall:
A blend of JRPG mechanics and WRPG presentation. It really feels like playing through a highlights package of all the series funniest moments. The focus is on the weird and wacky stuff from the show's long run, rather than anything political or topical. The game is short (approx 10 hours) and not particularly challenging, but lots of fun while it lasts. Worth buying at full price for long-time fans of the show who have been watching it since the 90s, teenage/college age gamers might be better off waiting for a sale.
Incidentally, as an Australian, I played the censored version. I'm of the opinion that Matt & Trey's open contempt for the Australian Classification Board is actually funnier than the scenes that were censored.
Pros:
* Amazing presentation - indistinguishable from the cartoons
* Genuinely funny humor
* Fun gameplay in first half of game - wide variety of viable combat tactics
* Flexible class system - Classes give unique abilities, but don't constrain your playstyle
* Huge amount of hidden content and references from the series
* Very stable for an Obsidian game - bugs are relatively minor, only encountered a game-stopping bug once (reloaded, bug did not re-occur).
Cons:
* Checkpoint based saves take 90s Nostalgia a bit too far
* Armor scaling issues and widespread immunity to status effects in the late game restrict viable combat tactics
* Keyboard layout not adjustable or even visible - bothersome if you forget which keys did what

Incredible game, had no problems from the start (including seamless batmobile animations), adds the mystery from Arkham City to a war-like situation, giving a completely fresh feel to the Arkham franchise. The graphics can be run on maximum settings with all settings maxed out with a gtx 780, at above 60fps ( dependng on other components ). As for all the complaints about the overusage of the batmobile in the campaign, well you asked for it... It feels like a more realistic approach as I doubt batman would not use the batmobile in fear of unavailable parking. much of the story can be completed without it, and travelling is amazing both in the car, on foot and in the air- I doubt humans will be punching tanks into submission anytime soon. I feel for those whom the game didn't run well for since the start, but that really shouldn't put people off now, especially with the patches and DLC available. The only things which are disappointing thus far are the lack of a Nolan skin, the lack of free roam for all characters (although mods take care of this), and the length of the Harley Quinn DLC-takes about 13 minutes, no exaggeration. Obviously, it being an Arkham game, we can't expect the mods to be Skyrim/Fallout/GTA standard, but MrJAG on youtube is doing a great job with this and the other arkham games, so check him out.
The best of the Arkham franchise, why?
1) Batmobile- enough said
2) Interesting and good looking skins
3) Overwhelming visuals, easily better than those of The Witcher 3 etc
4) Open world enough not to get bored, but not cumbersome and bland
5) Engaging and flowing narrative
6) Loads of interesting easter eggs
7) Somehow they improved the combat again...
8) Dual play is amazing
9) Narrative has a decent length- not witcher 3 by any stetch of the imagination, but longer than that of Asylum -or at least it felt this way
10) The ending- although lacking closure, is very symbolic, and very emotional
Compared to the other Arkham games:
1) Lacked the same level of mystery that was in city
2) No free roam catwoman etc :( as standard
3) Contrary to popular belief, it lacks the feel from origins which really made it a great game for me
4) Boss battles were nowhere near the other games
Conclusively, it is not a combination of the other Arkham games, however, it has its own new feel for the game, and gotham itself, with a story which-for comic readers is a refreshing and intelligent character development, with the addition of upcoming DLCs, and for non readers, is mindblowing- or so I've heard. The compensation for the game's late release isn't great for Arkham fans, but hopefully the fans's cries will be heard. However this shouldn't be a reason not to buy this game. A lot of developers worked really hard and have accomplished something breathtaking.
Yes, Rocksteady messed up big time, but if their previous games are anything to show their value as producers, then we should stop giving them the stick for the initial mess up that was the PC port, and enjoy the game with its patches.
And if you read this far, geez, you should be playing the game already.

I used to be a Halo fan. Then Halo 4 came out, which upset me so much that I ragequit Xbox Live altogether (well, that and the fact Microsoft lost my profile). I then became a PC gamer. Later, I realized that I never did beat Half-Life 2, and the last time I played it was renting it when I was a kid (and ragequiting on the 'We don't go to Ravenholm' chapter, lol).
I saw it as an opportunity to play a 'new' triple-A IP that wasn't utter COD copy-cat garbage, and I took it. I never felt so pleased with a game in a long time, and it was certainly a breath of fresh air.
I remember the days of the Halo vs. Half-life debate, and now I can say for certain: Half-Life 2 is longer and more exciting than any Halo campaign. And this is comming from a former Halo Fan. What makes it better then Halo is the fact that the game is harder by default, because there is NO REGENERATING HEALTH. Additionally, the game really likes to troll you (and this game came out before the term 'trolling' was even invented!) by throwing situations that can be both difficult, and also bring about an air of satire.
For example, there was one part where you had to crawl through a vent and had to leave a friend behind to open the way for them. As I went through, there was a branch off. One side had some energy pick-ups, so I naturally crawled in that direction. However, as soon as I got them, the vent broke and I plopped down directly back in front of the person I had left behind, who then smugly said "Back so soon?" I rolled my eyes, and then went back in the vent and took the other route. However, the vent broke again, but instead of falling out of it a whole section fell off the ceiling with me inside it. After it settled, I broke out of the vent's grate and tentatively poked my head out the top...
O_O
...
XD
Inches away and all around the fallen section of vent that I was inside, the entire room was filled with tripwires and explosive barrels! One wrong move and I'd be one fried Freeman. Like an idiot, my first idea was to chuck a grenade out of the vent section I was in, duck back inside, and hope for the best. Needless to say, it didn't work. Then I somehow jumped and bounced over all the trip-wires safely, and made it to an utility elevator at the other side of the room...only for that to fall down the shaft and into water that was at the bottom, which nearly drowned me.
It's that sort of thing that pervades much of the game, and you'll be entertained for hours on end. It is quite a long campaign, and for me, despite palying as much as I could and for as long as I could (before and after work), it took me over a week to beat on normal, and I wasn't really stuck on any part.
There is one warning though: this is not a mindless shooter. Besides shooting the bad guys, you ABSOLUTELY have to scavenge for ammunition and health packs, which may be hidden. Also, there are some logic/physics puzzles as well that might stump the ordinary player and prevent them progressing for upwards of half an hour or more. While I didn't usually have a problem with the puzzles, I'm pretty sure others might.
But if you aren't afraid of a challenge for both your gun skills and your noodle, and are actively looking for one, this is definately the game for you.

This game has the best enjoyment-to-cost value out there in the indie game world.  For only three dollars (fifty-nine cents if you bought it during the Autumn Sale) you can play a game so addicting that you think about it during school, work, or even free time.  Don't be flabbergasted by the trailer; the game is much more kind and forgiving than that.  This game starts slow and builds up in difficulty depending on how long you have survived, thusly making this game operate on your experience.  If you fail, it is only because "oh, I turned right when I should've turned left" or "agh!, I almost had it!".  Those situations entice a "challenge", a barrier that you can smash, a hurdle you can jump.  And when you do, you feel amazing... until it happens again.  This neverending cycle is what makes this game so appealing.  Once you play it, you're hooked.
In other words, this game is fantastic and you should play it.

This is the game to buy for Roguelike fans who want a little more action.
It combines the randomized levels and items, permanent death, and quick character progression of the roguelike genre with fast paced side-scrolling platformer/shooter mechanics.
Like most Roguelikes RoR is short on story, but there are little bits here and there.  The opening showcases a sci-fi space freighter being demolished by a mysterious being, and various bestiary entries that can be found are written from the point of view of the PC which expound on the disastrous inroduction.
Gameplay is definitely the showcase in any Roguelike, and Risk of Rain is thoroughly polished in that area.  Featuring 10 different characters each with their own suite of abilities, and an arsenal of 100+ items whose effects range from increasing your basic attack speed to infecting enemies in melee range with a damage over time toxin that jumps on death, replayability is essentially infinite.
What makes Risk of Rain unique in the genre is a time system that drives the player forward constantly.  As time passes during gameplay, a meter fills in the upper right corner of the screen increasing the difficulty at certain points.  A player must balance time spent hunting for experience and items in each level with finishing it early before the next stage spawns insurmountable hordes of enemies, providing a tense atmosphere during each playthrough.
Risk of Rain also boasts an excellent pixel art style, with expressive animations and distinct enemy outlines so the player can tell at a glance what they are facing.  A color-coded elite spawn system also mixes things up, also allowing instant recognition of immediate threats.
The soundtrack is probably the most impressive aspect of the game, with a general exploration theme and boss theme for each level.  It is at once atmospheric and blood pumping, and should be left on when playing.
Lastly, Risk of Rain also features online cooperative play, which can provide entire worlds of fun for a group of friends with a night to spare.
All in all, Risk of Rain is a real gem and if you enjoy Roguelikes, platformers, or side-scrolling shooters it really should be a part of your Steam library.

South Park: The Stick of Truth is a RPG with the aesthetics and humor of the South Park universe. The game's animations are very much like that of the show, which will tickle the fancy of the fans of the show. Along with that you have the combat and the RPG elements reminiscent of a decent Final Fantasy game. The combat is solid. The UI can be a tad finickey in the open world, but it's something you can get used to. The game play is not entirely linear, you are introduced to an open world but are limited to how much you can explore by how far into the story line you are in.
This game comes with roughly 9 hours of story line. I completed the game in 14 hours, 5 of which was added for exploration and side quests, which the game has a lot of. The side quests are most certainly very interesting and engaging enough for me to want more.
The game is, of course, meant for a more mature and tolerate audiance. The slap-stick humor may turn some off, while others will absolutely love it. I myself have only watched one South Park before playing this game, and I have to forwarn you now, the game certainly is a lot worse than the actual show. Do not let kids watch you play this.
My biggest let down with this game is how quickly I got to the character level cap, 15. I got to level 15 when I was just half way past the story. At that point I had little to no challenge finishing the game at all.
The Stick of Truth is a very good representation of a South Park episode in the form of a game. The animations were nailed, the combat is solid, the world is good, and the story is, perhaps, a little bit worse then the normal South Park style. Give it a try!
