I've intended this review to be mostly spoiler free, a lot of the fun is with how random the game is, so I'd advise not to go rummaging through the achievements and too many reviews so you don't spoil it for yourself.
If you like South Park even a little bit you should buy this game. Even if the game was rubbish - which it isn't - it would still contain more jokes and South Park footage than almost an entire series contains. The jokes are often quite entertaining standing alone, but there are plenty of references to the show and other pop culture references (including other game references). I'm a great fan of the show, and the game not only does it justice but takes the show to new heights.
The game is highly offensive and is really not afraid to press buttons. In fact, if it's a sensitive topic South Park pushes it even harder. The game has been censored in some regions (but not on Steam!) and in my opinion the censored scenes were not the worst in the game.
On the gameplay side the game is not particularly difficult, but not completely challenge-less. It's a turn based RPG and has lots of weapons, weapon modifiers. It also has 'magic'. The combat requires precise timing of specific button presses to get the full weapon strength and to block attacks. I found this a little infuriating at times, especially for the more complicated special moves (some of which are absolutely hilarious).
Make sure you go exploring, there is tons of content in the game and some of it is quite amusing. There are very few South Park characters that have not made an appearance.
I hit a couple of bugs when playing, in two cases I had to restart from an earlier save. Be careful around the save system too, it doesn't save at the exact point you are at. If you are in doubt, change area to save - although you may find the enemies re-spawn in some cases if you do this.
I finished the main storyline and side-quests in around 18 hours. Do I think this is too short for the money? No, the game is just the right length and there is more than enough content to justify the full price tag. Was it worth the wait? Most definitely, I'm glad they took the time to polish it.
This game is easily a 9/10 and probably in my top 10 games list of all time. Well done Obsidian, well done South Park Digital Studios!

Let me start this off by saying that this game is amazing fun and a definite must have.
Now for a real review.
Risk of Rain is a mix of a platformer, a rogue-lite and action. The player is dropped off on a strange and hostile planet after a crash with their spaceship. You set out as one of 10 characters that made an emergency landing far from the ship to make your way back to that very ship. Your goal is to survive the journey there, taking you through at least 5 levels (with 10 different ones) on the way. Reaching the ship will take quick thinking, combat capabilities and guts. Without these, you will not survive.
Risk of Rain plays through (mostly) randomly generated levels where death means death. No quickloading, no respawn points, nothing. You die you start over. On your way through the levels your character gains experience and money from killing enemies. Experience levels your character up and boosts it's stats (like health, damage output, HP regen etc). Money is spent on either chests for random items, vending stations to pick from 3 items, or on shrines to try your luck for an item. Items are either passive or 'use' items, and will prove valueable on your journey. Every item has it's own unique trait, and gathering as much as you can will definitly aid your survival.
Every level is filled with different enemies, from rock golems to big-horners (I hate these) to robot Temple Guardians. Each with their own attacks and strategy to approach. At the end of every level a teleporter awaits, setting in motion the final stage of a level. During 90 seconds the entire place fills up with enemies as well as a boss. Once are all defeated, the player can look around some more to pick up any items they might've forgotten (or couldn't afford yet) or progress to the next level.
The beauty about the game is how every playthrough is different. Every character has their own 4 unique moves and playstyle. Every enemy has their own unique attack and traits. Every boss requires a different strategy to take down. And in the end it's all about that final encounter with the very being that destroyed your ship. Will you defeat him, or fall before him?
Risk of Rain is amazing and I love it. 9/10

So, it's been just over half a year since KF2 hit Early Access, and despite some "controversy", I still fully recommend getting this game.
I'll go ahead and attempt to answer some common questions and concerns.
"Does Tripwire update the game frequently enough?"
-Not at all. Updates up until recently have been painfully slow for an EA game with no meaningful content usually added with them. They seem to be updating the game more often since adding The Patriarch back though.
"What about those microtransactions? I don't want this to be another PAYDAY 2!!!"
-So far, it's not a huge issue. All microtransactions are cosmetic in nature and do not affect the gameplay in any meaningful way (unlike with PD2), and you can also obtain them via drops. It's basically the exact same system as TF2/CS:GO. Only reason it's controversial to a lot of people is because of when it was implemented (during EA), and the timing of which it was implemented (just after the whole PD2 controversy).
If the microtransactions ever include content that affects gameplay in any way, expect this review to change to a negative one.
"Is the game fun?"
-♥♥♥♥ YES, ♥♥♥♥ YES, ♥♥♥♥ YES.
Ever since adding back The Patriarch and the new Gunslinger perk, the game has felt much more alive (heh) than it ever has before. It's still extremely satisfying to kill zeds no matter which perk or weapon you choose. It's extremely fun with friends, especially if you come across a server with custom maps (thanks modders).
And that's the crux of it honestly. Despite Tripwire taking forever to add meaningful content until recently, and despite the essentially non-issue microtransactions, the core game is still stupidly fun to play.
It's not the skins that make me come back to this game, it's just the core loop of using satisfying weapons to kills hoards of zeds with some friends. And as long as they don't go full PD2 with the microtransaction system, this won't be changing anytime soon.

If you are like me, then you find it almost impossible to resist the fabulous bargains to be had in the Steam sales and you have a strange stripe down your left thumbnail that just won't go away. Given that this is a game review, I will avoid discussing the compelling issue of the thumbnail at this point and stick to the problem of buying a crap-tonne of games that you never get around to playing.
I've just looked at my library of games on Steam and I have 25 games that I have never played. T-w-e-n-t-y F-i-v-e! "You must be some kind of rich lunatic buying all those games on a whim and never playing them!" I hear you shout. My response to that would be twofold, firstly, "shut up jerkface, I know you are but what am I?" And secondly, the cost of all these games combined would still be less than purchasing just one big new release title. Besides which, I WILL get round to playing them..eventually.
The problem is that recently, every time I open my game library and look at all the colourful alluring game icons brimming with promises of new challenge and adventure, I usually just play 'Civilization V.' I think I do this because it's something that lots of games aren't - it's relaxing, no it's more than relaxing, it's soothing.
If you've played a Civ game you'll probably know what I mean. This is a game about taking your time, about the most pleasant and amiable of rules entrenched in us since childhood - 'let's all just take turns.' There's no inhumanly fast paced clicking here, no angry competitor or ally calling you a noob and no hideous beast that will tear you limb from limb if you don't time that dodge just right. You can click calmly away with one hand whilst eating a bowl of ice-cream with the other. You can walk away at any moment to answer the phone or tear out a set of 25 push ups (theoretically). You can build, rule, vanquish and triumph all without elevating your heart rate or swearing at the screen. It's just nice. The sight of your workers happily building farms and constructing roads is nice. The charming English voice that reads great quotes from history as you discover new technologies is nice. The sea lapping at the shore as birds wheel and whales frolic is nice, and the feeling of satisfaction you get as your civilization expands and decimates rival populations in vicious bloody wars is just really, really quite nice.
At different times I want different things from a gaming experience, at this point I clearly desire the chilled, relaxing experience of guiding a civilization to glory with one hand, whilst eating ice-cream that has bits of rice bubbles in it with the other.

"5 STARS! A+! 4 MORE STARS!" is wah i wish i could say for this game.
now dont get me wrong, this game is phenomenal, but there are issues.
firstly the good:
-the graphics:
for an indie game, this game looks awesome! the enemies are varied and unique (most of the time), the particle effects are spot on, and the backdrops are beatiful. i'd put them in a frame if i had a printer.
-the music: it is again, very good. a very ambient, but somewhat blood-pumping sci-fi alien (almost metroid like) soundtrack. pretty much my favourite bits would be the guitar riffs in level 1 :)
-the Gameplay:
solid movement and hit detection. i never over estimate a jump. little to no glitches. and a fool proof way to stop people from farming the same mobs endlessly (that difficulty meter that fills as you spend more time in a stage. GENIUS.)
and did i mention mulltiplayer. because that is important. this game is worlds bette rwith multiplayer as you and your frined muck about and get killed. alot.
now the bad...
-graphics arent everything and in a game where the very asthectic is a simple but appealing 32 bit pixel asthetic, its hard to complain. but in later levels of the game (or just later difficulties)i would continually lose myself in the swarm of mobs and lose a chunk of my health because i couldnt see my tiny-as-an-atom charecter amongst all of these behemoths who were similarly colured, and end up accidentally jumping off a platform.

if i may present a solution to this problem: allow the player to pick how quickly they want the difficulty meter to fill
easy mode might be 8 mins to get from very easy > easy, normal can be the standard time, and hard can be 2-3 minutes between difficulties.
------
so despite the minor flaws with the game (and me sounding a little pretentious during this review), this game is definiteley worth your time for those who have never tried a rogue-lite game before. the multiplaayer is a great way for you to learn with a friend, and once your done learning, you'll see theres more depth, more challenge, than what you were already presented with (and you already had alot to begin with!)

Half Life 2. Called by many "The Greatest Game of All Time", the Half Life series has been known to deliver gameplay you don't see in any other series. ANY. Instead of treating you like a child with a hearing disorder by repeating dialogue to help you through the game and flashing button signs on your monitor at you when it's time to push a button, Half Life tells you to put your big boy pants, thinking cap, and awesome filter on, and to enjoy the ride. Half Life was stunning enough, but Half Life 2 really brought a new standard to the table.
You play as Gordon Freeman, the same badass scientist you played as in Half Life - but wait, what is this? You're 37 now? Insane, really, bloody insane! And who are these weirdos with respiratory issues that wear gasmasks, but are strangely awesome? Well, all these problems will be answered soon enough.
Valve didn't fail to deliver this game. They easily toppled the way we see games with one game: Half Life 2.
What you just read was a review I wrote for Half Life 2 back when it first came out. I still play it today, just to get a breath of fresh air. Do I reccommend this game? No. I treasure it for it's rich storytelling, exciting atmosphere, living, breathing characters.. The list goes on and on.
Truly a journey worth going on.

Great game if you're a fan of the show, and if you couldn't care less for the t.v. program then you're getting an alright RPG with South Park's trademark humour.
- I believe I was able to grab most of the sidequests in the first of the game's three acts, although a couple will have to be completed as the story progresses.
-There's a ton of equipment and items to collect as well as people to meet in your journeys, which in of itself is a collectathon, as the more friends you make the more perks you can unlock for your character.
- You will gain certain abilities for both in and out of combat, as well as some that are exclusively designed for exploration. These latter abilities can be used for getting more gear and items, however  the effort necessary to re-explore the town to find these hidden caches might put a damper on their overall usefulness.
- I never really felt like the game was that difficult, even on the hardest setting possible right from the start. I even gave the AI an accidental handicap by mismanaging my upgrade points! To explain: in my first run I was a warrior, and ended up wasting most of my points in my first three powers. But I managed to drop one point in my final and most destructive power, giving it more damage based off my armor score. Combat for me was then entirely based off how much armor I had from my gear, and how much I could slough off the enemy (if they had any: if not, they were already dead). To go back to my previous point, for my character only a select few armor sets were worth pursuing purely for combat purposes. Anything else was just to collect for an achievement.
All in all this is a decent game. Maybe not worth the $60 for how much game you get (I thought the game was about half way through, when really I was approaching the end), and definitely not worth it if you're not a fan of South Park in general, as most of the humour will derive from references within the show. However if you are, you're in for 15+ hours of "pretty funny", mixed with some truly ridiculous laugh out loud moments.

"5 STARS! A+! 4 MORE STARS!" is wah i wish i could say for this game.
now dont get me wrong, this game is phenomenal, but there are issues.
firstly the good:
-the graphics:
for an indie game, this game looks awesome! the enemies are varied and unique (most of the time), the particle effects are spot on, and the backdrops are beatiful. i'd put them in a frame if i had a printer.
-the music: it is again, very good. a very ambient, but somewhat blood-pumping sci-fi alien (almost metroid like) soundtrack. pretty much my favourite bits would be the guitar riffs in level 1 :)
-the Gameplay:
solid movement and hit detection. i never over estimate a jump. little to no glitches. and a fool proof way to stop people from farming the same mobs endlessly (that difficulty meter that fills as you spend more time in a stage. GENIUS.)
and did i mention mulltiplayer. because that is important. this game is worlds bette rwith multiplayer as you and your frined muck about and get killed. alot.
now the bad...
-graphics arent everything and in a game where the very asthectic is a simple but appealing 32 bit pixel asthetic, its hard to complain. but in later levels of the game (or just later difficulties)i would continually lose myself in the swarm of mobs and lose a chunk of my health because i couldnt see my tiny-as-an-atom charecter amongst all of these behemoths who were similarly colured, and end up accidentally jumping off a platform.
-the difficulty meter/timer is, as i said earlier: genius. but it fills a little too quickly. during the early hours of the game i found myself getting crushed by mobs as they were continually getting stronger at an alarming rate, while i  was struggling to pick them off.
if i may present a solution to this problem: allow the player to pick how quickly they want the difficulty meter to fill
easy mode might be 8 mins to get from very easy > easy, normal can be the standard time, and hard can be 2-3 minutes between difficulties.
------
so despite the minor flaws with the game (and me sounding a little pretentious during this review), this game is definiteley worth your time for those who have never tried a rogue-lite game before. the multiplaayer is a great way for you to learn with a friend, and once your done learning, you'll see theres more depth, more challenge, than what you were already presented with (and you already had alot to begin with!)

As a fan of the Arkham series from the very beginning, I highly reccomend this game. I have had a whale of a time playing through it to get the 100% ending and I don't regret it. As I said, I've been a fan of this series for a long time. Arkham Asylum was the first game that I ever got when I got a PS3 for my 13th birthday back in 2009. Since then, I have played through all of the Arkham Games and loved them all. With all that said, it makes me sad that this game get so much flack. I understand the criticisms over the game's outrageous launch, and understand that people continue to have issues to this day. However, the criticisms about the Batmobile are wrong in my opinion. I feel that it adds great variety to the gameplay, but doesn't take away from the overall package. If the batmobile wasn't in the game, it would be much too similar to the other Arkham Games. Rocksteady took a chance, and it paid off. It can get a bit tedious a few times throughout the story, but overall the batmobile was pulled off wonderfully by Rocksteady.
Without spoiling anything, I  would just like to say that I think this has my favorite storyline of all of the Arkham Games. It threw story points at me that I didn't see coming (not the identity of the Arkahm Knight) and I loved the suspense that built up. Rocksteady had a lot to live up to, and again I feel that they pulled it off.
My main complaint with the game is something I know many others share with me: the lack of fun boss fights. In the rocksteady batman games, the boss fights were never anything extravagant or really compelling, but it still gave the player a sense that they were going up against a supervillain interactively. For example; even thought the fight against Soloman Grundy in Arkham City wasn't all that innovative, it still gives the player an interactive experience about fighting an awesome villain. Unfortunatley, Arkham Knight doesn't really have any fights like that (except maybe one or two, but they still aren't comparable to the bosses in the other arkham games.) That would have to be my biggest complaint with the game as a whole.
In terms of performace, it ran fairly well for me on a not so powerful rig. I turned it down to low 1080p with my system  though and I had very few problems playing through it, and had a great time. My computer specs are a gigabyte gtx 660, 8gb ram, and an amd fx-8320. Close to the reccomended minimun settings and they worked just fine. The game still looks amazing on low settings, it honestly blew me away at first. The art design, models, and characters in this game are a step above anything else in the series.
The gameplay was phenomonoal just as in the other games, but the Batmobile provided nice variety as I already stated. I particularly enjoyed the riddler death races that you have to perform in the batmobile. The free-flow combat is better than ever, with even more moves and awesome ways to take guys out, and the predator is even more challenging.
As I said at the beginning of the review, this is a very worthy conclustion to the Arkham Series. While not perfect and with some flaws, I still highly reccomend it (as a person who has greatly enjoyed all of the other Arkham Games). The story is great, the gameplay is great, and the 45 hours that it took me to beat it and get the 100% ending went by lightening fast. I'm eagerly awaiting DLC for this game now, as there is supposed to be one coming out with more side missions for some awesome villains that weren't in the game. I hope I have given some informative thoughts to those who were skeptical about this game. While heavily criticized (deservedly for the awful port) by the PC community, the game is great, and if you can get it running well like I did, you're in for an absolute treat.

My only real gripe with the game is that it is 60 dollars currently, that being said the game has kept me busy for about 12 hours at this time and I plan on playing it a lot more to try different classes and make different decisions. All the other reviews on the store page will tell you its genre and gameplay mechanics, so you already know all about how awesome those are.  Instead, I'll tell you about what will happen after you obtain this game and try it out:
First, you'll be a little overwhelmed by the enemies and quickly advancing difficulty.  But, you'll figure out a good strategy or two for taking on some enemies, and feel pretty good about it.  "Perhaps this wasn't a bad purchase," you'll think.
Second, you'll begin to realize that several hours have passed and you have started over a few times.  You have two full rows of items at your disposal and you're going back through the first level for the second time.  You'll wonder if perhaps you should go to bed.
Third and finally, you'll experience a burning desire to play this game when you have some free time.  You'll listen to the soundtrack regularly because it's so delicious, and you'll see little item or teleporter outlines when you close your eyes at night.  You'll be able to identify and name all the items you see by icon alone, in no time.
It's really a wonderful game!  I had no idea, until I got sucked in.

A fast-paced and unforgiving 2D platformer-shooter with 8-bit, pixel graphics.
The storyline is rather thin, but solid enough to relay to the player who you are and what you're doing. A stranded pilot on an alien planet and trying to not die, respectively.
The gameplay starts off nice and easy, but gradually picks up the pace, ramping up the difficulty exponentially. Apart from 2D platforming and shooting things, this game can very well be categorized as a rogue-like. With permanent death, unforgiving difficulty and a lot of randomized items to aid you in combat, fans of rogue-likes and fast-paced action alike will appreciate Risk of Rain.
There are 10 classes to be unlocked, each with 4 distinct and unique abilites. The variety allows for an amazing amount of play styles and strategies. Combined with the at times randomness of items and shrines to waste your money on, players will need to hone their skills and rely on luck as well, if they are to escape this hostile and indomitable planet.

After having played it through and through, I can say I'm mostly satisfied with the game. Not entirely, however.
The graphics are of course amazing. The way they've added the rain effect to his armor (and his cape), the way the moon reflects on wet surfaces, special effects for blowing things up and the way things crumble in the smallest of details. To add to that, combat is a lot of fun as it has been in all the other games and you have a variety of gadgets to use against the enemies as well as against the Riddler as he throws his puzzles and riddles at you in countless waves.
The story is well done as well. It's a little extreme, but it plays its role. One unique character who tags along with you throughout your journey as the Dark Knight has been super well done and in the end makes up for any plot holes. There are no real plot twists unfortunately as you're entirely certain what will come next if you've seen a few Hollywood movies or played a few video games. Still, in the end it's a satisfying experience and a fantastic end to the series. Especially with Knightfall.
Now the bad side. I think the game's heavy weakness lies upon the usage of the Batmobile (more like bat-tank tbh). A number of boss encounters (including the Arkham Knight) ends up with you hopping into your batmobile, skirting around big tanks that can wreck you in more-or-less two hits and taking them out one by one. Meanwhile the boss person shouts taunts at you that get repetetive and rather annoying quickly. What takes satisfaction out of the game is also the fact that boss fights start and end with these tank battles. Instead of going toe-to-toe with a boss, much like you did in previous games (read: Arkham Origins), you're forced to fight with them tank-on-tank. It's a shame, really. Good characters thrown away to introduce this new and innovative tank thing.
What also takes enjoyment out of the game is the fact that you can't play with other characters in the city. For example, you encounter Robin, Catwoman and Nightwing. It would have been such an amazing feature to be able to swap between these characters and have them have their own little side missions (if not short campaigns, even) that you can complete to upgrade Batman and his tank. In your short encounters with them you're given the possibility to play with them, but only to complete a single area which is disappointing, really.
Other than that, the game in itself deserves worthy recongition for being done so well. Sure enough, the launch PC port was horrendous and rendered people unable to play the game, but in the end it's still a really great game. Voice acting is top notch, graphics are very well done, gameplay is a lot of fun (excluding the excessive  tank battles. A few times would be alright, but come on) and the narrative brings an awesome conclusion to the game.
I'd recommend this to anyone who's contemplating on whether or not it's worth 60 euros (and whatever equivalent dollars). It really is worth it.

If you are like me, then you find it almost impossible to resist the fabulous bargains to be had in the Steam sales and you have a strange stripe down your left thumbnail that just won't go away. Given that this is a game review, I will avoid discussing the compelling issue of the thumbnail at this point and stick to the problem of buying a crap-tonne of games that you never get around to playing.
I've just looked at my library of games on Steam and I have 25 games that I have never played. T-w-e-n-t-y F-i-v-e! "You must be some kind of rich lunatic buying all those games on a whim and never playing them!" I hear you shout. My response to that would be twofold, firstly, "shut up jerkface, I know you are but what am I?" And secondly, the cost of all these games combined would still be less than purchasing just one big new release title. Besides which, I WILL get round to playing them..eventually.
The problem is that recently, every time I open my game library and look at all the colourful alluring game icons brimming with promises of new challenge and adventure, I usually just play 'Civilization V.' I think I do this because it's something that lots of games aren't - it's relaxing, no it's more than relaxing, it's soothing.
If you've played a Civ game you'll probably know what I mean. This is a game about taking your time, about the most pleasant and amiable of rules entrenched in us since childhood - 'let's all just take turns.' There's no inhumanly fast paced clicking here, no angry competitor or ally calling you a noob and no hideous beast that will tear you limb from limb if you don't time that dodge just right. You can click calmly away with one hand whilst eating a bowl of ice-cream with the other. You can walk away at any moment to answer the phone or tear out a set of 25 push ups (theoretically). You can build, rule, vanquish and triumph all without elevating your heart rate or swearing at the screen. It's just nice. The sight of your workers happily building farms and constructing roads is nice. The charming English voice that reads great quotes from history as you discover new technologies is nice. The sea lapping at the shore as birds wheel and whales frolic is nice, and the feeling of satisfaction you get as your civilization expands and decimates rival populations in vicious bloody wars is just really, really quite nice.
At different times I want different things from a gaming experience, at this point I clearly desire the chilled, relaxing experience of guiding a civilization to glory with one hand, whilst eating ice-cream that has bits of rice bubbles in it with the other.
I feel like the only real improvement this has over the original is the graphics. I was very much in love with the original and super excited to hear about this, but fell asleep while playing it.
All I can say - great game!

So I waited since day one for the patch, and now that I've gotten 100% on normal difficulty, I have to say: I had some problems with Arkham Knight, but it wasn't enough to keep me from liking it. Probably the last Warner Brothers game I'm picking up considering the big fiasco regarding this port, but at least it seems they took/are taking the time to address our grievances.
+ The visuals are GORGEOUS, if the Youtube channel BatmanArkhamVideos is any indication (seriously, I envy them); the character animation in particular is wonderfully fluid and damn near lifelike, leagues ahead of the stiff mannequin-like motions in cutscenes in prior Arkham games. (Not that there aren't occasional oddities though.)
+ The combat and predator gameplay is just sublime, with lots of new tricks and twists added in (I had a blast with the Fear Takedowns, for instance). It's more difficult, but more satisfying IMO.
+ Very memorable side missions, especially the Perfect Crime one.
+ Great voice acting, not to mention Kevin Conroy stepping up his game after being so wooden in Arkham City.
+ Scarecrow is best villain. Like, really. Not to mention what he does in the finale proves he's worthy of being one of the A-listers in the Dark Knight's rogues gallery. I'm also glad that Hallucination!Joker, even with all his screentime, was kept somewhat to the sidelines plotwise, being an entirely internal conflict for Batman; the plot makes it clear that Scarecrow and Arkham Knight are the main threats in play here.
+ The Batmobile and Bat-Tank were decent enough. Though the tank is a bit...iffy in terms of lore, I can give that some leeway for the satisfying gameplay.
+/- Running this on my machine, I don't get 60fps that often, and the game lags sometimes (especially during car chases and going through places with tons of NPCs). But for me, it runs well and consistently so; with all that's happened regarding this port, that's really all I can ask for.
- The AR Challenges got old after a little while. I kind of miss the way the other games did it, featuring setpiece moments as replayable challenges. (Like, you could have the airship cargo hold as a combat challenge, or the last room in Arkham Knight HQ as a Predator challenge, for instance. But nope.)
- Paul Dini isn't present, and it shows. The plot, while otherwise decent and has a spectacular finale, seems to rely too heavily on kidnappings to keep things moving along and gets a tad repetitive.
- Arkham Knight's identity being obvious, of course, both in-game and out. And also not being an original character. (Technically, they were right in that it's a new IDENTITY, but...)
- Azrael and Hush/The Identity Thief were utterly wasted, and we never got to see Jack Ryder as The Creeper. The hell?
Verdict: Uh...mixed feelings, but leaning towards positive. If you like the Arkham series, have a higher-end machine, and are interested in this game, I'd at least think about it. I have definite reservations about buying it right off the bat though. I'd try the console version first if you can, to see what you think of it.

**Edited as of 11/24/2017** I recommend KF2 more now than when I bought it. It's a game you can keep comming back to over and over again, for both long and short stints. The devs are very active,  it's been over 2 years since I bought this and they have added many new boards (and that's not counting the community made ones), new guns,  3 more "perks" (playable classes) and daily events that allow you to build your Dosh Vault to gain wearables. They also had a "Summer side show" event, where they reskinned all the Zeds and gave them all new sounds (almost making the update like getting a whole new game). That Event has since ended and we're back in the normal game but I very much look forward to the next event. The community is still very active and very fun to play with (I've played with 1 toxic person in over 2 years). In short, KF2 has been worth every penny. I now buy keys to some of the crates for skins because I feel I've gotten my money's worth and then some. I really hope they keep these events comming too, because it really makes you want to play at least one match a night.

Long version -- I absolutely love this game. Mind you, I loved KF1 so it's no surprize. It's simple team survival done well. There are multiple classes that all play very differently and all are fun. You would think such a simple game wouldn't have much staying power but it's one of the few games that I just keep coming back to.
The devs are very active. There are consistent updates and most have added content to the game. Since I bought the game they have added two classes (Sharpshooter and SWAT) and both are very fun in their own way. They have improved the AI, which has made gameplay far more interesting and challenging. They added PvP, where you get to play the Zeds of all types.  They have added maps (although most servers have a few custom maps as well). The balance has changed (and will continue to do so) but I can tell you that, so far, all changes and additions have all been for the better.
There are micro-transactions but they are only for cosmetic items, not a single thing you can purchace effects gameplay in any way other than possibly making you look cool. I will probably eventually buy them just to support the developers and because I like to support any game that avoids pay-to-win.
The gameplay is similar to KF1, except with better graphics, more classes, more weapons and a LOT more gore. The addition of being able to earn weapons and outfits from other games is very nice too. I can't tell you how much I enjoy using a medeval two handed sword when playing a bezerker.

Let me start by saying that I'm a huge fan of Arkham Asylum and City. They're among my favorite games (City being my all time favorite). So naturally I was very excited for this game. I had full faith in Rocksteady after their previous works but unfortunately, they ♥♥♥♥ed up. Arkham Knight is one of the most disappointing games I've ever played. You probably already know how horrible the port is, so I'm not going to talk about that. I'll focus on the game itself.
Let's start with the story. I personally didn't like it. I found it cliche and boring. There is not a single memorable moment in the entire campaign. It is unbelievably cliche. Same with villains. Scarecrow was awesome in Asylum. Here, he is a joke. He doesn't do anything, just talks about fear. Arkham Knight is even worse. He is very boring and weak. He calls you a coward but hides behind an army of drones. His 'boss battles' are terrible. His identity is ridiculously obvious. If you have the slightest comic book knowledge you'll immediately know who he is and if not don't worry, game tells you who he is way before it is actually revealed. Also SPOILER ALERT I'm really sick of these people's obsession with Joker. I get it he's a good villain but he doesn't need to be the main villain in all Batman games. Oh yeah, you thought this was about Arkham Knight? Nope! Joker is the main villain again. ♥♥♥♥ you Rocksteady.
Gameplay is also kinda messed up. Many people claim it's the best in the series but it's not. It has a few nice improvements and it has much more depth but it lacks the smoothness that made Asylum and City so great. Input drops, attacking an armored enemy instead of the normal enemy right next to him, losing combo for no reason are only some of these problems. The new environmental takedowns look cool but they are unreliable. Sometimes they cause you to drop your combo for no reason. Same with picking weapons from ground. The detection on these thing was so bad, I stopped using them after a while. Also the camera during combat felt a little more zoomed in than previous games and it often caused me to lose my combo. I also hated the new big enemies. They're essentially the armored enemies from City but they're so hard to distinguish in the heat of combat. In City, they wore red vests so you'd immediately spot them. Here, they look like regular enemies but just bigger. Fear takedown is also a new addition, it looks cool but its implementation is awful. Forget about relying on that thing. Anytime I wanted to use a fear takedown in a tight spot Batman just punched air and got me killed.
Of course the big new thing in this game is the batmobile. It's fun for a bit but it's way overused. You use it to get around, solve puzzles, fight tanks. Game forces it on you so much. You can't take two steps without it and I'm sorry but that's just stupid. Just like Riddler race tracks. I mean, just think about it. Riddler creating race tracks for batmobile. Nice one Rocksteady.
Arkham City had great side missions. Admittedly, they were a little repetitive. What I mean is, they mostly consisted of doing the same thing 3-4 times. Arkham Knight takes this to a ridiculous level. Almost every side mission in the game has you doing the same thing time after time again. Specially those god damn Militia missions. They're just a cheap way to increase the game's length in my opinion.
Remember challenge maps? They're gone. They are replaced with AR challenges and these suck. You cannot play as other characters in them and they have awful blue walls around them. So disappointing. There is only one fun AR challenge and you don't even play as Batman in that one. More than half of these damn things are for batmobile. We get it Rocksteady. You're really proud of that damn tank. Stop shoving it to our faces.
If you've made it this far you probably noticed I suck at long reviews and I agree with you. So I'll stop here. Batman Arkham Knight is a terrible port, it has a boring, cliche story, good but not good enough combat, way too much batmobile, the worst villains of the series, awful side missions (a couple exceptions) and a very disappointing ending. Way to end your legacy Rocksteady.

Long version -- I absolutely love this game. Mind you, I loved KF1 so it's no surprize. It's simple team survival done well. There are multiple classes that all play very differently and all are fun. You would think such a simple game wouldn't have much staying power but it's one of the few games that I just keep coming back to.
The devs are very active. There are consistent updates and most have added content to the game. Since I bought the game they have added two classes (Sharpshooter and SWAT) and both are very fun in their own way. They have improved the AI, which has made gameplay far more interesting and challenging. They added PvP, where you get to play the Zeds of all types.  They have added maps (although most servers have a few custom maps as well). The balance has changed (and will continue to do so) but I can tell you that, so far, all changes and additions have all been for the better.
There are micro-transactions but they are only for cosmetic items, not a single thing you can purchace effects gameplay in any way other than possibly making you look cool. I will probably eventually buy them just to support the developers and because I like to support any game that avoids pay-to-win.
The gameplay is similar to KF1, except with better graphics, more classes, more weapons and a LOT more gore. The addition of being able to earn weapons and outfits from other games is very nice too. I can't tell you how much I enjoy using a medeval two handed sword when playing a bezerker.

Beautiuful 2D 'platformer' graphics (sidescroller?), fun action shooter with skills to add strategy making it more than running and gunning. Skills you need to have any chance of staying alive. For longer than you would without them. But you will die. It's a brutal game with permadeath, the roguelike aspect of the game. Normally, I might say this is a roguelike-like (rogue-lite, as the kids say I think. A game that isn't a roguelike but is influenced by them and uses roguelike mechanics in a unique way but isn't really a roguelike in the "pure" sense), however, in various ways it meets what I consider the core criteria of the roguelike genre. It's not turn based, but I think that's a standard roguelike feature, not a core one. It has a high difficulty level, classes with differnet skills, various items you find throughout the stages, and although there are no potions or items that are "cursed" (so far, in my playthroughs) - those things in roguelikes can be abstracted to the role they play: random danger from items that could be beneficial but you don't know until you use them. Risk of Rain has "shrines" that you pay to use, the shrines increase in cost with each use and you are not guarenteed anything - it's random and they could be really beneficial, and then sometimes it's just a waste of gold, and other times they can hurt you. They fulfill the role, to an extent, that unidentified items in more 'standard' roguelikes fulfill. Oh, and of course permadeath. Risk of Rain also starts off difficult (although after you play for awhile, the start of a game becomes a lot easier), however, it uses a timer feature that increases the diffculty the longer you're alive/in a stage (I can't honestly confirm if it resets when you activate the teleporter and go to the next stage since I've died at the last few seconds of the countdown when the teleporter is activating on the first level....) - when you start it tells you by the timer that it's "very easy", which in comparison to later difficulty ramps, is true. Very easy compared to what I think when I hear the term "very easy" though? Not so much...
Anyway, it's a great game, well worth it if you like challenging, pretty, roguelikes with a twist. Oh, and playing with a gamepad is so much better than using a keyboard, in my experience...

This game is fantastic, straight from the South Park creative book. It contains all the jokes and bad tasting gags you have came to love and loathe over the years from the TV series.
This game is very much an RPG where you begin life as the "New Kid" and within no time you are thrown into the chaotic world between elves and humans as they fight to control the "Stick of Truth" for whoever hold the stick, controls the universe.
You have a choice of 4 classes, Warrior, Mage, Thief and Jew each with their own strengths and weaknesses. The warrior playthrough was done within 2 days of playing, an all round tough character that can deal as well as recieve a beating. I have only just started out as a Jew so i've yet to see the strengths and weaknesses of this class.
The level up system is typical of your standard RPG, defeat foes to earn XP and level up choosing how you want to upgrade (there are 4 in total by games end) your special ability. Go around the town and chat to people and some become your "friend" on "facebook". the more you have the more abilities you can unlock to help your character progress easier. Same goes for weapons as well as the ability to add 1 or 2 extra "modifiers" to your weapon such as putting some pubic hair on the end to make your opponents gross out or a flame perk to set them on fire.
I found the warrior class once a few levels up had a wonderful blend of combining your characters ability with weapon abilities such as using a Ro-Sham-Bo (a square kick to the nuts) to gross out your opponent and his friends as well as rendering the target useless for 3 shots (not all enemies are effected this way). mix that with a powerfull weapon with say a burn and bleed mod on it and you are a pretty formidable force. oh also the abilites such as Ro-Sham-Bo use PP so can only be used as long as you have PP remaining.
Enemies differ throught the game forcing you to think about your layout before you engage. some cannot be grossed out, some cannot be stunned or shocked (Bosses cannot be stunned) but all can be frozen (causes a delay of 1 or 2 shots to them) or burned (damage everytime their turn ends) meaning a good mashup of powers and weapons is advisable.
The characters themselves are all ones you will recognize such as the ususal mob of Cartman, Stan, Kyle and Kenny as well as all their buddies plus other well known characters such as Jesus, Al Gore, ManBearPig and Chef.

As a huge South Park fan, this is without a doubt the funniest game I have played to date. It is full of excellent throwbacks and references to past shows and any fan will doubtlessly enjoy the new material as well even if the game is a little light on such material compared to the amount of throwbacks.
In terms of gameplay itself, the combat is perfectly serviceable; however it lacks any particular depth or difficulty, even on the highest difficulty setting. Similarly there are few differences to be found between the games classes besides their special abilities as each can wield all types of weapons and armour. This said the buddy system adds variety to fights and you will find yourself trying out a variety of tactics and buddies, to find the effective combat strategies, but more importantly to witness all these characters moves, which are hilarious extensions of their personalities.
This said, the real draw of the game is to be able to explore the town of South Park itself and interact with all the characters from the show in what essentially feels like one huge interactive . In this respect, you cannot fault the game at all as it provides an abundance of areas to explore from the kids houses to inside Mr. Slaves’…well to say anything more would be spoiling things. Rest assure though these areas are varied and full of gags as well as side quests and collectibles.
All in all I wouldn’t necessarily recommend this game to people looking for a rich RPG style game as the game does not offer this, although I personally believe it would feel out of place when you consider the source material for the game. If however, you are a fan of the series, then I cannot recommend this game enough, not only is it the finest piece of fan service to South Park, it is probably one of the finest pieces of fan service ever created for any form of entertainment to date.

I'm mixed with Half-Life 2.  The game has a lot of content in it which is great and will keep you going until the very end; about one-fourth of it is platforming, another is puzzles, another is shooting, and the last is cutscenes, which make you feel as if you were really part of the story when you control the action and not have to sit through a movie-like scene, something no other FPS  (modern or classic) has done.  My main problem with this game is that, as a whole, it only gives you the illusion of free choice with the exception of what weapon you decide to kill the enemies with.  What do I mean by this?  Well, my biggest gripe coincides with the end of the game as when you finally enter the citadel you LOSE all your weapons, but to counter that you get an upgraded gravity gun that has farther range and can now pick up bodies, something which you couldn't do FOR THE ENTIRETY OF THE GAME.  Why?  Because the game said so, that's why.  Don't get me wrong, the game has a lot of challenge, but it gets very boring when you're tired of using the same weapons over and over again that do the same damage to the enemies as the last playthrough.  To add to this, the game is long...very long and you'll want to take breaks every now and then (thank goodness for saving anytime, anywhere).  What this game should have is a New Game Plus that should let you go through levels faster and upgrade ALL your weapons.  To be fair, this is the ONLY VERY, VERY, VERY MINOR gripe that I have with this game.  The story will keep you on your toes and wanting more (which thankfully, will be continued in Half-Life 2: Episode One) and the environments are VERY well-rendered and make you feel as if you're actually living in the Half-Life unvierse itself.  All in all, Half-Life 2 has enough content to keep gamers busy for a while, and while there are Steam Achievements to do for replayability (I've gotten all but one), there should've been a New Game Plus to compensate for the long, tedious levels you have to go through in order to get to the next part of the story.

I consider myself a bit of an action junkie, so most of my games are shooters. Having only played a little bit of Half-Life 1 on PS2 (which really doesn't do justice to the PC version), I decided I'd give Half-Life 2 a try, and see what all the fuss was about. The gameplay is simple but smooth. The Gravity Gun is a great unique edge, setting the game apart from typical shooters. There are no gaping flaws. On top of this, I was immediately blown away by the dystopian setting, and brilliantly executed Orwellian atmosphere. The story of Half-Life is incredibly executed, and City 17 echoes the oppression of a Soviet dictatorship. The settings range from Vertigo style "fugitive-on-the-run" rooftop setpieces to dark, terrifying villages, overrun with monsters, to vehicular chase sequences on land and sea. This may evoke a worry of suffering the GTA syndrome, of having many features, but not being very good at any of them. The shooting is what it needs to be, and is on at least the same level as Halo. It is slick, and has a good feel to it. The story is one of the best gaming has told. It had me invested the whole way through. I don't want to say too much out of fear of spoiling it. Of course the opening "rooftop-runner" setpiece isn't a patch on Mirror's Edge, but that game was built around parkour, and so is an unfair comparison. The horror based level won't be as frightening as Amnesia or Penumbra, but if you aren't scared by it, you must lack a soul. The vehicles don't handle as well as in Forza or GT, but this ain't a racing game! And in relation to the chases they are utilised in, it is every bit as thrilling as being chased by cops through Liberty City/Los Santos. It surely beats an modern-military turret section by several, several, several, several miles.
Another incredible feat is that Half-Life isn't laid out in distinct levels. Chapter titles may flash on the screen, and you can choose a particular point in the game where to start from. But never do you leave Gordon Freeman's perspective. You are put in the shoes of a protagonist on what feels like an Odyssean epic, and it gives the game a liberatingly open feel. It may be seen as linear, as in the end, the aim is to get from Point A to Point B (as was almost the literal plot for Half-Life 1), but it's more a case of being given a vast map, and that map is your playground, to execute your objectives on your own terms. It. Is. Wonderful.
Overall, Half-Life 2 is nothing short of phenomenal. It is ten years old, but it blows every modern shooter out of the water. It even graphically holds up. You don't need to be a fan of action games or Sci-Fi. If you love games, you owe it to yourself to play Half-Life 2 (and check out it's predecessor).

Let me start by saying that I'm a huge fan of Arkham Asylum and City. They're among my favorite games (City being my all time favorite). So naturally I was very excited for this game. I had full faith in Rocksteady after their previous works but unfortunately, they ♥♥♥♥ed up. Arkham Knight is one of the most disappointing games I've ever played. You probably already know how horrible the port is, so I'm not going to talk about that. I'll focus on the game itself.
Let's start with the story. I personally didn't like it. I found it cliche and boring. There is not a single memorable moment in the entire campaign. It is unbelievably cliche. Same with villains. Scarecrow was awesome in Asylum. Here, he is a joke. He doesn't do anything, just talks about fear. Arkham Knight is even worse. He is very boring and weak. He calls you a coward but hides behind an army of drones. His 'boss battles' are terrible. His identity is ridiculously obvious. If you have the slightest comic book knowledge you'll immediately know who he is and if not don't worry, game tells you who he is way before it is actually revealed. Also SPOILER ALERT I'm really sick of these people's obsession with Joker. I get it he's a good villain but he doesn't need to be the main villain in all Batman games. Oh yeah, you thought this was about Arkham Knight? Nope! Joker is the main villain again. ♥♥♥♥ you Rocksteady.
Gameplay is also kinda messed up. Many people claim it's the best in the series but it's not. It has a few nice improvements and it has much more depth but it lacks the smoothness that made Asylum and City so great. Input drops, attacking an armored enemy instead of the normal enemy right next to him, losing combo for no reason are only some of these problems. The new environmental takedowns look cool but they are unreliable. Sometimes they cause you to drop your combo for no reason. Same with picking weapons from ground. The detection on these thing was so bad, I stopped using them after a while. Also the camera during combat felt a little more zoomed in than previous games and it often caused me to lose my combo. I also hated the new big enemies. They're essentially the armored enemies from City but they're so hard to distinguish in the heat of combat. In City, they wore red vests so you'd immediately spot them. Here, they look like regular enemies but just bigger. Fear takedown is also a new addition, it looks cool but its implementation is awful. Forget about relying on that thing. Anytime I wanted to use a fear takedown in a tight spot Batman just punched air and got me killed.
Of course the big new thing in this game is the batmobile. It's fun for a bit but it's way overused. You use it to get around, solve puzzles, fight tanks. Game forces it on you so much. You can't take two steps without it and I'm sorry but that's just stupid. Just like Riddler race tracks. I mean, just think about it. Riddler creating race tracks for batmobile. Nice one Rocksteady.
Arkham City had great side missions. Admittedly, they were a little repetitive. What I mean is, they mostly consisted of doing the same thing 3-4 times. Arkham Knight takes this to a ridiculous level. Almost every side mission in the game has you doing the same thing time after time again. Specially those god damn Militia missions. They're just a cheap way to increase the game's length in my opinion.
Remember challenge maps? They're gone. They are replaced with AR challenges and these suck. You cannot play as other characters in them and they have awful blue walls around them. So disappointing. There is only one fun AR challenge and you don't even play as Batman in that one. More than half of these damn things are for batmobile. We get it Rocksteady. You're really proud of that damn tank. Stop shoving it to our faces.
If you've made it this far you probably noticed I suck at long reviews and I agree with you. So I'll stop here. Batman Arkham Knight is a terrible port, it has a boring, cliche story, good but not good enough combat, way too much batmobile, the worst villains of the series, awful side missions (a couple exceptions) and a very disappointing ending. Way to end your legacy Rocksteady.

The script, the dialogues, the loot and its descriptions, and the side quests - it's all pure South Park, it's like you're actually playing the full-length South Park movie, although it's a great game by itself, an eclectic mix of RPG and adventure genres, so if you're new to the South Park franchise, but you have healthy some sense of humor of a grown person, you'd definitely enjoy the game. But if you're an ultra-religious person or simply boring, or, say, dumb, you should never play this game so you wouldn't bore everyone with your whine all over the Internet afterwards.
But for all the cool cats out there I would strongly recommend to buy this game and play the sh*t out of it, since it's really one of the best games out there in the market today and it never gets boring in the process - the gamplay is built that way so you'd have some good time exploring and leveling-up right to the level cap, and then it'd put you in the middle of the awesome storyline action, so you wouldn't wander somewhere out there aimlessly. There is always something to do and some places to reach as you progress in the game. And it's fun the whole time!

This is the series that actually brought Valve up.  Half Life 1 was huge.  This was even more to the company.  Bringing up Valve before TF2, this game featured the new Source engine, which was capable of much more than what was previously seen in the Half Life series.
As for the game itself?  Everything about it is great.  While it is linear to a certain extent, it still was fun-- and it was still a very long campaign.  The textures are still okay, and all of the mechanics are actually more functional than the things you see in newer games, like the Gravity Gun.  I still wish it had a built-in multiplayer like HL1, though... you don't really replay this once you beat it.
Like I said, this was also the huge showcase of Source, the latest engine from Valve, and owning this game gives you full access to the SDK tools.  If you don't feel like using the Hammer Editor or anything like that, the Source SDK still allows you to access the Sourcemods made by members of the community.  Most of these can be found on Moddb and other websites that host mods, while certain ones are picked out by Valve (or Greenlit) to use in Steam itself.  All of those mods only require this game, a certain Source SDK Base (all of which can be found in Library>Tools for free on Steam), and in the rarest of cases, possibly HL2E1 and HL2E2 or Counter Strike Source.
I got it both for the game itself, and the mods.  It was worth every penny.  If you're considering getting it, get it.  If you're still deciding, maybe wait for the big Summer Sale or whatever drags this into a price range of $2 or less.  I'm not kidding; the price gets that low, but don't let that fool you about quality.  It's still very well-built.

I got this game from the last Humble Bundle for Android, and decided to give it a shot. Boy am I glad I did. The new game from the mind of VVVVVV creator Terry Cavanaugh, this game finds you trying to survive what is essentially vectors. That, while the map keeps changing and playing tricks on you. It starts skewing, rotating, switching rotation, pulsing, and changing color, all while banging techno plays in the background. You might be preparing for the next vector coming one way, but woops! The opening may have been just a hair to the left, and now you get to start over, some times mere milliseconds before reaching the next level. The game is very tough though. I kept replaying it, and still am, because I can't let this goddamn game beat me! (that was on the lowest difficulty, of 3. Plus even harder "hyper" stages await you if you beat those). Also, word of caution... if you have any sort of epileptic seizure issue, or issues with motion sickness, this game might cause you some issues. I play on a very big monitor, and usually don't, and I was actually getting dizzy after about 20 minutes of play, so be careful. Besides that, the game is quite a lot of fun if you enjoy a challenge and can handle some bangin techno. Enjoy! :)

I'm mixed with Half-Life 2.  The game has a lot of content in it which is great and will keep you going until the very end; about one-fourth of it is platforming, another is puzzles, another is shooting, and the last is cutscenes, which make you feel as if you were really part of the story when you control the action and not have to sit through a movie-like scene, something no other FPS  (modern or classic) has done.  My main problem with this game is that, as a whole, it only gives you the illusion of free choice with the exception of what weapon you decide to kill the enemies with.  What do I mean by this?  Well, my biggest gripe coincides with the end of the game as when you finally enter the citadel you LOSE all your weapons, but to counter that you get an upgraded gravity gun that has farther range and can now pick up bodies, something which you couldn't do FOR THE ENTIRETY OF THE GAME.  Why?  Because the game said so, that's why.  Don't get me wrong, the game has a lot of challenge, but it gets very boring when you're tired of using the same weapons over and over again that do the same damage to the enemies as the last playthrough.  To add to this, the game is long...very long and you'll want to take breaks every now and then (thank goodness for saving anytime, anywhere).  What this game should have is a New Game Plus that should let you go through levels faster and upgrade ALL your weapons.  To be fair, this is the ONLY VERY, VERY, VERY MINOR gripe that I have with this game.  The story will keep you on your toes and wanting more (which thankfully, will be continued in Half-Life 2: Episode One) and the environments are VERY well-rendered and make you feel as if you're actually living in the Half-Life unvierse itself.  All in all, Half-Life 2 has enough content to keep gamers busy for a while, and while there are Steam Achievements to do for replayability (I've gotten all but one), there should've been a New Game Plus to compensate for the long, tedious levels you have to go through in order to get to the next part of the story.

I consider myself a bit of an action junkie, so most of my games are shooters. Having only played a little bit of Half-Life 1 on PS2 (which really doesn't do justice to the PC version), I decided I'd give Half-Life 2 a try, and see what all the fuss was about. The gameplay is simple but smooth. The Gravity Gun is a great unique edge, setting the game apart from typical shooters. There are no gaping flaws. On top of this, I was immediately blown away by the dystopian setting, and brilliantly executed Orwellian atmosphere. The story of Half-Life is incredibly executed, and City 17 echoes the oppression of a Soviet dictatorship. The settings range from Vertigo style "fugitive-on-the-run" rooftop setpieces to dark, terrifying villages, overrun with monsters, to vehicular chase sequences on land and sea. This may evoke a worry of suffering the GTA syndrome, of having many features, but not being very good at any of them. The shooting is what it needs to be, and is on at least the same level as Halo. It is slick, and has a good feel to it. The story is one of the best gaming has told. It had me invested the whole way through. I don't want to say too much out of fear of spoiling it. Of course the opening "rooftop-runner" setpiece isn't a patch on Mirror's Edge, but that game was built around parkour, and so is an unfair comparison. The horror based level won't be as frightening as Amnesia or Penumbra, but if you aren't scared by it, you must lack a soul. The vehicles don't handle as well as in Forza or GT, but this ain't a racing game! And in relation to the chases they are utilised in, it is every bit as thrilling as being chased by cops through Liberty City/Los Santos. It surely beats an modern-military turret section by several, several, several, several miles.
Another incredible feat is that Half-Life isn't laid out in distinct levels. Chapter titles may flash on the screen, and you can choose a particular point in the game where to start from. But never do you leave Gordon Freeman's perspective. You are put in the shoes of a protagonist on what feels like an Odyssean epic, and it gives the game a liberatingly open feel. It may be seen as linear, as in the end, the aim is to get from Point A to Point B (as was almost the literal plot for Half-Life 1), but it's more a case of being given a vast map, and that map is your playground, to execute your objectives on your own terms. It. Is. Wonderful.
Overall, Half-Life 2 is nothing short of phenomenal. It is ten years old, but it blows every modern shooter out of the water. It even graphically holds up. You don't need to be a fan of action games or Sci-Fi. If you love games, you owe it to yourself to play Half-Life 2 (and check out it's predecessor).

Batman Arkham Knight as far as preformance goes is a complete waste, I am running with a GTX 970 FTW+ and my framerate despite the patch still fluctuates like all hell. The game still suffers from hard crashes and while the framerate no longer drops to 1 and 2 frames and the framerate limiter has been removed I still deem this game unsatisfactory. Until they release a patch that fully prevents these massive framerate fluctuations I will not be installing and playing it. To give an example, I went ahead and set my framerate limit to 90 frames and turned off V-sync to get an idea where the framerate was going. When standing idle, even when looking into the city I was getting frames of around 80 and 90, however when I would start to fly it would drop down to about 65 and 70 frames, which is actually pretty decent. However when I started to use my grable accelerator, frames would drop down into the 35 and 45 range. To me this is very unsatisfactory as when you expirence massive frame fluctuations from 35 to 90 you can see the very obvious difference in the frame rates and 30 and 35 feel like you are actually lagging or choppy thus taking away from the experience leaving you focusing on the annoying framerate drops. I still hold onto hope for this game that they will release a patch to properly optimize this game. I find that since the release of Metal Gear Solid: V Phantom Pain, gaming companies no longer have an excuse for their poorly optimized games.

Just to get it out of the way, I'll talk about the performance issues first.
I've had the game since release and have played it consistently, and yes there's been stuttering and frequent issues with Windows complaining about low memoery etc., to me it's been fairly minor.  I'm running an older gen i5 (2500k) with 16GB of memory and a newer Gigabyte G1 970, so hardly an absolute top of the line PC but also not entry level.
I don't run games at ultra settings ever, although I do game at 1440p, and even with the stuttering I was able to play through to the underground fight with the Knight without an issue.  To date I have never had the game crash on me even once, and never had any in game issues that broke it (such as Batman being stuck somewhere, or a quest getting stuck etc.), which compared to the Witcher 3 (which crashes Nvidia drivers constantly it seems) and a few other games I play is better than average.
As for the gameplay itself, I love it.  No other way to describe it, but I really do enjoy the tank battles and the puzzles that require the Batmobile, and everything else people are saying is forced and boring.  I never completed Arkham City because of some of the gameplay elements that annoyed me (Batman being forced back from a window due to "wind"?), I haven't yet encountered anything in this game that's made me want to rage quit or otherwise just stuck out as stupid.  There are things that are hard for sure, but trial and error and practice helps with that, and eventually you get through it.
Overall I'm happy with the purchase, and I'm slowly working through the storyline as I try to finish as much of the side quests as I can (except Riddler, I hate that guy :(), and I'd say it's a worthwhile purchase.

Dustforce truly is a work of art. I don't mean that lightly. The way it's animated plus its music gives it that title in my book. I can find myself playing one level for an hour, maybe even hours at a time. The frustration of losing levels is filled with relaxation and calmness because of the ambient music. The way the levels are crafted is truly mindblowing. They had a system in which you had to perfect a level to earn a key, and you would use that key to earn more levels. In layman's terms, to earn more levels, you had to perfect current levels. They ditched that and added an XP system in which you gain more XP to earn a key the more levels you play and perfect. I'm very glad they added this system and was skeptical about buying it. But now that I did buy it, I do not regret it even for a second. One thing I really love about this game is how you don't have to unlock base levels. In a sense, this game is open world. That sense is that many levels are available to you, and you can choose whether you want to advance into more challenging levels, or stay where you're at. To get an S in completion, you have to sweep up EVERY leaf, and to get an S in Finesse, you have to maintain your combo throughout an entire level.
Another thing I absolutely enjoy about Dustforce is its expasive community. There are lots of Community Workshop maps for you to sharpen your skills on, and lots of people who can set a good example. I'm sure most of the people who get best times on all the levels have a Youtube channel, so you can probably catch them there. The community may or not be active, but it sure is good and friendly.
Overall, in terms of gameplay, music, artstyle, animation, and difficulty (it's not an easy game, but it's not that hard of a game either. It just depends on how much you want to play it), I rate this game:
10/10

Alright, I never thought I'd say a South Park game (after the old ones...) would be vicious competition for Game Of The Year.
Well, I was wrong. This game has easily been more fun and immersive than any other game that has come out this year.
I haven't beaten it all the way through and I do worry about replayability a bit due to the large portion of story driven content.
However, the RPG itself is very deep and fun to play as a game itself. The lack of a user interface is done well for once and it seriously plays like (several) episodes of South Park. I found myself enjoying the combat thoroughly!
I usually only buy things on humble bundle or if I will play them for a long time. I do not regret paying the full 60 for this one.
That really, really says something.
Be aware though, some countries have anal retentive demolition man government policy and so they won't be able to experience this game as the whole piece of art it is. If you are in those countries, I am doubting the game will be boring because of the changes (It is literally impossible to ruin this game even with a slight bit of creepy spying old guys in suits censorship) but that is something you may want to consider if you live in CensorShipistan or EasilyOffendedVille.
Myself, I am able to experience the full game and from what I have seen... Every bit of effort and care has been given to make the game an actually enjoyable experience. They did not rely on fans to buy it simply because they are fans. They wanted the game to stand on its own two feet. The npc dialogue is reactive to what you do, the game does not tend to keep you from doing something you want to do unless it has good reason and I found myself immersed in the South Park universe.
Although it is story driven, the "plot twists" are not toooo obvious and the game feels as crazy as South Park does.
This is a solid 10/10 singleplayer experience and I suspect that if you were to stream it for some friends or let them watch on the couch... A good time will be had by all involved.

Update for October 28, 2015:
I neglected to update my review when I found out how to access the New 52 Skins. They're in the Gallery. On to the more important update; the compensation for the PC players. We've been promised a few things.
First, we've been given the entirety of the Arkham Game Library. For me, this is a big plus, since Arkham Knight is the only Arkham game I have on the PC, now I'll have all five, which is very nice.
Second, we're getting the Community Challenge Pack DLC free and a week before the consoles, sometime in January 2016. Now, whether or not that DLC is free for consoles, I don't know. If it's free for consoles, it's not quite as nice of a gesture, but getting it before the consoles is still nice.
Third, for those who play Team Fortress 2, they are getting "Batman Arkham themed items" that will be created in a contest. A very neat gesture, and even though I don't play TF2, I think it's a very cool idea.
Another awesome thing about this, especially for those who were avoiding Batman: Arkham Knight on PC because of the massive issues, if you buy this game by 11:59PM on November 16, 2015, then you ALSO get all of these freebies. I think that's a great move by WB Games, and I'm quite pleased with that.
Original Review:
I am very much enjoying the game now the the September 3rd patch has been released. I have a GTX 960 2GB card, and it runs steadily at 30FPS at 1600x900 resolution. I know that FPS and resolution is everything, but after hearing about all of the issues that the PC port of this game had, I'm quite content with these settings. Probably because I got it as a freebie with my video card. Saved me spending the money on the PS4 version.
There is a minor issue I have right now, but I suppose WB is still working some kinks out. The issue is that, unless I'm missing something, the network features don't work. AT ALL. Can't access the DLC that I have (New 52 Skins) at all, and the leaderboards don't update with anyone else, just my own stats. If anyone can enlighten me on this, I'd greatly appreciate it.
The biggest problem that I see, however, has absolutely nothing to do with the game. It's the whole mess of taking over two months to actually make the PC version playable. That speaks VOLUMES of the lack of Quality Control. It's unfortunate, honestly. As of this writing, the game is still not for sale on Steam. Almost three months in, and people can't play it on the PC unless they either bought it before it was pulled from the store, or if they got a download code with their GPU.
Do I recommend this game? Yeah. Just...be COMPLETELY sure you can play it. When they say the minimum VRAM is 2 GB, they mean it. I just REALLY hope they throw the PC crowd a bone...we only just got to play it two and a half months after it was released, and I don't believe we even have online functionality.

From my point of view, this is not better than the first Half-Life game. This game pays too much attention to the physics engine, the puzzles are often physics related which can be fun, but I found them boring, useless and frustrating sometimes.
Don't get me wrong, I like the game, but not as much as the first one. This also has a few "Episodes", those episodes are not that long but quite fun. Sometimes I feel Valve did not pay too much attention for difficulty, I found it easier than the first Half-Life.
The soundtrack is quite good, but the fact that the NPCs control you, and tell you what to do... well... when I first played it, I thought it's going to be the same as in the first Half-Life. In Half-Life 1, Valve did not force you to listen conversations (that much) and they provided you some kind of freedom which Half-Life 2 fails to give us. There are parts where I just want to ripp off my ears and poke my eyes because the conversations takes too long.
Although they made some better AI, the game itself is not better at all... on the contrary, a bit worse because of the above. As the story continues in HL2, I recommend to play HL1 first.

This is honestly one of the most frustrating gaming experiences I've had in a very long while. Now I'm playing after the patch, I never got a chance to deal with the horribleness of pre-patch. What I'm talking about is the actual gameplay itself. I've never seen a game that tries so hard to ruin itself, it's astonishing really. I feel like there were one or two guys on the design team who were bound and determined to make this experience terrible. What is so frustrating is you keep seeing the game this could have been, but then they disappoint you...again. So here are some very specific examples of what I'm talking about.
•Absolutely nothing is added to the experience of the batmobile being shoehorned into the game. It is only there to annoy you, in extremely aggrivating vehicle segments that never make you feel like Batman. They force you to deal with the batmobile CONSTANTLY, even when doing indoor puzzles! It's utterly ridiculous and whoever thought this was a good idea should be fired.
•The puzzles in this game are not clever, they're just irritating. See the next section as to why.
•This game does something that modern horror movies do that really pisses me off. It establishes a set of rules, and then breaks those rules arbirarily in the name of shock value or an attempt at being "creative".
•I won't spoil the story, but if you're any kind of Batman fan, this story is one you've seen before and you that you've seen done better. Honestly I'm pretty insulted as a fan that they thought they could get away with this crappy storyline.
•Most of the villains are portrayed as cartoonish, two-dimensional cardboard cutouts of their comic counterparts. They try hamhandedly to interject depth and fall vastly short
•Game has a great soundtrack, shame we barely ever get to hear it. Too busy listening to the CONSTANT innane chatter of every thug. After a couple hours you've heard it all and it's just irritating.
•The way they wrote Batman in this game is really quite terrible. He makes every single wrong choice he could possibly make, and honestly it doesn't even feel like Batman. This is worth noting just because of how exceptionally terrible it is.
•The most interesting character in the game stops being present before you even hit the halfway mark.
•It wasn't until I got this far into the review that I realize what this game feels like. It's like playing a game version of the 3rd Nolan Batman.
•At least it runs perfectly now after the patch, right?
All in all you're much better off just replaying Arkham Asylum or City. Better yet, pick up a copy of Under the Red Hood, or just read some Batman comics. Rocksteady, you should be ashamed.
