I'm going to say this is one of the best RPG's ever made in my opinion. Yes, it IS short, be warned about that beforehand, you'll finish the game in 25 hours if you take your sweet time, and you should, because what makes this game so good it's the amount of detail put into it. Rushing past everything would be playing this game wrong, this isn't to be played in a hurry. Actually, the game expects a little of thinking and observation from your part with a lot of puzzles, for example those optional ones to take down enemies without the need to fight them.
Even if you're not a fan of the TV series or RPG's in general you'll find that this is a well made game, with a good flow both in history and combat. The battle and overworld mechanics are fresh, entertaining and feel just right. Obviously there is a lot of foul language and even things that people might find objectionable, but that and it's blend of comedy put into a videogame is what makes this one a unique experience you will never find elsewhere nowhere soon, because what the creators of this game took is a big risk, the kind of risk that videogame developers are less and less likely to take when it comes to games of this budget. Why? Because the game has no real replay value, all the effort that was put into this game, you will experience it in it's single run. No grinds, no replays, no hooks. If you're looking for a different experience when it comes to RPG's I really think you should give this one a try.

This game's description tells you a whole lot of nothing, so let me fix that. Super Hexagon is an arcade-style action game where you need to guide a little triangle (the one right outside the center hex if you look at the pictures) to avoid the incoming hexagon fragments. This game is frantic and it's difficult. You'll need perfect speed and precision to make it even part way through the first level. You will lose many, many times before you succeed, but you're instantly thrown back in the action.
As you play, the hexagons start coming at you in new, interesting patterns that will throw you off. You'll bob and weave, and then suddenly the hexagon becomes a pentagon and your careful plans need to change in a split second. The pace is really intense.
The graphics are basic but neat. The music is great; it's high-quality chiptune music, but that should be no surprise from the developer of VVVVVV.
It's an interesting game that's done very well, but it's just not for me. If you're looking for a unique, challenging game, you can do a lot worse than Super Hexagon, especially for the price. This game is cheap enough that there's really no need to wait for a sale if you're interested.

STORY:
The story of Half Life 2 is one I couldn't really understand. From what I gathered you had to fight the organization known as the Combine as Gordon Freeman who apparently is the most well known person around. Without spoiling much many question arise as you begin but as the game progresses nothing is really answered and just ended up leaving me confused. However, There are points in the story where the atmosphere is perfect and really gives the player a feeling of either true action and excitement or fear and horror. Overall, as for just Half Life 2, the story was nothing that great overall it honestly felt like Valve wanted to make a story but just forgot about it. I assume taht Half Life 2 Episode 1 and 2 explain the situation better
GAMEPLAY:
As for how the game controls it feels like any standard first person shooter. When walking on land Freeman's physics feel natural and make sense. The most shining endeavors of the game is its use of the gravity gun and the pheropod found later in the game. The gravity gun is something that I've never seen in a game to this day. It does have quite a few useful actions to help yourself on the adventure. Also the pheropod that controls antlions are great and does give a nice change in pace from just using a machine gun. However, both of these uses started to become useless after their use in one sequence of the game. Sadly, for the majority of the game I was just using a machine gun which became boring after a while. Now I don't want exclude the use of vehicles in the game that definetly were a fun time as well as the turrets, but there use was all focused in one portion and never revisited again making them feel more like pointless thrill rides. However the gun play is standard and is something you can find in any common first person shooter.
THE WORLD:
Even though I had no idea what was going on story-wise and the gun play was nothing special the world of City 17, Ravenholm, and all the other areas were quite interesting. The game definitely rewarded the idea of exploring the surrouding area. When it came to exploration it gave me a very similar feeling to that of Doom. Though the world was interesting to explore most of the area was required to progress in the actual game making the game feel like the world was more open than it actually was, which was a good way to hide the linearity of the game.
CONCLUSION:
Overall this is a good game. For a game originally on the Xbox it definitely had a lot of revolutionary aspects for the time but the game has aged and it certainly hasn't aged the best. This is a game you should buy if you want to experience a game with some of the best atmosphere I've ever seen in a game. However, the game can get repetitive and even frustrating sometimes, but luckily these points of boredom aren't as frequent as it may seem. If you have been hyped about this game being one of the best games ever made, it is not that. The game is an enjoyable experience that no one should miss out on.

STORY:
The story of Half Life 2 is one I couldn't really understand. From what I gathered you had to fight the organization known as the Combine as Gordon Freeman who apparently is the most well known person around. Without spoiling much many question arise as you begin but as the game progresses nothing is really answered and just ended up leaving me confused. However, There are points in the story where the atmosphere is perfect and really gives the player a feeling of either true action and excitement or fear and horror. Overall, as for just Half Life 2, the story was nothing that great overall it honestly felt like Valve wanted to make a story but just forgot about it. I assume taht Half Life 2 Episode 1 and 2 explain the situation better
GAMEPLAY:
As for how the game controls it feels like any standard first person shooter. When walking on land Freeman's physics feel natural and make sense. The most shining endeavors of the game is its use of the gravity gun and the pheropod found later in the game. The gravity gun is something that I've never seen in a game to this day. It does have quite a few useful actions to help yourself on the adventure. Also the pheropod that controls antlions are great and does give a nice change in pace from just using a machine gun. However, both of these uses started to become useless after their use in one sequence of the game. Sadly, for the majority of the game I was just using a machine gun which became boring after a while. Now I don't want exclude the use of vehicles in the game that definetly were a fun time as well as the turrets, but there use was all focused in one portion and never revisited again making them feel more like pointless thrill rides. However the gun play is standard and is something you can find in any common first person shooter.
THE WORLD:
Even though I had no idea what was going on story-wise and the gun play was nothing special the world of City 17, Ravenholm, and all the other areas were quite interesting. The game definitely rewarded the idea of exploring the surrouding area. When it came to exploration it gave me a very similar feeling to that of Doom. Though the world was interesting to explore most of the area was required to progress in the actual game making the game feel like the world was more open than it actually was, which was a good way to hide the linearity of the game.
CONCLUSION:
Overall this is a good game. For a game originally on the Xbox it definitely had a lot of revolutionary aspects for the time but the game has aged and it certainly hasn't aged the best. This is a game you should buy if you want to experience a game with some of the best atmosphere I've ever seen in a game. However, the game can get repetitive and even frustrating sometimes, but luckily these points of boredom aren't as frequent as it may seem. If you have been hyped about this game being one of the best games ever made, it is not that. The game is an enjoyable experience that no one should miss out on.

A game for the ages. No, seriously. Although hard-core South Park fans may be disappointed by the lack of 'topical' cntent, the show's humor and skewed take on life clearly shows in the writing, the gags, and the hundreds of in-jokes that cover all of the seasons to date. There are so many easter eggs and references that it will drive me, a 100% completionist, to absolute distraction. So, let's break down the gameplay:
Controls: easy, but somewhat non-intuitive when it comes down to the puzzle-solving aspects. As you gain levels and special powers, keeping their effects straight may get wearisome. Fortunately, the pause menu tutorials are well-written and easy to understand.
Combat: Moderate, depending on difficulty. There is a level of strategy involved between item management, special attack and buff/debuff parameters to keep min-maxers on the boards for a year. The basics are very intuitive and are well described during the tutorials, so I won't go into detail. Putting together effects management and planning for the next 3 turns of battle becomes essential during some of the boss fights.
Visuals/sound: Perfect. Captures both the visual effects and 'feel' of the show from the get-go, including character creation. Putting together my own paper doll to play the game with was one of the most enjoyable experiences, as a gamer and long-time fan of the show. Trey and Matt of course do the voice acting and it really feels like you're playing an episode. Even the grinding/exploration has just enough interjections from your AI companion to remind you you're supposed to be doing something on the main quest, without getting overly annoying.
RPG/customization elements: So simple they're frightening in their complexity. The amounts of perks/abilities and weapon/armor customizations run into the hundreds by the time you've completed your first series of main story quests. The ability to mod your weapons/armor perks just before a battle are going to fuel hours of debate between gamers of all stripes.
Fun level: 5 stars. The most subjective of all categories, I can't wait to finish my first run-through and try it all again with a new character build.

This game's description tells you a whole lot of nothing, so let me fix that. Super Hexagon is an arcade-style action game where you need to guide a little triangle (the one right outside the center hex if you look at the pictures) to avoid the incoming hexagon fragments. This game is frantic and it's difficult. You'll need perfect speed and precision to make it even part way through the first level. You will lose many, many times before you succeed, but you're instantly thrown back in the action.
As you play, the hexagons start coming at you in new, interesting patterns that will throw you off. You'll bob and weave, and then suddenly the hexagon becomes a pentagon and your careful plans need to change in a split second. The pace is really intense.
The graphics are basic but neat. The music is great; it's high-quality chiptune music, but that should be no surprise from the developer of VVVVVV.
It's an interesting game that's done very well, but it's just not for me. If you're looking for a unique, challenging game, you can do a lot worse than Super Hexagon, especially for the price. This game is cheap enough that there's really no need to wait for a sale if you're interested.

1.  As a functioning product.
2. As a work of art and entertainment.
A few months ago, this game was so bad as a functioning product that I refused to play it. Now, it works perfectly. The only functional issue I had was that mouse and keyboard controls are really bad. That lasted all of 2 minutes, until I used my controller. This game was made for controllers. Problem solved. So with that being said, let's move on to the second way of looking at games: as a work of art and entertainment.
( and I have played A LOT).
Think of the most detailed city you've seen in a game. Liberty City? Los Santos? One from Assassin's Creed? Forget about them. Gotham blows them out of the water. I cannot fathom how many unique 3D assets and textures were created for this game. There's nothing else like it. Even completely inconsequential, out-of-the-way rooms have so much detail and character that you'd swear it had an entire story of its own to tell. If I ever wanted a detailed world to be built, I would call up Rocksteady in a flash. These guys are the masters.
The progression of Batman and his skills match up beautifully with the challenging variety of enemies and puzzles you discover as time goes on. The whole game just feels like a perfectly graded slope curving upwards to a final explosive conflict. Being an open-world game, they could have just thrown markers all around the map and said "knock yourself out" and people still would have given it good scores. This is not good game design. Just look at Far Cry and Assassin's Creed in recent years. There's no thought put into them. Arkham Knight is one of the more finely tuned experiences in recent years. If you ever felt like there's too much to do in open world games these days and that you feel like you've lost focus, then fear not. Arkham Knight is your salvation. The enemy encounters, the puzzles, the mysteries; all of them know just when to mix it up to keep things interesting.
You've never seen so many 4K textures packed into one area in a 3rd person game. This game could easily be scrutinized as a first person game and hold its own with the best of them. The lighting is moody, the rain is the best I've ever seen in a game, the physics are on point. Unreal Engine and Rocksteady have done it again. This game looks fantastic.
First of all, I'm of the mind that all Arkham games have always had phenomenal combat. Arkham Knight gives you more control than in the past allowing even more specific moves for adapting to specific enemies, while still, of course, recycling old ones. If you liked it before, you'll love it now. If you didn't like it before, you might now.
Hollywood, take note. Comic book authors, take note. THIS is how you write an epic, sweeping superhero/supervillain story. Arkham Asylum's story was great. Arkham City's was ok. Arkham Knight's makes Christopher Nolan look like an amateur. I won't spoil anything for you, just play it or at the very least watch one of those youtube "video game, the movie" edits. It's emotional, it's deep, it's very (very) dark at times. It's beautiful.

Eat your heart out MGSV and The Witcher 3. I don't care about its rocky launch. That is over. This game needs to be judged for what it is right now. A masterpiece.

STORY:
The story of Half Life 2 is one I couldn't really understand. From what I gathered you had to fight the organization known as the Combine as Gordon Freeman who apparently is the most well known person around. Without spoiling much many question arise as you begin but as the game progresses nothing is really answered and just ended up leaving me confused. However, There are points in the story where the atmosphere is perfect and really gives the player a feeling of either true action and excitement or fear and horror. Overall, as for just Half Life 2, the story was nothing that great overall it honestly felt like Valve wanted to make a story but just forgot about it. I assume taht Half Life 2 Episode 1 and 2 explain the situation better
GAMEPLAY:
As for how the game controls it feels like any standard first person shooter. When walking on land Freeman's physics feel natural and make sense. The most shining endeavors of the game is its use of the gravity gun and the pheropod found later in the game. The gravity gun is something that I've never seen in a game to this day. It does have quite a few useful actions to help yourself on the adventure. Also the pheropod that controls antlions are great and does give a nice change in pace from just using a machine gun. However, both of these uses started to become useless after their use in one sequence of the game. Sadly, for the majority of the game I was just using a machine gun which became boring after a while. Now I don't want exclude the use of vehicles in the game that definetly were a fun time as well as the turrets, but there use was all focused in one portion and never revisited again making them feel more like pointless thrill rides. However the gun play is standard and is something you can find in any common first person shooter.
THE WORLD:
Even though I had no idea what was going on story-wise and the gun play was nothing special the world of City 17, Ravenholm, and all the other areas were quite interesting. The game definitely rewarded the idea of exploring the surrouding area. When it came to exploration it gave me a very similar feeling to that of Doom. Though the world was interesting to explore most of the area was required to progress in the actual game making the game feel like the world was more open than it actually was, which was a good way to hide the linearity of the game.
CONCLUSION:
Overall this is a good game. For a game originally on the Xbox it definitely had a lot of revolutionary aspects for the time but the game has aged and it certainly hasn't aged the best. This is a game you should buy if you want to experience a game with some of the best atmosphere I've ever seen in a game. However, the game can get repetitive and even frustrating sometimes, but luckily these points of boredom aren't as frequent as it may seem. If you have been hyped about this game being one of the best games ever made, it is not that. The game is an enjoyable experience that no one should miss out on.

Stick of Truth manages to be surprisingly faithful to the actual television version of South Park. Visually, the game manages to capture the art and animation style perfectly, bringing it into a real-time interactive medium. I'm pretty sure this is the best adaptation of any existing IP to a video-game that I've seen.
You're the "new kid" that just moved to South Park, and you make friends with the familiar local kids that happen to be role-playing (they take it pretty seriously.) The plot, events, and dialogue are all what you'd expect from South Park. There's tons of ridiculousness, racism, vulgarity, and nudity here. If you're offended by South Park, this isn't for you. If you enjoy a good laugh at typical South Park toilet humor, Nazi jokes, jabs at Canadians and just general over-the-line humor, then you'll love it. All of the environments and personalities are familiar from South Park. There are constant nods and references to the show, but they're not really tied together in any big way... usually just side-quest related things, or "junk items" that you find.
You create your own standard-body (Stan/Kyle as opposed to a Cartman) character by selecting a skin tone and outfitting it with different hair, clothing, and color options. As you play the game you'll acquire new items that you can equip on-the-fly that are all visually unique. Many item slots are purely cosmetic, but many have gear that will give you specific passive combat stats; many are situational and may purely depend on your playstyle to be any good.
The gameplay here is fantastic. The world is mildly open, with only a few sections closed off until you acquire a certain ability, or trigger a certain event in the plot. This game is one of the most easy-going that I've ever played. I didn't find it tedious unlike most RPGs and modern games. I don't feel like there was ANY filler, and nothing really overstays its welcome. There's always new enemies and environments from time to time to keep it feeling fresh. You're able to do side quests at your leisure without them detracting from the main story.
Out of combat, you often will have fairly basic puzzles involving only a few different mechanics, mainly to reach a partially obscured or obstructed area. There are often environmental triggers that can kill one or many enemies before a combat scenario, making the scenario much easier to pass. These triggers are extremely rewarding, fun, and sometimes funny, although they're not difficult to find as they are indicated by visual cues.
Combat flows very well and integrates turn-based mechanics and quick-time-events together. For instance, when it is your character's turn, you'll select an ability to use, and depending on that ability, you'll have a specific QTE to perform. If you fail the QTE, you will do minimal damage to a target. Many of the QTE's are not difficult, but some of stronger abilities may flash a button you have to hit within a very short period of time. The majority are on a very repeatable time-based mechanic, though. A sword that hits 3 times will require you to learn the timing of the 3 hits and hit the action button after the visual and audio cue triggers each time.
There are also QTE's for BLOCKING the enemy's attacks, to mitigate the incoming damage. Blocking is based on the enemy's attacks, so the timing and number of hits you need to block vary. The timing is extremely easy to learn through repetition. Normally I hate QTE's but they REALLY livened up the typical turn-based monotony of selecting the same menu items and spamming the action button until everything plays out and it gets back to your turn. It's rewarding to hit those perfect QTE's when attacking and blocking perfectly... however, you could see it as very punishing if you fail them frequently as you'll deal practically no damage, and you'll receive a lot more damage as well. Like I said though, it's a pretty forgiving system and is implemented extremely well and is engaging.
During combat, you're able use both a potion and an action. So, you can choose to heal yourself without losing out on a turn to do damage. You can also use this to buff your strength before an attack. You also have to be smart about which abilities to use and when. Some enemies have tons of armor, so you'd want to use armor-reducing abilities in order to cut their armor down to a reasonable amount, otherwise you'll do practically no damage. Likewise, debuffs and stuns are very powerful to weaken your opponents at specific points. Abilities also have different attack patterns; one ability may hit only one target, one may bounce, one may hit EVERYBODY, or one might hit only one ROW or COLUMN of enemies. Target prioritization is fairly important also, but maybe less-so than more hardcore RPGs.
I've mentioned the combat system so much because it is extraordinarily good. This is a really good RPG that just happens to be South Park themed. By no means is this game watered down because it's South Park. I never expected a system as good as what is implemented.
This is an exceptionally well-designed game that I've fully played through twice (to get all the achievements) because it was so good. I've only encountered a few bugs such as audio getting cut off, characters visually flickering or disappearing, and hidden collectable items not spawning where they should be (preventing achievements.) None of them really game-breaking except for the achievement-blocking one if that's what you're into.
I played with a controller, and would recommend it if you're considering playing. I didn't try with a keyboard and mouse, but I feel like some actions wouldn't translate well at all with a keyboard. Also, during certain sections of the game some QTEs are hard to pull off... almost impossibly difficult if you're holding the controller in a standard fashion. This COULD prevent you from progressing through certain sections of the game. A couple QTE's might feel unnatural to replicate with a keybaord as well. Your mileage may vary.
My first playthrough took about 13 hours, and my second one took around 10. I wish the game was longer and that there was more to explore, but that might be why I didn't feel the game was padded in length, or needlessly grindy or difficult. Normal difficulty was on the easy side, but I'm also pretty experienced with RPGs. You may want to try the hardest difficulty if you like more challenging games.
I HIGHLY recommend this game, as I've enjoyed every hour of it so much that I played it twice in succession, which is something I've never done with a game before. There's so many things from the show that I wish were included, but I guess you can't expect to have over a decade's worth of content replicated in this manner.

About the Game
1998. HALF-LIFE sends a shock through the game industry with its combination of pounding action and continuous, immersive storytelling. Valve's debut title wins more than 50 game-of-the-year awards on its way to being named "Best PC Game Ever" by PC Gamer, and launches a franchise with more than eight million retail units sold worldwide.
NOW. By taking the suspense, challenge and visceral charge of the original, and adding startling new realism and responsiveness, Half-Life 2 opens the door to a world where the player's presence affects everything around him, from the physical environment to the behaviors even the emotions of both friends and enemies.
The player again picks up the crowbar of research scientist Gordon Freeman, who finds himself on an alien-infested Earth being picked to the bone, its resources depleted, its populace dwindling. Freeman is thrust into the unenviable role of rescuing the world from the wrong he unleashed back at Black Mesa. And a lot of people he cares about are counting on him.
The intense, real-time gameplay of Half-Life 2 is made possible only by Source®, Valve's new proprietary engine technology. Source provides major enhancements in:
Characters: Advanced facial animation system delivers the most sophisticated in-game characters ever seen. With 40 distinct facial "muscles," human characters convey the full array of human emotion, and respond to the player with fluidity and intelligence.
Physics: From pebbles to water to 2-ton trucks respond as expected, as they obey the laws of mass, friction, gravity, and buoyancy.
Graphics: Source's shader-based renderer, like the one used at Pixar to create movies such as Toy Story® and Monster's, Inc.®, creates the most beautiful and realistic environments ever seen in a video game.
AI: Neither friends nor enemies charge blindly into the fray. They can assess threats, navigate tricky terrain, and fashion weapons from whatever is at hand.

If you like South Park the TV show, and you enjoy the type of humor that its known for, you'll probably enjoy this game.  I've watched most of the episodes since the pilot and I thought this game was in part a tribute to South Park's hardcore fanbase.  That said, the game has interesting rpg elements that make it playable even if you've never seen the show regularly.  Turn based timing attacks and lots of new gear keep the relatively actionless gameplay interesting.  Normally, when I play games, I will have something playing on my second monitor, like a TV show or a movie, but when I played through this game, it was compelling enough for me to turn off my second monitor.  There are bugs in the windows version of the game, and some of the controls are unweildly.  The inventory system is brutal, requiring a carpal tunnel inducing amount of clicks to unload an entire inventory.  There are some elements of the game that are left unexplained and some that are explained every time you do a specific action.  That said, I was highly entertained by the game overall.  The format was successful and my biggest complaint is that it wasn't longer.  I really feel like this game could be adapted for a sequel, or maybe an even larger more open world fallout/skyrim type game.  I know its a longshot, but I felt a sense of emotional connection with the characters, music, sound effects and visual elements of this game and I'd love for it to be the first in a long franchise.  9.5/10

About the Game
1998. HALF-LIFE sends a shock through the game industry with its combination of pounding action and continuous, immersive storytelling. Valve's debut title wins more than 50 game-of-the-year awards on its way to being named "Best PC Game Ever" by PC Gamer, and launches a franchise with more than eight million retail units sold worldwide.
NOW. By taking the suspense, challenge and visceral charge of the original, and adding startling new realism and responsiveness, Half-Life 2 opens the door to a world where the player's presence affects everything around him, from the physical environment to the behaviors even the emotions of both friends and enemies.
The player again picks up the crowbar of research scientist Gordon Freeman, who finds himself on an alien-infested Earth being picked to the bone, its resources depleted, its populace dwindling. Freeman is thrust into the unenviable role of rescuing the world from the wrong he unleashed back at Black Mesa. And a lot of people he cares about are counting on him.
The intense, real-time gameplay of Half-Life 2 is made possible only by Source®, Valve's new proprietary engine technology. Source provides major enhancements in:
Characters: Advanced facial animation system delivers the most sophisticated in-game characters ever seen. With 40 distinct facial "muscles," human characters convey the full array of human emotion, and respond to the player with fluidity and intelligence.
Physics: From pebbles to water to 2-ton trucks respond as expected, as they obey the laws of mass, friction, gravity, and buoyancy.
Graphics: Source's shader-based renderer, like the one used at Pixar to create movies such as Toy Story® and Monster's, Inc.®, creates the most beautiful and realistic environments ever seen in a video game.
AI: Neither friends nor enemies charge blindly into the fray. They can assess threats, navigate tricky terrain, and fashion weapons from whatever is at hand.

Arsenal of Batgadgets

Batman: Arkam Knight. Came free with my GPU. Yay, I guess. But not so great news. I willl review it though as if I bought it full price to make it fair for all.
Everyone knows who Batman is, and what this game is about so I'm not going to go on.
Alright, let's go.
Graphics. Game looks okay I guess. Not the greatest, but not the worst. I did have some texture clipping but I have an eagle eye for those things so you'll more than likely not see it. I get a stable 30 fps, at high on my rig. And only 30fps. No more, no less. I'll talk about why that is later. Or now. The game has a 30fps lock on it. Yes, on default. The fix is to go into the game config file and change it (look up how if you don't know). I did it but never booted the game again. Why? Other reasons.
Mechanics and physics. Some things don't work as intended. Or I must suck at playing this. Either one, maybe a little of both. The car/Batmobile/destruction thing handles kinda bad. Like it's floating on air. No jokes. Yep. I'll just move on.
Now, why didn't I play it again? I got a little bored of it. I mean, it's okay but not really my cup of tea (look at my library, this doesn't really belong with my other games). Maybe if you were more into this kind of stuff, you'll have more replay value.
Now here is where I get a little uncertain, to put it nicely. The game costs, what $20? I don't know because Warner decided to remove the game until it gets fixed. Why is this so? It's because Warner did so poorly. To recap, 30fps lock, bad optimization for a big release, and removel of it to get it where it needs to be. Sigh. You know what that tells me? Warner is afraid of their own product. Simple.
Conclusion- Don't buy until bugs get worked out. If you get it free, fine. I guess it's okay then. But it's a waiting game to see what they do.
Update after patch: Well, this game has been fixed on performance. Very much. I am now going to recommend this. Like I said in my original review, if they worked out the performance and bugs and stuff, I'll recommend it. And sure enough, they did. So I'll stick to what I said. I recommend.

I originally had issues running this game when I first got it, but between the time of the release and the patch, I upgraded my hardware and it was running without a problem.  I was getting 60 FPS and all the settings where set to 'normal'.  After the patch, I am getting 30 FPS on 'low'.  I  can set the game to 'high' for parts, and it will run just fine, but then it will drop to 0 FPS for a few seconds, and depending on when that happens, it can be fatal.  During fights, using the quick attacks seems to make the game lag so much that I just don't use them.  While having more in-game graphics options is nice, the stability has not improved at all.  Even launching the game can be troublesome, sometimes it takes a few minutes for the splash screen to pop up, and once or twice it refused to launch.
While this game has too many bugs to list, the story is interesting and the game delivers a true Batman experience.  I wish the Riddler quest was not 'puzzle' solving with a car, and by puzzles I mean time trials.  There is also too much forced use of the Batmobile.  When I think of the Dark Knight, I think of fist fighting, not tank combat.  I'd only suggest this game to people who are dedicated to the series.  If it was not so buggy, then I would be more willing to promote this to friends, but I don't want to be slinging crap.

I won't lie. I've never been much of a fan of South Park. I think it's quite funny, but I rarely watch more than a couple of episodes a year. So I wasn't too sure if I would like this game or not, and in the end I found that I loved this game! It's unbelievable crude, but that's okay. They handle it in a way that all the sick humor feels like it's there for a reason rather than just there for shock value. The game play is pretty solid too. All in all I had a good time with this game.
One of the biggest draws to the game is that it was written by the show's writers and voiced by the entire cast. If that hadn't been true this game probably would have sucked quite a bit more. Mostly because without the clever cast and writing the game couldn't have held my attention as long as it did. The plot is... weird, but fun. And in the end that's what is important.
The gameplay caught me by surprise. I'm not going to say that it was stupendous. Because it wasn't. I found myself spamming quite a few attacks over and over again. It's a good thing that some of them are so much fun to use (like anything from Princess Kenny or the Thief's final ability). The game could have stood for a little bit more variety with the combat. It holds up for the duration of the game, but by the end I was kind of sick of seeing the same moves over and over again.
Honestly the most entertaining thing for me was finding as many costume pieces as I could. I had fun dying the pieces and mixing and matching them. There is a huge variety of pieces and the depth of the dress-up mechanic really makes me sad that you HAVE to play as a boy. I would love to see an update to the game that let's you start out as a girl and work up the political backstabbing. It would be a way of retelling the plot from a fun perspective. At least I think that would be fun.
All in all I enjoyed this game. I don't see myself coming back to replay it over and over again, but I don't regret the purchase at all. It was a very fun time that I had trouble pulling myself away from.
If you love South Park you will love this game!

I bought Batman Arkahm Knight after the big patch came out for 14$ which is a steal for this game
(kind of).
-------------------------------------------------Gameplay----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
What can i say to anyone who played the other Batmam games? you may ask.
Well it's another night where Batman is the only one who can save Arkham city. Going through the main quest is definitely the most enjoyable of them all, but I found myself having fun clearing the Arkahm from bombs, patrol cars, tanks, drones and more. I'd say that the main quest is great and could be played alone but without the other quests you are leaving the city full with criminals and chaos which that's not something A TRUE BATMAN WOULD DO.
------------------------------------------------Performance-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
On my part I have a powerful PC which can run any game on max settings.
(r9 290x,i5 4670k 3.8ghz,windows 10, 256gb ssd)
Although my PC is poweful I were struggling a bit with bugs:
The game lags every several minutes for a second or two.
The game mutes as much as lags but it lasts 5 to 10 seconds.
I never had any game breaking glitches or any craches, and most of the time it ran smoothly on constant 90 fps.
------------------------------------------------Overall---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I never rate a game by it's compatibility or performance unless it's game breaking for example: Fallout 3 for windows 10 or even worse Takedown: Red Sabre (Don't buy it)
So for Batman Arkham Knight i'm going to rate it only by gameplay experience.
The vanilla version of batman arkham knight is great and worth spending 18$ for it (current price for Batman Arkham Knight on key sites.) but 18$ for around 40 hours if you complete all of the riddles (35 hours without) in my opinion isn't much.
I'm giving the vanilla version 9.5/10.
I bought the season pass for another 10$ and yet i can't play it :(
The only DLC i played is the Harely Quinn DLC which was fun with thief and rage mode, but there's a plot twist to this "great" dlc IT'S ONLY 10 MINUTES!!!. felt so disappointed completing it in such a short time. Cool,fresh gameplay that shows the criminal side of Arkham city but yet SHOCKINGLY SHORT
in this case I see this two factors as equals
so my rating for Harely Quinn dlc is 5/10 (And I'm being nice!).
---------------------------------------------Conclusion-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Batman Arkham Knight is a great addition to the Batman Arkham series. It's thrilling, challenging, interesting and overall great!. Although you should probably stay away from the Season Pass at this moment because it's seems sketchy and cheap.

I don't reiew often but after being addicted to this game for some time now I think a review is overdue...
My first and foremost advice, the DLC, wait for it to go on sale youre going to be playing this game hours upon hours what's a little more waiting. The money saved makes the game so much more sweeter trust me. The game itself I don't know where to begin to state it simply and loosly think a digital game of risk. You play a leader of an empire that must strive to survive in a world full of other empires. There will be strong military-based empires who either defend the weak or bully all around them and weaker more culture based empires (which still shouldnt be taken lightly) capable of befriending city states.. My first complete playthrough start to finish i played as Japan (thier strong military at weak hp was acctractive to me) i always had the pointiest sticks, went with honor and commerce. I even founded the first world congress. This was before i understood the importance of diplomacy in the game mechanics.. 7 wars and 3 capitals later  I am the biggest warmonger in the game, the cultural empire was at war with from the start now asssumes a dominant control over the world congress im talking 23 delegates to the next top empire being 10 delegates and me with 3 delegates lol. Oh ya i was the most powerful military force in game by far... but even the strongest military can only cover so much ground in x-amount of turns even with the help of airports and paratroopers/xcoms. Siam (the congress dominating super power) put an embargo on me and my allies they both pass even with our combined delegates we could not stop that from happening... by the end of the game, Siam is pushing for world leader a diplomatic victory and Persia is pushing for scientific victory launching space parts all over. (I only know this cause he went to war with a ally i was in defence pact with so i sent help) when i seen this though i started dropping nukes unmercilessly over his lands by sea in a futile attempt to seize the citys launching parts with my ally. The exact number was 8 nuclear missles(not atomic bombs) 2 per carrier plus 1 guided in each. Trust me at mid game i thought for sure i had a domination victory in the bag.. I learned if you want to dominate, start early, before empires make pacts together, become strong, or use the diplomacy mechanics against you like the embargo would have hurt my military to the point of no return if i had not gone commerce social policy... lol oh persia won, I couldn't seize the right citys in time with my massive military force my land forces dedicated to fighting siam on a northern front and my navy with nuclear missles helping my ally fight persia on the southern front all parts eventually launched and game over... you might think i would be done for a while but nope lol started a new game and back in it right away ... IF YOU HAVE AN ADDICTIVE PERSONALITY BEWARE!! you will love this game and "one more turn" will become your motto

How can you top up Half-Life? So many versatile challenges filled with both action and exploration? Half-Life 2 attempts to do it hollywood style: impressive visuals and a clever narrative playing around with your expectations. Like many sci-fi sequels, the moody horror survival shifts progressively towards pure action. You will be joining the resistance and getting help from the creatures that were your worst enemy on the previous installment (like in Terminator 2) to destroy the combine soldiers and robots (occasionnaly with the use of vehicules like a sand boggie and an airboat). Weirdly enough there aren't any new alien characters here and the ending is rather abrupt. But worry not, the rollercoaster continues in episodes 1 & 2 picking the action right where you left it off.

The characters are there, the humour is there, the music is there and ofc the raunchiness is there. If you are into SP you will not be disappointed.
So, you are the new kid - in my case a black Jewish kid with freckles and purple hair - and you just moved into SP. It is your mission to make friends, beat up elves and bums, loot what you can and deal with a fair deal of anal probing. Your charter is customizable up to the balls (no pun intended, you can have balls on your chin) with various clothes, weapons, haircuts, glasses etc. As in most rpg-s you get levels from fighting and questing and upon levelling up your stats go up (you can’t pick which stats) and you unlock more abilities (you can choose perks and you gain magic spells and special abilities that level up). The battle is turn based, but has a quick time event system built into it every step of the way. Oddly enough, I really did not not like it! In fact, the game is pretty solid all around. It’s a good RPG.
True RPG fans will ofc be missing the ability to assign your str/agi/int etc and maybe they will expect a larger variety of skills and especially magic (8h in, I find the magic/fart system to be perhaps the most disappointing part of it, but still ok) but you do get to shape how you do your damage so you feel in control all the time.
The game is well paced, there is always something for you to do, the game world is easy to travel /a bit small maybe even/ so you don’t waste time just travelling. New areas of the world open up as you gain new abilities giving you reasons to go back to places you have visited already.
If you can take the SP humour, you will never have a dull moment and you will be adventuring with smile on your face the whole time.  This game is fab aside from the lacklustre magic system.

What can i say to anyone who played the other Batmam games? you may ask.

------------------------------------------------Performance-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
On my part I have a powerful PC which can run any game on max settings.
(r9 290x,i5 4670k 3.8ghz,windows 10, 256gb ssd)
Although my PC is poweful I were struggling a bit with bugs:
The game lags every several minutes for a second or two.
The game mutes as much as lags but it lasts 5 to 10 seconds.
I never had any game breaking glitches or any craches, and most of the time it ran smoothly on constant 90 fps.
------------------------------------------------Overall---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I never rate a game by it's compatibility or performance unless it's game breaking for example: Fallout 3 for windows 10 or even worse Takedown: Red Sabre (Don't buy it)
So for Batman Arkham Knight i'm going to rate it only by gameplay experience.
The vanilla version of batman arkham knight is great and worth spending 18$ for it (current price for Batman Arkham Knight on key sites.) but 18$ for around 40 hours if you complete all of the riddles (35 hours without) in my opinion isn't much.

Cool,fresh gameplay that shows the criminal side of Arkham city but yet SHOCKINGLY SHORT
in this case I see this two factors as equals
so my rating for Harely Quinn dlc is 5/10 (And I'm being nice!).
---------------------------------------------Conclusion-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Batman Arkham Knight is a great addition to the Batman Arkham series. It's thrilling, challenging, interesting and overall great!. Although you should probably stay away from the Season Pass at this moment because it's seems sketchy and cheap.

I like it a lot.  It has a simple, intuitive interface, it's tech tree is both interesting and fairly accurate (emphasis on "fairly"), and the combat system is a vast improvement over past versions of the game.  My basic impression is that they took Civ 4, which was already an improvement over the old Civ 1-3 models, cut out the worst aspects of it, and improved upon the best parts.  I really think the game works best with the Gods & Kings and Brave New World expansions, and especially the latter.  These added greatly to the experience, and Brave New World overhauled the game in ways that I feel make it a truly great experience.
That said, the game is not without its flaws.  The AI is a bit stupid, so the devs got around that by giving them ridiculously unfair advantages on higher difficulty settings.  Diplomacy is kind of a crapshoot in single player, because the AI's opinion of you will swing wildly and for completely asinine reasons.  300+ turns of friendship will all fall apart in an instant with little to no provocation.  Worse yet, the AI will become completely unreasonable with their trade requirements in the late game.  They'll demand all of your luxury and strategic resource and tons of gold for a single one of their luxury resources, and this is simply unacceptable.  Worse yet, they'll impose these limitations on trade even when your military vastly outclasses theirs.  Also, for whatever reason, AI players are awful at economic planning.  This is especially true of militaristic civilizations, like Denmark, whom I will routinely see making -100+ gold per turn, regardless of difficulty setting.
If anything, the AI seems to try HARDER to provoke you into war if you're much more powerful than they are, issuing threats and insults, and refusing any even remotely fair trade.  I'm sure this was meant as a way to ostracize a player who is clearly winning the game, but it really makes non-aggression play-throughs irritating, since you lose the ability to make reasonable trades once you start pulling ahead.  Galactic Civilization 2 handles diplomacy far better, with lesser civilizations doing their best to keep you from wanting to kill them, being willing to offer you good deals on anything non-military, and roughly equal civs being more or less cooperative, so long as it's in their best interests.  In that game, you only really need to watch out for equal civs who think they have a shot against you and want you out of the way for economic/political reasons, or much larger civs who are looking for easy prey.
In all, Civilization 5 is a good game, and with its expansions, a great game.  It has its issues, but they aren't deal-breakers by any stretch, and the modding community has a few really good gems hidden amongst the trash.  If you like strategy or resource-management games (because there's some serious resource-management on higher difficulty settings), I'd recommend it.

It's kind of hard to sum up Civlization. The series has been around for a very long time, and has worked from a formula that has differed only slightly from the series beginning.
It's an incredibly slow-paced experience. Especially on larger maps and harder difficulties. It's not an RTS. Everything is turn based. It's better not to think of it as a game like we normally do, rather it's more akin to a much more traditional kind of game, i.e. chess.
I've read about people playing chess over correspondence, taking weeks or months to plan each move, resulting in chess games that are ultimate battles of strategy taking years to complete a game. Civilization V is kinda like that.
It's also an epic alternate history simulator. Any civilization throughout history either already exists in game, or is available through mods.
Just recently I downloaded an Acadian (Cajun) civilization mod and had them create a global trading empire that was the envy of the modern world. For some reason all the other AI civs were Asian civilizations like Japan and Polynesia, so it was an alternate history world populated solely by the great empires of Asia, and for some reason, dirty French people from Louisiana. It was glorious.

So I've been playing the Civilization titles for many turns in my life.  Unlike real life, the Civ titles' turns can be paused and strategized; in real life, there is no pause button, and most of my plans go to waste.  So that is why I turn to Civ when I need or want to - it's more fun than real life sometimes.
That said, Civ 5 is yet another fantastic addition to the franchise.  I will review the base game, the Gods & Kings expansion, and the Brave New World expansion here.  I might even drop a tad on Civilization: Beyond Earth if I find the time.
Civ 5 has a hexagon-based map where units cannot stack on top of each other.  If you ask me (and no one ever does), this is how all Civilization titles were supposed to be from the beginning!  It just makes more sense when playing a strategy game, I feel.  I was super-stoked to learn about this when they were promoting the game years ago, and my dreams were fulfilled when I finally got to play it.
Civ 5 also has good graphics, but they are not three-dimensional.  Of course, there are no 3-D Civilization games, but that does not take away from the "mapboard" experience, as I call it.  That is, it's like playing a board game on a map; and that's what I like.
The music is just perfectly awesome just like in Civ 4.  I was always pleased that Firaxis went above and beyond in the music department.  It just makes the game legendary at that point: when everything makes sense, goes together, and all the human senses are tickled pink.
The Gods & Kings expansion was pretty dang good, as Civ 4 made Civilization fans crave religion in the franchise.  So the religions and their alterable attributes made customization fun and added a new layer of strategy, as religion attributes were on a first-come-first-served basis.  And these religions augmented various aspects of Civ 5, including military, population growth, production, etc.  And the spreading of religion was similar to Civ 4's model: send out the missionaries or prophets and convert towns.
The Brave New World expansion disappointed me for the most part only because much of its features were unimportant to me.  For example, the whole thing with trade routes: you can't lose money from them, only gain.  So if I was making an extra 7 gold per turn due to a trade route, then I wouldn't know it or miss it if it went away.  But then the typical confusion surrounding the purported difference between "gold" and "commerce."  Really, what is the difference?  You won't figure it out by reading the Civilopedia, and this carryover from Civ 4 is just pointless, and Brave New World does nothing to make me care enough about it.
But yeah, who cares... Civ 5 is a title every single human being needs to own whether you want it or not; so get it.  I already loved turn-based strategy games: I have been genetically predispositioned for such things.  But if you love world history, then Civ 5 (and the other titles in the franchise) will fit your bill - plenty to learn from this video game, which only adds to its status as a classic game franchise that all must own.
To close...  Civilization: Beyond Earth.  If you ask me (and no one ever does... still), that entire game is just a Civ 5 mod.  It's like the colors were changed and the game concepts of Civ 5 were just renamed to give it a futuresque appeal.  That said, Civ: BE is therefore super-fun, as well.  But don't pay more than you would for an add-on for it.  But for Civ 5: Complete Edition, you can get the whole caboodle for well under $20, including all the DLC.  Like I said, everyone needs to own this title.

This is the game that sparked a host of mods, and presented the Source Engine to the gaming world.  There's a reason VALVe is known for this game.  It is truly amazing!  Many features of the Portal series, including sounds and objects, got their start here and helped define Portal.  The graphics are amazing for 2004, and nowadays will look sweet without melting your computer.  As for the story, it blew me away.  It starts some time after Half-Life, and uses the same style of storytelling they invented there and utilized through the rest of the Half-Life series and in both Portal games.  It is immersive, has lots of action in all the right places, includes puzzles made from the environment that really make you think creatively, and doesn't use cutscenes, but keeps you in the game at all times.  After playing Half-Life, I wanted Half-Life 2 right then!  The same goes for when I beat HL2, my first thought was: "When I can I get the next game!?"  The story is that good.  On top of all that, Half-Life 2 features some great instrumental music, which was designed like a movie score: The music starts where the action does and fits the mood perfectly.  I would say the music got me more excited and "in the zone" than seeing the hordes of CPs, Walkers, or even Headcrab Zombies.  That said, there is some blood, more gore than I expected (you can kill zombies by decapitation and slicing in half using saw blades and the gravity gun, and you discover burned and/or mutilated bodies from past battles and alien attacks) and some strong language.  Overall, a great game for a great price.

You are the reason why you fail at Super Hexagon. The spinning psychedelic hexagon moves too fast for your conscious mind to process, so you must learn to let go and trust your instincts. Don't plan, don't consider, don't hesitate. Just react to the shapes on the screen and you will succeed. Every single time you make a mistake, you lose. There is no forgiveness, there is only restart. And that is why I love this game.

Super Hexagon is a fun and addictive game that involves surviving for as long as possible as obstacles close in.
The player rotates a little outward facing triangular turtle (to borrow the Logo term) to avoid getting trapped by barriers.
The game features 6 difficulty levels total with 3 base levels and "hyper" versions of each. A level is considered cleared if the player survives in it for at least 60 seconds.
Super Hexagon encourages - without frustration - better and better performances. Initially, surviving for over 15 seconds will seem like a great accomplishment while the 60 second goal is thought to be impossibly out of reach. The barrier patterns are randomly strung together with each playthrough. This allows for techniques to be developed without the need for rote learning. Along the way to 60 seconds the player will repeatedly attempt to improve upon the current best score. Doing so will be met with visual and audio rewards.
The game's minimalistic design is rounded out with brilliant subtleties. Only the front tip of the turtle must be kept out of harm's way, allowing the sides to make contact. The turtle has a terrific little wobble as it is moved left and right. The color changes and playing field rotation change between difficulty levels and also at different time marks within each level. On the most difficult level, shadows are used to pull off a pseudo 3D effect.
For controls, use WASD + spacebar or arrow keys + Enter. Use long continuous movements by pressing, holding, and releasing instead of repeated smaller movements.
Super Hexagon supports Steam cloud syncing and online leaderboards which can be filtered to only display the results of Steam friends.

My initial review of Batman Arkham Knight wasn’t a good one…. And it was for very good reason.
My experience was the same as 90% of people, with glitchy frame drops, no “ultra” settings… Blah blah blah. I don’t have to elaborate on all the problems as the internet is full of them.
My rig:
i7 3770k @ 4.2GHz
8GB DDR3 2133 RAM
EVGA GTX980 SC ACX2.0
Samsung 850 EVO 250GB SSD & Seagate 3TB HDD
As you can see, I should not have any problem running 90% of the AAA titles @ “Ultra” setting @ 1920x1080 resolution and maintaining 50 – 60 FPS average.
Issues:
Even 3 months after launch and the “supposed patch that will fix all the glitches” the game was still causing a lot of issues for me and so I made the decision to not play the game until they resolved the issues.
A little more than a year has gone by since launch and I finally decided to give it another go and I’m glad to report that most of the issues have been resolved, however the game is still not as smooth as I would’ve hoped for and as long as I don’t enable the extra NVidia specific settings, the game runs pretty smooth on “ultra” and I only experience the odd frame drop and stuttering. 99% of the time it is only when entering the batmobile and once you’re in, no glitches.
However, switching on the above mentioned NVidia settings, changes everything. Sure it looks amazing, but the frame drops and stuttering is awful and ruins the experience to such an extent that I switched them off for the remainder of my play through.
Gameplay:
Okay with all the game breaking issues out of the way, let’s get to the gameplay itself and this is where the game really shines. The story is so amazingly rich and by far the best of the Arkham series and I’ve played all of them. I enjoyed roaming around the city in the batmobile getting side tracked by all the extra/side quests, putting the batmobile into battle mode and destroying the militia tanks or the thugs running in the streets, is just so much fun. I particularly enjoy the disruptor gadget and remote hacking tool when scoping out the enemies from above. I’ve you’ve played any of the other games in the Arkham series, then you’ll feel right at home with the controls and mechanics. It really is simple and straight forward.
Without giving away any spoilers will just say this… The ending is just EPIC!!!
It really was the best of the series for me and I enjoyed it even more that Arkham City
Overall:
For performance, I will score the game at 5/10. It was a very poor console port at game launch and Rocksteady Studios should really be ashamed to launch a game with so many problems. Too many issues with graphics settings and if you really want to get it to run smooth, there are a lot of tweaks online that help you to optimize the gameplay.
Design and graphics, I will score it a 9/10. The graphics looks amazing… after they enabled “Ultra”
Gameplay and story I will give it 10/10. The story is simply amazing and the best batman story I’ve seen so far.

So I've been playing the Civilization titles for many turns in my life.  Unlike real life, the Civ titles' turns can be paused and strategized; in real life, there is no pause button, and most of my plans go to waste.  So that is why I turn to Civ when I need or want to - it's more fun than real life sometimes.
That said, Civ 5 is yet another fantastic addition to the franchise.  I will review the base game, the Gods & Kings expansion, and the Brave New World expansion here.  I might even drop a tad on Civilization: Beyond Earth if I find the time.
Civ 5 has a hexagon-based map where units cannot stack on top of each other.  If you ask me (and no one ever does), this is how all Civilization titles were supposed to be from the beginning!  It just makes more sense when playing a strategy game, I feel.  I was super-stoked to learn about this when they were promoting the game years ago, and my dreams were fulfilled when I finally got to play it.
Civ 5 also has good graphics, but they are not three-dimensional.  Of course, there are no 3-D Civilization games, but that does not take away from the "mapboard" experience, as I call it.  That is, it's like playing a board game on a map; and that's what I like.
The music is just perfectly awesome just like in Civ 4.  I was always pleased that Firaxis went above and beyond in the music department.  It just makes the game legendary at that point: when everything makes sense, goes together, and all the human senses are tickled pink.
The Gods & Kings expansion was pretty dang good, as Civ 4 made Civilization fans crave religion in the franchise.  So the religions and their alterable attributes made customization fun and added a new layer of strategy, as religion attributes were on a first-come-first-served basis.  And these religions augmented various aspects of Civ 5, including military, population growth, production, etc.  And the spreading of religion was similar to Civ 4's model: send out the missionaries or prophets and convert towns.
The Brave New World expansion disappointed me for the most part only because much of its features were unimportant to me.  For example, the whole thing with trade routes: you can't lose money from them, only gain.  So if I was making an extra 7 gold per turn due to a trade route, then I wouldn't know it or miss it if it went away.  But then the typical confusion surrounding the purported difference between "gold" and "commerce."  Really, what is the difference?  You won't figure it out by reading the Civilopedia, and this carryover from Civ 4 is just pointless, and Brave New World does nothing to make me care enough about it.
But yeah, who cares... Civ 5 is a title every single human being needs to own whether you want it or not; so get it.  I already loved turn-based strategy games: I have been genetically predispositioned for such things.  But if you love world history, then Civ 5 (and the other titles in the franchise) will fit your bill - plenty to learn from this video game, which only adds to its status as a classic game franchise that all must own.
To close...  Civilization: Beyond Earth.  If you ask me (and no one ever does... still), that entire game is just a Civ 5 mod.  It's like the colors were changed and the game concepts of Civ 5 were just renamed to give it a futuresque appeal.  That said, Civ: BE is therefore super-fun, as well.  But don't pay more than you would for an add-on for it.  But for Civ 5: Complete Edition, you can get the whole caboodle for well under $20, including all the DLC.  Like I said, everyone needs to own this title.

Back in 2004, it was nearly impossible to detach this game from the dramatic, soap opera-like stories that surrounded its release. It is because of this perhaps that Half-Life 2 seems somewhat underwhelming. Its predecessor also encountered many a delay until it reached store shelves in November of 1998, but these were more industry-common delays and not anything of the caliber of Half-Life 2's drama.
Because it is a sequel, the original Half-Life has to be considered as a valid comparison but its successor and Half-Life 2 does not seem to manage to match the awe the original game inspired among gamers. That being said, Half-Life 2 is a fantastic game nonetheless and the beauty of the world it recreates as well as the depth of the characters involved in the game's story make it a worthy successor to Half-Life.
The post-soviet feel of City 17, the eastern european countryside atmosphere of Ravenholm in the first half of the game are more than enough to justify almost all the drama around its release. Gordon Freeman remains the main character and his mute involvement in the story works exactly as well as it did in '98 or as it did in Grand Theft Auto 3; you may believe that this approach lacks depth or you may think that it is the right decision on the part of the developers because of the way one could identify with Freeman. Sadly, the plot of the story itself also matches the levels of frustration Half-Life attained, a convoluted, somewhat bittersweet ending is the cherry on top of an engaging, yet not entirely satisfying dramatic experience.
On other fronts, the game excels: its graphics engine is able to bring unparalleled life to every character you meet along the way, from facial expressions to their every slight movement. Large outdoor environments as well as cramped quarters are equally well rendered and may bring some joy to those who were disappointed by Doom 3's delivery. If the new Source engine is not able to represent lighting effects as beautifully and make them as believable as the Doom 3 engine, it surpasses the latter in every other respect.
Valve has also made great efforts to give gamers an inspired soundtrack and sound effects, from tasteful techno at key moments in the game to looming horror movie music for atmosphere in appropriate environments, the music in the game is well executed; but the sound effects are what make this game aurally impressive. This is perhaps more evident in Ravenholm where the tortured cries of zombies and countless other creatures manages to do what the original Resident Evil on the PlayStation did for those who first played it: make them look around for something or someone about to attack, make them catch their breath after a fierce fight only to have it taken away again by a monstrous and hideous creature that launches horrendous, life-sucking leeches at them. Without a cleverly orchestrated soundtrack, all this emotion could not reach the levels it does in Half-Life 2.
This whole, immersive experience is even more rewarding because Half-Life 2 did not require you to own an incredibly powerful PC to enjoy the game at its fullest. The only downside to this is that if you did not own a powerful PC, the loading times at the heart of every level in the game may take you away from the whole experience, much like it may have back in '98; but it seems like a small price to pay and it is soon forgotten once you are back into the thick of the game again.
Because of the new graphics engine, new weapons like the gravity gun are quite a novelty and may become a source of extra joy in an already great game that translates real-world physics like no other. In the end, once you finish Half-Life 2 and get past the possible frustration surrounding its storyline, you may have forgotten that this game should have been in your hands over a year ago, in a time where it could have amazed you even more and rewarded you even more.
Still the best game I've ever played, nearly 10 years later. The pacing of the narrative complements the combat and puzzle solving perfectly, and still looks beautiful!

There are going to be reviews that comment that the comedy is outrageous; it deals with concepts that are offensive on every front.   But you knew that going in, and that's part of what attracts people to southpark.  Nazi Zombies?  Stuttering?  Token african americans?  Self made abortions?   It's all here.
All of that said, what isn't here is an effective control system.   Playing the game on an I7-4770, 290X Video + QDH (2560x1440) it looks beautiful, but the controls are out of whack in a way that doesn't impact any other game I play.. the game seems to respond to controllers (I use the XBOX360 Controller for windows) in a way that seems either slow or just.. wrong.   Making the game very difficult to play, even on casual levels.   I've tried editing some settings, but adjusting to the timing is.. not really something that is consistent.  This is a downfall from someone who had no problem grabbing up time at Tomb Raider, Dishonored and other games.. but here, simple tasks can be downright daunting as a button press on my keypad seems to take forever to come into place in the game.
The game has a big problme here in that it's all or not; you're on the controller or the keyboard, there is no option to switch back and forth between the two, and the game doesn't provide you any options to reset the key layout for those of us who have seperate keypads.   That said, it's quite fun and I'll remain hopeful that an update provides for these issues.

HALF LIFE 2 REVIEW
Half Life 2 is the first FPS I ever played. I remember when I bought the Orange Box on PS3 I was just amazed! 5 years later replaying it on PC it just adds to the amazing quality of the game. I loved every single second of it and is one my most favorite games of all time. Half Life 2 is a tense, thrilling, and all around amazing game that should be played by everyone.
NOT FOR: People who don't like FPS's. I would still recommend trying it out, but if that's not really your thing, I don't think Half Life 2 would change your mind all that much. However keep in mind that this is more of an old school first person shooter, unlike say Call of Duty. This game doesn't tell you where to go or how to get there, maybe not as much as the original Half-Life, but still a far cry from the crazy hand holding a lot of modern games have today.
FOR: People who want to play or try out a different stlye of FPS. This is not Call of Duty. No constant checkpoints or arrows showing you where to go. While this may prove frustrating for some...(It was for me the first time I tried it.) It proves to be extremely rewarding. On a other note this game doesn't have regenerating health which up's the challenge factor considerably. Even on easy you can every easily die if you don't react fast enough.
IN CONCLUSION: I hope this review finds you well and if you want some other games like Half Life 2, make sure to get it's sequels Episode 1 & 2 . Also try out Portal and Portal 2 as they are in the same universe. (The Portal series is a puzzle game so it's different, but it's in the same story universe.)  Lastly play the originaly it'll be worth it.
I'm not really fond of FPS in general. But i've really enjoyed playing HL2. Surprised? Me neither.

All of that said, what isn't here is an effective control system. Making the game very difficult to play, even on casual levels.   I've tried editing some settings, but adjusting to the timing is.. not really something that is consistent. The game has a big problme here in that it's all or not; you're on the controller or the keyboard, there is no option to switch back and forth between the two, and the game doesn't provide you any options to reset the key layout for those of us who have seperate keypads. I wish Super Hexagon were an arcade cabinet so that people could gather to watch me play and cheer me on; I have never felt that way about a game before.
It's rewiring my brain.  I can feel it.  The experience is euphoric.
There are many, many hours yet ahead of me in Super Hexagon, and I have only attempted half of its content thus far.  Even so, I feel confident in saying that this is an all-time classic, one of the greatest games ever made.
Buy Super Hexagon.  Play it for dozens of hours.  Play it with a gamepad's shoulder buttons; using your hands separately will improve cognitive separation between moving left and right over, say, clicking a mouse, and the response is much better than keys on a keyboard.  Turn off v-sync.  Practice using your peripheral vision.  Don't confuse the music tempo for the game speed.  Learn precise button timing so that you can move to your desired position without always staring directly at the center of the screen.  Develop the ability to remain calm at the moment of greatest pressure.
Experiment with your mind: distract yourself while you play, reminisce about something unrelated, talk to somebody, look through the screen, put yourself in an abstract place as you try to visualize a vast plane of shapes converging upon you, just zone out, or try the opposite and allow your eyes to dart about the screen in a hyper-aware state.
Fall in love.  You'll feel such admiration for the simplicity of this game design, the mechanical and visual beauty of the patterns, the perfect balance that somehow always keeps the accelerating and randomly generated landscape plausibly navigable, and the devious implementation of visual effects to sabotage your sense of absolute motion.  You'll develop an inexplicable punk zeal for geometry as Jenn Frank nonchalantly announces your longevity: "Triangle.  Square.  Pentagon."  You'll ♥♥♥♥♥♥ uncontrollably at the sound of "Hexagon" as the colors melt into a deep blue or shift to white and candy pink.  You'll know that this is where the true game begins.  You'll suddenly notice the enormous unrestrained grin on your face as you finally, finally beat your previous record... and go on for another fifteen seconds.  You're in the ♥♥♥♥ing groove.  You're zen now.
"Game over."  You feel goddamned amazing.  You need to take a break for a minute because your hands are shaking and your heart is pounding.  Just for a minute.  "Begin."

This is something that Super Meat Boy also has in common with this game. A difficulty curve and easing-in to the game, along with instant respawn for its one shot deaths.

The game breeds the snark / toilet humor of south park, with a turn based paper-mario style rpg. Characters are lively and true to the original southpark formula, all of which are fully voiced with their television persona's. The game pokes fun at various video game memes and archetypes, such as the Silent Protaginist, and the players need to loot everything he or she sees. Combat is simplistic but encourages interaction, and openly punishes button mashing. This, combined with a wide array of combat partners, classes (each with their own skill tree's.) and various equipment mods to customize how you play; you are likely to never run out of fun ways to synergize and kill enemies.
While it can be compelted in under 10 hours. Many achievement hunters who wish to see the entire game will likely get 40 or so out of it in a single playthrough. The best part of the game, in my frank opinion, is the ability to create your own south park character dubbed "the new kid" and join the infamous party of 4 throughout their adventures in Southpark. Although lacking a female option, the customization is so good, that you can play as one if you desire, provided you find and purchase the costumes / makeup to make yourself appear as such. Which works quite well as there are various female style armors to further this sort of cosplay.
The game is not without faults though. There are various bugs which can prevent the player from advancing, and even causing them to lose progress due to the poorly implemented save system. DLC may encourage 2nd or 3rd playthroughs, provided they can add to what the game already provides.
